items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d013", row n="5", KO field
items.original: EN: "For instance, he can drive a car, he can fly a plane, and he can sail a boat. But he can't ride a bicycle."  KO: "예를 들어 그는 자동차를 운전할 수 있고 그는 비행기를 운전할 수 있고 그는 배를 운전할 수 있다. 그러나 그는 자전거를 탈 수 없다."
items.problem: The whole point of the English sentence is that English uses a different verb for each vehicle — drive / fly / sail / ride. The Korean flattens drive, fly and sail into one verb, 운전하다, three times. "비행기를 운전하다" and "배를 운전하다" are also not idiomatic Korean; a plane is 조종하다 and a boat is 몰다 or 항해하다.
items.correction: KO: "예를 들어 그는 자동차를 운전할 수 있고, 비행기를 조종할 수 있고, 배를 몰 수 있다. 그러나 그는 자전거를 탈 수 없다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d014", row n="1", KO field
items.original: EN: "He's a very good athlete. He can play basketball, football, and baseball. He is an excellent runner."  KO: "그는 매우 훌륭한 운동 선수다. 그는 농구, 축구, 야구를 할 수 있다. 그는 훌륭한 달리기 선수다."
items.problem: The surrounding corpus is unmistakably American — dollars in d018 and d020, "an American millionaire", "New Jersey police", "an American and a Frenchman" — and "basketball, football, and baseball" is the standard American trio, in which football means 미식축구, not soccer. Translating it as 축구 gives Korean learners the British reading in an American passage, and 축구 is the word they will later need for "soccer".
items.correction: KO: "그는 농구, 미식축구, 야구를 할 수 있다." If the American reading is thought too uncertain to assert, "미식축구(축구)" or a short footnote would also resolve it.

items.lesson: d014, d015, d019, d020, d022, d024 (script pages)
items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d014-1.json blocks[3] and blocks[7]; d015-1.json blocks[2]; d019-1.json blocks[2],[5],[6]; d020-1.json blocks[2] and blocks[13]; d022-1.json blocks[9]; d024-1.json blocks[3],[4],[6]
items.original: d020-1: "나는 결코 구라파로 여행해본 적이 없지만 Guadaloupe는 가본 적이 있다." and "나는 올해 다시 Guadaloupe로 가기로 이미 결정했다."   d014-1: "그는 또 테니스와 골프롤 할 수 있다." and "그는 러시아어, 폴튜갈어, 독일어, 이태리어, 중국어를 안다."   d015-1: "디스코택"   d019-1/d024-1: "불란서", "개스스토브", "개스가"   d022-1: "텔레비젼"   d013-1: "할 수 있 다."
items.problem: The -1 script pages carry a set of spelling and orthography defects that the scripts file does not. The worst is "Guadaloupe", a misspelling of the proper noun Guadeloupe — which the English script and d020.json's own hints block spell correctly, so the page contradicts its own lesson. "골프롤" is a keystroke corruption of 골프를. "폴튜갈어" is a third spelling of Portuguese in a course that already has 포르투갈어 and 폴투갈어. 구라파, 불란서, 이태리, 개스 and 텔레비젼 are pre-standardisation forms replaced by 유럽, 프랑스, 이탈리아, 가스 and 텔레비전. "할 수 있 다" has a space inside the word.
items.correction: d020-1: Guadaloupe → 과들루프 (matching the scripts file) or Guadeloupe; 구라파 → 유럽. d014-1: 골프롤 → 골프를; 폴튜갈어 → 포르투갈어; 이태리어 → 이탈리아어. d015-1: 디스코택 → 디스코텍. d019-1/d024-1: 불란서 → 프랑스; 개스 → 가스. d022-1: 텔레비젼 → 텔레비전. d013-1: "할 수 있 다" → "할 수 있다". The simplest fix for the whole class is to regenerate every -1 page's Korean blocks from ld_english_scripts.json, which is the file actually rendered.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d014" row n="4", "d017" row n="3", "d020" row n="1", "d024" row n="9", KO field
items.original: d014 #4: "…여러분은 그가 보트타는 것을 좋아하지 않을 것이라고 생각할꺼야."   d017 #3: "계곡에 혹은 언덕에? 호수가에 혹은 해변에? 산속에 혹은 숲속에?"   d020 #1: "나는 결코 유럽로 여행해본 적이 없지만 과들루프에는 가본 적이 있다."   d024 #9: "…군중은 그 기구가 착륙했을 때 매우 놀랬다."
items.problem: Four Korean orthography errors in rendered rows. "생각할꺼야" should be 생각할 거야 (거 is never spelt 꺼). "호수가" needs the 사이시옷: 호숫가. "유럽로" takes the wrong particle after a consonant-final noun: 유럽으로. "놀랬다" is a nonstandard form of 놀랐다.
items.correction: d014 #4: "…여러분은 그가 보트 타는 것을 좋아하리라고는 생각하지 않을 것이다."   d017 #3: "…호숫가에 혹은 해안에?"   d020 #1: "나는 결코 유럽으로 여행해 본 적이 없지만…"   d024 #9: "…매우 놀랐다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d015", row n="5", KO field; same sentence in content/lessons/ld/d015-1.json
items.original: EN: "I sat around for a while and then I walked home early. I'm going to go again next Saturday though."  KO: "나는 한 동안 그 주변에 앉아있은 다음 일찍 집으로 걸어갔다. 그러나 나는 다음 토요일에 다시 가겠다."
items.problem: "sit around" is a phrasal verb meaning to sit doing nothing, to hang about idly. The translator read "around" as a preposition of place and produced "그 주변에 앉아" (sat near it / sat around it), which is a different claim and loses the idiom the sentence exists to teach. "앉아있은 다음" is also ungrammatical Korean (the adjectival -은 cannot attach to 있다 this way).
items.correction: KO: "나는 한동안 우두커니 앉아 있다가 일찍 집으로 걸어갔다. 그래도 나는 다음 토요일에 또 갈 것이다."

items.original: "피터 패트랄리스는 그의 어머니를 돕고 있었다. 그녀는 새 집을 갖고 있었다."
items.problem: The English is "They had a new house." and ld_english_scripts.json correctly has "그들은 새 집을 갖고 있었다." The -1 page says 그녀는 (she), which changes who owns the house and contradicts the rendered Korean of the same round. It also breaks the story's setup, since the joke at the end depends on the house being the family's, not the mother's alone.
items.correction: "피터 패트랄리스는 그의 어머니를 돕고 있었다. 그들은 새 집을 갖고 있었다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d018", rows n="6" and n="7", EN field
items.original: row 6 EN: "I don't believe it, his friend answered. I will make a bet with you."   row 7 EN: "The millionaire replied, It will cost you $500 to find out who is right."
items.problem: Both rows are direct speech printed with no quotation marks. As written, row 6 is a comma splice ("I don't believe it, his friend answered") and row 7 puts a capitalised independent clause after a comma. This is the only round in the batch that uses direct speech, and it is punctuated incorrectly throughout. Every other row of this round is correct, so the reader has no cue that these two are quotations.
items.correction: row 6 EN: "\"I don't believe it,\" his friend answered. \"I will make a bet with you.\""   row 7 EN: "The millionaire replied, \"It will cost you $500 to find out who is right.\""   (Punctuation-only changes: the dictation checker strips punctuation, so the Step 2 answer key is unaffected. Confirm whether unifiedSpeechKey treats the added quotation marks as a text change; if it does, regenerate with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs`.)

items.original: EN: "The passengers, 2 Americans and one Frenchman, kept chickens in the ship for food."   hints block in d019.json: "Jules Verne, French 1865, two Americans one Frenchman 97 hours, 13 minutes,"
items.problem: The same sentence writes one small number as a digit ("2") and the next as a word ("one"). Standard English style spells out both at this size, and the audio says "two" either way. The dictation checker in Step 2 (LdLearningView.tsx:308-328) strips punctuation and compares strings, so a learner who hears "two Americans" and types "two Americans" is marked WRONG, while only the digit "2" is accepted. items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d020", row n="9", KO field; same sentence in content/lessons/ld/d020-1.json
items.original: EN: "I often had fresh, juicy fruit and little rolls with sweet butter."  KO: "나는 종종 신선하고 즙이 많은 과일과 맛있는 버터를 곁들인 작은 롤(빵)들을 먹었다."
items.problem: In American English "sweet butter" is the standard term for UNSALTED butter, not butter that tastes sweet. The Korean "맛있는 버터" (delicious butter) invents a meaning that is not in the English and hides the real one.
items.correction: KO: "나는 종종 신선하고 즙이 많은 과일과 무염 버터를 곁들인 작은 롤빵을 먹었다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d022", row n="5", KO field
items.original: EN: "Nobody tells them what they should or shouldn't be doing."  KO: "아무도 그들에게 무엇을 하고 있거나 하고 있지 말아야한다고 말하지 않는다."
items.problem: The Korean is not parseable as written. It renders "what they should or shouldn't be doing" as "무엇을 하고 있거나 하고 있지 말아야한다고", which drops the interrogative 무엇을 …하는지 structure and leaves 하고 있거나 dangling with no 해야 한다. A Korean reader cannot recover the English from it. "말아야한다" is also missing its space (말아야 한다).

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d023", row n="4", KO field
items.original: EN: "This time, though, the police feel they have put an airtight case together against Morton."  KO: "그러나 이번에 경찰은 Morton에 대하여 바람샐틈없는 소송을 만들어냈다고 느낀다."
items.problem: "a case against someone" in a police context is the body of evidence, not a lawsuit. 소송 means litigation, which police do not file — prosecutors do. "바람샐틈없는" is also written without spaces (바람 샐 틈 없는) and is an odd register next to 소송.
items.correction: KO: "그러나 이번에는 경찰이 Morton에 대해 빈틈없는 증거를 확보했다고 보고 있다."

items.original: I see, the doctor asked Bobby.
items.problem: As a standalone dictation item this is not grammatical English: the reporting verb asked has no question attached to it — the question it introduces ("How do you feel now, my boy?") is in the next row, #7. Read on its own the sentence says the doctor asked the words "I see", which is impossible. The rows are split one sentence-group per dictation item, so the learner assembles and is graded on this broken sentence as a model.
items.correction: Move the reporting clause to the question: row #6 → "I see, the doctor said." (KO: “알겠습니다.” 그 의사가 말했다.) and row #7 → "The doctor asked Bobby, how do you feel now, my boy? Bobby answered, Terrible. I think I'm going to die." Both rows' English changes, so regenerate their Azure clips in the same task with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs`.

items.original: “너는 지금 어떻게 느끼니, 나의 소년아?” Bobby는 “끔찍합니다. 나는 죽을 것이라고 생각합니다.”라고 대답했다.
items.problem: 나의 소본아-type vocatives do not exist in Korean: a doctor addressing a child says 얘야 or 아가, never 나의 소년아, which reads as a translation-machine artifact. 너는 지금 어떻게 느끼니 is likewise a word-for-word rendering of "How do you feel" — Korean asks 지금 기분이 어떠니 / 지금 좀 어떠니.
items.correction: “지금은 좀 어떠니, 얘야?” Bobby는 “끔찍해요. 저는 죽을 것 같아요.”라고 대답했다.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d037-1.json blocks[6] and blocks[10]; d038-1.json blocks[4] and blocks[5]; d047-1.json blocks[3]
items.original: “오, 의사, 당신은 정말 그렇게 생각하십니까?” Bobby의 어머니는 매우 기뻐보였다.
items.problem: The -1 pages are an older copy of the Korean. Two kinds of difference from the scripts file. (1) Wording: 오, 의사, 당신은 정말 그렇게 생각하십니까? — 의사 is never used as a form of address in Korean (you call a doctor 선생님), and 당신은 to one's own doctor is rude; the scripts file already has the natural “오, 선생님, 정말 그렇게 생각하세요?”. (2) Non-standard spellings the scripts file has already fixed: 오렌지 쥬스 (→ 주스) in d037-1 blocks[6], 텔레비젼 (→ 텔레비전) twice in d038-1 blocks[4]/[5], 다양한 개스 (→ 가스) in d047-1 blocks[3].
items.correction: Copy the scripts-file Korean into these -1 blocks: “오, 선생님, 정말 그렇게 생각하세요?”, 오렌지 주스, 텔레비전, 가스.

items.original: 이제 저를 용서해주신다면 저는 Morton의 집안의 아들 Alfred를 보기 위하여 길을 건너가야 합니다.
items.problem: "Now if you will excuse me" is a fixed parting formula meaning 이만 실례하겠습니다 / 실례지만 저는 이제 …. Rendering it as 저를 용서해주신다면 ("if you forgive me") teaches the learner that excuse here means 용서, which is exactly the false friend Korean learners already fall for. 아무 잘못도 없는 상황이라 한국어로도 뜻이 통하지 않는다. (Minor, same line: Mortons' is the family's plural possessive, so Morton의 집안의 아들 is clumsy — Morton 씨 댁 아들.)
items.correction: 이제 실례하겠습니다. 저는 Morton 씨 댁 아들 Alfred를 보러 길을 건너가야 합니다.

items.original: He is almost sick when my mother calls, Herbert, it's 7:00. Get up.
items.problem: Worse case of the digit problem above: the target normalizes to "... calls herbert its 700 get up" (the colon is stripped by normalizeTyped, src/components/LdLearningView.tsx:314-320). Whatever the synthesizer says for "7:00" ("seven o'clock" or "seven"), no learner transcribing by ear can produce "7:00" or "700" — "it's seven o'clock" and "it's seven" are both graded wrong.
items.correction: Either accept the spoken forms in grading (normalize times/numbers before comparing), or change the `en` to "it's seven o'clock" and regenerate that row's Azure clip in the same task with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs`. The Korean guide already reads 지금 7시다, so no translation change is needed.

items.original: 나는 그를 부르고 말한다. “일어나. 당장 일어나지 않으면 엄마가 너를 침대로부터 끌어내기 위하여 여기 위에 계실꺼야.”
items.problem: "Mom will be up here" means she will come up here (2층으로 올라오실 거야) — the threat is that she will come, which is exactly what happens in row #9 (어머니는 이층으로 올라와서). 여기 위에 계실꺼야 says she will BE above here, which is not the meaning and is not idiomatic Korean. 계실꺼야 is also misspelled: the bound noun 것 contracts to 거, so it is 계실 거야.
items.correction: “일어나. 당장 일어나지 않으면 엄마가 너를 침대에서 끌어내려고 여기로 올라오실 거야.”

items.original: 그것은 내 동생과 함께 매일 그런 방식이다. 어쩌면 언젠가는 그는 제 시간에 일어나는 것을 배 울 것이다. 그러나 나는 정말 그렇게 생각하지 않는다.
items.problem: 배 울 is one word broken by a stray space (배울), left over from the legacy page's line wrap. This is the rendered Korean, so the space is on screen.
items.correction: … 제 시간에 일어나는 것을 배울 것이다. …

items.original: 우리 선생님 Miss Ellis는 자연에 대한 전문가였고 나는 그가 식물과 동물에 대하여 우리 반원들에게 말하 는 것들의 모두를 언제나 믿었다.
items.problem: Wrong pronoun gender. Miss Ellis is a woman and the English is "all of the things SHE told our class", but this page writes 그가. The scripts file has the correct 그녀가 for the same row, so the -1 page is the stale copy. (The stray space in 말하 는 is a legacy line-wrap artifact in the same line.)
items.correction: 나는 그녀가 식물과 동물에 대하여 우리 반원들에게 말하는 것들의 모두를 언제나 믿었다.

items.original: 내가 16살이었을 때 나는 우리 부모님께서는 매우 좋으신 분들이고 나는 그분들을 사랑하지만 정말로 매우 많이 알지 않는다는 생각을 얻었다.
items.problem: Two broken pieces of Korean. 알지 않는다 is not Korean — 알다 is negated as 모르다 / 알지 못하다, so "didn't know very much" must be 잘 알지 못하신다 / 많이 모르신다. And 생각을 얻었다 is a word-for-word calque of "got the idea"; Korean says 생각이 들었다 / 생각을 하게 되었다. The honorific is also dropped mid-sentence (부모님께서는 … 알지 않는다).
items.correction: 내가 16살이었을 때 나는, 우리 부모님께서는 매우 좋으신 분들이고 나도 그분들을 사랑하지만 정말로 아는 것이 별로 없으시다는 생각이 들었다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d041 #1 and #3; d045 #7 and #8; d046 #2
items.original: When I was 16 years old I got the idea that my parents, while they were very nice people and I loved them, really didn't know very much.
items.problem: The English script writes these numbers as digits, but the learner only ever hears them spoken. In Step 2's typing mode (⌨️ 직접 키보드 타이핑 모드) the answer is graded by normalizeTyped in src/components/LdLearningView.tsx:314-323, which lowercases and strips everything except [a-z0-9 ] — so digits are kept and "sixteen" is simply not equal to "16". A learner who types exactly the words the voice says is marked 틀림. The same rows show the course is not even self-consistent: d041 #3 is "when I was 18 ... in just two years", d045 #7 is "Bill has three English classes a week. He'll get 3 credits for English." and d045 #8 is "John has two German classes. He'll get 2 credits for the German course." — the same number is spelled out and written as a digit in one sentence. The hints block, which exists precisely to show 숫자 to the learner, is never rendered by LdLearningView (it is read only by the disabled quiz at LdLearningView.tsx:129-131), so there is nothing on screen telling the learner to type a digit. Affected rows in this scope: d041 #1 ("16"), d041 #3 ("18"), d045 #7 ("3 credits"), d045 #8 ("2 credits"), d046 #2 ("Within 2 years").
items.correction: Safer fix (no clip loss): make the typed-answer comparison accept spelled-out numbers, i.e. normalize digits↔number words on both sides in handleCheckDictation before comparing. Content fix (spelling the numbers out in `en`: "sixteen", "eighteen", "three credits", "two credits", "within two years") also works and would make each sentence internally consistent, but it changes the English text, so the Azure clips for those rows must be regenerated in the same task with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs`.

items.original: Pete는 좋은 타자수가 아니었지만 다행히도 조지는 빠르고 정확했다.
items.problem: The same characters are written in Latin letters and in Hangul at random, sometimes inside one sentence. d042 introduces them as George Holmes와 Pete Wendel in #1, then row #3 writes Pete in Latin and 조지 in Hangul side by side, and rows #5-#7 keep 조지. d043 #5 then switches Pete to 피트. d044 mixes Bill Patterson/빌 and John/존 across rows #1-#5, and d045 uses 존 and 빌 throughout while d044 #1 used the Latin names. Nothing distinguishes the two forms — it is an uncorrected legacy inconsistency.
items.correction: Pick one convention per character for the whole story arc (d042-d045) — keeping the English spelling is the more useful one here, since the learner has to type the name in the dictation — and apply it to every Korean row.

items.original: 그는 언제나 Pete의 리포트틀 그를 대신해서 타자쳐주곤 했다.
items.problem: 리포트틀 is a typo for 리포트를 (틀/를 keystroke slip). The scripts file has the correct 리포트를.
items.correction: 그는 언제나 Pete의 리포트를 그를 대신해서 타자쳐주곤 했다.

items.original: 다행히 그는 일전 날 시내에서 그와 마주쳤다. 그들은 다음 토요일에 함께 저녁을 먹을 것이다.
items.problem: 일전 날 is not a Korean word form. 일전(日前) already means "a few days ago" and is used as 일전에; "the other day" is 일전에 or 며칠 전에.
items.correction: 다행히 그는 며칠 전에 시내에서 그와 마주쳤다.

items.original: 졸업 후에 조지는 미국에서 두 번째로 큰 도시인 쉬카고로 갔다.
items.problem: Two problems in one line. (1) Factually wrong: Chicago is the THIRD largest city in the United States (New York, then Los Angeles, then Chicago at about 2.74 million); it has not been second since the 1990 census. (2) It contradicts the English the learner is supposed to produce — the script says "one of the largest cities in the United States", and the scripts file's own Korean for the same row is the correct 미국에서 가장 큰 도시 중 하나인 시카고로 갔다. Also 쉬카고 is not the standard Korean transliteration (시카고).
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file wording: "졸업 후에 조지는 미국에서 가장 큰 도시 중 하나인 시카고로 갔다."

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d044-1.json blocks[2]; d045-1.json blocks[6] and blocks[7]; d046-1.json blocks[4]
items.original: 지금은 6월이고 Bill Patterson과 John Cocoran은 그들의 일학년을 끝낼 것이다.
items.problem: Three proper names are misspelled in the -1 Korean scripts, each one letter short of the English and of the scripts file: John Cocoran (d044-1) for John Corcoran; Charles M. Mcarthy and Mcarthy 교수 (d045-1, two places) for McCarthy; Phil Stricklan (d046-1) for Phil Strickland. The main lessons' hints blocks spell all three correctly, so only the -1 pages are wrong.
items.correction: d044-1: John Corcoran. d045-1: Charles M. McCarthy / McCarthy 교수. d046-1: Phil Strickland.

items.original: 그의 영어 교사는 Charles M. McCarthy 교수이다. M은 그의 가운데 이름인 Mark를 대표한다.
items.problem: "M stands for Mark" means the letter is short for Mark. 대표한다 means "represents" in the sense of acting on behalf of a group, and is not used for an abbreviation; the Korean reads as if the letter M is Mark's delegate. Also, the man is a 교수 teaching a required university subject, so 영어 교사 is off (교수님 / 영어 담당 교수).
items.correction: 그의 영어 담당 교수는 Charles M. McCarthy 교수이다. M은 그의 가운데 이름인 Mark의 약자이다.

items.original: 존은 두 독일어 수업이 있다. 그는 독일어 과정에서 2학점을 받을 것이다.
items.problem: 두 독일어 수업이 있다 is ungrammatical: Korean needs a counter and normal word order — 독일어 수업이 두 개 있다 / 일주일에 독일어 수업이 두 번 있다. The parallel row #7 gets it right (빌은 일주일에 세 번 영어 수업이 있다), so this one row is the odd one out.
items.correction: 존은 일주일에 독일어 수업이 두 번 있다. 그는 독일어 과정에서 2학점을 받을 것이다.

items.original: Ben Frank는 성공한 사업가이다. 몇 년 전에 그는 그의 고향에 작은 잡화점을 열었다.
items.problem: 잡화점 is a variety/general store (household sundries). A grocery store is 식료품점, and the very next row confirms it — he sells 육류, 과일, 야채, 차, 커피. The learner is given the wrong Korean word for a common English noun.
items.correction: 몇 년 전에 그는 고향에 작은 식료품점을 열었다.

items.original: Phil은 쇼핑가에 좀처럼 가지 않지만 오늘 그는 그의 딸에게로 집으로 가져갈 달콤한 어떤 것을 찾고 있다.
items.problem: 그의 딸에게로 집으로 가져갈 stacks two directional particles (에게로 + 으로) on one verb, which is not grammatical Korean. "to take home to his daughter" is 집에 있는 딸에게 가져다줄 / 집에 가져가 딸에게 줄.
items.correction: Phil은 쇼핑가에 좀처럼 가지 않지만, 오늘은 집에 있는 딸에게 가져다줄 달콤한 것을 찾고 있다.

items.original: Ben은 쇼핑구역에 대한 모든 것을 안다. 그는 가까운 한 과자 가게를 추천했다. Phil은 그들과 그들의 가족들이 언제 함께 할 것을 제언했다.
items.problem: "sometime" is 언젠가, not 언제. As written, 언제 함께 할 것을 제언했다 reads as a question word ("when") and the clause does not hold together. Also 쇼핑구역 here and 쇼핑가 in row #3 translate the same English phrase "the shopping district" two different ways in the same round.
items.correction: Phil은 언젠가 두 사람의 가족이 함께 모이자고 제안했다. (and use the same word — 쇼핑가 — as row #3 for "the shopping district")

items.original: 한 속담은 우리에게 만일 어떤 것이 잘 되기를 원한다면 직접 해야 한다고 우리에게 말한다.
items.problem: 우리에게 appears twice in one sentence (한 속담은 우리에게 … 우리에게 말한다). One of them is a leftover from an edit.
items.correction: 한 속담은 만일 어떤 것이 잘 되기를 원한다면 직접 해야 한다고 우리에게 말한다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d049" row n=3 (KO); same wording in content/lessons/ld/d049-1.json blocks[4]
items.original: 그 청중의 일부 회원들은 그 피아니스트가 어린애처럼 행동했다고 말했다.
items.problem: "회원" means a member of a club or organisation — a person who has joined and is on a roll. It cannot mean a member of an audience. The English is "Certain members of the audience said ...", where "member of the audience" is simply a person in the audience (관객/청중 가운데 일부).
items.correction: 청중 가운데 일부는 그 피아니스트가 어린애처럼 행동했다고 말했다.

items.original: 즉, 그들은 쉽게 화내낸 것처럼 보인다. 예를 들어 한 유명한 피아니스트는 맨 앞 줄의 일부 사람들이 많은 소음을 만들고 있었기 때문에 그의 콘서트 중의 하나 동안 무대를 떠났다.
items.problem: "화내낸" is not a Korean word — a corrupted form. ld_english_scripts.json d049 row 2 has the correct "즉, 그들은 쉽게 화를 내는 것처럼 보인다."
items.correction: 즉, 그들은 쉽게 화를 내는 것처럼 보인다. 예를 들어 ...

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/dNNN.json → blocks[] — the block immediately after the "hints" block
items.original: { "type": "hints", "text": "1893, Detroit, Michigan amazed motor vehicle Henry Ford. mechanical 1876 13. 1903," }, { "type": "instruction", "text": "found Ford Motor Company. Model T. 15 million 1908 1927. 1924, 7500 5 dollars large sum" }
items.problem: Long hint lists were split across two blocks when the legacy pages were extracted, and the continuation was typed as "instruction" instead of "hints". Seven of the twelve rounds in scope are affected (d050, d053, d054, d056, d058, d059, d060; d054 has two such continuation blocks). The consequence is that half of each round's hint list is not hint data at all — it sits in the same block type as the task instruction "다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서 영어로 받아쓰기를 하세요." Repo-wide there are 122 such blocks across the 276 main lessons.
items.correction: Merge each continuation into the preceding hints block (single "hints" block per lesson), or retype it as "hints". Either way, a lesson's hint text must not share a block type with its task instruction.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d050" rows n=5, n=8 and n=9 (EN and KO)
items.original: But you would be surprised how some of these people neglect their own children. … Mrs. Brown always says he should be glad to do this, but her husband believes that she should stay home and take care of the children. He believes that there is no need to leave one's own home in order to practice charity.
items.problem: The round's moral is built entirely on a woman being wrong to leave the house. Mrs. Brown goes out twice a week, the narrator calls this neglecting her children, her husband cooking dinner on those two evenings is framed as an imposition, and the husband's view that she "should stay home and take care of the children" is given the closing, unchallenged word. As a values message shipped in a 2026 paid course this is a dated gender-role lesson, and nothing in the text marks it as one character's opinion rather than the point.
items.correction: Rewrite the example so the neglect is not gendered — e.g. make the busy charity volunteer a couple, or Mr. Brown, or drop rows 6-8 and keep the abstract point in rows 1-5 and 9. If the round is kept as is, the closing row should at least be neutral: "He believes that charity should not mean leaving one's own family behind." Update d050-1 and regenerate the clips for any changed lines.

items.original: 이것은 우리가 다른 사람의 책임에 대하여 염려하기 전에 가정에서의 우리의 책임을 돌보야야 한다는 것 을 단순히 의미한다.
items.problem: Two corruptions: "돌보야야" is a typo for "돌보아야", and "것 을" is split by a stray space. ld_english_scripts.json d050 row 2 has both correct: "... 우리의 책임을 돌보아야 한다는 것을 단순히 의미한다."
items.correction: 이것은 우리가 다른 사람의 책임에 대하여 염려하기 전에 가정에서의 우리의 책임을 돌보아야 한다는 것을 단순히 의미한다.

items.original: Actually however, most newspaper reporters lead rather routine lives.
items.problem: "however" is a parenthetical adverb and needs a comma before it as well as after: "Actually, however,". The same course gets it right in d049 row 5 ("Actually, however, they should have blamed ..."), so this is an inconsistency within the same corpus, not a style choice.
items.correction: Actually, however, most newspaper reporters lead rather routine lives.

items.original: The average young reporter spends most of his day at his desk. His job is to rewrite the stories that the older and more experienced men bring in.
items.problem: The round describes journalism as an all-male occupation: the generic reporter is "his", and the senior reporters are "the older and more experienced men". This was ordinary 1960s textbook English, but as a description of the profession presented to learners in 2026 it is simply out of date, and the course has no framing that marks it as a period text.
items.correction: "The average young reporter spends most of the day at a desk. Their job is to rewrite the stories that the older and more experienced reporters bring in." Update the Korean rows and d051-1; regenerate the clips.

items.original: 가끔 상사가 그를 한 이야기를 취재하도록 내보내낼지 모른다.
items.problem: "내보내낼지" is a corrupted form. ld_english_scripts.json d051 row 7 has the correct "가끔 상사가 그를 한 이야기를 취재하도록 내보낼지 모른다."
items.correction: 가끔 상사가 그를 한 이야기를 취재하도록 내보낼지 모른다.

items.original: 게다가 텐트에서 사는 것이 훨씬 더 재미있다. 어두워진 다음에 대부분의 캠핑객들은 모닥불 주위에 모여 서 노래부르는 것을 좋아한다.
items.problem: "모여 서" is split by a stray space inside the verb form 모여서 — a line-wrap artifact from the legacy extraction. This is the rendered Korean, shown in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: ... 대부분의 캠핑객들은 모닥불 주위에 모여서 노래 부르는 것을 좋아한다.

items.original: 미국인들에게 좋아하는 휴가 장소 중의 하나는 천개의 호수의 땅인 Northern Wisconsin이다.
items.problem: The -1 page says "a land of a thousand lakes" (천개의 호수). The English script and its Korean in ld_english_scripts.json say "a land of thousands of lakes" / "수천 개의 호수가 있는 땅인 위스콘신 북부". Wisconsin actually has about 15,074 lakes, so "thousands" is the correct figure and the -1 page understates it by more than an order of magnitude while also contradicting the round's own English.
items.correction: 미국인들에게 좋아하는 휴가 장소 중의 하나는 수천 개의 호수가 있는 땅인 위스콘신 북부이다.

items.original: 일주일 남짓 캘핑 후에는 정말로 휴식하고 릴랙스했다고 느낀다.
items.problem: "캘핑" is a typo for "캠핑" (camping). ld_english_scripts.json d052 row 7 has it correctly: "일주일 남짓 캠핑 후에는 ...".
items.correction: 일주일 남짓 캠핑 후에는 정말로 휴식하고 릴랙스했다고 느낀다.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d053-1.json → blocks[6] and blocks[8] (5th and 7th Korean script lines)
items.original: 그러나 대부분의 시간 그녀는 참을성이 있고 이해한다. 그녀의 남편의 수집은 만불 가까운 가치가 있 다. … 심지어 값싼 성냥곽의 수집도 그것의 주인에게는 중요한 가치가 있다.
items.problem: Three defects on this page. "있 다" is split by a stray space. "성냥곽" is a non-standard spelling (standard: 성냥갑, as in ld_english_scripts.json d053 row 7). And the page drops "보다시피", the rendering of the English "You see," that the scripts file does carry in row 6. The same page also writes "쉬카고" in blocks[3] where the scripts file writes the standard "시카고".
items.correction: 그러나 대부분의 시간 그녀는 참을성이 있고 이해한다. 보다시피 그녀의 남편의 수집품은 거의 만 달러의 가치가 있다. … 심지어 값싼 성냥갑의 수집도 그것의 주인에게는 중요한 가치가 있다. (and 시카고 for 쉬카고)

items.original: When he reached the New World, however, he thought he had arrived at India.
items.problem: Two problems in one clause. (1) Wrong preposition: with a country you arrive *in*, not *at* — "arrived at India" is ungrammatical. (2) Historically, Columbus believed he had reached the Indies (las Indias — the islands off East Asia), which is precisely why the next sentence can explain the word "Indians"; "India" alone loses that link and is not what he thought.
items.correction: When he reached the New World, however, he thought he had arrived in the Indies. Update the Korean row ("자신이 인도에 도착했다고" → "자신이 인도 제도에 도착했다고") and d054-1 to match; regenerate the clip.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d054" row n=4 (KO); same wording in content/lessons/ld/d054-1.json blocks[5]
items.original: 심지어 오늘날에도 아메리카의 원주민들은 콜럼버스의 위대한 실수에 대한 찬사로써 인디언이라고 불린다.
items.problem: "찬사" means praise or a eulogy. The English "a tribute to the great mistake of Columbus" uses "tribute" in its ironic sense of a lasting monument or reminder, not praise. Rendering it as 찬사 makes the sentence say that a colonial misnomer is *praise for* a mistake, which is both nonsense and uncomfortable. Separately, the particle is wrong: "찬사로써" (로써 = by means of) should be "찬사로서" (로서 = as, in the capacity of).
items.correction: 심지어 오늘날에도 아메리카의 원주민들은 인디언이라고 불리는데, 이는 콜럼버스의 커다란 실수가 남긴 흔적이다.

items.original: 특히 관광객들은 굉장한 사진 팬이다. 그들이 집에 돌아갈 때 그들은 자신이 방문했던 장소들의 사진을 친 구들에게 보여줄 수 있기를 원한다.
items.problem: "친 구들에게" is split by a stray space in the middle of the word 친구들 — a line-wrap artifact from the legacy HTML extraction. This is the rendered Korean, shown to the learner in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: ... 자신이 방문했던 장소들의 사진을 친구들에게 보여줄 수 있기를 원한다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d055" row n=7 (KO); same wording in content/lessons/ld/d055-1.json blocks[8]
items.original: 그때 그는 렌즈로부터 커버를 벗기는 것을 잊었었다는 것을 주목했다(알게 되었다).
items.problem: An editorial remnant has been shipped to the learner: the translator wrote 주목했다, then added the correction "(알게 되었다)" in parentheses and never removed either. "주목하다" (to pay attention to) is in fact the wrong verb for "noticed" here; the parenthesis is the right one. "렌즈로부터" is also unnatural (렌즈에서).
items.correction: 그때 그는 렌즈에서 커버를 벗기는 것을 잊었다는 것을 알아차렸다.

items.original: One tourist in Rome, for example, spent a lot of time and money taking colored pictures. … He had wasted a whole roll of colored film, but he never made the mistake again.
items.problem: The standard English collocations are "color pictures" and "color film" (AmE) or "colour film" (BrE). "colored film" means film that has been coloured, and "colored" as a bare modifier is a word current American usage otherwise avoids. Both rows use it.
items.correction: "... spent a lot of time and money taking color pictures." and "He had wasted a whole roll of color film ...". Regenerate the clips for both lines.

items.original: He started to make marionettes when he was a young boy and soon became so good at putting on marionette shows that he opened a small theater of his own.
items.problem: Tony Sarg (1880-1942) was raised around puppets and inherited his grandmother's collection, but he did not build a marionette career as a boy. He became seriously interested after seeing Thomas Holden's marionette company in Britain as an adult, and turned puppetry into a profession only in 1917, aged about 37, when he founded Tony Sarg's Marionettes in New York. "Soon ... opened a small theater of his own" compresses roughly thirty years into childhood.
items.correction: "He grew up around puppets and later became so good at putting on marionette shows that he opened a small theater of his own." Update the Korean row and d056-1 to match; regenerate the clip.

items.original: He specialized in children's shows, but he also put on plays for grown-ups too.
items.problem: "also" and "too" are both used for the same addition in one clause — a redundancy that no careful writer or editor would leave. One of the two must go.
items.correction: He specialized in children's shows, but he also put on plays for grown-ups. (Regenerate the clip.)

items.original: As a matter of fact, older people sometimes seem to enjoy the plays more than children.
items.problem: Tense error. Every other sentence in this round narrates Tony Sarg in the past ("He started", "He specialized", "he put on"), and the Korean row for this very line is past: "더 나이많은 사람들이 어린이들보다 그 연극을 더 즐기는 것처럼 보였다." The English "seem" is present, so it neither matches its own Korean nor the surrounding narrative.
items.correction: As a matter of fact, older people sometimes seemed to enjoy the plays more than children. (Regenerate the clip for this line.)

items.original: 그는 자신의 marionette로 오페라, 희극, 비극 - 사람들이 즐길 것이라고 생각하는 것은 무엇이든지 공연 했다.
items.problem: "공연 했다" is split by a stray space in the middle of the verb (should be "공연했다") — a line-wrap artifact from the legacy HTML extraction. This Korean row is what the learner actually sees in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: 그는 자신의 marionette로 오페라, 희극, 비극 등 사람들이 즐길 것이라고 생각하는 것은 무엇이든지 공연했다.

items.original: 그가 노인이 될 무렵에는 그의 단순한 취미는 고도로 세련된 예술로 발전했고 Tony Sarg는 “marionette man"으로 유명하게 되어있었다.
items.problem: Mismatched quotation marks: a curly opening “ closed by a straight ". Rendered to the learner in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: ... Tony Sarg는 “marionette man”으로 유명하게 되어 있었다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d057" row n=1 (KO); same wording in content/lessons/ld/d057-1.json blocks[2]
items.original: 시골 생활은 많은 유리한 점이 있다. 한 가지로써 공기는 신선하고 깨끗하며 많은 평화와 고요함이 있다.
items.problem: Particle error: "한 가지로써" should be "한 가지로" or "우선". 로써 marks a means or instrument; the English "For one thing" is an enumerating discourse marker, not an instrument. (The same 로써/로서 confusion appears in d054 row 4.)
items.correction: 시골 생활은 많은 유리한 점이 있다. 우선 공기가 신선하고 깨끗하며 평화롭고 조용하다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d057" row n=3 (KO); same wording in content/lessons/ld/d057-1.json blocks[4]
items.original: 필요로 하는 대부분의 야채를 공급해줄 정원을 간직할 수 있다.
items.problem: "정원을 간직하다" is wrong Korean. 간직하다 means to keep something safe or treasure it (a memory, a keepsake); it cannot take a vegetable garden as its object. The English is "You can keep a garden that will supply you with most of the vegetables that you need", where "keep a garden" means to maintain or tend one — 가꾸다 / 일구다.
items.correction: 필요한 야채의 대부분을 얻을 수 있는 텃밭을 가꿀 수 있다.

items.original: His mother had died in 1876 when he was only 13.
items.problem: Henry Ford was born 30 July 1863; his mother Mary Litogot Ford died in March 1876, so he was 12, not 13. The Korean row ("그가 겨우 13살이던 1876년에") repeats the error, and the hints block repeats it a third time ("1876 13.").
items.correction: "His mother had died in 1876 when he was only 12." / "그의 어머니는 그가 겨우 12살이던 1876년에 돌아가셨다." / hints "... mechanical 1876 12. 1903,". Regenerate the Ava clip for this line.

items.original: 그의 어머니는 그가 겨우 12살인 1875년에 죽었다. 학교에서 그는 좋은 학생이 아니었다.
items.problem: The -1 script page says the mother died in 1875 when Ford was 12; ld_english_scripts.json d058 row 3 says "His mother had died in 1876 when he was only 13." / "그의 어머니는 그가 겨우 13살이던 1876년에 돌아가셨다." The two files disagree on both the year and the age, and 1875 is simply wrong — Mary Litogot Ford died in 1876.
items.correction: Make d058-1 match the corrected fact: "그의 어머니는 그가 겨우 12살이던 1876년에 돌아가셨다. 학교에서 그는 좋은 학생이 아니었다."

items.original: At the same time the play began, America's most popular radio show was ending on another station.
items.problem: The Chase and Sanborn Hour (Edgar Bergen) did not end when The War of the Worlds began — both ran 8:00-9:00 p.m. ET in the same hour. The documented mechanism is that listeners switched away from Chase and Sanborn about twelve minutes in, when the comic sketch ended and a musical number began, and so joined the play already in progress. As written, the sentence is also self-defeating: if the rival show had been ending exactly as the play began, listeners would have switched at the start and would not have "missed the very beginning" as row 5 says.
items.correction: "The play ran at the same time as America's most popular radio show on another station." plus, in row 5's spirit, "Many listeners switched over in the middle and missed the very beginning of The War of the Worlds." Update the Korean rows and d059-1 to match, and regenerate the clips.

items.original: 많은 청취자들은 ”The War of the Worlds"의 맨 첫 부분을 놓쳤다.
items.problem: The opening quotation mark is a right (closing) curly quote ” and the closing one is a straight ". Row 1 of the same round uses the correct pair “ … ”. This is a legacy-extraction artifact and it is rendered to the learner in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: 많은 청취자들은 “The War of the Worlds”의 맨 첫 부분을 놓쳤다.

items.original: 1938년에 “The War of the World"라는 연극이 라디오에서 방송되었다.
items.problem: Two defects in one line: the title is written "The War of the World" — the final s of "Worlds" is missing, so the title of the work is wrong; and the quotation marks are mismatched (curly opening “ closed by a straight "). ld_english_scripts.json d059 row 1 has the title and the quotes correct: 1938년에 “The War of the Worlds”라는 연극이 라디오에서 방송되었다.
items.correction: 1938년에 “The War of the Worlds”라는 연극이 라디오에서 방송되었다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d060" row n=1 (EN and KO); repeated in content/lessons/ld/d060.json hints block "Six thousand 120 ..."
items.original: 6,000 soldiers attacked the object, but only 120 lived to tell about it.
items.problem: The round retells the 1938 War of the Worlds broadcast. The broadcast script's own line is "seven thousand men armed with rifles and machine guns pitted against a single fighting machine of the invaders from Mars. One hundred and twenty known survivors." The number of soldiers is 7,000, not 6,000 (the 120 survivors figure is correct). The wrong number is repeated in the hints block.
items.correction: "7,000 soldiers attacked the object, but only 120 lived to tell about it." / "칠천 명의 군인들이 그 물체를 공격했지만 120명만이 살아남아서 그것에 대하여 이야기했다." / hints "Seven thousand 120 six million Martian invaders. panic". Also fix d060-1's matching Korean block. Regenerate the Ava clip.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → "d060" row n=3 (KO); same text in content/lessons/ld/d060-1.json blocks[4]
items.original: 사람들은 소식을 알기 위하여 초조하게 그 라디오 방송국으로 전화했다
items.problem: The Korean sentence has no sentence-final period, unlike every other Korean row in the round. This text is rendered to the learner in Steps 2-5.
items.correction: 사람들은 소식을 알기 위하여 초조하게 그 라디오 방송국으로 전화했다.

items.original: 그 연극을 들은 600만명 정도의 사람 중에서 이백만명 이상이 그것이 진짜 뉴스 보도라고 생각했다.
items.problem: The -1 page claims more than 2 million believed the broadcast. ld_english_scripts.json d060 row 2 says only "many thought it was a true news report" / "많은 사람이 ... 생각했다". The scripts file was evidently corrected and the -1 page was not. "Over 2 million" also overstates even Cantril's own 1940 estimate (~1.7 million believed it was news), and modern scholarship puts the figure far lower still.
items.correction: 그 연극을 들은 600만명 정도의 사람 중에서 많은 사람이 그것이 진짜 뉴스 보도라고 생각했다.

items.original: 수천명이 그 화성 침입자들을 피해서 달아나기 위하여 그들의 집을 떠났다.
items.problem: The -1 page asserts "thousands" left their homes. ld_english_scripts.json d060 row 4 says "Some people even left their homes to escape the Martian invaders." / "어떤 사람들은 화성 침입자들을 피해 달아나려고 집을 떠나기까지 했다." The scripts file's deliberately cautious wording is undone on the -1 page by a hard quantity that the panic research does not support.
items.correction: 어떤 사람들은 화성 침입자들을 피해 달아나려고 집을 떠나기까지 했다.

items.original: 많은 날들이 지난 후에야 생활이 정상으로 돌아왔다. 그 연극이 어떻게 끝났나?
items.problem: This whole first sentence has no counterpart in the English script. ld_english_scripts.json d060 row 5 is "Newspapers wrote about the panic for days. How did the play end?" / "신문들은 며칠 동안 그 소동에 대해 썼다. 그 연극이 어떻게 끝났나?" The -1 page still carries the older claim that it took many days for life to return to normal — a different assertion, and one that the panic research does not support.
items.correction: 신문들은 며칠 동안 그 소동에 대해 썼다. 그 연극이 어떻게 끝났나?

items.original: What luck I thought then. Taggy had been a favorite of ours for a long time.
items.problem: "What luck I thought then." has no punctuation between the exclamation and the reporting clause, so it reads as one ungrammatical string. The corpus systematically strips quotation marks from the en column, but here the result is not merely unquoted — it is unparseable.
items.correction: "What luck, I thought then." (or restore the quotation: "What luck!" I thought then.). Answer checking strips punctuation (LdLearningView.tsx:308-328), so this does not change grading, but the Step 5 script text should be readable. NOTE: if the letters change, regenerate the clip.

items.original: 그 남자는 얼마나 환상적인 공연자였던가! 청중은 모든 하나의 노래 후에 더욱 더 열성적이 되었다.
items.problem: "after every song" is rendered word-for-word as "모든 하나의 노래 후에", which is not Korean ("every" is being translated twice, as 모든 + 하나의).
items.correction: "...청중은 노래를 한 곡씩 들을 때마다 점점 더 열광했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d061-1.json blocks[10]).

items.original: 나의 여자 친구와 내가 Tony Montag를 보러갔던 때가 생각난다.
items.problem: Wrong character name. The performer in this story is Taggy Montag — every other line in d061, d062 and the matching row in content/ld_english_scripts.json says "Taggy Montag". "Tony Montag" appears nowhere else in the corpus.
items.correction: "나의 여자 친구와 내가 Taggy Montag를 보러갔던 때가 생각난다."

items.original: 갑자기 우리는 Taggy의 분장실 밖의 우리를 발견했다. 우리는 안을 들여다보고 싶어서 견딜 수가 없었다.
items.problem: "we found ourselves outside Taggy's dressing room" is translated word-for-word as "분장실 밖의 우리를 발견했다" (= we discovered the us that was outside the dressing room). The idiom "find oneself + place" means "정신을 차려 보니 ~에 와 있었다", and the literal rendering is not Korean at all.
items.correction: "갑자기 정신을 차려 보니 우리는 Taggy의 분장실 밖에 와 있었다. 우리는 안을 들여다보고 싶은 것을 참을 수가 없었다." (also content/lessons/ld/d062-1.json block[3]).

items.original: 그녀는 분노로 빨갛게 변했었다. 우리는 벽장 문을 열고 우리의 사인들을 탁자 위로 던지고 그 방으로부터 행진해나갔다.
items.problem: "marched out of the room" is translated as "행진해나갔다", which in Korean means to parade/march in formation. Here "march out" means to walk out angrily and deliberately (성큼성큼 나가 버리다). "그 방으로부터 행진해나갔다" also uses "~로부터" where Korean takes "~에서".
items.correction: "...우리의 사인을 탁자 위에 던져 놓고 그 방에서 성큼성큼 걸어 나왔다." (also content/lessons/ld/d062-1.json block[9]).

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d062, rows n=5, n=6, n=7 (KO)
items.original: Taggy가 “맥주 좀 주게. 그리고 자선을 위한 한 수표를 써라.
items.problem: One continuous speech by one character shifts through three Korean speech levels: "주게" (하게체) in row 5, "써라" (해라체) in row 5, "태워 버려" (해체) in row 6, "아니야" (해체) in row 7. Korean learners are sensitive to 화계, and a single quoted speech must keep one level. "자선을 위한 한 수표를" also carries a redundant "한" (a literal copy of the English article).
items.correction: Keep one level throughout, e.g. "맥주 좀 줘. 그리고 자선 단체에 낼 수표를 한 장 써 줘. / 언론이 사진을 몇 장 찍게 한 다음 그걸 태워 버려. / 나는 내 돈을 남에게 나눠 주려고 일하는 게 아니야."

items.original: I wasn't sure exactly where it was, but I walked with a stranger to the end of High Street.
items.problem: The man was already introduced in row 2 ("A man stopped me"), so the second mention must be definite: "the stranger". Row 9 of the same round correctly writes "the piece of paper the stranger had given to me", and the Korean for row 3 already says "그 낯선 사람과" (definite), so the English is the odd one out.
items.correction: "I wasn't sure exactly where it was, but I walked with the stranger to the end of High Street." NOTE: this changes the English text, so regenerate the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: 나는 나의 지갑(wallet)을 위하여 지갑(purse)을 들여다 보았고 그 낯선 사람이 준 그 종이 쪽지를 발견했다. 그것은 사진이었다.
items.problem: "I looked in my purse for my wallet" is mistranslated. "look in X for Y" means "X 안에서 Y를 찾다", not "Y를 위하여 X를 들여다보다". "지갑을 위하여 지갑을 들여다 보았고" is incomprehensible Korean and hides the actual British-English contrast (purse = 핸드백/손가방, wallet = 지폐 지갑) that the sentence exists to teach.
items.correction: "나는 핸드백(purse) 안에서 지갑(wallet)을 찾다가 그 낯선 사람이 준 종이 쪽지를 발견했다. 그것은 사진이었다." (also fix content/lessons/ld/d063-1.json block[10], which carries the identical wording).

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d063, rows n=8 and n=10 (KO)
items.original: “Fantastic Five"가 최고 20위 중에서 2위인 새 레코드를 갖고 있었다. 나는 그것을 사기로 했다.
items.problem: Mismatched quotation characters. Row 8 opens with a curly opening quote “ and closes with a straight ". Row 10 is worse — it opens with a curly CLOSING quote: "그 사람은 ”Fantastic Five"의 가수였다." Both are conversion artifacts.
items.correction: Use a matched pair in both rows: “Fantastic Five” (rows 8 and 10 of content/ld_english_scripts.json, and blocks[9]/blocks[11] of content/lessons/ld/d063-1.json).

items.original: 자신에 대하여 신사라고 여기는 어떤 사람도 숙녀가 방안에 있을 때 담배를 피워서 자기 자신을 바보로 만 들려고 하지 않았다.
items.problem: "만들려고" is broken by a stray space into "만 들려고" — a line-wrap artifact from the legacy HTML conversion. This is in the file the learner actually sees (the ko column is rendered in every step).
items.correction: "...자기 자신을 바보로 만들려고 하지 않았다." (also content/lessons/ld/d064-1.json blocks[4], which has the same break).

items.original: 사회적이 관습과 행동 방식은 변한다. 많은 해 전에 실례라고 여겨졌던 것들이 지금은 용납된다.
items.problem: "사회적이 관습" is a typo for "사회적 관습" (content/ld_english_scripts.json d064 row 1 has it right, so the two files disagree). Separately, "많은 해 전에" is a word-for-word rendering of "many years ago" that is not idiomatic Korean.
items.correction: "사회적 관습과 행동 방식은 변한다. 여러 해 전에는 실례라고 여겨졌던 것들이 지금은 용납된다." — and fix "많은 해 전에" in content/ld_english_scripts.json d064 row 1 as well.

items.original: 사회적인 관습에 대하여 기억해야 할 중요한 것은 다른 사람들이 불편하게 느끼도록 만들지 모르는 어떤 것도 하지 않는 것이다 특히 그들이 당신의 손님이라면 -.
items.problem: The sentence has no punctuation between "것이다" and "특히", and ends with a stray "-." left over from a dash in the legacy source. The result is a run-on with a dangling hyphen at the end.
items.correction: "사회적인 관습에 대하여 기억해야 할 중요한 것은, 다른 사람들이 — 특히 그들이 당신의 손님이라면 — 불편하게 느낄 만한 일은 어떤 것도 하지 않는 것이다."

items.original: 다른 손님들은 재미있어 하거나 충격을 받았지만 그 귀족은 조용히 자신의 나이프를 집어들고 똑같은 방 식으로 먹기 시작했다.
items.problem: "방식으로" is broken by a stray space into "방 식으로" — the same legacy line-wrap artifact, in the rendered ko column.
items.correction: "...똑같은 방식으로 먹기 시작했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d065-1.json blocks[5]).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d065-1.json → blocks[2] and blocks[3] vs content/ld_english_scripts.json d065 rows 1–2
items.original: 특히 그들이 당신의 손님이라면 -. 매우 공식적인 만찬을 베푼 한 부유한 귀족에 대한 오래된 이야기가 있 다.
items.problem: The Korean rows on the -1 script page do not line up with the English sentences. English row 1 ends with "...especially if they are your guests.", but its Korean tail ("특히 그들이 당신의 손님이라면") has been pushed into the next block, where it is glued to the whole of English row 2. So Korean block[2] is a truncated row 1 and block[3] is "tail of row 1 + all of row 2". The word "있 다" is also broken by a stray space (a line-wrap artifact from the legacy conversion).
items.correction: Split at the sentence boundary: blocks[2] = "사회적인 관습에 대하여 기억해야 할 중요한 것은 다른 사람들이 불편하게 느끼도록 만들지 모르는 어떤 것도 하지 않는 것이다. 특히 그들이 당신의 손님이라면 더욱 그렇다."; blocks[3] = "매우 공식적인 만찬을 베푼 한 부유한 귀족에 대한 오래된 이야기가 있다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d066, row n=1 (KO); same error at row n=5
items.original: 불과 얼마 전에 한 시카고 양조장이 시장에서 가장 지방질이 적다고(살찌지 않는다고) 생각되는 새로운 맥주를 소개했다.
items.problem: "the least fattening" is rendered as "가장 지방질이 적다" (= lowest in fat). "Fattening" means 살찌게 하는 (calorie-dense), not 지방질이 많은. Beer contains essentially no fat at all, so "지방질이 가장 적은 맥주" is also factually meaningless as a product claim. The parenthetical "(살찌지 않는다고)" is the correct gloss, so the line gives the wrong meaning first and the right one in brackets. Row 5 repeats it: "비록 그것이 지방질이 없다고(살찌지 않는다고) 하더라도" for "non-fattening".
items.correction: Row 1: "...시장에서 가장 살이 덜 찌는(칼로리가 가장 낮은) 맥주로 여겨지는 새로운 맥주를 소개했다." Row 5: "비록 그것이 살이 찌지 않는다고 하더라도 누가 비누맛이 나는 맥주를 원했나?" Drop the misleading 지방질 gloss in both rows (and in content/lessons/ld/d066-1.json blocks[2] and [6]).

items.original: 그것은 더 순했으므로 그들은 그것을 LITE라고불렀다.
items.problem: Missing space: "LITE라고불렀다" should be "LITE라고 불렀다".
items.correction: "그것은 더 가벼웠으므로 그들은 그것을 Lite라고 불렀다." (also content/lessons/ld/d066-1.json blocks[3]).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d066-1.json → blocks[2] and blocks[4] vs content/ld_english_scripts.json d066 rows 1 and 3

items.problem: Chicago is transliterated "쉬카고" on the -1 page but "시카고" in content/ld_english_scripts.json for the same two sentences. "시카고" is the 국립국어원 standard form; "쉬카고" is non-standard, and the two files disagree with each other.
items.correction: Use "시카고" in blocks[2] and blocks[4] of content/lessons/ld/d066-1.json.

items.original: They planned to ignore the Lite tastes soapy ad since the public knew which Lite was which.
items.problem: The advertising slogan is embedded as an unquoted noun modifier — "the Lite tastes soapy ad" — which is very hard to parse: the reader hits a full clause inside a noun phrase with no quotation marks to mark it. The hint block for this round does keep quotes ("LITE TASTES SOAPY."), so the script and the hint disagree on the convention.
items.correction: "They planned to ignore the \"Lite tastes soapy\" ad since the public knew which Lite was which." NOTE: quotation marks are stripped by the answer normalizer, so grading is unaffected; regenerate the clip if the text is touched.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d067, rows n=5 and n=7 (KO)
items.original: 그 광고는 ”LITE는 옷을 빨기에 좋다.“라고 할 것이다.
items.problem: The quotation marks are reversed: the quote opens with the closing character ” and closes with the opening character “. Row 5 of the same round has the other variant of the fault — “LITE tastes soapy"광고를 — a curly opening quote closed by a straight one, plus no space before "광고를".
items.correction: Row 7: "그 광고는 “LITE는 옷을 빨기에 좋다.”라고 할 것이다." Row 5: "...“LITE tastes soapy” 광고를 무시하기로 계획했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d067-1.json blocks[6] and blocks[8]).

items.original: 내가 십대일 때 우리는 바깥 시골에 살았다. 우리가 시내로 가기를 원한다면 우리는 걸어야 했다.
items.problem: "out in the country" is translated word-for-word as "바깥 시골에"; "out" here is an intensifier meaning "way out in the countryside", not a separate place called 바깥. Also "If we wanted to go to town, we had to walk" is a past habitual, so "원한다면" (present) should be "가고 싶으면" in past-habitual framing.
items.correction: "내가 십대였을 때 우리는 시골 외딴 곳에 살았다. 시내에 가고 싶으면 걸어가야 했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d068-1.json blocks[2]).

items.original: 우리가 집에 도착할 무렵에는 나는 마을로 걸어갔으면 좋았을 걸하고 소원했다.
items.problem: "I wished I had walked to town" is a counterfactual regret (~할 걸 그랬다고 후회했다), but "소원했다" means "wished for / desired", which is the wrong sense of "wish". "좋았을 걸하고" is also missing a space ("걸 하고").
items.correction: "우리가 집에 도착할 무렵, 나는 차라리 시내까지 걸어갈 걸 그랬다고 후회했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d069-1.json blocks[6]).

items.original: 아버지가 한번이라도 운전한 것은 여러 해가 지나고 나서였다.
items.problem: The Korean drops "again". "It was years before my father ever drove again" means he did not drive again for years after that trip; the Korean says he did not drive at all until years later. That contradicts the story itself — the father does drive the car home in row 6 ("The ride home was unbelievable"), which is the whole joke.
items.correction: "아버지가 다시 운전대를 잡은 것은 그로부터 여러 해가 지나서였다." (also content/lessons/ld/d069-1.json block[8]).

items.original: 그는 나에게 어떻게 운전하는지 보여주면 단지 너무 기쁠 것이라고 말했다.
items.problem: Mistranslation of "He said he would be only too pleased to show me how to drive." "only too pleased to V" is a fixed phrase meaning "기꺼이 ~해 주겠다", not "~하면 단지 너무 기쁠 것이다". The -1 page also reads the infinitive as a conditional ("보여주면"), and "단지 너무 기쁠" is not Korean. content/ld_english_scripts.json has the correct version for the same line ("그는 기꺼이 나에게 운전하는 법을 가르쳐 주겠다고 말했다."), so the two files disagree.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file wording: "그는 기꺼이 나에게 운전하는 법을 가르쳐 주겠다고 말했다."

items.original: 그 개통일은 큰 성공이었다 - 즉 Mr.Huskisson에게만 제외하고는. 8대의 열차가 개회식에 참여했다.
items.problem: "~에게만 제외하고는" is ungrammatical Korean: 제외하다 takes 을/를, not 에게만. "Mr.Huskisson" is also missing the space after the period (the English row correctly reads "Mr. Huskisson").
items.correction: "그 개통일은 큰 성공이었다 — Mr. Huskisson 한 사람만 빼면 말이다. 8대의 열차가 개통식에 참여했다." ("개회식" is also better as "개통식" for a railway opening.)

items.original: 철로를 반쯤 건넜을 때 그는 갑자기 한 열차가 자신을 향하여 질주해오는 것을 보았다.
items.problem: "locomotive" is translated as "열차" (train). A locomotive is 기관차 — and that detail matters here, because what hit Huskisson was a locomotive (Rocket) running light on the adjacent track, not a train of carriages. The same round uses "열차" for "train" in rows 3, 4, 5 and 8, so the distinction the English draws is erased.
items.correction: "철로를 반쯤 건넜을 때 그는 갑자기 기관차 한 대가 자신을 향해 질주해 오는 것을 보았다." (also content/lessons/ld/d070-1.json blocks[7]).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d070.json → blocks[4] (third instruction block, hint continuation)
items.original: halfway across the track locomotive fantastic speed 23 panick froze
items.problem: "panick" is not an English word. The script line it points at is "Mr. Huskisson panicked and froze with fear." The hint list is supposed to give the learner the hard words spelled exactly as they appear, so a misspelled hint is worse than no hint.
items.correction: "halfway across the track locomotive fantastic speed 23 panicked froze"

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d071, row n=2 (EN); contradicts d072 row n=4
items.original: The train was made up of 13 coaches.
items.problem: The 1963 Great Train Robbery mail train had 12 carriages, not 13. The wrong number also creates an internal contradiction two rounds later: the robbers uncoupled the locomotive plus the first two coaches, so d072 row 4 says "The last 10 coaches with all the mailmen had been disconnected by the robbers." With 13 coaches that leaves 11, not 10; with the real figure of 12 the arithmetic works exactly. A learner who adds the numbers up gets a contradiction inside one continuous story.
items.correction: Change to "The train was made up of 12 coaches." and update the matching hint block in content/lessons/ld/d071.json ("made up of 13 coaches." → "made up of 12 coaches.") and the Korean in both content/ld_english_scripts.json ("그 열차는 13대의 차량으로 이루어져있었다." → "12대의") and content/lessons/ld/d071-1.json block[3]. NOTE: changing the English text destroys this line's Azure Ava clip (clip key = text hash) — regenerate with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: 8월8일 오전 3시에 Jack Mill가 Glasgow로부터 London으로의 우편 열차의 조종석에 앉아있었다.
items.problem: The driver's name is truncated to "Jack Mill". The English row and every later Korean row in the same file say "Mills" (the real driver was Jack Mills). The particle is also wrong for the truncated form ("Mill가" — with "Mills" it should be "Mills가"). "8월8일" is missing a space.
items.correction: "8월 8일 오전 3시에 Jack Mills가 Glasgow에서 London으로 가는 우편 열차의 조종석에 앉아 있었다."

items.original: 그 다리에서 돈가방들이 열차로부터 내려져서 기다리는 트럭들에게로 던져넣어졌다.
items.problem: "트럭들에게로" uses the animate particle 에게 for trucks; Korean requires 에/으로 for inanimate objects. The double passive "던져넣어졌다" is also unnatural.
items.correction: "그 다리에서 돈가방들이 열차에서 내려져 기다리던 트럭들에 실렸다." (also content/lessons/ld/d072-1.json blocks[6]).

items.original: 3시 45분에 그는 “그것으로 충분해야 할꺼야.”라고 말했다.
items.problem: "할꺼야" is a misspelling; standard Korean orthography is "할 거야". The rendering also reads oddly — "that will have to be enough" is "이만하면 됐다 / 그 정도면 충분할 거야", not "충분해야 할 거야".
items.correction: "3시 45분에 그는 “이 정도면 충분할 거야.”라고 말했다." (also content/lessons/ld/d072-1.json blocks[8]). The same class of spacing error appears at d069 row 8: "대신하지 않을거야" → "대신하지 않을 거야".

items.original: 모든 그 우체부들이 있었던 그 마지막 10대의 챠량은 강도들이 분리시켜두었다.
items.problem: "챠량" is a misspelling of "차량". Every other occurrence in d071/d072 spells it correctly.
items.correction: "우체부들이 모두 타고 있던 마지막 10량의 차량은 강도들이 분리해 두었다."

items.original: 공기 오염은 오늘 날 세계에서 가장 심각한 문제 중의 하나이다.
items.problem: "오늘 날" is misspelled — 오늘날 ("nowadays") is a single word. The same file spells it correctly in d100 row 2 and d103 row 3, so it is a typo, not a house style.
items.correction: "공기 오염은 오늘날 세계에서 가장 심각한 문제 중의 하나이다."

items.problem: "개스" is a non-standard transliteration of "gas"; the standard 외래어 표기 is 가스, which is what content/ld_english_scripts.json d097 row 2 uses. The two copies disagree.
items.correction: "사람들은 가스와 연기를 만들어내는 기계로 공기를 더럽게 만든다."

It is also inconsistent with the `label`/`menuLabel` fields in the same files, which are correct.
items.correction: Either derive `title` from `unit` ("수능영어 듣기 - 제 097 회") or drop the field, since curriculumPresentation.ts ignores it. This is one repo-wide fix, not 24 edits — flagging here because it falls inside my scope, not as a separate task per round.

items.original: 아무도 공기 오염을 좋아하지 않는다. 그것은 깨끗하고 신선한 공기가 구름낀 것처럼 보이게 또 나쁜 냄새 가 나게 만든다.
items.problem: Two spacing defects, both line-wrap artefacts from the legacy HTML: a stray space inside "냄새 가" (should be "냄새가"), and "구름낀" run together (should be "구름 낀").
items.correction: "아무도 공기 오염을 좋아하지 않는다. 그것은 깨끗하고 신선한 공기가 구름 낀 것처럼 보이게 하고 나쁜 냄새가 나게 만든다."

items.original: “Oscar, 나는 시장으로써 나의 일에 대하여 정말 흥분된다. 나는 내가 교통 문제를 해결할 방법을 찾을 수
items.problem: "시장으로써" uses the instrumental particle 으로써 where the required form for "as mayor" is 으로서. content/ld_english_scripts.json d099 row 3 has the correct "시장으로서", so the two copies disagree.
items.correction: "시장으로써" → "시장으로서", matching content/ld_english_scripts.json d099 row 3.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d100", row n=1 (EN and KO)
items.original: Fishing is one of the world's oldest industries. People have been catching fish for over 4,000 years.
items.problem: Literally true because of "over", but it presents 4,000 years as the age of fishing and is wrong by an order of magnitude. Jerimalai cave in Timor-Leste has 42,000-year-old bones of pelagic fish such as tuna, and fish hooks dated 16,000-23,000 years — i.e. people have fished for at least 40,000 years. Placed next to two other stale figures in the same five-sentence round.
items.correction: "People have been catching fish for tens of thousands of years." Korean: "사람들은 수만 년 동안 고기를 잡아 왔다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d100", row n=2 (EN and KO)
items.original: Today, there are over 5 million people in the world who make their living by catching fish.
items.problem: FAO counts 37.9 million fishers in the primary capture-fisheries sector, within 61.8 million people employed in fisheries and aquaculture (2022). "over 5 million" understates the real figure by roughly a factor of seven and is framed with "Today" as a current fact.
items.correction: "Today, there are about 38 million people in the world who make their living by catching fish." Korean: "오늘날 세계에서 어업으로 생계를 유지하는 사람은 약 3천8백만 명이다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d100", row n=5 (EN and KO)
items.original: The fishing industry catches over 66 billion kilograms of fish a year. This is about 17 kilograms for each person in the world.
items.problem: Both figures are stale and, together, internally impossible today. FAO SOFIA 2024 puts 2022 capture-fisheries production at 92.3 million tonnes (≈92 billion kg), not 66 billion kg. And 66 billion kg divided by today's ~8.1 billion people is about 8 kg per person, not 17 — the two numbers only reconcile at a world population of ~3.9 billion (roughly 1974). Per-capita apparent consumption of aquatic animal foods was 20.7 kg in 2022 (capture + aquaculture). The sentence is presented in the present tense as a current fact.
items.correction: Refresh both numbers together, e.g. "The fishing industry catches over 90 billion kilograms of fish a year." and drop or recompute the second sentence ("This is about 11 kilograms for each person in the world."). Korean: "어업은 매년 900억 킬로그램 이상 고기를 잡는다. 이것은 세계의 각 사람에게 약 11킬로그램이다."

items.original: 4,000 five million 140,000 commercial fishermen. 66 billion kilograms 17 kilograms
items.problem: The hints block spells one number as a word while the script writes it as a digit: the script has "over 5 million people" (row 2), but the hint says "five million". Every other number in the same hint (4,000 / 140,000 / 66 billion / 17) matches the script's digit form. If the hints block were rendered, a learner following it would type "five million" while the dictation normaliser compares against "5", and the answer would be marked wrong.
items.correction: Change "five million" to "5 million" in the hints text so it matches content/ld_english_scripts.json d100 row 2.

items.original: 공장 선박들은 즉시 고기를 씻고 포장하는 수백명의 근로자들을 태우고 다닌다.
items.problem: "clean the fish" in a fishing context means to gut, scale and dress the fish (손질하다), not to wash it. "씻고" teaches the wrong sense of a word the learner is being asked to reproduce in English.
items.correction: "공장 선박들은 즉시 생선을 손질하고 포장하는 수백 명의 근로자들을 태우고 다닌다."

items.original: 그들은 너무 많은 고기들이 잡히고 있는지 결정할 수 있다.
items.problem: "determine" here means "find out / establish", not "decide". "결정할 수 있다" says oceanographers can *decide* whether too many fish are being caught, which reverses the sense: they measure, they do not choose. The English is "They can determine if too many fish are being caught."
items.correction: "그들은 너무 많은 고기가 잡히고 있는지 판단할 수 있다." (or "알아낼 수 있다")

items.original: It lasts from 2 to 3 weeks and covers almost 1,700 kilometers.
items.problem: The distance (≈1,688 km / 1,049 miles) is right, but the duration is decades out of date. Iditarod officials now expect the winner in 9-12 days, and the full field typically finishes in under two weeks (in 2025 the last mushers came in just under 14 days after an unusually slow race). "2 to 3 weeks" described the race in its first decade, not today.
items.correction: "It lasts from 9 to 15 days and covers almost 1,700 kilometers." Korean: "그것은 9일에서 15일 계속되며 거의 1,700 킬로미터를 달린다."

items.original: The race also follows the route of several brave Alaskans who brought medicine from Anchorage to Nome in the winter of 1925.
items.problem: In the 1925 serum run the 300,000 units of diphtheria antitoxin travelled Anchorage → Nenana **by train** on the Alaska Railroad; the dog-sled relay of 20 mushers then covered the 674 miles (1,085 km) from **Nenana** to Nome. No musher carried the serum from Anchorage. The sentence attributes the whole Anchorage-to-Nome journey to the mushers whose route the race follows, and the Iditarod only shares the serum-run route from Ruby to Nome, not from Anchorage. "several" also understates the 20 mushers involved.
items.correction: "The race also follows part of the route of the twenty brave Alaskans who carried medicine by dog sled from Nenana to Nome in the winter of 1925." Korean: "그 시합은 1925년 겨울에 개썰매로 Nenana에서 Nome까지 약을 운반했던 20명의 용감한 알래스카 사람들의 길 일부도 따라간다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d107", row n=5 (EN and KO); same sentence in content/lessons/ld/d107-1.json blocks 7-8
items.original: Franklin and his brother had many arguments so when he was 17, Franklin went to Philadelphia and started his own printing business.
items.problem: The sentence coordinates "went to Philadelphia" and "started his own printing business" under "when he was 17", so it asserts Franklin founded his own printing house at 17. He did arrive in Philadelphia at 17 (6 October 1723), but he went to work for the printer Samuel Keimer, then for Denham, then spent 1724-1726 in London. He set up in business for himself only in 1728, in partnership with Hugh Meredith, and took sole control of the printing house in 1730 — at age 22-24, not 17. The Korean translation repeats the same claim ("17살이었을 때 Franklin은 필라델피아로 가서 자기 자신의 인쇄업을 시작했다").
items.correction: Split the claim, e.g. "Franklin and his brother had many arguments, so when he was 17, Franklin went to Philadelphia. A few years later he started his own printing business." Update the Korean to match: "…17살이었을 때 Franklin은 필라델피아로 갔다. 몇 년 뒤 그는 자신의 인쇄업을 시작했다."

items.original: Franklin과 그의 형은 많이 다투었다 그래서 17살이었을 때 Franklin은 필라델피아로 가서 자기 자신의 인쇄업을 시작했다.
items.problem: Run-on: "다투었다 그래서" joins two sentences with no connective ending and no punctuation. Korean needs either "다투었고, 그래서" / "다투었기 때문에" or a sentence break "다투었다. 그래서".
items.correction: "Franklin과 그의 형은 자주 다투었다. 그래서 17살이었을 때 Franklin은 필라델피아로 갔다." (see the d107 factual finding for the second clause)

items.original: 블록2: "Benjamin Franklin은 아마 그의 시대의 가장 유명한 미국인이었다. 그" / 블록3: "는 1706년에 보스톤에서 태어났다."  …  "소년으로써 그는 인쇄업자였던 그의 형을 위하여 일하러 다녔다."  …  "필라델피아로 가서 자시 자신의 인쇄업을 시작했다."
items.problem: Four defects. (1) The word 그는 is split across two blocks ("…미국인이었다. 그" / "는 1706년에…") — a raw line-wrap from the legacy HTML kept as a block boundary. (2) "보스톤" instead of the standard "보스턴" (the scripts file has 보스턴). (3) "소년으로써" — wrong particle; 으로써 is instrumental, the required form is 으로서 ("as a boy"); the scripts file avoids it with "소년 시절". (4) "자시 자신의" is a typo for "자기 자신의" (the scripts file is correct).
items.correction: Rejoin the split sentence into one block, and fix 보스톤 → 보스턴, 소년으로써 → 소년 시절 (or 소년으로서), 자시 자신의 → 자기 자신의, matching content/ld_english_scripts.json d107.

items.problem: "혹성" is the obsolete Japanese-derived term for planet. Korean science education standardised on 행성 decades ago; 혹성 now survives mainly in old film titles. A learner under 40 may not recognise it.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → key "d108", row n=5 (EN and KO)
items.original: Most of Franklin's proverbs were about saving money and working hard, such as, A penny saved is a penny earned.
items.problem: Two problems in one line. (1) Misattribution: Franklin never wrote "A penny saved is a penny earned." Poor Richard's Almanack has "A penny saved is two pence clear" (1737) and "A penny saved is a penny got" (1758); the "earned" wording is an anonymous English proverb first recorded in 1804, after Franklin's death. The Franklin Institute lists it among things Franklin never said. (2) Punctuation: "such as," takes no comma, and the quotation marks around the proverb have been lost — the Korean row still has the proverb as a separate quoted sentence, so this is a conversion artefact.
items.correction: Use a proverb Franklin actually printed and restore the quotation marks, e.g. "Most of Franklin's proverbs were about saving money and working hard, such as \"A penny saved is a penny got.\"" If the familiar wording must be kept, attribute it correctly rather than as Franklin's. Korean: "…다음과 같이 돈을 아끼고 열심히 일하는 것에 대한 것이었다. \"한 푼을 아낀 것은 한 푼을 번 것이다.\""

items.original: Franklin의 격언은 Poor Richard's Almanac을 그 시대의 가장 성공적인 출판물의 하나를 만드는데 도움이 되었다.
items.problem: Wrong case particle: the object complement of "make X (into) Y" takes 로/으로, not 를. As written the sentence has two accusative objects ("Almanac을 … 하나를 만드는데") and is ungrammatical; it reads as "helped make one of the most successful publications" rather than "helped make the Almanac one of the most successful publications". "만드는데" should also be spaced "만드는 데" (dependent noun 데).
items.correction: "Franklin의 격언은 Poor Richard's Almanac을 그 시대의 가장 성공적인 출판물의 하나로 만드는 데 도움이 되었다."

items.original: He invented the Franklin stove, which was another important discovery.
items.problem: An invention is called a discovery within the same sentence. The stove is invented ('invented'), so the relative clause should say invention; "another important discovery" also implies the lightning rod of the previous line was a discovery, when the line says he 'developed' it. The Korean repeats the error: "그것은 또 다른 중요한 발견이었다."
items.correction: He invented the Franklin stove, which was another important invention. / 그것은 또 다른 중요한 발명이었다.

items.original: Later, he became the United States representative to Great Britain and France.
items.problem: Franklin was never the United States' representative to Great Britain. He was a colonial agent in London (for Pennsylvania and later Georgia, New Jersey and Massachusetts, 1757–1775) — that is, before the United States existed — and the first US Minister to France (commissioned 1778, formally minister 1779–1785). The first United States minister to Great Britain was John Adams, appointed in 1785. The Korean "나중에 그는 영국과 프랑스에서 미국의 대표가 되었다." repeats the error.
items.correction: English: "Earlier, he had represented several colonies in Great Britain, and later he became the first United States representative to France." Korean: "그는 앞서 영국에서 여러 식민지를 대표했고, 나중에는 프랑스 주재 미국의 첫 대표가 되었다."

items.problem: "dig" is missing from the Korean. The English is "The anthropologists plan to dig carefully and examine the contents of the area." The Korean reads "조심스럽게 하고" — an adverb with no verb — which is ungrammatical Korean and gives the learner no cue for the word "dig". "내용물들" for the archaeological "contents" of a site is also wrong register (내용물 = the contents of a container); 출토품/유물 is what is meant.

items.problem: The same person is named three ways inside one round: "Margaret Perkins 교수" (n=1), "Perkins 교수" (n=2), and "퍼킨즈 교수" (n=8, n=9). "퍼킨즈" is also non-standard; the 외래어 표기법 form is 퍼킨스.
items.correction: Use one form throughout — either "Perkins 교수" in every line (matching n=1–2) or "퍼킨스 교수" in every line.

items.problem: The reporting clause is misaligned with the English rows. English n=4 is a plain sentence, "They built canoes for fishing and traveling on the river.", with no "she said"; the Korean row adds a closing quotation mark and "고 말했다" that belong to n=3 ("She said that the Pomo used to fish..."), whose Korean row is left with an unclosed opening quote. Row 4's Korean therefore contains material with no counterpart in row 4's English.
items.correction: Close the quotation inside row 3 ("그녀는 “포모족은 그 강에서 고기를 잡고 작은 동물을 사냥하곤 했다.”고 말했다.") and make row 4 "그들은 그 강에서 고기를 잡고 여행하기 위하여 카누를 만들었다."

items.problem: Hint words are spelled differently from the script line the learner must write. d117 hints "seventeenth century" but the script says "17th century"; d118 hints "chicken pox" but the script says "chickenpox" (one word); d116 hints "Great plains" but the script says "Great Plains"; d113 hints "local native Americans" but the script says "local Native Americans"; d120 hints "bureau of Indian Affairs" but the script says "Bureau of Indian Affairs". d116's hints also contain "American bison", which appears nowhere in the script.

items.original: At that time, most of the northern half of the world was covered with ice.
items.problem: An overstatement. At the Last Glacial Maximum ice sheets covered roughly 8% of Earth's surface (about a quarter of the land), concentrated over Canada, the northern US, Scandinavia and northern Britain; most of Siberia, central Asia, southern Europe and the southern US were ice-free. The claim also sits badly with lines 8–9 of the same round, which have people walking across an unglaciated Beringia into North America.
items.correction: At that time, much of the northern part of the world was covered with ice. / 그 당시에 세계의 북쪽 지역 상당 부분이 얼음으로 덮여 있었다.

items.problem: The number contradicts the English line the learner dictates and the Korean in the scripts file. English d114 #5 is "The first Indians, or Native Americans, probably came from Asia more than 15,000 years ago." and content/ld_english_scripts.json d114 #5 ko is "첫 번째 인디언 즉 미국 원주민들은 아마 15,000년도 더 전에 아시아로부터 왔을 것이다." The lesson's own hints block also lists "15,000". The -1 archive says 25,000 and additionally turns the hedged "probably ... would have come" into a flat assertion ("왔다").

items.problem: Garbled case marking. The English is "connected Asia with Alaska"; "알라스카로 아시아와 연결되어" leaves it unclear what is connected to what, and the subject of the connecting is the land area, not Alaska. "알라스카" is also non-standard (알래스카). The scripts file has the correct "아시아와 알래스카를 이어 주었다".

items.original: Some societies, like the Maya and Aztec civilizations of Central America, built great cities with large buildings.
items.problem: The Aztec empire was centred on Tenochtitlan in the Valley of Mexico — central Mexico, which is in North America, not Central America. (Maya territory did extend into Guatemala and Belize.) The Korean "중앙 아메리카의 마야 및 아즈텍 문명" repeats it. The correct umbrella term for both is Mesoamerica.
items.correction: Some societies, like the Maya and Aztec civilizations of Mesoamerica, built great cities with large buildings. / 메소아메리카의 마야 및 아즈텍 문명 같은 몇몇 사회들은 큰 건물이 있는 큰 도시들을 건설했다.

(1) The two place phrases are nested the wrong way: the English is "West of the Mississippi River, on the Great Plains" (two separate locators), but "대평원의 미시시피 강의 서쪽" reads as "west of the Great Plains' Mississippi River". items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json d116 n=5 and n=6 (en and ko)
items.original: When the Europeans first arrived, there were about 20 million Native Americans.
items.problem: This figure and the next line are mutually impossible. The following sentence is "About 300,000 of them were living east of the Mississippi River." — i.e. 1.5% of the stated total — yet the Eastern Woodlands were among the most densely settled parts of the continent north of Mexico (the Mississippian societies alone are estimated at roughly half a million at contact). Scholarly estimates for North America north of Mexico at contact run from about 1.2 million to 18 million, so "about 20 million" is at or above the extreme upper bound while "300,000 east of the Mississippi" is far below any published estimate. One of the two numbers is wrong and neither is supported as stated.
items.correction: Expert review required to choose the pair of figures the course wants to teach; a defensible version is "When the Europeans first arrived, there were several million Native Americans north of Mexico." / "About two million of them were living east of the Mississippi River." Whatever is chosen, the two lines must be arithmetically compatible, and the Korean ("약 2천만명", "약 30만명") must be updated with them.

items.original: They introduced the settlers to new crops such as corn, sweet potatoes, cotton, beans, tobacco, peanuts and maple sugar.
items.problem: Peanuts do not belong in this list. The peanut is South American; it reached West Africa with Portuguese traders and then North America through the Atlantic slave trade, arriving in the English colonies in the 1600s–1700s by that route, not from the Native peoples of the Atlantic coast. Corn, beans, tobacco, squash and maple sugar are the standard and defensible items.
items.correction: They introduced the settlers to new crops such as corn, sweet potatoes, cotton, beans, tobacco, squash and maple sugar. (and remove 땅콩 from the Korean)

items.original: One Native American leader asked, how can we sell the land?
items.problem: A direct question is introduced with "asked," but has no quotation marks and no capital letter. As written it is neither direct nor indirect speech (indirect would be "asked how we could sell the land"). Line 7, "Why not sell the air, the clouds, or the ocean?", continues the same unmarked quotation.
items.correction: One Native American leader asked, "How can we sell the land?" / "Why not sell the air, the clouds, or the ocean?"
