items.correction: “어떻게 지내세요?”나 “건강하시길 바랍니다.” 같은 표현은 다른 사람의 안녕에 대한 우리의 관심을 나타내기 위한 것이다.

items.original: 심지어는 good bye같은 말도 God be with ye의 축소형이다.
items.problem: The English answer is "goodbye" (one word). The Korean guide, which keeps English words as spelling cues, shows "good bye" as two words. In typing mode "good bye" normalizes differently from "goodbye", so a learner who copies the cue is marked wrong. "같은 말도" also mistranslates "the word goodbye", which is a single specific word, not "words such as".
items.correction: 심지어 goodbye라는 말도 God be with ye가 줄어든 형태이다.

items.original: Therefore, when two travelers met, they commonly extended their hands to show that they carried no weapons.
items.problem: The passage says the handshake began with medieval travelers showing they carried no weapon. The weapon explanation is only a guess (Wikipedia: 'may have originated'). Handshakes are also recorded far earlier than the Middle Ages: an Assyrian relief from the 9th century BC and Greek funerary art from the 5th century BC.
items.correction: Hedge it, e.g. #3 "According to one popular explanation, when two travelers met, they extended their hands to show that they carried no weapons." KO #3 "흔히 전해지는 설명에 따르면 두 여행자가 만났을 때 무기를 갖고 있지 않다는 것을 보이려고 손을 내밀었다고 한다." (Optionally, #2 could say the custom is much older than the Middle Ages.) Regenerate the Ava clips for the changed English.

items.original: Such expressions as how are you and I hope you are feeling well are designed to express our interest in the welfare of others.
items.problem: The quoted expressions have no quotation marks or capitals, so the displayed sentence (Steps 3-5 and the correct-answer banner) is hard to parse: "as how are you and I hope you are feeling well are designed". #6 has the same problem: "Even the word goodbye is a shortened form of God be with ye."
items.correction: #5 Such expressions as "How are you?" and "I hope you are feeling well" are designed to express our interest in the welfare of others. #6 Even the word "goodbye" is a shortened form of "God be with ye." The quotes change the clip key, so regenerate the Ava clips. Grading ignores punctuation.

items.original: 저녁 식사는 웨이터가 따뜻한 물이 담긴 두 개의 작은 은사발을 신랑신부 앞에 놓은 거의 끝까지 사건없이 진행되었다.
items.problem: The clause order is garbled. "…놓은 거의 끝까지" makes it read as "until almost the end that the waiter placed…". The English means "until, near the end, the waiter placed…". There is also a spacing error (사건없이).
items.correction: 저녁 식사는 거의 끝날 무렵 웨이터가 따뜻한 물이 담긴 작은 은사발 두 개를 신랑 신부 앞에 놓을 때까지 별일 없이 진행되었다.

items.original: 사교적(사회적)인 사용법의 무지는 많은 어처구니없는 실수의 결과를 낳을 수 있다. / 그 소녀가 질겁하게도 그녀의 남편이 그 접시를 집어들고는 그 물을 마시기 시작했다.
items.problem: #1: "social usage" means social custom or etiquette, not 사용법 ("how to use something"). #5: "the girl" is the young bride. 소녀 means a young girl or teenager, which is wrong for a newlywed.
items.correction: #1 사교 예법을 모르면 어처구니없는 실수를 많이 저지를 수 있다. #5 신부가 질겁하게도 남편이 그 그릇을 집어 들고는 물을 마시기 시작했다.

items.original: When reading a mystery story alone at night, one's imagination is more active than ever.
items.problem: Dangling modifier: the implied subject of "reading" is the reader, but the main-clause subject is "one's imagination".
items.correction: When one reads a mystery story alone at night, one's imagination is more active than ever. Regenerate the clip.

items.locator: d249 rows #3, #5, #8 ko; d250 rows #3, #4, #5 ko (미스테리); d250 #2 ko (셜록홈즈)
items.original: 좋은 살인 미스테리나 탐정 이야기를 읽는 것에는 … / 좋은 미스테리 이야기를 읽는 것은 한 동안 경찰의 일원이 되는 것과 같다.
items.problem: The standard loanword spelling of "mystery" is 미스터리, not 미스테리. It is wrong in 6 rows. "Sherlock Holmes" is normally written 셜록 홈스, with a space.
items.correction: 미스테리 → 미스터리 (6 rows); 셜록홈즈 → 셜록 홈스.

items.original: 우리는 모두 실생활에서 셜록홈즈가 될 수 없지만 책장 속에서 우리는 모두 안락의자 탐정이 될 기회를 찾을 수 있다.
items.problem: The English "We cannot all be Sherlock Holmes" is a partial negation (not everyone can be). Partial vs total negation (부분부정) is a core school grammar point. "우리는 모두 … 될 수 없지만" reads as total negation (none of us can). Also, 책장 is ambiguous (bookcase or page) for "within the covers of a book", and the standard spelling of the name is 셜록 홈스.
items.correction: 우리 모두가 실생활에서 셜록 홈스가 될 수는 없지만, 책 속에서는 누구나 안락의자 탐정이 될 기회를 찾을 수 있다.

items.original: The personnel specialist can usually make fairly accurate judgments about an applicant's character through means of the interview.
items.problem: "through means of" is not idiomatic. The fixed phrase is "by means of" (or simply "through the interview").
items.correction: … about an applicant's character by means of the interview. Regenerate the clip.

items.original: 면담은 인사 책임자의 사무실 문을 두드리는 순간에 시작된다.
items.problem: The rest of d251-d252 translates "interview" as 면접. Here it is 면담 (counselling or consultation meeting), which is inconsistent.
items.correction: 면접은 인사 책임자의 사무실 문을 두드리는 순간부터 시작된다.

items.original: 많은 직종이 구체적인 기술과 재능을 요구한다는 사실에도 불구하고 그러나 어떤 직장에 지원할 때 보여줄 수 있는 가장 소중한 자산은 아마 잘 발달된 성격이다.
items.problem: The Korean stacks two contrast markers ("~에도 불구하고 그러나"), which is ungrammatical Korean. It copies the redundant English "In spite of the fact that …, however, …" (EN: "In spite of the fact that many jobs require specific skills and talents, however, probably the most valuable asset …").
items.correction: KO: 많은 직종이 구체적인 기술과 재능을 요구하지만, 직장에 지원할 때 보여 줄 수 있는 가장 소중한 자산은 아마 잘 다듬어진 인품일 것이다. (Optionally drop ", however," from the English and regenerate the clip.)

items.original: Kim Norris Ocean City, New Jersey, Becky Field. Laura Beckett. Washington boardwalk..
items.problem: Defects in the hint data for the rounds in scope. (a) d011's hints end in a stray double period, "boardwalk..". (b) Hint words that do not match the script they are meant to support: d006 hints "fix" where the script says "fixes"; d003 hints "sixty" where the key says "60"; d008 hints "five miles", "four bedrooms", "ten cows", "hundred chickens" where the key says 5, 4, 10, 100 (see the separate d008 finding). (c) Names run together without spaces - "Mrs.Watson." (d001), "Dr.William N.Green" (d006), "Mrs.Wenger," (d007) - where the scripts write "Mrs. Watson", "Dr. William N. Green", "Mrs. Wenger". (d) In d002, d004, d006, d007, d008 and d010 only the first line of hints sits in a `hints` block and the remaining hint words sit in `instruction` blocks (e.g. d002's "Clayton Street. 1490. ... government employee."), so they are typed as instructions to the learner rather than as hints. Per docs/qa-2026-09-18/maps/listening.md section 12 A-18, no hint block is rendered today, so this is data hygiene rather than a live defect.
items.correction: Drop the extra period in d011; make hint spelling follow the script ("fixes", and whatever form the numbers settle on); restore the spaces in the Mrs./Dr. names; and move the continuation lines of d002, d004, d006, d007, d008 and d010 into their `hints` block so each lesson's hint text is one field.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/{d004-1,d006-1,d007-1,d009-1,d010-1,d011-1,d012-1}.json block text, compared with the `ko` fields of the same rounds in content/ld_english_scripts.json
items.original: 그는 인명구조원으로써 잘 생기고 매우매우 좋아.
items.problem: Each -1 page keeps a second, older copy of the Korean script. In 7 of the 12 rounds in scope it no longer matches the copy in content/ld_english_scripts.json (compared whitespace-normalised). d009-1 changes the meaning: "슬라이드를 가져왔고" (brought the slides) where the English is "They took slides of their trip" and the scripts file correctly has 찍었고. d012-1 has the quoted 인명구조원으로써 (wrong particle; the English is just "He is a lifeguard, good looking and very, very nice") and 글세 for 글쎄. d004-1 and d010-1 write Portuguese as 폴튜갈 어 / 폴튜갈어 instead of 포르투갈어. d007-1 has 폴랜드어 (for 폴란드어), 불란서어, 이태리어, 펜실바니아 and "Berne" against the scripts file's 폴란드어 / 프랑스어 / 이탈리아어 / 펜실베이니아 / 베른. d006-1, d011-1 and d012-1 write 와싱턴 instead of 워싱턴. Three files also carry words broken by the legacy line wrapping: "재배할 것이 다." (d008-1), "찍었 다." (d010-1), "희망한 다." (d012-1). Separately, d001-1 to d004-1 open with a `sentences` block whose item number is the round number rather than 1 (d002-1 numbers its first line "2", d003-1 "3", d004-1 "4"), while d005-1 to d012-1 have no `sentences` block at all and put every Korean line in `instruction` blocks. Per docs/qa-2026-09-18/maps/listening.md section 1.2 the LD view renders none of these blocks today, so none of this is currently on screen.
items.correction: Regenerate every dNNN-1.json Korean block from content/ld_english_scripts.json (single source of truth), or remove the block text from the -1 files so only one copy exists; fix 가져왔고 to 찍었고, 인명구조원으로써 to 인명구조원이고, 글세 to 글쎄, 폴튜갈어 to 포르투갈어, 폴랜드어 to 폴란드어, 와싱턴 to 워싱턴 and the three split words at the same time, and make the block types consistent across the 12 pages.

items.original: 톰은 생선과 해산물을 좋아하며 프레드도 그들을 좋아한다.
items.problem: "them" refers to fish and seafood. Korean 그들 is a plural pronoun for people; using it for food is ungrammatical and reads as though Fred likes some group of people. The inanimate form is 그것들, and in natural Korean the pronoun is normally dropped.
items.correction: "톰은 생선과 해산물을 좋아하며 프레드도 그것들을 좋아한다." or, more naturally, "...프레드도 좋아한다." Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.original: Well, they don't like school very well and they don't like to study.
items.problem: "like ... very well" is not the standard collocation; the verb like takes "very much". "Very well" means in a satisfactory manner, which is not what is meant. The same course uses the correct form elsewhere - d001 row 4: "...but we like it very much." As a model sentence the learner hears, shadows in Step 4 and types in Step 2, it drills a collocation that would be marked wrong in a Korean school or 수능 setting.
items.correction: "Well, they don't like school very much and they don't like to study." The existing KO ("매우 좋아하지 않으며") already matches "very much", so only the English changes. NOTE: this changes the clip key - regenerate with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs` in the same task.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json -> d005 n=5; d009 n=1, n=3 (quoted), n=5; d011 n=6 - `ko` fields
items.original: 그들은 그들의 여행의 슬라이드를 찍었고 우리는 어젯 밤 그중의 일부를 보았다. Keith는 한 전국 잡지의 사진사이고 그가 그 모든 사진을 찍었다.
items.problem: Korean spacing and orthography errors in text the learner reads: 어젯 밤 should be the single word 어젯밤 (d009 rows 3 and 5), and d009 row 1 writes the same word a third way, 어제 밤; d005 row 5 has "그들 둘다 테니스를 잘 한다" where 둘다 should be 둘 다 and 잘 한다 should be 잘한다; d011 row 6 has "항상 미소짓고 웃는" where 미소짓고 should be 미소 짓고.
items.correction: 어제 밤 / 어젯 밤 -> 어젯밤 (d009 rows 1, 3, 5); 둘다 -> 둘 다 and 잘 한다 -> 잘한다 (d005 row 5); 미소짓고 -> 미소 짓고 (d011 row 6). Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json -> d006 rows n=2 and n=8, `ko` field
items.original: 어린이들은 그의 사무실에 오는 것을 좋아한다. 그는 그들에게 그들의 치아에 대하여 말한다.
items.problem: "office" here is a dentist's practice - the whole round is about Dr. Green's practice, where he cleans teeth, treats toothaches and hands out a gift. 사무실 means a desk-work office and is simply the wrong sense of the word. Row 8 repeats it: "그는 8시 경에 그의 사무실에 도착한다." The same round gets it right in row 5, where "his dental office" becomes "그의 치과 병원", so the translation contradicts itself inside one lesson.
items.correction: Row 2: "어린이들은 그의 치과에 오는 것을 좋아한다. ..." Row 8: "그는 8시쯤 치과에 도착한다. ..." - use 치과 or 진료실 consistently with row 5's 치과 병원. Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json -> d007 row n=6 (contradicts rows n=3 and n=5)
items.original: John's mother and father were married on May 9, 1953. His mother was 20 years old and his father was 22.
items.problem: Both ages are one year too high given the birthdates stated two and three rows earlier in the same round. Row 3: "Mrs. Wenger, John's mother, was born in Germany on September 9, 1933." - on 9 May 1953 her birthday had not yet come round, so she was 19, not 20. Row 5: "John's father was born in Bern, Switzerland on November 12, 1931." - on 9 May 1953 he was 21, not 22. This round is built entirely around dates and ages (its hint block is literally "September 9, 1933 ... May 9, 1953. 20 22. June 4, 1954. 22"), so the arithmetic is the point of the lesson, not incidental.
items.correction: "John's mother and father were married on May 9, 1953. His mother was 19 years old and his father was 21." - and update the KO row to "그의 어머니는 19살이었고 그의 아버지는 21세였다." and the hint numbers "20 22" to "19 21". If the intended ages are 20 and 22, move the marriage date to after 12 November 1953 instead. NOTE: changing the English line changes its clip key - regenerate with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs` in the same task.

items.original: 내 이름은 Henry Wells다. 나의 아내 Helen과 나는 어제 밤 Andrew 부부의 집으로 갔다.
items.problem: The English is "the Andrews' house" - the family name is Andrews, and this round's hint block also gives "Andrews'". The Korean drops the final s and turns them into the Andrew family. The couple is referred to again in d009 rows 3-4 and throughout d010. (The same row also writes 어제 밤 for 어젯밤 - see the orthography finding.)
items.correction: "내 이름은 Henry Wells다. 나의 아내 Helen과 나는 어젯밤 Andrews 부부의 집에 갔다." Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.original: Kim Norris는 뉴저지의 Ocean City에 있는데 그곳에서 그녀는 그녀의 친구 Becky Field의 숙객이다.
items.problem: 숙객 is a rare Sino-Korean word that almost no learner at this level will know, and it is used as the gloss for "houseguest", the one new word in the sentence. Glossing an unfamiliar English word with an unfamiliar Korean one teaches nothing.
items.correction: "Kim Norris는 뉴저지의 Ocean City에 있는데, 그곳에서 친구 Becky Field의 집에 손님으로 머물고 있다." Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.original: 자전거타는 사람이 약 300명 있었어. 나는 집에서 새로운 흰색 수영복을 샀고 그런데 나는 그것을 가져오는 것을 잊었어.
items.problem: "샀고 그런데" is ungrammatical: the connective ending -고 already joins the clauses, so the contrastive conjunction 그런데 cannot follow it. "자전거타는" is also missing its space (자전거 타는).
items.correction: "자전거 타는 사람이 약 300명 있었어. 나는 집에서 새 흰색 수영복을 샀는데, 그것을 가져오는 걸 잊어버렸어." Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.original: 제발 빨리 편지해줘.
items.problem: The English row is "Please write soon. Love, Kim." - the Korean drops the closing signature "Love, Kim." entirely. The parallel letter in d008 row 15 does translate it ("제발 빨리 와서 우리를 만나줘. 사랑하는 낸시."), so this is an omission, not a policy. Step 2 shows the learner only the Korean and asks them to rebuild the whole English sentence, so the word-bank tiles "Love" and "Kim" have no cue at all in the prompt. Separately, "제발" renders "Please" as a desperate plea (roughly "I beg you"), the wrong register for a friendly sign-off, in this row and in d008 row 15.
items.correction: "곧 편지해줘. 사랑을 담아, Kim." - restore the signature and replace 제발 with 곧 or 부디. Korean is not part of the clip key, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.locator: round d025, sentences n=2, n=5, n=6 (EN)
items.original: The drive took about an hour because of the traffic.
items.problem: The passage says they left the apartment "around 10 a.m." (n=2) and reached the beach "around 11:30" (n=5), which is about an hour and a half, then says the drive took "about an hour" (n=6). The three numbers do not add up, and the "because of the traffic" clause implies the drive was longer than normal, which makes the understatement more conspicuous.
items.correction: Make one of the three consistent, e.g. change n=6 to "The drive took about an hour and a half because of the traffic." Changing the English deletes this line's Azure clip, so re-run node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same task and update the Korean row and content/lessons/ld/d025-1.json block 6.

items.original: 가장 많은 군중들이 퍼레이드와 축제를 곁들인 연례적인 Mardi Grass 축하를 위하여 뉴올린즈로 온다.
items.problem: The -1 script pages carry a cluster of spelling and transliteration defects that the scripts file does not have: "Mardi Grass" for Mardi Gras (d034-1 blocks[11]); "뉴올린즈"/"뉴 올린즈" instead of the standard 뉴올리언스, with the spacing varying inside one file (d033-1 blocks[1,4,5,7,8]; d034-1 blocks[3,7,8,9,11,12]); "불란서 사람들", an archaic word for the French, where the scripts file says 프랑스 (d034-1 blocks[2]); "Kevin taylor" with a lowercase surname (d028-1 blocks[1]); "Jim Eliott" for Elliott, in a line that spells it "Elliott" three other times (d032-1 blocks[2]); "쥬스" for the standard 주스 (d025-1 blocks[4]); "스포츠 작가협회" for Association of Sportswriters, where 기자 (journalist), not 작가 (author), is the right word (d027-1 blocks[2]).
items.correction: Bring each -1 page's Korean into line with the corresponding row in content/ld_english_scripts.json, which is already correct in every one of these cases: 뉴올리언스, 프랑스, Kevin Taylor, Jim Elliott, 주스, 스포츠 기자협회, Mardi Gras.

items.locator: the hints block of content/lessons/ld/d025.json, d026.json, d027.json, d028.json, d030.json, d031.json, d032.json, d035.json
items.original: Kevin Taylor, Canadian national swimming competition. twenty sports clubs women's 100 meter free style.
items.problem: The lesson instruction tells the learner to use the hints for the dictation ("다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서 영어로 받아쓰기를 하세요"), but the hints spell words differently from the script they are hinting at, so a learner who copied them would be graded wrong. d028: "twenty sports clubs" vs script "20 sports clubs", "free style" vs "freestyle". d025: "ten a.m." vs "10 a.m.". d026: "took turn rowing" vs "They took turns rowing", "six o'clock" vs "6:00". d027: "association of sports writers" vs "Association of Sportswriters". d030: "4 dollars and 95 cents" vs "$4.95", "Mr.Biggs" vs "Mr. Biggs". d031: "Mt.Everest" vs "Mount Everest". d032: "Mt. Everest" vs "Mount Everest", "5 or six" vs "5 or 6". d035: "fifty years" vs "50 years", and the extra instruction block "step-sisters" vs script "stepsisters".
items.correction: Spell every hint exactly as the script line spells it, or drop the hint word. If the number-word normalisation fix is applied to the grader (see the d028 numeral finding), the numeric mismatches stop mattering and only the proper nouns need fixing.

items.locator: round d026, sentences n=11 and n=12 (KO)
items.original: 그들이 떠날 때 Kim이 Carlos에게 물었다. “너는 내일 해변으로 갈꺼냐?”
items.problem: "갈꺼냐" is a misspelling. The standard orthography for the future/prospective -ㄹ 것 construction is -ㄹ 거다 (거냐/거야), never -ㄹ 꺼다. The same error appears twice more in n=12: "나는 그럴꺼야" and "그 보트를 집에 남겨둘꺼야".
items.correction: n=11: "“너는 내일 해변에 갈 거니?”"  n=12: "Carlos는 “그래, 나는 그럴 거야. 그러나 나는 그 보트를 집에 남겨 둘 거야.”라고 대답했다."

items.locator: d027-1 blocks[3] and blocks[10]; d032-1 blocks[2]
items.original: 우리는 오늘 밤 특별한 손님을 모시게 되어서 행운입니다. 저는 Fernando Marcos를 소개하고 싶습니 다.
items.problem: Line-wrap artifacts from the legacy HTML extraction have left a space inside single Korean words: "싶습니 다" (d027-1 blocks[3]), "좋습니 다" (d027-1 blocks[10]) and "떨어 졌다" (d032-1 blocks[2]).
items.correction: Close the spaces: "싶습니다", "좋습니다", "떨어졌다".

items.locator: round d028, sentences n=3, n=6, n=8 (EN)
items.original: Teams have come from 20 sports clubs and their fans have come with them.
items.problem: Within eight sentences this round writes numbers three different ways — "20 sports clubs" (n=3), "100 meter freestyle" (n=4), "three races" (n=6), "4 records" (n=8) — and the typing-mode grader compares strings after stripping everything except [a-z0-9 ] (src/components/LdLearningView.tsx:314-323). A learner who hears "twenty sports clubs" and types "twenty" is marked wrong, and one who hears "four records" and types "four" is marked wrong, because nothing normalises a spelled-out number to its digits. Synthesised speech gives the learner no way to know which form the writer used, so the item is ungradable as written. The same trap exists in the other rounds in scope (d027 "1975/1978", d029 "50/100 meter", d031 "seven other women" vs "27 days", d032 "5 or 6 meters", d033 "160 kilometers", d034 "100 parks"/"38 kilometers", d035 "50 years"), but d028 is the clearest case because both styles appear in one passage.
items.correction: Either (a) pick one convention per passage (spell out numbers under 100, keep digits for years, measurements and times) and re-generate the affected Azure clips, or (b) accept both forms in the grader by normalising number words to digits before comparison (add a word→digit map to normalizeTyped). Option (b) is the safer fix because it does not delete any voice clips.

items.original: Sally Miller is the community sports club swimmer in lane 4.
items.problem: Every other club in this two-round passage is capitalised as a proper noun — "City Sports Club" (d028 n=5), "Lakeside Sports Club" (d029 n=3) — and both the Korean row of this very sentence ("4번 레인의 Community Sports Club 수영 선수") and the d029.json instruction block ("Sally Miller Community Sports Club cheer for") capitalise it. Only the English script line leaves it lowercase, so the same club is a proper name in three places and a common noun in one.
items.correction: Capitalise for consistency: "Sally Miller is the Community Sports Club swimmer in lane 4." (The typing grader lowercases everything, so no graded item changes, and the Azure clip key is unaffected only if the text itself changes — re-generate the clip in the same task.)

items.original: Marta Perez가 2번 레인에서 그녀를 대신했습니다.
items.problem: "Marta Perez has taken her place in lane 2" means she has taken up her own position in lane 2 — "her place" is Marta's place. This renders it as "replaced her (someone else) in lane 2", inventing a substitution that does not happen in the race. The scripts file has it right ("2번 레인에 자리를 잡았습니다").
items.correction: Replace with "Marta Perez가 2번 레인에 자리를 잡았습니다."

items.original: 33번 레인에서 우리는 Lakeside Spots Club을 위한 Elizabeth Norris를 봅니다.
items.problem: Two defects in one line. The English is "In lane 3, we see Elizabeth Norris for Lakeside Sports Club": the lane number is doubled to "33번 레인" (a pool has lanes 1-4 in this passage, so lane 33 is impossible), and the club name is misspelled "Spots Club" for "Sports Club".
items.correction: Replace with "3번 레인에서 우리는 Lakeside Sports Club을 위한 Elizabeth Norris를 봅니다."

items.locator: round d030, sentences n=2 and n=8 (KO); also the d030.json hints block
items.original: 나는 나의 새 직장을 잃었다. Mr.Biggs가 지난 주 자신의 보석 가게에 나를 고용했지만 그가 오늘 나를 해고시켰다.
items.problem: The Korean writes "Mr.Biggs" with no space after the period, while the English of the same sentence has "Mr. Biggs". The same missing space appears in n=8 ("나중에 Mr.Biggs가 …") and in the hints block of content/lessons/ld/d030.json.
items.correction: Write "Mr. Biggs" in both Korean rows and in the hints block, matching the English.

items.original: kathy는 나에게 자신의 일기장과 몇몇 아름다운 사진들을 보여주었습니다.
items.problem: The name is written in lowercase, "kathy", while the same name is capitalised everywhere else in the round (n=2 "Kathy Austin", n=6 "Kathy는") and in the English of this sentence ("Kathy showed me her diary").
items.correction: Change to "Kathy는 나에게 자신의 일기장과 몇몇 아름다운 사진들을 보여주었습니다."

items.locator: round d031, sentences n=2 and n=4/n=5/n=8 (KO)
items.original: 그녀가 그 탐험에 대하여 나에게 말할 때 우리는 저녁을 먹고 있었습니다.
items.problem: All nine Korean rows render one continuous quoted letter from Irene Watson to her editor, but the first-person pronoun switches inside it. n=2 uses the humble forms ("제가 지난 주 Sacramento를 방문하고 있었을 때 저는 …"), while n=4, n=5 ("나는 우리가 그녀의 이야기를 사용할 수 있다고 생각합니다") and n=8 switch to 나/나에게 while keeping the -습니다 ending. Mixing 저 and 나 inside one polite letter is inconsistent in Korean.
items.correction: Use 저/제 throughout the quoted letter: n=4 "그녀가 그 탐험에 대하여 저에게 말할 때 우리는 저녁을 먹고 있었습니다.", n=5 "저는 우리가 그녀의 이야기를 사용할 수 있다고 생각합니다.", n=8 "Kathy는 저에게 자신의 일기장과 …".

items.original: Elliott는 바위 한 조각이 그의 손에 부딪쳤을 때 지도자였다.
items.problem: In a roped climb, "the leader" is the climber going first on the rope (선등자), which is why Byram can hold him when he falls. "지도자" means leader in the sense of a guide, mentor or head of a group — and that role in this passage belongs to Kathy Byram, the instructor the students are climbing with (n=1). The translation therefore contradicts the story it is glossing.
items.correction: Replace with "Elliott는 바위 한 조각이 그의 손에 부딪쳤을 때 선등자(앞장서서 오르는 사람)였다."

items.original: 그 등산가는 또 다른 로프를 그녀의 허리에 묶고 Smith가 서있는 ledge(등성이)로 기어내려 갔다.
items.problem: The Korean leaves the English word "ledge" untranslated inside the Korean sentence and glosses it as "등성이", which is wrong. 등성이/산등성이 is the ridge or spine of a mountain (the Korean for 'ridge'); a ledge is a narrow rock shelf on a cliff face — 암붕, or 바위 턱/좁은 바위 선반. Glossing 'ledge' as 'ridge' teaches the wrong word, and in this passage it makes the scene incoherent: Smith is standing on a shelf part-way up a cliff, not on a mountain ridge.
items.correction: Replace with "그 등산가는 또 다른 로프를 그녀의 허리에 묶고 Smith가 서 있는 암붕(바위 턱)으로 내려갔다."

items.original: 그를 붙잡았다. 그 등산가는 또 다른 로프를 그의 허리에 묶고 Smith가 서있는 ledge(등성이)로 기어내려 갔다.
items.problem: The English is "The mountain climber tied another rope around HER waist" — the mountain climber is Kathy Byram, a woman. This page says "그의 허리" (his waist), which points at Elliott or Smith and makes the rescue nonsensical. The scripts file has "그녀의 허리" correctly. (The "ledge(등성이)" gloss in the same line is the mistranslation reported separately against content/ld_english_scripts.json.)
items.correction: Change "그의 허리에" to "그녀의 허리에", matching content/ld_english_scripts.json d032 n=5.

items.locator: round d033, sentence n=4 (EN and KO)
items.original: New Orleans has more trade with Latin America than any other United States port.
items.problem: This superlative cannot be confirmed for 2026. The Port of New Orleans does market Latin America as its core trade lane (nine weekly container services, most calling Veracruz and Altamira; imports from Mexico growing ~20% a year), but no published ranking shows it ahead of Port Everglades, PortMiami or Houston for total Latin America trade, and the claim originates in a 1980s encyclopaedia entry. I could not find a source that settles it either way.
items.correction: Expert review required, or replace the superlative with a claim the port itself makes, e.g. "New Orleans has close trade ties with Latin America." Whichever wording is chosen, re-generate the clip and update the Korean row and content/lessons/ld/d033-1.json block 4 together.

items.locator: round d033, sentence n=6 (EN and KO)
items.original: The city is the leading business, cultural, and industrial center in the southern United States.
items.problem: Presented as a present-tense fact, this is no longer true. New Orleans metro has roughly 1.2 million people and is not the South's leading business or industrial centre by any measure: Dallas-Fort Worth (8.48 m people, ~$770 bn metro GDP), Houston (7.90 m, ~$551 bn) and Atlanta (6.48 m, ~$604 bn) are an order of magnitude larger. The sentence is a 1970s-80s encyclopaedia claim carried over unchanged.
items.correction: Soften to a claim that is still true, e.g. "The city is a leading business, cultural, and industrial center in the southern United States." (a → the), or "The city is one of the cultural centers of the southern United States." Re-generate the clip and update the Korean row ("그 도시는 미국 남부의 주요 사업, 문화, 산업 중심지 중 하나이다.") and content/lessons/ld/d033-1.json block 6 in the same task.

items.original: 뉴올린즈는 미국에서 두 번째로 바쁜 항구이다.
items.problem: The English says "New Orleans is ONE OF the busiest seaports in the United States", and content/ld_english_scripts.json renders it correctly as "미국에서 가장 바쁜 항구 중 하나이다". This companion page instead asserts a specific rank — "the second busiest port in the United States" — which is both unfaithful to the source sentence and factually false: by tonnage the Port of New Orleans ranks about 6th (behind Houston, South Louisiana, Corpus Christi, New York/New Jersey and Long Beach).
items.correction: Replace with "뉴올리언스는 미국에서 가장 바쁜 항구 중 하나이다." (matching content/ld_english_scripts.json d033 n=1).

items.locator: round d034, sentence n=5 (EN and KO)
items.original: Many sports events, exhibitions and conventions take place in the Louisiana Superdome.
items.problem: The venue has not been called the Louisiana Superdome since 2011. It was the Mercedes-Benz Superdome from 2011 to 2021 and has been the Caesars Superdome since 2021. The lesson presents the 1975-2011 name as the current one.
items.correction: Use the name-neutral form the venue is universally known by: "Many sports events, exhibitions and conventions take place in the Superdome." (This also survives the next naming-rights sale.) Re-generate the clip and update the Korean row and content/lessons/ld/d034-1.json block 5 in the same task.

items.original: 많은 스포츠 행사, 전시회 및 대회가 the Louisiana Superdome에서 발생한다.
items.problem: "발생하다" is used for things that happen unintentionally — accidents, incidents, problems. Scheduled events "take place" = 열리다/개최되다. Also, the English article "the" is carried into the Korean sentence ("the Louisiana Superdome에서"), which is not Korean; the same happens in n=1 ("the French Quarter를 보러 온다").
items.correction: "많은 스포츠 행사, 전시회, 대회가 루이지애나 슈퍼돔에서 열린다." and n=1 "많은 사람들은 프렌치 쿼터를 보러 온다." (keep the English proper nouns if that is the house style, but drop the article).

items.original: 그것은 세계 최대의 실내 경기장 혹은 스테디엄이다.
items.problem: The English is "It is ONE OF the world's largest indoor arenas." This renders it as "the world's LARGEST indoor arena or stadium", an absolute superlative the source does not make and that is not true of the Superdome today. "스테디엄" is also an unnecessary transliteration with no counterpart in the English.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file wording: "그것은 세계에서 가장 큰 실내 경기장 중 하나이다."

items.original: 세계에서 가장 긴 다리인 the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway가 뉴 올린즈에 있다.
items.problem: Two errors against the English "The world's longest continuous bridge over water, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway, is NEAR New Orleans." (1) "물 위를 잇는 교량으로는" is dropped, turning a true qualified claim into the false claim that it is the longest bridge in the world outright — it is not (the Causeway holds only the Guinness category "longest bridge over water (continuous)"; far longer bridges such as the Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge exist). (2) "뉴 올린즈에 있다" says the bridge is IN New Orleans; it crosses Lake Pontchartrain between Metairie and Mandeville, i.e. near the city.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file wording: "물 위를 잇는 교량으로는 세계에서 가장 긴 Lake Pontchartrain Causeway가 뉴올리언스 근처에 있다."

items.original: 이 다리는 47km 이상의 길이이다.
items.problem: The English says "This bridge is over 38 kilometers long" and the scripts file translates it as 38km. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is 23.83 miles = about 38.4 km. "47km" is wrong both against the source sentence and against reality.
items.correction: Change to "이 다리는 38km 이상의 길이이다." (matching content/ld_english_scripts.json d034 n=9).

items.original: Dorothy는 나의 친사촌이다.
items.problem: The very next clause of the same sentence says "그녀의 어머니는 나의 아버지의 누이인 Helen 고모이다" — Dorothy's mother is the speaker's father's SISTER (고모). A cousin through 고모 is 고종사촌; 친사촌 means specifically the child of the father's BROTHER. The translation therefore contradicts itself inside one sentence, in a passage whose entire subject is kinship terms.
items.correction: Replace with "Dorothy는 나의 고종사촌이다." (or, if the aim is only to render 'first cousin' as opposed to 'second cousin', "Dorothy는 나와 사촌 간이다").

items.locator: round d036, sentence n=1 (EN); same claim echoed in the d036.json hints block
items.original: As the American author Mark Twain once said, everybody talks about the weather but nobody does anything about it.
items.problem: The quotation is not Mark Twain's. The earliest known appearance is an unsigned Hartford Courant editorial of 27 August 1897 written by Twain's friend and neighbour Charles Dudley Warner, and Twain himself credited Warner when asked. The line appears nowhere in Twain's writings or recorded speeches. The lesson states the false attribution as plain fact in its opening sentence, and the hints block reinforces it with "American author, Mark Twain".
items.correction: Rewrite as: "As the American writer Charles Dudley Warner once said, everybody talks about the weather but nobody does anything about it." If the Twain association is wanted, say "a line often credited to Mark Twain, but actually written by his friend Charles Dudley Warner". Note: changing the English text deletes the Azure clip for this line, so re-run node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same task, and update the d036.json hints block and the Korean row together.

items.original: 그녀는 대부분의 사내들보다 축구를 잘했고
items.problem: 'most boys' is translated 대부분의 사내들. 사내 means a grown man; the sentence is about Amy Johnson's schoolmates, who are boys. The preceding line (n=2) correctly renders 'other girls in her school' as 다른 소녀들, so the pair 소녀들/사내들 is also internally inconsistent in register.
items.correction: '그녀는 대부분의 남자아이들보다 축구를 잘했고' (or 남학생들). Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d073 n=3, d075 n=2 and n=3, d076 n=3, d078 n=8 (KO)
items.original: 그녀는 대부분의 사내들보다 축구를 잘했고 불행히도 그녀의 교사 중의 많은 사람들에게 좀 좋지 않은 인 상을 주었다.
items.problem: Line-wrap artifacts from the original HTML left a space inside single Korean words in the rendered translation: d073 n=3 '인 상을' (인상을), d075 n=3 '건 설되었다' (건설되었다), d076 n=3 '불타는 고 무로부터' (고무로부터), d078 n=8 '팔거나 임 대하려고' (임대하려고). Separately, d075 n=2 has a space before a particle: 'Drag racing 은 1953년…' should be 'Drag racing은'. These are in the file the LD view actually renders, so learners see them.
items.correction: Close the four intra-word spaces (인상을 / 건설되었다 / 고무로부터 / 임대하려고) and remove the space before 은 in d075 n=2. Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.lesson: LISTENING d074 / d076 / d077 / d082 / d083 (main lesson JSON)
items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d074.json blocks[3] and [4]; d082.json blocks[3]; d083.json blocks[3]; d084.json blocks[3]; plus hints text in d076.json blocks[2], d077.json blocks[2], d082.json blocks[2], d083.json blocks[2]
items.original: { "type": "instruction", "text": "sandstorm emergency landing India six days later. two days. Burma, monsoon football field." }
items.problem: Two related defects. (1) In d074 (two blocks), d082 ('1908, Griffith director New York..' — note the doubled period), d083 ('July 23, 1948') and d084 ('fragile. packages'), continuation hint word-lists are stored with "type": "instruction" instead of "type": "hints", so they are typed as directions to the learner rather than as the vocabulary aid the first instruction block points at. (2) Several hint tokens do not match the script spelling a learner must produce: d076 hints 'teen-age pastime' vs script 'teenage pastime'; d077 hints 'three room apartment' vs script 'three-room apartment'; d082 hints 'D.W.Griffith' vs script 'D.W. Griffith'; d083 hints 'American civil war' vs script 'American Civil War' and 'July 23, 1948' vs script 'July 23rd, 1948'; d081 hints '1440 pictures' vs script '1,440 pictures'.
items.correction: Retype the five continuation blocks as "type": "hints", remove the stray doubled period in d082 ('New York..' → 'New York.'), and align the listed hint tokens to the exact script spelling (teenage, three-room, 'D.W. Griffith', 'American Civil War', 'July 23rd, 1948', '1,440 pictures'). JSON-only changes, no audio regeneration.

items.original: 그녀의 항로는 그녀를 비엔나, 콘스탄티노불과 바그다드 상공으로 데려갔다.
items.problem: Two place names are misspelled in this file only. Constantinople is 콘스탄티노플 in Korean, not 콘스탄티노불. Australia is 오스트레일리아, not 오스트렐리아 — the latter appears three times in this file (blocks 2, 6 and 9). The scripts-file Korean for the same round spells both correctly, so this file is the outlier.
items.correction: Replace 콘스탄티노불 → 콘스탄티노플 and all three 오스트렐리아 → 오스트레일리아, matching content/ld_english_scripts.json. JSON-only change.

items.original: Drag racing started in the United States in 1953.
items.problem: Drag racing began in the United States in the 1940s, on decommissioned airfields; the first commercial strip (Santa Ana) opened in 1950 and the NHRA was founded by Wally Parks in 1951. 1953 is the year of the first NHRA-sanctioned drag strip/event, not the year the sport started. The sentence as written is false, and the Korean ('Drag racing 은 1953년 미국에서 시작되었다.') repeats it.
items.correction: Either 'Drag racing started in the United States in the 1940s.' or, to keep 1953, 'The first official drag races in the United States were held in 1953.' Korean: '드래그 레이싱은 1940년대 미국에서 시작되었다.' Editing the English requires regenerating the d075 clip.

items.original: A track is an absolutely straight course about 1200 feet long.
items.problem: The standard drag strip is a quarter mile — 1,320 feet (402 m) under both NHRA and FIA rules. Shorter distances in use are 1,000 feet (Top Fuel and Funny Car since 2008) and 1/8 mile (660 feet). 1,200 feet matches none of them. The Korean ('약 1200피트 길이의') and the hints block ('1200 feet long') repeat the figure.
items.correction: Use the real standard: 'A track is an absolutely straight course about 1320 feet long.' / '트랙은 약 1320피트(약 400미터) 길이의 완전히 곧은 코스다.' Update the d075 hints block to '1320 feet long' and regenerate the d075 clip.

items.original: A good drag racer can earn as much as $65,000 a year.
items.problem: The passage is written in the present tense ('There are professional races now') and presents $65,000 as today's ceiling for a successful professional drag racer. That figure reflects the late-1970s/1980s source material; top NHRA professionals today earn multiples of it in winnings and sponsorship alone. The Korean ('일년에 무려 65,000불까지') keeps the 무려 ('as much as') framing, which makes the staleness more obvious to a Korean reader.
items.correction: Either date the claim ('In the 1980s a good drag racer could earn as much as $65,000 a year.') or drop the figure. If the number is kept for dictation purposes, add a Korean note that it is a historical figure. Editing the English requires regenerating the d076 clip.

items.original: 그들은 많은 아파트에 대하여 전화했다. 집주인들이 이미 그들의 대부분을 이미 세놓았었다.
items.problem: '이미' appears twice in one clause — a duplication left in the text. Separately, '그들의 대부분' uses the human pronoun 그들 for apartments and reads as 'most of them (the landlords)', which inverts who is being referred to. The same duplicated 이미 is present in content/lessons/ld/d077-1.json.
items.correction: '그들은 많은 아파트에 전화해 보았다. 집주인들은 그중 대부분을 이미 세놓은 상태였다.' Korean-only change, no audio regeneration. Fix the identical line in content/lessons/ld/d077-1.json in the same edit.

items.original: 그들의 아파트는 Oswald가 건축가로써 집에서 일하는 것을 시작할 때까지 충분히 컸었다.
items.problem: 로써 is the instrumental particle ('by means of'); the particle for a role or status is 로서. 'as an architect' = 건축가로서. The same error appears in d078-1 blocks[4] ('때때로 그들은 평가사로써 활동한다'). Both scripts-file versions use 로서 correctly, so these two files are the outliers.
items.correction: 건축가로써 → 건축가로서, 평가사로써 → 평가사로서. JSON-only change in both files.

items.original: 때때로 그들은 평가사로서 활동한다. 첫째 평가사들은 하나의 재산을 본다.
items.problem: Across both rounds 'property' is translated 재산 (assets/wealth in general). In a real-estate passage the Korean word is 부동산, or 매물/물건 for an individual listing. '하나의 재산을 본다' for 'a piece of property' is not Korean anyone would say and obscures that the appraiser is looking at one house or lot. The same substitution appears in d078 n=1 ('재산을 팔고 세놓는다'), n=8 ('팔거나 임대할 재산'), d079 n=2, 3, 5, 6.
items.correction: Replace 재산 with 부동산 (or 매물) throughout d078 and d079, e.g. '첫째, 평가사들은 부동산 한 건을 살펴본다.', '부동산 중개업자들은 부동산을 팔고 세놓는다.' Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: 그들은 또 몇몇 시간제 직원들을 고용해도 좋다.
items.problem: The English (d078 n=7) is 'They may also hire some part-time workers', where 'may' expresses possibility — 'they sometimes also hire'. '고용해도 좋다' renders it as permission ('they are allowed to hire'), which changes who is deciding. The scripts-file Korean for the same line is correct ('고용하기도 한다'), so this file contradicts the rendered translation.
items.correction: '그들은 또 몇몇 시간제 직원들을 고용하기도 한다.' — align with content/ld_english_scripts.json. JSON-only change.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d080 n=1,3,4,5,6 and d081 n=1,2,4,5 (KO)
items.original: 매분 1440개나 되는 사진들이 그 빛 앞에서 움직인다. 셔터는 매 그림에 대하여 열리고 닫힌다.
items.problem: The English uses one word, 'picture', for a single film frame throughout both rounds, but the Korean alternates between 사진 and 그림 — sometimes within one sentence (the quoted line uses 사진들 then 그림). d080 n=3 '각 사진은', n=4 '그 그림을', n=5 '그 사진을'; d081 n=1 '사진들'/'그림', n=2 '그 그림이', n=4 '그 그림을', n=5 '그 그림을'.
items.correction: Pick one rendering and use it consistently across d080 and d081 — 사진 (or the more precise 화면/프레임 for a film frame) — e.g. '셔터는 매 사진마다 열리고 닫힌다.' Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: 다른 어떤 감독보다도 D.W. Griffith는 영화 제작의 기술을 발전시킨 책임이 있었다.
items.problem: 'was responsible for developing' here means Griffith did more than anyone else to develop the art of filmmaking — it is credit. The Korean '발전시킨 책임이 있었다' reads as 'bore the responsibility/blame for having developed it', which is the opposite register and, in Korean, sounds like he was held accountable for something. The sentence is the opening thesis of the whole Griffith unit, so the distortion sets up the rest wrongly.
items.correction: '다른 어떤 감독보다도 D.W. Griffith가 영화 제작 기술을 발전시킨 주역이었다.' (or '…발전시키는 데 가장 크게 기여했다.'). Korean-only change, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.original: When David was seven years old, his father died and his family moved to Louisville.
items.problem: D.W. Griffith was ten, not seven, when his father Jacob Wark Griffith died (1885; Griffith was born 22 January 1875). The Korean translation repeats the error ('David가 7살이었을 때 그의 아버지가 죽었고'), so both the dictation audio and the translation teach the wrong fact. The lesson's hints block also carries the wrong number ('seven Louisville').
items.correction: Change to 'When David was ten years old, his father died and his family moved to Louisville.' and the Korean to 'David가 10살이었을 때 그의 아버지가 죽었고 그의 가족은 Louisville로 이사했다.' Also change 'seven' to 'ten' in the d082 hints block. This edits an English line, so the d082 clip must be regenerated with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: 다른 어떤 감독보다도 D.WGriffth는 영화 제작의 기술을 발전시킨 책임이 있었다. / David Wark Griffith는 1875년 1월 22일에 켄터키주, Floydsfo가에서 태어났다.
items.problem: Two corrupted proper nouns. 'D.WGriffth' is missing the second period and the space, and misspells Griffith as 'Griffth'. 'Floydsfo가' is a mangled remnant of the place name — the English line says 'Floyds Fork, Kentucky' and the scripts-file Korean correctly says '켄터키주 Floyds Fork에서'. '가' is left over from a broken conversion.
items.correction: '다른 어떤 감독보다도 D.W. Griffith가 영화 제작 기술을 발전시킨 주역이었다.' and 'David Wark Griffith는 1875년 1월 22일에 켄터키주 Floyds Fork에서 태어났다.' JSON-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: Griffith's most famous movie was The Birth of a Nation. / The film is about the American Civil War and the years that followed. / The movie was very popular and it made Griffith famous.
items.problem: The three lines introduce The Birth of a Nation purely as a famous, popular success with no mention of what it actually is. The 1915 film portrays Black characters as brutish and dangerous, presents the Ku Klux Klan as heroic, and its success is directly tied to the Klan's 1915 revival and to a documented rise in lynchings where it was screened. A paid course recommending it to Korean learners with zero context can reasonably be read as endorsement.
items.correction: Keep the English (it is factually true and the audio exists) but add a short Korean editorial note on the d083 round and in the translation area, e.g. '※ 이 영화는 흑인을 악의적으로 묘사하고 KKK를 미화한 작품으로, 영화사적 기법의 중요성과는 별개로 심각한 인종차별 논란의 대상입니다.' No audio change is needed if only the Korean note is added.

items.original: 그 영화는 미국의 내전과 뒤이은 여러 해에 대해서이다.
items.problem: 'the American Civil War' is a fixed proper noun whose Korean equivalent is 남북 전쟁 (or 미국 남북전쟁). '미국의 내전' is a literal calque that most Korean learners will not recognise as the Civil War, so the historical reference is lost. 'and the years that followed' means the Reconstruction era, which '뒤이은 여러 해' renders vaguely.
items.correction: '그 영화는 미국 남북 전쟁과 그 이후의 재건 시대를 다룬다.' Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: Griffith continued to make movies until 1930.
items.problem: Griffith's final feature as director was The Struggle, released in 1931; Abraham Lincoln (1930) was his second-to-last. 'Until 1930' cuts his career one film short. The Korean ('Griffith는 1930년까지 영화를 만드는 것을 계속했다') and the hints block ('1930.') repeat it.
items.correction: 'Griffith continued to make movies until 1931.' / 'Griffith는 1931년까지 영화를 만드는 것을 계속했다.' Update the d083 hints block to 1931 and regenerate the d083 clip.

items.original: 그는 1948년 7월 22일 캘리포니아의 헐리웃에서 죽었다.
items.problem: Wrong date. The English line (d083 n=12) says 'July 23rd, 1948', the scripts-file Korean says 7월 23일, the d083 hints block says 'July 23, 1948', and Griffith did die on 23 July 1948 — only this script-page block says 22일. Secondary: 헐리웃 should be 할리우드 (standard Korean spelling, used nowhere else in the course files I checked).
items.correction: '그는 1948년 7월 23일 캘리포니아의 할리우드에서 죽었다.' JSON-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: 그녀가 파는 컴퓨터는 미국에서 만들어지고 종종 다른 나라로 보내진다 그들이 선적되기 전에 컴퓨터들은 조심스럽게 포장된다.
items.problem: Two problems in the same passage. (1) A sentence-final period is missing between '보내진다' and '그들이' — the English is two sentences. (2) The English 'they' referring to computers is translated 그들 throughout the round (n=2 '그들이 선적되기 전에', n=3 '그들은 무게가 측정되고', n=4 '그들은 비행기로 옮겨져서', n=5 '그들은 매우 조심스럽게 내려진다'). 그들 is the animate/human pronoun; for objects Korean uses 그것들 or simply drops the pronoun.
items.correction: '그녀가 파는 컴퓨터는 미국에서 만들어져 종종 다른 나라로 보내진다. 선적되기 전에 컴퓨터들은 조심스럽게 포장된다.' and replace 그들 with 그것들 or omit it in n=3, 4, 5. Korean-only change, no audio regeneration.

items.original: When the computers arrive in another country, they are unloaded very carefully they are given special care because they are very fragile.
items.problem: Two independent clauses are run together with no punctuation between 'carefully' and 'they are given'. The Korean translation and the d084-1 script page both split this into two sentences, confirming a sentence boundary is missing. Because learners transcribe this line and the synthesized voice reads it as one breath, the run-on is both an English error and a listening problem.
items.correction: 'When the computers arrive in another country, they are unloaded very carefully. They are given special care because they are very fragile.' Editing the English requires regenerating the d084 clip.

items.original: The computer records the information and stores it. The large amount of information can be stored in a very small space.
items.problem: "The large amount of information" uses a definite article with no antecedent - no particular large amount has been mentioned. The Korean says "많은 양의 정보가" (a large amount), confirming the intended indefinite reading.
items.correction: "A large amount of information can be stored in a very small space." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json, key d085, rows n=7, n=8, n=9 (ko)
items.original: 산술적인 유닛은 문제들을 풀기 위하여 그 정보를 이용한다.
items.problem: "memory unit" and "arithmetic unit" are translated as "메모리 유닛" and "산술적인 유닛". The established Korean terms are 기억 장치 and 연산 장치(산술 장치); "산술적인 유닛" additionally turns the noun "arithmetic" into an adjective, so it reads as "the arithmetical unit", which is not a term at all.
items.correction: n=7 "...컴퓨터의 기억 장치(memory unit)에 저장된다", n=8 "연산 장치(arithmetic unit)는 문제를 풀기 위해 그 정보를 이용한다", n=9 "기억 장치와 연산 장치는...".

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json, key d086, rows n=2 and n=3 (ko)
items.original: 산업체들과 은행들은 재정 기록을 유지하기 위하여 컴퓨터를 사용한다.
items.problem: "Businesses" is translated as "산업체들" (industrial establishments) in n=2, and the different English word "industries" is translated with the same "산업체들" in n=3. Two distinct English words collapse into one Korean word, and neither mapping is right: businesses = 기업(체), industries = 산업.
items.correction: n=2: "기업과 은행은 재정 기록을 관리하기 위해 컴퓨터를 사용한다." / n=3: "많은 산업 분야에서 컴퓨터는 제품을 만드는 다른 기계를 제어하는 데 사용된다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d086 n=5 (로케트), d087 n=5 (컨서트), d095 n=1 (컨테스트)
items.original: 로케트, 비행기, 선박, 자동차를 위하여 특별 컴퓨터들이 개발되어왔다. / 만일 그가 표를 예약했더라면 그는 재즈 컨서트에 갈 수 있었을 것이다. / 그녀는 한 컨테스트에서 수상시를 썼습니다.
items.problem: Three loanwords are spelled in obsolete forms that the standard Korean loanword orthography replaced: 로케트 -> 로켓, 컨서트 -> 콘서트, 컨테스트 -> 콘테스트. (See also 와싱턴 -> 워싱턴 and 샌프랜시스코 -> 샌프란시스코 on the -1 pages, reported separately.)
items.correction: 로켓 / 콘서트 / 콘테스트 (또는 '대회').

items.original: 그는 강의 배(riverboat)를 타러 갈 수 있었을 것이며 혹은 그는 박물관들을 방문할 수 있었을 것이다.
items.problem: "go for a riverboat ride" is rendered as "강의 배를 타러 가다" - a literal calque - and the translator then had to paste the English word in parentheses because the Korean does not convey it. No other line in these twelve rounds parenthesises an English word this way. In New Orleans a riverboat ride is 유람선 관광.
items.correction: 그는 유람선을 타러 갈 수도 있었고, 박물관을 방문할 수도 있었다.

items.original: They first became interested in mechanical flight in 1899.
items.problem: 1899 is when the Wrights began their serious research (Wilbur's 30 May 1899 letter to the Smithsonian, which the next line refers to), but it is not when they first became interested: their interest was sparked by news of Otto Lilienthal's death in 1896 (and by a toy helicopter in childhood).
items.correction: "They began serious work on mechanical flight in 1899." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: Wilbur built a wind tunnel and used it to test more than 200 different wing surfaces.
items.problem: The 1901 wind tunnel was designed and built by both brothers, not by Wilbur alone; museum sources consistently say "the Wright brothers" / "Wilbur and Orville". (The next line, n=10, about turning the wings - wing warping - is correctly Wilbur's work.) "more than 200" is also slightly high: sources say they tested as many as 200 model wing shapes and recorded formal data on about 50.
items.correction: "The brothers built a wind tunnel and used it to test about 200 different wing surfaces." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d088-1.json, blocks[4] (4th Korean script line, = script row n=3)
items.original: 가장 긴 비행은 59초 내에 200미터를 여행했다.
items.problem: Wrong distance. The English line and the rendered Korean say 260 meters in 59 seconds ("The longest flight traveled 260 meters in 59 seconds." / "가장 긴 비행은 59초 동안 260미터를 여행했다."). 260 m (852 ft) is the historically correct figure for the fourth flight of 17 Dec 1903; 200 m is wrong and contradicts the English the learner transcribes. (The same line also changes 59초 동안 to 59초 내에.)
items.correction: 가장 긴 비행은 59초 동안 260미터를 여행했다.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d088-1.json, blocks[6] and blocks[10] (Korean script lines for rows n=5 and n=9)
items.original: 그 두 형제 Wilburt와 Orville Wright는 오하이오주 데이턴에서 자전거 가게를 운영했다.
items.problem: The name is spelled "Wilburt" twice on this page (also in the wind-tunnel line: "Wilburt는 하나의 바람 터널을 만들고..."). The correct name is Wilbur, as the English script and the rendered Korean have it, and as the lesson's own hint block has it ("Flyer Wilbur Orville Dayton,").
items.correction: Wilbur (both occurrences).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d088-1.json, blocks[7] (7th Korean script line, = script row n=6)
items.original: 그들은 1809년에 기계적인 비행에 처음으로 흥미를 느끼게 되었다.
items.problem: The year is 1809, which is 62 years before Orville Wright was born (1871). The English line and the rendered Korean in content/ld_english_scripts.json both say 1899 ("They first became interested in mechanical flight in 1899." / "그들은 1899년에..."). A digit transposition (1899 -> 1809) in the -1 page copy of the same sentence.
items.correction: 그들은 1899년에 기계적인 비행에 처음으로 흥미를 느끼게 되었다. (See also the separate finding on the 1899 claim itself.)

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d088 n=1, d089 n=8, d089 n=9, d094 n=2 (ko)
items.original: 라이트 형제가 the Flyer를 건조하기 위하여 사용했던 기본적인 아이디어들은 그때 이래로 비행한 모든 비 행기에서 사용되어왔다.
items.problem: A word is split by a stray space in the middle, left over from line-wrapping in the legacy HTML: "모든 비 행기에서" (d089 n=9), "곧 라이트 형 제는" (d089 n=8), "결코 행해질 수 없을 것이 라고" (d088 n=1), "관습, 관 심사들을" (d094 n=2). The same corruption appears on the -1 pages as well, plus more there: "운반했 다", "놀라 지 않았다", "사용했 다" (d088-1), "학교에 다녀야 한 다" (d090-1), "그릴 수 있 다" (d094-1).
items.correction: Delete the stray spaces: 비행기에서, 형제는, 것이라고, 관심사들을 (and the -1 page equivalents).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d088.json blocks[3]; d090.json blocks[3]; d091.json blocks[3]; d092.json blocks[3] and blocks[4]; d095.json blocks[3]; d096.json blocks[4]
items.original: { "type": "instruction", "text": "bachelor of arts Bachelor of science degree. business, education, engineering, law, medicine." }
items.problem: In 6 of the 12 rounds in scope the hint list is longer than one line, and the continuation lines are stored as `instruction` blocks instead of being part of the `hints` block. Only the first line is in `hints`, so any consumer that reads the hints (today, only the disabled quiz; tomorrow, a restored hints panel) gets a truncated hint list, and the rest would render as instruction paragraphs. The d092 continuation also has inconsistent capitalisation of the degree names ("bachelor of arts Bachelor of science") against the script's "Bachelor of Arts"/"Bachelor of Science".
items.correction: Merge the continuation `instruction` blocks into the round's `hints` block (keeping the reading order) and normalise the degree-name capitalisation. Do not merge the genuine instruction lines ("다음에 나오는 ... 받아쓰기를 하세요", and the d096 recording note).

items.original: 그것은 90미터를 기어올라가서 40킬로미터를 여행할 수 있었다.
items.problem: "climb" said of an aircraft means to gain altitude (상승하다). "기어올라가다" means to crawl/clamber up, so the Korean describes the aeroplane crawling up 90 metres. It also turns the altitude figure into a distance travelled upward.
items.correction: 그것은 90미터 상공까지 상승할 수 있었고 40킬로미터를 비행할 수 있었다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json, key d089, rows n=1 and n=6 (ko)
items.original: 자동차 엔진은 너무나 무겁기 때문에 the Wrights는 그들의 비행기를 위한 특별한 엔진도 건조해야 했다.
items.problem: "건조하다" is used only for building ships (and, rarely, buildings); an engine and an aeroplane are 제작/제작되다. Both n=1 ("엔진도 건조해야 했다") and n=6 ("the Flyer III은 1905년에 건조되었다") use it, and n=9 repeats it ("the Flyer를 건조하기 위하여"). n=1 also leaves "the Wrights" untranslated while the rest of the round says 라이트 형제.
items.correction: n=1: "...라이트 형제는 비행기에 쓸 특별한 엔진까지 직접 제작해야 했다." / n=6: "...1905년에 제작되었다." / n=9: "...제작하기 위하여".

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json, key d089, rows n=4 and n=9 (en)
items.original: Orville climbed into the flyer and became the first man to fly in an airplane.
items.problem: The aircraft's name is inconsistent within one round: lowercase "the flyer" in n=4, indefinite "a Flyer" in n=9 ("The basic ideas that the Wright brothers used to build a Flyer..."), against "the Flyer" in n=5, n=6, n=10 and in every Korean line. A named aircraft takes the definite article and a capital.
items.correction: n=4: "Orville climbed into the Flyer..."; n=9: "...used to build the Flyer...". Changing the English requires regenerating those clips with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: 그 기계가 준비되었을 때 그들은 그것을 노스캐롤라이나의 KittyHawk로 옮겼다. / 오늘날 그 최초의 Flyer는 와싱턴 DC의 National Air and Space Museum에서 볼 수 있다.
items.problem: "KittyHawk" is missing the space (the place is Kitty Hawk, as the English script and the lesson hint both write it), and "와싱턴" is an obsolete transcription of Washington (standard: 워싱턴, which is what the rendered Korean in ld_english_scripts.json uses). The two copies of the sentence disagree.
items.correction: Kitty Hawk / 워싱턴 DC.

items.original: School attendance is required in every state of the United States. In most states, students must attend school until the age of 16.
items.problem: Presented as a current fact, but it has not been true for well over a decade. Education Commission of the States' 50-state review: 28 states plus DC require attendance to 18 (or graduation), 10 states to 17, and only 15 states to 16. So "most states" require attendance past 16, not until 16.
items.correction: "In most states, students must attend school until the age of 17 or 18." (Or neutrally: "Depending on the state, students must attend school until the age of 16, 17, or 18.") Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: 학교 참석은 미국의 모든 주에서 요구되어 진다. 대부분의 주에서 학생들은 16세까지 학교에 다녀야 한다.
items.problem: "School attendance is required" is rendered word-for-word: "학교 참석" (attendance at an event) instead of 취학/학교 출석, and "요구되어 진다" is a double passive that is also mis-spaced (요구되어진다 / 요구된다). Natural Korean here is "미국의 모든 주에서 취학은 의무이다".
items.correction: 미국의 모든 주에서 학교에 다니는 것은 의무이다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d090 n=1, d091 n=2, d095 n=5, d096 n=3 (en)
items.original: Education in the United States is usually divided into 4 levels. These are early childhood, elementary, secondary, and higher education.
items.problem: Small numbers are written as digits where the synthesized voice says the word, and the typing check rejects number words for digits (LdLearningView.tsx:308-328 strips everything except [a-z0-9 ], so "four levels" != "4 levels"). A learner who hears "four levels" and types "four levels" is marked wrong. Same trap at d091 n=2 "Elementary education is divided into 6 or 8 grades" (heard "six or eight"), d095 n=5 "At 8 that night, she got up for dinner" (heard "eight"), d096 n=3 "28 people were killed in the disaster" (heard "twenty-eight", and a sentence should not start with a numeral). The lessons' own hint blocks spell these out - d090 "four levels", d091 "six eight grades", d096 "Twenty eight people" - which is evidence the source text had words. The same rounds already spell other numbers out ("under six years", "for five days", "two-year programs").
items.correction: Spell these out in the English: "divided into four levels", "divided into six or eight grades", "At eight that night", "Twenty-eight people were killed". NOTE: changing the English deletes that sentence's voice clip (clip key = text hash), so run node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change. The alternative, accepting number words in normalizeTyped, is a code change that would affect every course.

items.original: The second level elementary education is for children from age 6 to 12 or 14.
items.problem: The appositive is not set off, so the subject reads as one long noun pile ("the second level elementary education"). Compare n=5 in the same round, which uses a clean structure: "The third level is secondary education."
items.correction: "The second level, elementary education, is for children from age 6 to 12 or 14." (or "The second level is elementary education. It is for children from age 6 to 12 or 14.") Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: 초등 교육은 6 내지 8 등급으로 나뉘어진다. 어린이들은 보통 하루의 대부분을 한 교사와 만난다.
items.problem: "grades" here means school years (1st grade, 2nd grade...), which is 학년 in Korean. "등급" means rank/grade-level of quality, so the Korean says elementary education is divided into 6 to 8 quality ranks. ("나뉘어진다" is also a double passive; 나뉜다 is correct.)
items.correction: 초등 교육은 6개 또는 8개 학년으로 나뉜다.

items.original: Some students take courses to prepare themselves for college other students take technical or vocational courses that prepare them for jobs after they graduate from high school.
items.problem: Run-on: two independent clauses are joined with no punctuation at "...for college other students take...". The Korean translation correctly splits it into two sentences, so the English and Korean do not match in structure. Learners shadow and transcribe this line.
items.correction: "Some students take courses to prepare themselves for college. Other students take technical or vocational courses that prepare them for jobs after they graduate from high school." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json, key d091, rows n=4 and n=5 (ko)
items.original: 제3 단계는 이차 교육이다. 그것은 중고교 학생을 위해서이다. 중학교는 보통 12세에서 14세의 학생들을 위해서이다.
items.problem: "secondary education" is rendered as "이차 교육" here and as "제2차 교육" in n=4 - both read as "second-round/secondary-in-sequence education" and are not Korean terms for the school level. The correct term is 중등 교육, which this very course already uses correctly in d090 n=1 ("초기 아동, 초등, 중등, 고등 교육"). The inconsistency also breaks the four-level framework the unit is teaching.
items.correction: n=5: "제3단계는 중등 교육이다." / n=4: "그들은 중등 교육에 대비하기 위한 여러 과목과 기능을 배운다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d091 n=4, d091 n=8, d092 n=2 (ko)
items.original: 이것은 다양한 주제가 같은 학교에서 가르쳐진다는 것을 의미한다.
items.problem: In a school context "subject" means 과목 (a school subject), not 주제 (a topic/theme). All three lines mistranslate it: d091 n=4 "다양한 주제와 기술", d091 n=8 "다양한 주제가 ... 가르쳐진다", d092 n=2 "전자, 엔지니어링, 사업 및 다른 주제들". The passage is explaining that US high schools teach many subjects in one school, which the Korean obscures.
items.correction: d091 n=8: "이것은 다양한 과목을 같은 학교에서 가르친다는 뜻이다." / d091 n=4: "다양한 과목과 기능" / d092 n=2: "전자공학, 공학, 경영 등 여러 분야의 2년 과정".

items.original: 더 고등 교육은 고등 학교 이후의 교육 과정을 계속한다. 많은 종류의 더 고등교육 기관들이 있다.
items.problem: "더 고등 교육" / "더 고등교육" is not Korean - the comparative "더" has been translated literally from "higher" and glued onto the fixed term 고등 교육, which already means higher education. The same course translates it correctly in d090 n=1 ("초기 아동, 초등, 중등, 고등 교육"). ("고등 학교" is also written with a space; the word is 고등학교.)
items.correction: 고등 교육은 고등학교 이후의 교육 과정을 이어간다. 고등 교육 기관에는 여러 종류가 있다.

items.original: 기술 연구소들은 전자, 엔지니어링, 사업 및 다른 주제들에 있어서의 2년 프로그램을 제공한다.
items.problem: "Technical institutes" are post-secondary schools; "기술 연구소" means a technical research laboratory, which does not offer two-year programs to students. The sentence therefore contradicts itself in Korean.
items.correction: 기술 전문학교(technical institute)는 전자공학, 공학, 경영 등 여러 분야의 2년 과정을 제공한다.

items.original: Some of these programs are vocational others are academic. After two years at a junior college, students receive an associate degree.
items.problem: Run-on in the first sentence: "are vocational others are academic" joins two independent clauses with no punctuation. The Korean splits it into two sentences ("이 프로그램의 일부는 직업적이다. 다른 것들은 학술적이다."), so English and Korean do not match.
items.correction: "Some of these programs are vocational; others are academic." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: These provide training in business education, engineering, law, and medicine.
items.problem: A comma is missing after "business". As written, "business education" reads as a single field, giving four items; the Korean lists five ("사업, 교육, 공학, 법, 의학"), and this lesson's own hint block reads "business, education, engineering, law, medicine." So the English is a transcription error and it no longer matches its translation or its hint.
items.correction: "These provide training in business, education, engineering, law, and medicine." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d092-1.json, blocks[9] (9th Korean script line, = script row n=8)
items.original: 이것들은 문학사나 공학사 학위로 이어진다. 대부분의 종합대학은 또 직업학교들도 있다.
items.problem: "a Bachelor of Science degree" is rendered as "공학사" (Bachelor of Engineering) on this page, while the rendered Korean in ld_english_scripts.json says "이학사" (Bachelor of Science), which is correct. The two copies of the same sentence disagree, and this one names the wrong degree.
items.correction: 이것들은 문학사나 이학사 학위로 이어진다. (The 직업학교 half of the sentence is wrong on both copies - see the d092 n=8 finding.)

items.original: They might like the colors that the artists use or the way that the subjects are arranged on the surface.
items.problem: The English says "the artists use" (plural, present) while the Korean says "그 화가가 사용한" (singular, past), and the neighbouring line n=7 uses the singular past ("the way the artist expressed an emotion"). The sentence is about one painting, so the singular is intended.
items.correction: "They might like the colors that the artist used or the way that the subjects are arranged on the surface." Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs. (Alternatively align the Korean to the plural present.)

items.original: prehistoric entertaining informative. subjects arrange surface. realistically.
items.problem: "informative" does not occur anywhere in the d093 script. The sentence it is meant to support (n=4) reads "...they can be both entertaining and educational", and the Korean agrees ("교육적일 수 있다"). So the hint word is stale or was changed in the script without updating the hint.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d093 n=4, n=8, n=9; d094 n=1, n=2 (ko)
items.original: 그림은 또 가르칠 수 있다. 그들은 우리에게 그 화가가 한 중요한 대상에 대하여 무엇을 느꼈는지를 말해 줄 수 있다.
items.problem: "그들" is used for paintings and for things throughout these two rounds ("많은 그림들은 ... 그들은 동시에", "그들은 과거 사회의 건축...을 보여줄 수 있다", "많은 사람들은 그들의 대상물을...", "그 화가가 그들이 실제 보이는 방식과 다르게"). In Korean 그들 is for people; inanimate plurals take 그것들 or, more naturally, are dropped. This is literal translationese that reads as if the paintings were people.
items.correction: Drop or replace the pronoun, e.g. "그림은 또 가르칠 수도 있다. 화가가 중요한 소재에 대해 무엇을 느꼈는지 우리에게 말해 준다." / "오래된 그림은 과거 사회의 건축, 의상, 관습, 관심사를 보여 준다."

items.original: 당신은 미국에서의 Pat의 일주일에 대하여 들었습니까? 그녀는 한 컨테스트에서 수상시를 썼습니다.

items.correction: Put n=1 in the same register as the rest: "미국에서 Pat가 보낸 일주일 이야기를 들었는가? 그녀는 어느 대회에서 수상작으로 뽑힌 시를 썼다."

items.original: The fire that followed the explosion burned for two days.
items.problem: The passage describes the Flixborough (Nypro UK) explosion - 1970s, small town in the north of England, chemical factory, 28 killed, roofs torn off - every other detail matches. But the fires did not burn for two days: HSE's case study says "The fires burned for several days and after ten days those that still raged were hampering the rescue work." (Also note the injured figure: HSE records 36 injured on site plus 53 reported off site, so "more than 100 were injured" in n=3 is higher than the official count - that one needs the owner's source for the original passage before changing.)
items.correction: "The fire that followed the explosion burned for more than a week." (If the text is left as is, at least do not present it as a documented event.) Changing the English requires regenerating the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: (원래부터 엔진 및 공장 기계 소음을 넣어서 녹음한 자료이므로 시끄럽습니다. 참고 해주세요).
items.problem: This apologises for noise in the original recording, but the site never plays the original /audio/ld/dNNN.mp3 - every sound the learner hears is a synthesized Azure clip of the English sentences (map §6.4, §12 P-2). The note is therefore obsolete and would confuse a learner who hears clean speech. ("참고 해주세요" is also mis-spaced: 참고해 주세요.)
items.correction: Delete the block, or rewrite it if the original recording is ever played again.

items.problem: "28 people were killed in the disaster" is an industrial accident. "살해되다" means to be murdered, which implies a crime; the rendered Korean in ld_english_scripts.json correctly says "사망했고". The two copies of the same sentence disagree.
items.correction: 그 재난에서 28명이 사망했고 100명 이상이 부상당했다.

items.original: Dexter는 못(lagoon)과 저수지를 건설했는데 그들은 함께 4백만 갤런의 물을 담았다.
items.problem: 그들 is a Korean pronoun for people; it cannot refer back to 못 and 저수지. The relative-clause structure "…건설했는데 그들은 함께…" is a calque of the English "a lagoon and a reservoir that together held…".
items.correction: Dexter는 못(lagoon)과 저수지를 건설했는데, 두 곳을 합치면 4백만 갤런의 물이 담겼다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d169 rows n="4" and n="7" (en, present tense)
items.original: Surfing in the desert is a fantastic success.
items.problem: The round describes Big Surf in Tempe, Arizona (Phil Dexter's wave pool, opened 1969) in the present tense throughout — row 4 "Gates in the reservoir open for 1 1/2 seconds…", row 5 "The surfers catch the waves and ride them…", row 7 "Surfing in the desert is a fantastic success." The park closed permanently in March 2020 and was demolished; the site was sold in 2022 for an industrial park. A 2026 learner is given a closed, demolished facility as something currently operating.
items.correction: Put the description in the past tense and close the story, e.g. row 7: "For fifty years, surfing in the desert was a fantastic success."

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d169-1.json … d180-1.json — the first Korean `instruction` block after "한글 대본을 보면서 말하고 영작해보세요."
items.original: { "type": "instruction", "text": "그냥 웃으면서 그녀에게 걱정하지 말하라고 말했다." }
items.problem: Every one of the 12 -1 script pages in scope is missing the opening sentence (or opening clause) of its round's Korean. d171-1 starts mid-sentence — the head "나의 사촌은 매우 당황했지만 다행히 친구들은" from row 1 is gone, leaving a fragment. d177-1 drops row 1 entirely and starts at row 2. The other ten drop the first sentence of row 1 (d169-1 loses "Dexter는 애리조나로 돌아와…", d170-1 "얼마 전 내 사촌이…", d172-1 "1840년대에 캘리포니아에는…", d173-1 "1848년에는 작은 마을에 불과했던…", d174-1 "John Henry는 미국 민간 설화의…", d175-1 "그는 자신이 어떤 기계보다도…", d176-1 "나는 예전에 기억력이 아주 나쁜…", d178-1 "다음 숫자들을 읽어 보라.", d179-1 "전쟁 중에 한 전투기 조종사가…", d180-1 "그는 수녀들과도 간호사들과도…"). It looks like a systematic loss in the legacy HTML→JSON conversion, not 12 separate edits.
items.correction: Re-extract the first Korean line of each -1 page from ld_english_scripts.json row 1, or drop the now-unused Korean blocks from the -1 files altogether so the data does not look authoritative.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d170 row n="2" (en and ko)
items.original: en: "Cold meat and salad from a nearby restaurant, bread and cake from the bakery, and wine from the local winery."  /  ko: "가까운 식당으로부터 찬 육류와 샐러드를 빵집으로부터 빵과 케익을 그리고 현지 양조장으로부터 와인을,"
items.problem: This row is a verbless fragment continuing row 1 ("she ordered the food in advance"), but the LD view presents every row as a standalone sentence with its own 문장 N of M counter, its own word bank and its own 한글 번역 가이드. The Korean guide is itself a fragment with object markers and no predicate, ending in a comma, so the learner has no way to know the English is deliberately verbless.
items.correction: Fold the list into row 1, or make it a sentence: en "She ordered cold meat and salad from a nearby restaurant, bread and cake from the bakery, and wine from the local winery." / ko "그녀는 가까운 식당에서 찬 육류와 샐러드를, 빵집에서 빵과 케이크를, 현지 양조장에서 와인을 주문했다."

items.original: 그러나 응급실의 의사는 그들에게서 아무런 잘못된 것도 발견하지 않았다.
items.problem: "couldn't find" is rendered as 발견하지 않았다, which means "did not find / chose not to find" and loses the inability. The faithful form is 발견하지 못했다. This row is the set-up for the riddle answer on row 8 (고양이는 식중독이 아니라 차에 치였던 것이다), where the point is precisely that the doctor was unable to find anything wrong.
items.correction: 그러나 응급실의 의사는 그들에게서 아무런 이상도 발견하지 못했다.

items.original: 그냥 웃으면서 그녀에게 걱정하지 말하라고 말했다.
items.problem: 걱정하지 말하라고 is ungrammatical: the negative imperative quotative is ~지 말라고, so it must be 걱정하지 말라고. The rendered text in ld_english_scripts.json d171 row 1 has it right ("걱정하지 말라고"), so this file alone carries the error.
items.correction: 그냥 웃으면서 그녀에게 걱정하지 말라고 말했다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d172 row n="1" (en, first sentence)
items.original: In the 1840s, California was almost uninhabited. There were a few Spanish missions, some ranchers and farmers, and of course dangerous bandits who robbed anybody they could find.
items.problem: Factually wrong. About 150,000 Native Americans were living in California in 1848 — some 500 self-governing tribal societies speaking more than 100 languages — alongside the Californios and settlers the passage does mention. "Almost uninhabited" is only true if Native Americans are not counted as inhabitants, which is exactly the erasure historians identify in gold-rush-era accounts. The claim is also load-bearing for the passage's whole framing (empty land → gold → rush).
items.correction: "In the 1840s, few settlers lived in California, though about 150,000 Native Americans did. There were a few Spanish missions, some ranchers and farmers, and of course dangerous bandits who robbed anybody they could find."

items.original: 보통 이런 마을들은 한 개의 살롱, 한 호텔, 하나의 마굿간, 하나의 감옥, 그리고 하나의 공동 묘지보다 별로 더 많지 않게 구성되어 있었다.
items.problem: Two problems. (1) 마굿간 is a misspelling; the standard form is 마구간(馬廏間). (2) "consisted of little more than X" is calqued as "X보다 별로 더 많지 않게 구성되어 있었다", which is close to unreadable Korean; the idiomatic rendering is "X 정도밖에 없었다". The string of 한 개의 / 한 / 하나의 also renders English articles that Korean does not use.
items.correction: 보통 이런 마을에는 술집(살롱), 호텔, 마구간, 감옥, 공동묘지 정도밖에 없었다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d172 row n="4" (ko) and d173 row n="4" (ko)
items.original: d172 #4 ko: "그들은 금을 찾기 위하여 체를 치면서 모두 재산을 일구는 꿈을 꾸었다."  /  d173 #4 ko: "현재 금을 찾아 체를 치는 사람은 별로 없고 로스앤젤리스는 더 이상 영화 도시가 아니다."
items.problem: "pan for gold" is translated as 체를 치다 (to sift with a sieve). Panning is done with a shallow pan by swirling water, not with a sieve; the Korean term is 사금을 일다 / 사금을 채취하다. The phrase is one of the round's target expressions (it is also listed in the d172 hints as "panning for gold"), so the wrong gloss is the one the learner will memorise.
items.correction: d172 #4 ko: "그들은 모두 사금을 일어 재산을 모으는 꿈을 꾸었다."  /  d173 #4 ko: "요즘은 사금을 캐는 사람이 별로 없고 로스앤젤레스는 더 이상 영화 도시가 아니다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d173 row n="4" (ko) vs row n="1" (ko)
items.original: row 4 ko: "현재 금을 찾아 체를 치는 사람은 별로 없고 로스앤젤리스는 더 이상 영화 도시가 아니다."
