items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d173 rows n="1" and n="2" (ko)
items.original: row 1 ko: "1848년에는 작은 마을에 불과했던 로스앤젤레스는 거대한 도시이자 세계 영화의 중심지가 되어 있었다. 이때는 위대한 스타들 - 케리 그랜트와 리타 헤이워스 같은"  /  row 2 ko: "남녀 배우들 - 존 웨인과 수전 헤이워드 같은 남녀 영웅들의 시대였다."
items.problem: The Korean is split across the two rows at the wrong point. English row 1 ends with "actors and actresses like Cary Grant and Rita Hayworth", but the Korean head noun for that phrase ("남녀 배우들") sits at the start of row 2's Korean. Row 1's Korean therefore ends mid-phrase with no predicate, and row 2's Korean opens with words that have no counterpart in English row 2 ("Heroes and heroines like John Wayne and Susan Hayward."). In Step 2 each row's Korean is shown alone as the "한글 번역 가이드" for that one English sentence, and in Step 5 the rows are shown as a 1:1 원문/완역 대역, so both rows mislead.
items.correction: row 1 ko: "1848년에는 작은 마을에 불과했던 로스앤젤레스는 거대한 도시이자 세계 영화의 중심지가 되어 있었다. 이때는 캐리 그랜트와 리타 헤이워스 같은 위대한 스타, 즉 명배우들의 시대였다."  /  row 2 ko: "그리고 존 웨인과 수전 헤이워드 같은 남녀 영웅들의 시대였다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d173 rows n="4", n="5", n="9"
items.original: Few people pan for gold now and Los Angeles is no longer a movie city.
items.problem: Stated in the present tense as a current fact, and it is not true. Los Angeles is still the single largest filming location in the world — FilmLA/Variety report it retained the top spot in 2024 and 2025 even while global production volume fell, and California's expanded film tax credit drew a 400%+ jump in applications. Rows 5 ("It's a factory town where time is money and television companies control the time.") and 9 ("Most films are now made indoors") carry the same dated 1980s framing as present fact.
items.correction: Rewrite in the past tense or qualify, e.g. "Few people pan for gold now, and Los Angeles is no longer only a movie city — television and streaming production share it." Row 9: "Many films are now made indoors, and the best place to find gold is in a jewelry store."

items.original: blocks[2]: "이때는 위대한 스타들 - 케리 그랜트와 리타 헤이워즈 같은"  /  blocks[4]: "수천명의 스타 지망생들이 헐리웃의 왕자나 공주가 되는 꿈을 꾸었다."
items.problem: Two proper nouns are spelled differently here from the rendered file and from standard Korean: 리타 헤이워즈 (ld_english_scripts.json has 리타 헤이워스; Rita Hayworth → 헤이워스) and 헐리웃 (ld_english_scripts.json has 할리우드; the 국립국어원 standard is 할리우드).
items.correction: blocks[2]: "…캐리 그랜트와 리타 헤이워스 같은"  /  blocks[4]: "수천 명의 스타 지망생들이 할리우드의 왕자나 공주가 되는 꿈을 꾸었다."

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d174 row n="1" (en, second sentence) and the matching ko "19세기 말 경에"
items.original: He worked on the construction of the Chesapeake and Ohio railroad toward the end of the 19th century.
items.problem: Misdates the events by roughly two decades. John Henry's steel-driving work on the C&O's Big Bend (Great Bend) Tunnel is placed in 1870–1872: construction began in February 1870 and the tunnel was completed in 1872. "Toward the end of the 19th century" / "19세기 말 경에" points at the 1880s–1890s.
items.correction: en: "He worked on the construction of the Chesapeake and Ohio railroad in the early 1870s."  /  ko: "그는 1870년대 초에 Chesapeake와 Ohio 철도의 건설 현장에서 일했다."

items.original: 호기심에 찬 사람들이 그가 거대한 바위와 단단한 땅을 통하여 차가운 스틸 드릴을 박는 것을 보기 위하여 멀리 넓은 곳으로부터 왔다.
items.problem: "from far and wide" is calqued word-for-word as 멀리 넓은 곳으로부터, which is not Korean; the idiom is 사방에서 / 방방곡곡에서. "through the huge rocks" is likewise calqued as 통하여 where 뚫고 is meant.
items.correction: 호기심에 찬 사람들이 그가 거대한 바위와 단단한 땅을 뚫고 차가운 강철 드릴을 박아 넣는 것을 보려고 사방에서 몰려왔다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d175 row n="1" (en, second sentence)
items.original: He insisted he could work harder and faster than any machine. I'll die with a hammer in my hand before I let a machine make a fool out of me, he said.
items.problem: John Henry's line is direct speech with no quotation marks, so the sentence reads as an unmarked shift into first person in the middle of third-person narration. The Korean for the same row does use quotation marks (“기계가 나를 바보로 만들게 두느니…”), confirming the English lost them.
items.correction: He insisted he could work harder and faster than any machine. "I'll die with a hammer in my hand before I let a machine make a fool out of me," he said.

items.original: 수백명의 사람이 이 굉장한 구경꺼리를 보기 위하여 Big Bend로 몰려왔다.
items.problem: 구경꺼리 is a misspelling; the standard form is 구경거리.
items.correction: 수백 명의 사람이 이 굉장한 구경거리를 보려고 Big Bend로 몰려왔다.

items.original: 그는 Rudd가 그가 행선지를 알아내기 위하여 집으로 돌아가는 동안 아이들을 돌봐주겠다고 제의했다.
items.problem: "Rudd가 그가" puts two nominative subjects in a row for the same referent, so the clause is garbled: the reader cannot tell whether 그 (the friend) or Rudd is going home. The English is unambiguous ("while Rudd went back home to find out where he was going").
items.correction: 그는 Rudd가 행선지를 알아내러 집에 다녀오는 동안 아이들을 돌봐주겠다고 제의했다.

items.original: 876 935 290 143 841 986 405 Believe it or not, there are people who can read these numbers as quickly as a flash and remember them for the rest of their lives.
items.problem: The seven-number list and the following sentence are jammed into one row with no punctuation or boundary between "405" and "Believe". In Step 2 the tokenizer keeps digits (src/lib/listeningUtils.ts:241-243 `/[a-zA-Z0-9'’\-]+/g`), so the word bank for this single item becomes roughly 30 tiles — seven three-digit numbers plus 23 words — that must be tapped in exact order. The TTS clip likewise reads "…nine hundred eighty-six four hundred five believe it or not" with no pause.
items.correction: Split into the list and the sentence, and punctuate the list: "876, 935, 290, 143, 841, 986, 405. Believe it or not, there are people who can read these numbers as quickly as a flash and remember them for the rest of their lives." Better still, put the number list in its own row so it is not part of a 30-tile graded item.

items.original: The girl studied the giant board for only a few minutes months later, she could still describe the position of all the squares perfectly.
items.problem: Two sentences have been merged with the sentence boundary lost: "…for only a few minutes" and "Months later, she could still describe…". As written the string "for only a few minutes months later" is ungrammatical and unparseable. The Korean for the same row is correctly two sentences ("…단지 몇 분 동안만 연구했다. 몇 개월 후에 그녀는…"), which confirms the English lost a period. This row is the Step 2 tap-dictation target, the Step 4 shadowing target, the Step 5 bilingual transcript line and the text fed to the Azure TTS clip, so the synthesized audio also runs "minutes months later" together with no pause.
items.correction: The girl studied the giant board for only a few minutes. Months later, she could still describe the position of all the squares perfectly.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d178 row n="10" (ko), against row n="5"

items.problem: Rows 8–10 refer to the subject as "the girl" / "그 소녀", but row 5 introduces her as "A 23-year-old American college student" / "한 23세된 미국인 대학생". 소녀 in Korean means a girl of school age, so the Korean contradicts the age given three rows earlier. (The English "the girl" for a 23-year-old woman is itself dated usage.)
items.correction: Use 그 학생 or 그 여학생 in rows 8–10 ko, and change "the girl" to "the student" in rows 8 and 10 en.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json → d178 rows n="9" and n="10" (ko)
items.original: 그들은 만개의 흑색 사각형과 백색 사각형이 무작위로 놓여진 거대한 “장기판”을 만들었다.
items.problem: "chessboard" is translated as 장기판. 장기 is Korean chess (janggi), a different game played on a 9×10 grid of intersecting lines, not on a checkered board of squares — so 장기판 contradicts the "black and white squares" in the same sentence. Row 10's Korean repeats 장기판. The correct word is 체스판.

Row 7's Korean therefore renders on the page as a floating close-quote before the sentence.

items.problem: Direct speech with no quotation marks, and the quoted sentence begins with a lower-case "please" after the comma. Whether or not quotation marks are restored, "said, please" is wrong: a sentence after a reporting comma must be capitalised. This row is the Step 2 model answer, the Step 4 shadowing target and the Step 5 transcript line, so the wrong mechanics are displayed as the correct answer.
items.correction: He crossed over to her and said, "Please don't turn away. I've fallen in love with you."

items.original: 그녀는 매우 조용하고 수줍어서 그가 자신의 길을 보는 것을 볼 때마다 돌아섰다.
items.problem: "whenever she saw him glancing her way" means 그녀 쪽을 흘끗 볼 때마다. Rendering her way as 자신의 길 (his own road/path) turns the sentence into nonsense. ld_english_scripts.json d180 row 5 has it right ("그가 자기 쪽을 흘끗 보는 것을 볼 때마다"), so this file contradicts it.

items.locator: round d205, script row #1, Korean field (key "d205", n="1")
items.original: 복숭아 파이 사건은 문자 그대로 친절로 죽이는 경우다. 그러나 상징적으로 친절로 사람잡는 것도 가능하다.
items.problem: 'figuratively' is translated as "상징적으로" (symbolically). The literal/figurative contrast is the entire point of this round — the English deliberately pairs 'literally' with 'figuratively' — and the pair returns in d213 #8 ('literally kill it with kindness'). "상징적으로" is the wrong half of the pair; the Korean term that opposes "문자 그대로" is "비유적으로".
items.correction: "복숭아 파이 사건은 문자 그대로 친절로 사람을 죽인 경우다. 그러나 비유적인 의미로 친절이 사람을 잡는 것도 가능하다."

items.locator: round d205, script row #5, English field (key "d205", n="5")
items.original: An old saying puts it this way, one man's meat is another man's poison.
items.problem: Comma splice: a full independent clause is joined to the introducing clause by a bare comma, and the quoted proverb has no quotation marks and no capital. The Korean line already punctuates it correctly with quotation marks, so the two halves of the transcript disagree. This is a model sentence learners copy out in dictation.
items.correction: An old saying puts it this way: "One man's meat is another man's poison."

items.locator: round d206, script rows #3, #5 and #6, Korean field (key "d206")
items.original: 당연히 학교 당국은 상당히 흥분해서 그 사라진 조각에 대한 수색을 시작했다. | 그 조각은 낚싯대를 잡고 있었고 밤 사이에 고기 한 마리가 미끼를 물고 잡혀 있었다. | 학교 당국은 격분했으나 몇몇 사람은 그 조각이 미소짓고 있는 것 같이 보였다고 말한다.
items.problem: 'the statue' is rendered as the bare noun "조각" in rows #3, #5 and #6. "조각" on its own means 'a piece/fragment' or sculpture as an art form; a statue of a founder is "동상" or "조각상". Row #2 shows the translator knew this — it writes "조각(동상)" — but the gloss is then dropped, so "그 조각이 미소짓고 있는 것 같이 보였다" reads oddly.
items.correction: Use "동상" consistently from row #2 onward: "그 사라진 동상에 대한 수색", "그 동상은 낚싯대를 잡고 있었고", "그 동상이 미소짓고 있는 것처럼 보였다".

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d206-1.json, blocks[2] (instruction), corresponding to script row #1
items.original: 미국 학생들은 실질적인 농답(짖궂은 장난)을 하는 것으로 악명이 높다.
items.problem: Three errors in one line. "실질적인 농답" is a word-for-word mis-gloss of 'practical joke' (실질적인 = actual/substantial, which is not what 'practical' means here); "농답" is a typo for "농담"; "짖궂은" is a misspelling of "짓궂은". ld_english_scripts.json d205 #1 already has the correct "짓궂은 장난". NOTE: LdLearningView only falls back to these -1 blocks when ld_english_scripts.json has no rows, which never happens here, so this text is not currently rendered — it is stale data that would resurface if the fallback ever fires or if the file is reused.
items.correction: "미국 학생들은 짓궂은 장난을 하는 것으로 악명이 높다." (i.e. match the scripts file)

items.locator: round d207, script row #3, Korean field (key "d207", n="3")

items.problem: The English hedge 'about' ('spends about 15 hours a week') is dropped, so the Korean asserts exactly 15 hours. In the English-production step the learner reconstructing from this prompt will write '15 hours' and not match the model sentence.
items.correction: "일반적인 대학생은 일주일에 약 15시간을 교실에서 보낸다."

items.locator: round d207, script row #6, Korean field (key "d207", n="6")

items.correction: "… 유명한 배우로 오늘날 알려진 일부 사람들은 …"

items.locator: round d207, script row #7, Korean field (key "d207", n="7")
items.original: 몇 가지 면에서 이 과외 활동들은 마음을 훈련시키는 것을 위하여 정규 수업만큼 똑같이 중요하다.
items.problem: 'training young minds' loses 'young' entirely, and 'minds' becomes "마음", which in Korean is the heart/feelings sense rather than the intellect. "~것을 위하여" is also clumsy Korean for a purpose clause.
items.correction: "몇 가지 면에서 이 과외 활동들은 젊은이들의 지성을 훈련시키는 데 있어서 정규 수업만큼 중요하다."

items.original: 다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서 영어로 받아쓰기를 하세요.
items.problem: The instruction tells the learner to refer to the proper nouns, numbers and difficult words that follow, but neither d207.json nor d212.json contains a `hints` block — there is nothing to refer to. (23 of the 276 main lessons are in this state repo-wide; d207 and d212 are the two in this scope.) d212 in particular would benefit from hints: its script contains 'amputated', 'at their own risk' and 'strangely enough'.
items.correction: Either add a hints block (d207: "extracurricular debating dramatic production journalists 15 hours"; d212: "pet gentle at their own risk amputated strangely enough") or drop the clause "다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서" from the instruction on these two lessons.

items.locator: round d208, script row #5, Korean field (key "d208", n="5")
items.original: 체육관에서 한 시간 동안 운동한 후에 학생들은 유쾌한 마음으로 공부할 열의를 갖고 그의 책으로 돌아갈 수 있다.
items.problem: Number mismatch inside one sentence: the subject is plural "학생들은" but the possessive is singular "그의". The English is singular throughout ('the student can return to his books'), and 'his books' is plural while the Korean says "그의 책". 'refreshed' as "유쾌한 마음으로" (in a cheerful mood) is also off — it means physically and mentally refreshed.
items.correction: "체육관에서 한 시간 동안 운동한 후에 학생은 상쾌한 기분으로, 공부할 열의를 가지고 자기 책으로 돌아갈 수 있다."

items.original: If accepted, he will be put through an initiation ceremony during which the old members will test his good nature with various pranks and jokes.
items.problem: Written in the present/future tense as a description of how US fraternities work today. Hazing — subjecting a new member to pranks, ordeals or humiliation as a condition of membership — is prohibited by anti-hazing statutes in 44 states and the District of Columbia, is a felony in 13 of them, and since December 2024 is covered by the federal Stop Campus Hazing Act. National fraternities ban it outright. Presenting initiation pranks as a benign, current tradition is out of date and misinforms Korean learners about US campus life.
items.correction: Move it into the past and mark it as no longer allowed, e.g. "In the past, new members were often put through an initiation ceremony full of pranks and jokes, but such hazing is now illegal in most states and banned by the fraternities themselves." (Korean: "과거에는 신입 회원이 장난과 농담으로 가득한 신고식을 치르는 경우가 많았지만, 이런 '헤이징'은 현재 대부분의 주에서 불법이며 각 클럽 자체도 금지하고 있다.")

items.locator: round d209, script row #5 (key "d209", n="5"), English and Korean
items.original: Traditionally, fraternities and sororities are designated by names consisting of several Greek letters. | 전통적으로 fraternities와 sororities는 몇몇 희랍어 글자로 구성되는 이름이 지정된다.
items.problem: Two small errors. (1) Fraternity and sorority names consist of two or three Greek letters (Sigma Chi, Alpha Phi Alpha); 'several' normally implies more than that. (2) The Korean uses "희랍어", an archaic word for Greece that modern Korean textbooks have replaced with "그리스", and "희랍어 글자" says 'letters of the Greek language' where the term is simply "그리스 문자" (Greek letters/alphabet).
items.correction: English: "Traditionally, fraternities and sororities are named with two or three Greek letters." Korean: "전통적으로 fraternity와 sorority는 두세 개의 그리스 문자로 이루어진 이름을 갖는다."

items.original: 받아들여지면 그는 신고식을 통하여 놓여(부쳐)지는데 그 동안에 기존 회원들이
items.problem: "신고식을 통하여 놓여(부쳐)지는데" is a word-by-word rendering of 'be put through' that produces meaningless Korean, with a parenthetical alternative left in as if it were an unfinished draft. ld_english_scripts.json d209 #4 has the correct "신고식을 치르게 되는데". Same rendering caveat as the d206-1 finding: this block is not currently displayed.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d210.json blocks[2]+[3]; d214.json blocks[2]+[3]; d215.json blocks[2]+[3]
items.original: {"type":"hints","text":"practice hang scalps conquered foes belt wore waists. wearers immune physical danger. good"} followed by {"type":"instruction","text":"fortune. white buffalo worship sacred. superstition took the place"}
items.problem: The hints list is cut in half: the first part is stored as a `hints` block and the remainder as a second `instruction` block. In d215 the cut falls inside a phrase — the hints block ends with the dangling word "good" and the instruction block begins "fortune.", i.e. 'good fortune' is split across two block types. d210 and d214 have the same split. LdLearningView reads only the first `hints` block (LdLearningView.tsx:59), so the second half would be lost if hints were ever displayed; and any code that treats `instruction` blocks as Korean prompt text (the koSentences fallback at LdLearningView.tsx:70-89) would pick up English hint words as if they were Korean script lines. 104 of the 276 main lesson files are affected repo-wide; 3 of them are in this scope.
items.correction: Merge the trailing instruction text back into the preceding `hints` block so each lesson has exactly one hints block: d215 → "practice hang scalps conquered foes belt wore waists. wearers immune physical danger. good fortune. white buffalo worship sacred. superstition took the place". Same for d210 and d214.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d210-1.json, blocks[2] (instruction), corresponding to script row #1
items.original: 기록된 역사를 통털어 우리는 가장 흥미있는 형태의 수집 중의
items.problem: "통털어" is a misspelling; the standard form is "통틀어". ld_english_scripts.json d210 #1 spells it correctly, so the two copies of the same sentence disagree. Not currently rendered (same fallback caveat).
items.correction: "기록된 역사를 통틀어 우리는 가장 흥미있는 형태의 수집 중의"

items.original: Dr. Raymond L. Ditmars, for example, working in his laboratories at the New York Bronx Zoo, discovered a way to use snake poison to cure certain types of nervous diseases.
items.problem: Two errors in one sentence. (1) No source credits Ditmars with discovering a snake-venom treatment for nervous diseases; his venom work was antivenom against snakebite. Snake venom has never been a 'cure' for nervous diseases — the historical use (from the 1930s, by David I. Macht and others, not Ditmars) was cobra venom as a pain reliever for conditions such as trigeminal neuralgia. 'Cure certain types of nervous diseases' overstates even that. (2) 'the New York Bronx Zoo' is not the institution's name: it was the New York Zoological Park, universally known as the Bronx Zoo.
items.correction: Rewrite, e.g. "Dr. Raymond L. Ditmars, for example, working in his laboratories at the Bronx Zoo in New York, helped develop the antivenom that is used to treat snakebite." (Korean: "예를 들어 뉴욕 브롱크스 동물원의 실험실에서 일하던 Dr. Raymond L. Ditmars는 뱀에 물린 상처를 치료하는 항독소(혈청)를 개발하는 데 기여했다.")

items.locator: round d211, script row #4, Korean field (key "d211", n="4")
items.original: 예를 들어 뉴욕 Bronx 동물원의 그의 실험실에서 일하는 Dr.Raymond L Ditmar는 어떤 유형의 신경병을 고치기 위하여 뱀의 독을 사용하는 한 가지 방법을 발견했다.
items.problem: The proper noun does not match the English line, which reads 'Dr. Raymond L. Ditmars'. The Korean drops the final s of the surname ('Ditmar'), drops the period after 'L', and closes up 'Dr.Raymond'. The correct spelling is Ditmars. Proper nouns are exactly what this course's hints block exists to support, and the two spellings sit side by side in the 1:1 transcript that the learner checks their dictation against.
items.correction: "… Dr. Raymond L. Ditmars는 …" (and 'Bronx 동물원' → '브롱크스 동물원', per the same fix as the English line).

items.locator: round d213, script row #4, Korean field (key "d213", n="4")
items.original: 그들은 정반대의 표지가 분명히 붙어있는데도 동물에게 먹을 것을 주는 것을 고집한다.
items.problem: 'signs to the contrary' means signs saying the opposite of what the visitors are doing — i.e. DO NOT FEED THE ANIMALS signs. The word-for-word rendering "정반대의 표지" ('signs of the exact opposite') gives no clue what the sign says, so the Korean sentence is unintelligible on its own and the point of the whole round (people feed animals despite the prohibition) is lost. This row is shown in the 1:1 transcript and is the prompt in the English-production step.
items.correction: "그들은 먹이를 주지 말라는 표지가 눈에 잘 띄게 붙어 있는데도 동물에게 먹이 주는 것을 고집한다."

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d213-1.json, blocks[3] (instruction), corresponding to script row #2
items.original: 동물원을 방문하러 가는 사람들은 그들 자신의 권리로 매혹적이다.
items.problem: 'in their own right' is translated literally as "그들 자신의 권리로" ('by their own legal right'), which is not what the idiom means. ld_english_scripts.json d213 #2 has the correct "그들 나름대로". Not currently rendered (same fallback caveat as above).
items.correction: "동물원을 방문하러 가는 사람들은 그들 나름대로 흥미롭다." (match the scripts file)

items.locator: round d214, script row #3, Korean field (key "d214", n="3")
items.original: 예를 들어 천둥 소리는 여러 하늘의 무서운 신들 사이의 전투와 전쟁의 으르렁대는 소리라고 생각되었다.
items.problem: 'in the heavens' is rendered as "여러 하늘의" ('of several heavens'), a word-for-word carry-over of the English plural. Korean 하늘 has no such plural and the phrase reads as nonsense; the meaning is simply 'gods in the sky/heaven'.
items.correction: "예를 들어 천둥 소리는 하늘에 있는 무서운 신들 사이의 전투와 전쟁의 으르렁거리는 소리라고 여겨졌다."

items.locator: round d214, script row #5, Korean field (key "d214", n="5")
items.original: 무지함 속에서 원시인은 변덕스런 신들이 땅의 거주자들에게 화풀이하기 위하여 폭풍, 지진, 태풍같은 천연재해를 사용한다고 생각했다.
items.problem: 'hurricanes' is translated as "태풍", which is 'typhoon' — a different named storm system (Atlantic/eastern Pacific vs. western Pacific). Korean has the loanword "허리케인". A learner producing English from this prompt will write 'typhoons' and not match the model sentence. 'storms, earthquakes, and hurricanes' also loses the serial comma spacing in "태풍같은" (should be "태풍 같은").
items.correction: "… 폭풍, 지진, 허리케인 같은 자연재해를 사용한다고 생각했다."

items.locator: round d215, script row #3, Korean field (key "d215", n="3")
items.original: 예를 들어 많은 아메리카 인디언들은 그들의 정복된 적의 머리가죽을 그들의 허리 주위에 걸치는 허리끈에 매다는 관습을 만들었다.
items.problem: 'made a practice of ~ing' means 'habitually did', not 'created a custom'. "관습을 만들었다" says they invented the custom, which is a different claim. (Note: the English sentence itself is flagged separately as a stereotype — if it is rewritten this row disappears, but if any part is kept the Korean idiom must be fixed.)
items.correction: If the sentence survives the rewrite above: "… 매다는 것을 관례로 삼았다."

items.original: Some animals, such as the white buffalo, were even worshipped because they were thought to be sacred.
items.problem: 'Worshipped' mischaracterises the belief. In Lakota tradition the white buffalo is holy because of White Buffalo Calf Woman, who brought the sacred pipe (čhaŋnúŋpa) and the Seven Sacred Rites; the animal is revered and treated as sacred, not worshipped as a god. The past tense also implies the belief is extinct — it is a living tradition. The Korean "심지어 숭배받기까지 했다" carries the same error.
items.correction: "Some animals, such as the white buffalo, are still held sacred today." (Korean: "흰 들소 같은 일부 동물들은 오늘날까지도 신성하게 여겨진다.")

items.original: It is probably true to say that in ancient civilizations superstition took the place of religion.
items.problem: A contested value judgement presented as 'probably true', and it contradicts the passage itself: rows #1 and d214 #6 describe priests, intercession and prayer, and row #6 describes sacred animals — that is religion, not a substitute for it. The claim reduces the religions of ancient and Indigenous peoples to superstition, which is exactly the framing the rest of the finding set flags.
items.correction: Replace with a neutral, defensible closing line, e.g. "In ancient civilizations, charms and religious ritual often existed side by side." (Korean: "고대 문명에서는 부적과 종교 의식이 나란히 존재하는 경우가 많았다.")

items.locator: round d215, script rows #3 and #4 (key "d215", n="3" and n="4")
items.original: Many of the American Indians, for example, made a practice of hanging the scalps of their conquered foes on a belt which they wore around their waists. | These scalps were considered to be good luck charms which made their wearers immune to physical danger.
items.problem: Two problems. (1) Over-generalisation: scalping was practised by SOME Indigenous societies, not by 'many of the American Indians' as a shared custom, and European colonists both practised it and paid scalp bounties — the 'scalping is an Indian thing' framing is a documented stereotype. (2) The stated motive is unsupported: where scalps were taken they functioned as war trophies and proof of a warrior's prowess, and in the Southeast were tied to earning warrior status and placating the spirits of the dead. No source supports 'good luck charms which made their wearers immune to physical danger'. The whole d214–d215 sequence frames these peoples as 'primitive man' whose beliefs are 'superstitions', which compounds the problem.
items.correction: Remove the scalping example. If an example of a protective charm is needed, use one that is documented and non-stereotyping (e.g. amulets in ancient Egypt or Rome), and drop 'primitive man' in favour of 'early peoples' / '초기 인류'. If the owner wants to keep a Native American example at all, it needs a cited source and accurate wording — expert review required for how to present it.

items.locator: round d216, script row #4, Korean field (key "d216", n="4")
items.original: 미국에서는 몇몇 미신적인 사람들은 임박한 죽음이 열린 창문을 통하여 집으로 날아들어오는 야생의 새에 의하여 상징된다고 믿는다.
items.problem: 'is signified by' is translated as "상징된다" (is symbolised by). In a superstition, the bird is an omen — it foretells the death, it does not symbolise it. Double topic marking ("미국에서는 … 사람들은") also makes the sentence clumsy.
items.correction: "미국에서는 열린 창문으로 집 안에 날아든 야생의 새가 임박한 죽음을 알리는 징조라고 믿는 미신적인 사람들도 있다."

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d216-1.json, last instruction block, corresponding to script row #7
items.original: 그들은 단지 그런 것들을 늙은 아낙네의 이야기들의 흥미있는 예로 단지 여긴다.
items.problem: The adverb "단지" appears twice in one sentence ('merely … merely'), which is a clear duplication error. "늙은 아낙네의 이야기들" is also a literal and mildly derogatory rendering of 'old wives' tales'; ld_english_scripts.json d216 #7 has the better "옛날부터 전해 오는 미신". Not currently rendered (same fallback caveat).
items.correction: "그들은 그런 것들을 옛날부터 전해 오는 미신의 흥미로운 예로 여길 뿐이다." (match the scripts file)

items.original: They spend their days fishing, hiking, or just resting, and their evening sitting around the campfire telling stories of the adventures and delights of trailer life.
items.problem: 'their evening' is not parallel with 'their days' in a habitual statement. It should be 'their evenings'. The old STT transcript likely lost the plural because the s-sound runs into 'sitting' ("evenings sitting"). The synthesized voice now reads the wrong singular, and the dictation answer requires it.
items.correction: '...and their evenings sitting around the campfire telling stories of the adventures and delights of trailer life.' Regenerate the clip. The Korean ('밤은 ...') can stay, or become '저녁은'.

items.original: 많은 면에서 그들은 유럽의 집시와 비슷하다.
items.problem: The -1 page Korean still has the pre-fix line that uses '집시' (Gypsy, generally considered a slur by Roma). The scripts file (the rendered source) was corrected to '현대의 유목민과 비슷하다' / 'like modern nomads' (L-89). It is not rendered today (LdLearningView renders ld_english_scripts.json), but the stale data carries the removed ethnic term.
items.correction: Change the block to '많은 면에서 그들은 현대의 유목민과 비슷하다.', or rebuild all -1 Korean blocks from ld_english_scripts.json ko.

items.original: Some of the trees were standing before the birth of Christ, and some are so wide that automobiles can be driven through tunnels cut into their trunks.
items.problem: The sentence says in the present tense that some of 'these' giant sequoias have car tunnels through their trunks. The standing drive-through giant sequoias are gone: the Wawona Tree fell in 1968-69 and the Pioneer Cabin Tree in 2017. The only standing giant-sequoia tunnel tree (California Tunnel Tree) is walk-through only. Cars can still drive only through the Tunnel Log, which is a fallen tree. The drive-through trees still standing are coast redwoods, a different species.
items.correction: '...and a tunnel cut through one fallen giant is wide enough for cars to drive through.' KO '...쓰러진 거대한 나무 하나에는 자동차가 지나갈 수 있을 만큼 넓은 터널이 뚫려 있다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.original: 요세미티는 미국에서 가장 높은 것인 그것의 숨을 죽이게 하는 폭포들의 하나를 따서 이름지어져있다. / 요세미티의 멀지 않은 남쪽에 세콰이에 국립공원이 있는데 ... / 세콰이어 나무는 오늘날 세상에서 가장 크고 가장 오랜 살아있는 물건이다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the pre-fix Korean with two false claims fixed in L-87: Yosemite named after a waterfall, and the sequoia as the oldest living thing. It also has the misspellings '세콰이에/세콰이어' (standard '세쿼이아'). The rendered scripts file is correct.
items.correction: Rebuild the -1 Korean from ld_english_scripts.json d230 ko.

items.locator: d230.json, d238.json, d240.json blocks[1] (instruction), no hints block
items.original: 다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서 영어로 받아쓰기를 하세요.
items.problem: The instruction tells learners to refer to the proper nouns, numbers and hard words 'below', but these three main lessons have no hints block. Neither block is rendered by LdLearningView today (map A-18). If the hints are restored, these three would show a pointer to nothing. Useful hint words exist: d230 Yosemite, Sequoia National Park, General Sherman Tree; d238 novice, groundless, sickening; d240 golf course, neglect.
items.correction: Add hints blocks (for example d230 'Yosemite breathtaking Sequoia National Park giant sequoia General Sherman Tree'), or drop the instruction for these three.

items.original: Millions of years ago, this area was a dense forest, but the fallen trees were buried under mud and volcanic ash. / KO: 수백만 년 전에 이 지역은 울창한 숲이었지만 쓰러진 나무들이 진흙과 화산재에 묻혔다.
items.problem: This row was rewritten in the last audit. The wood is over 200 million years old. The Korean '수백만 년 전' (a few million years) understates the age by about 100 times. NPS also says the logs were washed into an ancient river system and buried there. And 'but' links two clauses that do not contrast.
items.correction: EN: 'More than 200 million years ago, trees here fell and were washed into rivers, where they were buried under mud and volcanic ash.' KO: '2억여 년 전, 이곳의 쓰러진 나무들이 강물에 떠내려가 진흙과 화산재 속에 묻혔다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.original: As they point out, it is better to be safe than sorry. / KO: 그들이 지적하듯이 섭섭해하는 것보다 안전한 것이 더 낫다.
items.problem: In the proverb 'better (to be) safe than sorry', 'sorry' means regretting it later after something bad happens. It does not mean 'feeling hurt or disappointed' (섭섭해하다). The Korean gets the meaning of a very common idiom wrong.
items.correction: KO: '그들이 지적하듯이, 나중에 후회하는 것보다 미리 조심하는 편이 낫다.' (English unchanged, so no clip change.)

items.original: 수천년전에 이 지역은 울창한 숲이었으나 격렬한 지진이 그것을 큰 바다로 바꾸었다. / 그것의 많은 순한 곰도 관광객에게 즐거운 것으로 판명된다. / 그 곰들은 관광객과 점심을 같이하는 것을 주저하지 않는다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the pre-fix Korean: the false geology (thousands of years, an earthquake turning the area into a sea) and the unsafe 'tame bears happily share picnickers' lunch'. It also has the old spelling '아리조나'. The rendered scripts file has the corrected text.
items.correction: Rebuild the -1 Korean from ld_english_scripts.json d231 ko.

items.original: 가장의 것에 탐닉하고자 하는 인간의 욕구는 다양한 형태로 표현을 발견하지만 연극이 이런 욕구에 대한 최고의 출구의 하나이다.
items.problem: 'make-believe' is rendered as '가장의 것'. In Korean '가장' is easily read as 'most', 'head of household' or 'pretense', so the phrase is unclear. The rest of the sentence is a stiff word-for-word calque.
items.correction: '꾸며 낸 세계에 빠져들고 싶은 인간의 욕구는 여러 방식으로 표현되지만, 연극은 이 욕구를 풀어 주는 가장 좋은 통로 중 하나이다.'

items.original: Every country of the world has some form of dramatics. / KO: 세계의 모든 나라는 어떤 형태의 연출법을 갖고 있다.
items.problem: 'dramatics' here means drama and theatrical performance as an activity. It does not mean '연출법' (directing technique). The Korean changes the claim and teaches a wrong meaning for the key word.
items.correction: KO: '세계의 모든 나라에는 어떤 형태로든 연극이 있다.'

items.original: They dealt with such topics as death, judgment, heaven, hell, virtue, and vice. / KO: 그들은 죽음, 재판, 천국, 지옥, 덕, 악 같은 주제를 다루었다.
items.problem: Next to death, heaven and hell, 'judgment' means the divine Last Judgment (심판), not a court trial (재판).
items.correction: KO: '그 연극들은 죽음, 심판, 천국, 지옥, 미덕, 악덕 같은 주제를 다루었다.'

items.original: These abstractions were presented as living characters in the plays in order to give the spectators a graphic lesson in morality. / The mystery and morality plays were usually presented on the front steps of large churches and cathedrals, but in order to accommodate the large crowds, they gradually moved to the town marketplace. / This was the beginning of the modern theater.
items.problem: The passage treats mystery plays and morality plays as one genre. Personified abstractions (Death, Virtue, Vice) are the defining feature of morality plays such as Everyman. Mystery plays dramatized Bible stories from Creation to Doomsday. The move from the church steps to the marketplace describes liturgical and mystery drama, not the later morality plays, which were performed by touring troupes. 'This was the beginning of the modern theater' overstates it: medieval drama is one root of later theater, not its beginning.
items.correction: #4 'In the morality plays, these abstractions were presented as living characters...'; #6 'The mystery plays, which acted out stories from the Bible, were at first presented on the front steps of churches and cathedrals, but ... they gradually moved to the town marketplace.'; #7 'This helped lay the foundations of the modern theater.' Update the Korean and clips to match.

items.locator: d234 row n=2 (en + ko); hints block '75'
items.original: Traditionally, the minstrel show is associated with the colorful showboats that traveled up and down the inland waterways of the United States about 75 years ago. / KO: 전통적으로 minstrel show는 약 75년 전에 미국의 내부수로를 오르내리던 다채로운 showboat와 관련있다.
items.problem: 'About 75 years ago' was relative to when the textbook was written. Read in 2026, it means about 1951. The showboat era ran from 1831 to the 1940s and peaked in the early 1900s. Minstrel shows were most popular from the 1840s to the 1890s. As written, the sentence teaches a date that is off by 50 to 100 years, and the number '75' is also a hint and part of the dictation answer. Separately, the Korean '내부수로' is not a standard term for 'inland waterways'. This is separate from L-84 (the minstrel-show content, which the owner is deciding). It matters only if the round is kept.
items.correction: If the owner keeps the round (L-84): EN '...that traveled up and down the inland waterways of the United States more than a hundred years ago.' (or 'in the late 1800s and early 1900s'). KO '...100여 년 전 미국의 내륙 수로를 오르내리던...'. Update the hint '75' and regenerate the clip.

items.original: Their gay music and carefree jokes filled the air with holiday mood.
items.problem: (1) 'with holiday mood' lacks an article: it should be 'with a holiday mood'. (2) 'gay' in its old sense 'cheerful' is taught with no note, and it is also a hint word. In current English 'gay' almost always means homosexual, so a learner who reuses it will be misunderstood. This is separate from the L-84 decision on the round. It matters only if the round is kept.
items.correction: If the round is kept: 'Their cheerful music and carefree jokes filled the air with a holiday mood.' Update the hint and regenerate the clip.

items.original: 쇼보트가 다른 마을로 떠난 오랜 후에도 그 벤조의 소리는 / 큰 제트 엔진이 우르렁거리기 시작하고 비행기가 활주로로 미끄러져 내려가기 시작하면
items.problem: These -1 pages differ from the scripts file only in spelling: '벤조' vs '밴조', and '우르렁' vs '우르릉'. The corrected spellings (L-91) were applied only to ld_english_scripts.json.
items.correction: '밴조', '우르릉'. Better: rebuild all -1 Korean from the scripts file.

items.original: The early settlers made the trip by covered wagon and frequently spent a year or more struggling through the wilderness in an attempt to reach their destination. / KO: 초기 정착민들은 포장마차로 여행을 했고 그들의 목적지에 도착하려는 시도로써 광야를 통하여 고투하면서 일년 혹은 그 이상을 종종 보냈다.
items.problem: Overland covered-wagon emigrants usually took 4 to 6 months, not 'a year or more'. The next round (d236 #2, already corrected) says 'the same journey took many months', so the two rounds now contradict each other. Row #3 also puts these wagon trips in 'the early days of the settlement of America'. The wagon migrations were in the 1840s to 1860s, about two centuries after settlement began.
items.correction: EN: 'The pioneers made the trip by covered wagon and often spent four to six months struggling through the wilderness in an attempt to reach their destination.' KO: '개척민들은 포장마차로 여행했고, 목적지에 닿기 위해 넉 달에서 여섯 달 동안 황야를 헤치며 고생하는 일이 많았다.' Regenerate the clip, because the English changes. Optionally change #3 'In the early days of the settlement of America' to 'In the days of the westward migration'.

items.original: If one of the pioneers could see the ease and comfort with which the modern Americans travel, he would be truly astonished. / KO: ...정말 탄복할 것이다.
items.problem: For a general group the idiomatic form is 'modern Americans' (no article). 'the modern Americans' sounds like a specific group. The Korean '탄복하다' means 'admire deeply', not 'be astonished'.
items.correction: EN '...with which modern Americans travel, he would be truly astonished.' KO '...정말 깜짝 놀랄 것이다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.original: Delicious meals are served in fashionable dining cars and some of the more modern trains have television and telephone service.
items.problem: This round opens with 'Today' (#1, already modernized to 'about 6 hours'), but #5 still gives television and telephone service as the modern train amenity. That was true in the 1960s. Current US trains list Wi-Fi and power outlets, not TV or phone service. #6 ('Thus a businessman can conduct his affairs...') depends on this sentence.
items.correction: '...and many modern trains offer Wi-Fi and power outlets at every seat.' KO '...많은 현대 열차는 좌석마다 와이파이와 전원 콘센트를 제공한다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.original: 오늘날 뉴욕으로부터 샌프랜시스코로의 삼천 마일의 여행은 비행기로 열 시간 내에 될 수 있다. / 가까운 장래에, 제트비행기가 이 여행을 심지어 더 짧게 만들 것이다. / 몇몇은 텔레비젼과 전화 서비스가 있다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the pre-fix Korean ('10 hours', the future-jets sentence that was replaced by 'In pioneer days, the same journey took many months') and the old spellings '샌프랜시스코' and '텔레비젼'. Its row #2 has entirely different content from the rendered script.
items.correction: Rebuild the -1 Korean from ld_english_scripts.json d236 ko.

items.original: ...ask the stewardess to stop the plane and let him out...
items.problem: 'stewardess' is a dated, gendered job title. Current English uses 'flight attendant'. It is also a hint word, so learners are pointed to the old term.
items.correction: '...ask the flight attendant to stop the plane and let him out...' Update the hint to 'flight attendant' and regenerate the clip. The Korean '스튜어디스' can become '승무원'.

items.original: 큰 제트 엔진이 우르릉거리기 시작하고 비행기가 활주로로 미끄러져 내려가기 시작하면 ... 그러나 이것이 어리석은 두려움이라는 것을 알며 스토아 학파의 강인함으로 앞에 놓여있는 시련에 대하여 각오한다.
items.problem: (1) 'the great engines' has no 'jet' in it; '제트' is added. (2) 'taxi down the field' means rolling slowly on the ground toward the runway. It is not '미끄러져 내려가다' (sliding down). (3) lowercase 'stoic fortitude' means calm endurance, not 'the strength of the Stoic school' (스토아 학파).
items.correction: '거대한 엔진이 굉음을 내기 시작하고 비행기가 활주로 쪽으로 천천히 움직이기 시작하면 ... 그러나 그는 이것이 어리석은 두려움임을 알고, 의연하게 마음을 다잡고 앞으로 닥칠 시련에 대비한다.'

items.original: 그가 기다려오고 있는 그 병드는 느낌은 결코 오지 않는다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the mistranslation '병드는 느낌' for 'sickening sensation'. The scripts file was corrected to '메스꺼운 느낌' (L-90).

items.original: 모든 사람이 좋은 싸움을 즐기는데 특히 그것이 진짜가 아니라면 그렇다. / 스포츠는 정말로 일종의 싸움이지만 그들은 좋은 성격의 싸움이다.
items.problem: 'good-natured fights' means friendly fights with no ill will. '좋은 성격의 싸움' (fights with a good personality) is a calque that does not carry that meaning. 'a good fight' means a fight worth watching, not a morally 'good' fight.
items.correction: #1 '누구나 볼 만한 싸움을 즐긴다. 특히 그것이 진짜 싸움이 아니라면 더욱 그렇다.' #2 '스포츠는 사실 일종의 싸움이지만, 악의 없는 우호적인 싸움이다.'

items.original: 그런 사람들은 불쌍한 패배자라고 불린다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the mistranslation of 'poor losers' as '불쌍한 패배자' (pitiable losers). The scripts file was corrected to '패배를 못 견디는 사람' (L-90).

items.original: 일부 여성들은 비록 결혼했지만 과부처럼 느낀다고 말한다. / 그들의 남편들이 너무나 많은 시간을 골프장에서 보내서 / 그들의 아내들이 단지 이따금씩만 보는 것같다. / 남자의 첫 의무는 그의 가정과 가족에 대해서이다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the gender-stereotyped pre-fix Korean (golf widows, 'a man's first duty'). The English and scripts-file Korean were made gender-neutral in L-89.
items.correction: Rebuild the -1 Korean from ld_english_scripts.json d240 ko.

items.original: Evidently, he believed in the motto of the ancient Greeks, Know thyself.
items.problem: The quoted maxim has no quotation marks, which leaves a capitalized 'Know' mid-sentence. The Korean row quotes it (“너 자신을 알아라”). As the model answer for dictation, the English shows non-standard punctuation.
items.correction: Evidently, he believed in the motto of the ancient Greeks, "Know thyself." (Check whether the clip key changes. If it does, regenerate the clip.)

items.original: 그는 아마 자신의 두 가지 간단한 질문에 대답할 수 있는 사람들은 그를 그의 직원에 대한 소중한 추가적인 인물로 만들어줄 자기 개선을 위한 인격과 열의를 갖고 있다는 추측을 했다.
items.problem: The Korean is hard to follow and partly wrong. '그를 그의 직원에 대한 소중한 추가적인 인물로' is a word-for-word rendering of 'a valuable addition to his staff' and does not make clear that the applicant would become a valuable member of the manager's staff. 'integrity' (정직성/성실성) becomes 인격 (personality/character). 'the person' becomes plural 사람들은 but is then referred to as 그를. 'went on the assumption' (acted on the premise) becomes 추측을 했다 (made a guess).
items.correction: 그는 아마 자신의 간단한 두 질문에 대답할 수 있는 사람이라면 정직성과 자기 계발 의지를 갖추고 있어 자기 직원으로서 귀중한 인재가 될 것이라는 전제하에 판단했을 것이다.

items.original: d253: "assumption possess integrity desire self-improvement valuable addition staff." / d259: "over the frozen surface pond glide swiftly down slope snow-covered mountain." / d262: "course."
items.problem: In two lessons a hint word is not spelled the way it appears in the script: the script has 'possessed' (d253 #6) and 'gliding' (d259 #5), but the hints give 'possess' and 'glide'. In d262 the whole hints block is the bare fragment 'course.' (from 'as a matter of course'), which is useless as a hint. None of these hints are rendered today.
items.correction: d253: use 'possessed'. d259: use 'gliding'. d262: use 'as a matter of course' (or add real hints such as 'drastic', 'recreation', 'brought up').

items.original: 면접 동안 질문에 정확하고 솔직하게 대답할 준비가 되어야 한다.
items.problem: The -1 page has 정확하고 (accurately), while the scripts file has 정직하고 (honestly), which is correct for 'honestly'. This is a real meaning difference. Per maps/listening.md §1.2 the -1 JSON blocks are not rendered, so this is data inconsistency, not a visible error.
items.correction: 면접 동안 질문에 정직하고 솔직하게 대답할 준비가 되어 있어야 한다.

items.locator: d253 row n=3 (ko); d262 row n=4 (ko)
items.original: 대부분의 지원자들은 이 질문에 대답할 수 없었다 . / 일부 사람들은 심지어 가장 추운 겨울 오후도 아이스 스케이팅이나 스키를 타면서 보낸다 .
items.problem: There is a stray space before the final period in the rendered Korean text.

items.original: 잘 발달된 개성의 분명한 징표 중의 하나는 농담을 받아들이는 능력이다. / 만약 그가 조용하고 심각하다면 자신의 분위기를 그의 분위기에 맞추는 것이 최상이다.
items.problem: #5 drops the superlative 'surest' (가장 확실한) and renders 'well-developed personality' as 개성 (individuality) rather than maturity of character. 'take a joke' means taking teasing in good humour, which 받아들이는 only loosely conveys. #2: 심각하다 describes a grave situation, and a person who is 'serious' in manner is 진지하다.
items.correction: #5 '원만한 인격을 가장 확실하게 보여 주는 징표 중 하나는 농담을 웃어넘길 줄 아는 능력이다.' #2 '만약 그가 조용하고 진지하다면 그 분위기에 자신을 맞추는 것이 가장 좋다.'

items.locator: d254.json blocks[3]; d255.json blocks[3]; d260.json blocks[3] (instruction blocks that follow the hints block)
items.original: d254 blocks[3] instruction: "all things, go to extremes. prerogatives." / d255 blocks[3]: "tribes Africa" / d260 blocks[3]: "figures sledding children. take a few sled rides on the sly."
items.problem: In three lessons the hint list is cut in two: its second half sits in an 'instruction' block instead of the 'hints' block. For example, the d254 hints end with 'as in', and 'all things, go to extremes. prerogatives.' follows as an instruction. Any consumer of hints (the disabled quiz, a future hint display) sees a truncated hint list, and any instruction renderer shows English fragments as instructions. Neither block is rendered by LdLearningView today (maps/listening.md §1.2, A-18).
items.correction: Merge each spilled instruction text into the preceding hints block, for example d254 hints = 'surest signs well-developed personality take a joke. on the part of the applicant out of place. as in all things, go to extremes. prerogatives.', and delete the stray instruction block. Do the same for d255 and d260.

items.original: 한 직장에 지원하는데 있어서 면접관이의 성격을 고려하여 자신을 그에게 맞추는 것이 현명하다. / 고용주로써 면접관이 어떤 특권들을 갖고 있다는 것을 명심해야 한다.
items.problem: There are two Korean errors on the -1 page, and the scripts file is correct in both places: 면접관이의 is a typo for 면접관의, and 고용주로써 (instrument) is wrong where 고용주로서 (capacity) is meant. The -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: …면접관의 성격을… / 고용주로서 면접관이…

items.original: 이 때문에 의사의 직업은 보통 제사장 계급을 위하여 보존되었다.
items.problem: 'was reserved to the priest caste' means the profession was restricted to, or held exclusively by, the priest caste. 보존되었다 means 'was preserved/conserved', which is a different meaning. '을 위하여' (for the sake of) also misreads 'reserved to'.
items.correction: 이 때문에 의사라는 직업은 대개 사제(제사장) 계급만이 맡았다. (or: …사제 계급에게 한정되어 있었다.)

items.problem: 때가지 is a typo for 때까지. The scripts file is correct. The -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: 그의 춤은 그가 지쳐서 땅에 쓰러질 때까지 점점 더 격렬해진다.

items.original: A modern doctor makes a vivid contrast to a primitive Indian medicine man. || 현대 의사는 원시적인 인디언 주술사와는 극명한 대조를 이룬다. / His remedies are not paints and weird dancing but scientific knowledge, skillful technique, and effective chemicals. || 그의 치료제들은 페인트와 기괴한 춤이 아니라 과학적인 지식, 숙련된 기술, 효과적인 화학약품이다.
items.problem: This continues the d255-d256 framing: 'primitive Indian medicine man' and 'weird dancing' are derogatory. In the Korean of #2, 'paints' (the healer's face paint) is translated as 페인트, which a Korean reader takes to mean house paint.
items.correction: EN #1 'A modern doctor makes a vivid contrast to the healers of earlier times.' EN #2 'His remedies are not face paint and ritual dances but scientific knowledge, skillful technique, and effective medicines.' KO #2 '그의 치료법은 얼굴에 칠하는 물감과 의식용 춤이 아니라 …'. Regenerate the clips for any English line that changes.

items.original: The most obvious cure for their illness is to simply cut down on their food, but some people prefer the misery of excess weight to the cure of dieting. || 그들의 병에 대한 가장 명백한 치료법은 그저 음식을 줄이는 것이다. 그러나 일부 사람들은 식이요법의 치료제보다는 과체중의 비참함을 선호한다.
items.problem: Presented as fact, the text says being overweight is simply cured by eating less and that overweight people 'prefer the misery'. This is weight-stigmatizing and outdated. WHO now describes obesity as a chronic, relapsing disease arising from complex interactions (genetics, neurobiology, environment) and says that environmental and societal conditions 'greatly constrain personal choice'. In the Korean, '식이요법의 치료제' is also an unnatural rendering of 'the cure of dieting' (식이요법이라는 치료법).
items.correction: Soften the English, for example: 'The advice is often to eat less, but some people find it hard to follow a diet.' / KO '흔히 음식을 줄이라는 조언을 듣지만, 식이요법을 지키기 어려워하는 사람들도 있다.' If the English is kept, at least fix the KO to '…식이요법이라는 치료법보다 과체중으로 인한 고통을 택한다.' Regenerate the clip if the English changes.

items.original: 그들은 병에 대한 가장 명백한 치료제는 단지 음식을 주이는 것이다.
items.problem: The line has a typo (주이는 for 줄이는) and a broken subject (그들은 … 치료제는). The scripts file has '그들의 병에 대한 가장 명백한 치료법은 그저 음식을 줄이는 것이다.' The -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: 그들의 병에 대한 가장 명백한 치료법은 그저 음식을 줄이는 것이다.

items.original: 어린 소년들은 맹렬한 눈싸움을 벌이며 때로는 만약 그들이 현지의 말괄량이 여자에게 눈덩이를 던지게 되면 그 싸움에서 지기 쉽다.
items.problem: 'the local tomboy' means the neighbourhood tomboy (a girl). 현지의 means 'on-site / in the foreign locale' and 여자 means 'woman'. 'soon' (곧) is dropped.
items.correction: 어린 소년들은 곧 격렬한 눈싸움에 빠져들고, 어쩌다 동네 말괄량이 여자아이에게 눈덩이를 던지기라도 하면 싸움에서 지기 십상이다.

items.original: 이린이들의 모습으로 가득 차게 될 것이다.
items.problem: 이린이들 is a typo for 어린이들. The scripts file is correct. The -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: 어린이들의 모습으로 가득 차게 될 것이다.

items.locator: d263 rows n=1, n=2, n=4, n=5 (ko)
items.original: 캐롤을 부르는 것은 고대 성탄절 관습이다. / …노래를 부르면서 거리를 쏘다닌다. / 캐롤 대원들이 거리를 쏘다니는 동안… / 그들은 친구들과 병자들의 집에서 그리고…
items.problem: (1) The standard Korean loanword spelling of 'carol' is 캐럴, not 캐롤 (#1, #4). (2) 쏘다니다 has a negative 'gad about aimlessly' connotation, which does not fit carolers going through the streets (#2, #4). (3) 고대 means classical antiquity, while carolling is a medieval or later custom; the English 'ancient' here only means 'very old' (#1). (4) 'stop in front of the homes' is rendered 집에서 (at/inside the homes) (#5).
items.correction: #1 '캐럴을 부르는 것은 오래된 성탄절 관습이다.' #2 '…노래를 부르며 거리를 돌아다닌다.' #4 '캐럴을 부르는 사람들이 거리를 누비는 동안…' #5 '그들은 친구들과 아픈 사람들의 집 앞, 그리고…'

items.locator: d263.json menuLabel; d263-1.json menuLabel and order
items.original: d263.json "menuLabel": "[ D 263-1 ]" / d263-1.json "menuLabel": null, "order": 552
items.problem: The main lesson carries the script page's label, and the script page has no label. page.tsx:80-82 builds the meta description from lesson.menuLabel, so /ld/d263 publishes '[ D 263-1 ] — …' and /ld/d263-1 has no label at all. d263-1.json also has order 552, out of sequence (neighbours are 523/524).
items.correction: d263.json menuLabel → "[ D 263 ]"; d263-1.json menuLabel → "[ D 263-1 ]", and set its order to match the sequence (the course index content/courses/ld.json already has d263-1 at order 525).

items.locator: d264 rows n=5 (en + ko) and n=4 (ko)
items.original: Naturally, however, the children would rather show their devotion by giving presents that they have earned themselves. || 그러나 당연히 그 어린이들은 그들이 스스로 번 선물을 줌으로써 그들의 헌신을 보여주기를 더 원한다. / 만약 그들이 스스로 해낼 수 없다면 보통 그들의 형들과 누나들이 그들에게 약간의 도움을 줄 것이다.
items.problem: #5 KO: 선물을 벌다 is an ungrammatical collocation (you earn money, not presents), and 헌신 (self-sacrifice/dedication) is an odd word for a child's love for its parents. The English 'presents that they have earned themselves' is also ambiguous, because 'earn a present' usually means 'deserve a present'. The intended meaning is presents bought with money they earned. #4 KO: 형들과 누나들 assumes every child is a boy, while the English 'older brothers and sisters' is neutral.
items.correction: EN #5 (optional) '…by giving presents bought with money they have earned themselves.' KO #5 '그래도 아이들은 당연히 자기가 직접 번 돈으로 산 선물을 드려 부모님에 대한 사랑을 표현하고 싶어 한다.' KO #4 '…보통 손위 형제자매들이 조금 도와준다.' Regenerate the clip if the English changes.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d265.json and content/lessons/ld/d276.json, instruction block 1 (neither file has a hints block)
items.original: 다음에 나오는 고유 명사, 숫자, 어려운 단어를 참조하면서 영어로 받아쓰기를 하세요.
items.problem: The instruction tells learners to use the proper nouns, numbers and hard words 'shown below', but neither d265 nor d276 has a hints block. This is latent today because the LD view renders neither the instruction nor the hints (maps/listening.md A-18).
items.correction: Add a hints block (e.g. d265: 'Christmas Eve stockings fireplace practice spirit of the season three kings of old Christ child'; d276: 'precious possessions fellow men mentality accordingly rewards'), or use an instruction without the hint reference for these two rounds.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d266, row n=4 (en). The d266 hint 'graphic arts sketching, painting, sculpturing' repeats it.
items.original: The graphic arts such as sketching, painting, and sculpturing help to satisfy this desire.
items.problem: 'Graphic arts' are the two-dimensional arts made on a flat surface, such as drawing, painting and printmaking. Sculpture is a three-dimensional (plastic) art and is not one of the graphic arts, so the sentence teaches the term wrongly.
items.correction: The visual arts such as sketching, painting, and sculpturing help to satisfy this desire. (KO '미술' can stay.) Update the hint and regenerate the clip.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d266, row n=4 (ko). The same text is in content/lessons/ld/d266-1.json, instruction block 6.
items.original: 스켓치, 그림그리기, 조각 만들기 같은 미술은 이런 욕구를 만족시키는 것을 돕는다.
items.problem: '스켓치' is a misspelling of the standard loanword '스케치', and row 6 of the same lesson spells it correctly ('스케치').
items.correction: 스케치, 그림 그리기, 조각 같은 미술은 이런 욕구를 채우는 데 도움이 된다.

items.original: 일반적으로 여러 시대에 걸쳐 화가들은 다소 가난에 쪼들렸다. / 화가에 대해서도 비슷한 것이 사실이다.
items.problem: The passage is about art and artists in general ('Art and poverty seem to go hand in hand', the prophet comparison), and the same rows translate 'art' as '예술'. 'artist(s)' is nevertheless always translated as '화가' (painter), which narrows the meaning and is inconsistent with '예술'.
items.correction: Use '예술가' for 'artist(s)' in rows 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 (e.g. '일반적으로 여러 시대에 걸쳐 예술가들은 다소 가난에 쪼들렸다.').

items.original: want. devote prophet recognized false of genius recognized aware of extraordinary talent
items.problem: The hint word 'false' is not in any d267 script row. Row 7 is 'A similar thing is true of the artist.', so the hint points the learner to the opposite word. This is latent today because hints are not rendered (maps/listening.md A-18), but the hint feeds the quiz and any future display of hints.
items.correction: Remove 'false' (or use 'true' if a word from row 7 is wanted): 'want. devote prophet recognized true of genius recognized aware of extraordinary talent'.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d267-1.json, instruction block for script line 1
items.original: 일반적인 규칙으로써 여러 세대를 걸쳐 화가들은 다소 가난에 쪼달렸다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the typos that L-91 fixed in the scripts file: '쪼달렸다' should be '쪼들렸다', and '규칙으로써' should use '로서' or be rephrased. It also says '세대' ('generations') where 'the ages' means '시대'. The line differs from scripts ko row 1 ('일반적으로 여러 시대에 걸쳐 화가들은 다소 가난에 쪼들렸다.'). This is latent today because the -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: 일반적으로 여러 시대에 걸쳐 예술가들은 다소 가난에 쪼들렸다.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d268, row n=7 (en/ko). Context: rows 1 and 6
items.original: Consequently, Picasso's art is called Cubism.
items.problem: The sentence equates all of Picasso's art with Cubism. Cubism is a movement that Picasso created together with Georges Braque in Paris, mainly between 1907 and 1914. Picasso's work also spans the Blue and Rose periods, neoclassicism and later styles, so 'Picasso's art is called Cubism' is wrong as a general statement, and the sentence leaves out Braque. Row 1 ('The present day has seen the rise of a new type of art.') also presents this c.1907–1914 movement as current.
items.correction: EN: 'Picasso, together with Georges Braque, developed a style called Cubism.' (or 'Consequently, the style Picasso developed with Braque is called Cubism.') KO: '피카소는 브라크와 함께 입체파(큐비즘)라는 양식을 만들었다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.original: The spirit of a modern business world is similarly reflected in the skyscraper.
items.problem: The indefinite article is unnatural here: there is one modern business world, as there is one 'God-centered world of the Middle Ages' in row 2. The natural phrase is 'the modern business world'.
items.correction: The spirit of the modern business world is similarly reflected in the skyscraper. Regenerate the clip.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d270, row n=6 (en). Related: the hints block in content/lessons/ld/d270.json
items.original: On occasions of great emotions such as weddings and funerals, people find a natural outlet for their feelings and songs of joy or sorrow.
items.problem: With 'and songs', the sentence says people find an outlet for their feelings and also for songs, which makes no sense. The intended meaning is that songs are the outlet, and the Korean row says exactly that ('기쁨이나 슬픔의 노래에서 그들의 감정에 대한 자연스러운 배출구를 발견한다'). 'occasions of great emotions' is also unidiomatic: 'emotion' is uncountable in this phrase, and the lesson's own hint says 'occasions of great emotion,'. The dictation model answer therefore teaches a broken sentence, and a learner who follows the hint and types 'emotion' is marked wrong.
items.correction: On occasions of great emotion such as weddings and funerals, people find a natural outlet for their feelings in songs of joy or sorrow. Regenerate the Azure clip for this row (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d270-1.json, instruction blocks for script lines 4, 5, 7
items.original: 모든 나라는 듣는 사람의 가슴에 애국심의 감정을 휘젓는 애국가를 갖고 있다. / 도시의 마을들은 그 지역의 역사와 민속을 보존하는 다채로운 민속노래와 밸라드를 갖고 있다. / 그들의 감정에 대한 자연스로운 배출구를 발견한다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps errors that L-90 and L-91 fixed only in the scripts file. '애국가' is the proper name of Korea's anthem, not the generic 'national anthem'. '도시의 마을들' mistranslates 'Cities and towns'. '밸라드' and '자연스로운' are misspellings. The text also differs from the scripts ko rows 4–6. This is latent today because the -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file ko: '...애국심의 감정을 불러일으키는 국가를 갖고 있다.' / '도시와 마을들은 ... 민속노래와 발라드를 갖고 있다.' / '...자연스러운 배출구를 발견한다.'

items.original: The New Thought and Romanticism of the 19th century were well portrayed by great masters such as Beethoven and Brahms.
items.problem: Capitalized, 'New Thought' is the name of a 19th-century American mind-healing religious movement (Quimby), which has nothing to do with Beethoven or Brahms. The Korean row ('새로운 사상') shows the intended meaning is just 'new ideas', but the capitals point to the wrong thing.
items.correction: The new thinking and Romanticism of the 19th century were well portrayed by great masters such as Beethoven and Brahms. (Lower-case 'new thought' would also avoid the proper-noun reading.)

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json: d271 rows n=2 and n=3, d272 row n=3, d273 row n=5, d274 row n=3. Also the d271 hints block in content/lessons/ld/d271.json
items.original: d271#2 '...the dignity and grace of the 18th century are reflected in stately minuets.' / d271#3 '...Romanticism of the 19th century were well portrayed...' / d272#3 '...the other forms of 20th century music...' / d274#3 '...by the 18th century, French had become the language of diplomacy.' / d273#5 'Today, more than 7,000 languages are spoken.' / d271 hint 'worship dignity grace eighteenth century stately minuets. romanticism nineteenth century well'
items.problem: The typing check (LdLearningView.tsx:308-328, maps/listening.md §5.1) compares the typed text with the English row after only lower-casing and removing punctuation, so a number written as a word never matches a digit. The synthesized audio says 'eighteenth century', 'nineteenth century', 'twentieth century' and 'seven thousand', and learners who write what they hear ('eighteenth century', 'seven thousand') are marked wrong even though both spellings are correct English. In d271 the round's own hint spells the words out ('eighteenth century', 'nineteenth century'), which directly contradicts the graded answer.
items.correction: Either make the typing check accept number words for digits and ordinals (18th = eighteenth, 7,000 = seven thousand), or write these rows in words to match the hint ('eighteenth century', 'nineteenth century', 'twentieth-century music', 'seven thousand languages') and regenerate the clips. At minimum, make the d271 hint and script use the same form.

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d272, rows n=1 and n=3 (en/ko)
items.original: A few years ago most intellectuals scorned popular music. / But today people are becoming increasingly aware that jazz, swing, and the other forms of 20th century music are a valid and worthwhile trend in music.
items.problem: These rows present mid-20th-century attitudes as current ('a few years ago', 'today ... becoming increasingly aware'). In 2026 jazz has long been an established academic and concert-hall art form, which row 4 of the same passage admits, and swing is a 1930s–40s style, not a current trend. (A similar era expression in d271 #4 was kept under L-92. The owner may want to decide both cases the same way.)
items.correction: Reframe the passage as history, e.g. 'In the early 20th century, many intellectuals scorned popular music.' / 'Over time, people became aware that jazz, swing, and other forms of 20th-century music were a valid and worthwhile trend in music.' Update the Korean to match and regenerate the clips.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d272-1.json, instruction blocks for script lines 5 and 7–8
items.original: 모든 가족은 그 야만적인 소음에 대한 더 젊은 세대의 관심을 내려다보는 노처녀 이모가 있다. / 그러나 그녀는 바그너같은 사람들의 고전적인 “소음”의 일부는 즐겨 귀기울일 것이다. / 오늘날 많은 대학은 미국 문화의 일부로써 재즈의 역사에 대한 수업을 한다.
items.problem: The -1 page still has the 'maiden aunt' stereotype ('노처녀 이모', 'she') that L-89 replaced with 'an older relative' in the English and the scripts ko. It also renders 'looks down on' word for word as '내려다보는' (which means looking downward, not despising), and it uses '로써' where '로서' is correct. The text no longer matches English row 6. This is latent today because the -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file ko: '어느 가족에나 젊은 세대가 좋아하는 그 야만적인 소음을 깔보는 나이 든 친척이 있다. 그러나 그 사람도 바그너같은 사람들의 고전적인 “소음”의 일부는 즐겨 귀기울일 것이다.' / '...미국 문화의 일부로서...'

items.original: In an attempt to understand the mysteries of God, man tried to build a tower that would reach to heaven.
items.problem: The passage opens by saying it retells the Old Testament story (row 1). Genesis 11:4, however, gives a different motive for the tower: 'so that we may make a name for ourselves; otherwise we will be scattered over the face of the whole earth.' Nothing in the story says the builders wanted to understand the mysteries of God, so the lesson misstates what the text says. The Korean row repeats the invented motive ('하나님의 신비를 이해하기 위한 시도에서').
items.correction: EN: 'In an attempt to make a name for themselves, people tried to build a tower that would reach to heaven.' KO: '자신들의 이름을 떨치려고 사람들은 하늘에 닿을 탑을 쌓으려 했다.' Regenerate the clip.

items.locator: content/lessons/ld/d273-1.json, instruction blocks for script lines 3, 5, 7
items.original: 그들의 교만에 대한 처벌로써 그 탑이 무너져서 근로자들의 언어가 혼돈되었다. / 오늘날 천개 이상의 언어가 사용된다. / 불어, 스페인어, 이태리어 같은 로망스말은 모두 라틴어로부터 파생되었다.
items.problem: The -1 page keeps the pre-L-85 errors: the tower 'collapsed', which is not in Genesis 11 (the builders stopped building), and 'more than 1,000 languages', while the English row and the scripts ko say 7,000. It also keeps the non-standard '이태리어' that L-00b fixed. None of this matches the current English rows 3 and 5. This is latent today because the -1 blocks are not rendered.
items.correction: Replace with the scripts-file ko: '그들의 교만에 대한 벌로 일꾼들의 언어가 뒤섞였고, 그들은 탑을 완성할 수 없었다.' / '오늘날 7,000개가 넘는 언어가 사용된다.' / '불어, 스페인어, 이탈리아어 같은 로망스어는 모두 라틴어로부터 파생되었다.'

items.locator: content/ld_english_scripts.json key d274, rows n=1 and n=2 (en/ko)
items.original: In the Middle Ages, Latin was the universal language. / ...and all important documents were written in that language. / KO '중세에는 라틴어가 범세계적인 언어였다.'
items.problem: In the Middle Ages Latin was the common language of scholarship, the Church and law in Western Europe. It was not universal: Byzantium used Greek, the Islamic world used Arabic, and vernacular documents existed. The Korean '범세계적인' ('worldwide') makes the overstatement worse, telling learners that Latin was a global language.
items.correction: EN: 'In the Middle Ages, Latin was the common language of learning in Western Europe.' / '...and most important documents were written in that language.' KO: '중세 서유럽에서는 라틴어가 학문의 공통어였다.' / '대부분의 중요한 문서들'. Regenerate clips if the English changes.

items.original: 영어에 방언이 적은 것이 그것이 표준 언어가 되기에 유리하게 해준다. / 게다가 영어는 매우 정확하다. 그것은 많은 다른 현대 언어에서 발견되는 애매모호한 것이 별로 없다. / 이것이 그것을 사업 및 국제 문제의 처리를 위하여 이상적으로 만들어준다. / 그러나 범세계적인 언어로써 영어의 가장 큰 결점은...
items.problem: The -1 page Korean still has the old text that audit L-85 removed as false ('English has few dialects', 'English is very exact / has few ambiguities'). It no longer matches the English rows 2–4 ('The spread of the British Empire and the power of the United States…', 'English grammar is fairly simple… nouns have no gender', 'useful for…'). It also uses '로써' where '로서' is correct. This is latent today because the LD view renders the scripts file, not these blocks (maps/listening.md line 82 and §4.9).
items.correction: Replace the Korean lines with the current content/ld_english_scripts.json d275 ko rows (e.g. '대영 제국의 확장과 미국의 힘은 영어가 국제 공용어가 되는 데 도움이 되었다.' / '게다가 영어 문법은 어떤 면에서는 꽤 단순하다. 예를 들어 영어 명사에는 성(性)이 없다.' / '...유용하게 만들어준다.' / '...언어로서...').

items.locator: voca_dictionary.json line 918 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 17); lessons hv-08, mv3-04
items.original: "absolutely": { "meaning": "절대적으로", "searchWord": "absolutely" }
items.problem: 절대적으로 is the mechanical -ly derivation of `absolute`=절대적인 and, in Korean, is used almost only in fixed collocations such as 절대적으로 필요하다/우세하다. It misses the sense the word actually carries in ordinary English — the intensifier 완전히/전적으로 ('You're absolutely right', 'I absolutely agree') and the one-word answer 물론이지 ('Absolutely!'). In mv3-04 this is a plain middle-3 word list with no sentence context, so the single gloss is everything the learner gets.
items.correction: "완전히, 전적으로; (대답) 물론이지"

items.locator: voca_dictionary.json line 8042 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 24); lessons hv-70, mv3-04
items.original: "abuse": { "meaning": "남용", "searchWord": "abuse" }
items.problem: 남용 is correct and is the root-appropriate sense in hv-70, where `abuse` sits inside the use/usage/utilize family (ab- + use). But mv3-04 is a general middle-3 word list, and there the sense a learner meets in reading passages and news English is 학대 (child abuse, animal abuse) and, secondarily, 욕설/폭언. One gloss serves both lessons, and it omits the sense that carries most of the word's modern usage.
items.correction: "남용; 학대; 남용하다, 학대하다"

items.original: "accustom": { "meaning": "익숙해지다", "searchWord": "accustom" }
items.problem: `accustom` is a TRANSITIVE causative verb — 'to make familiar by use; to habituate', used mostly in the passive or reflexive with `to` (be accustomed to / accustom oneself to). The gloss 익숙해지다 is the opposite direction: it describes the subject BECOMING used to something, i.e. it glosses `become accustomed`, not `accustom`. The file itself gets this right for the identical pattern one entry away in the same lesson family — `acquaint` = "알게 하다, 익히다" (line 53) is correctly causative — so this entry is inconsistent as well as wrong.
items.correction: "익숙하게 하다 (be accustomed to ~에 익숙하다)"

items.locator: voca_dictionary.json line 12958 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 49); lessons mv2-13, mv3-26
items.original: "ache": { "meaning": "아픔", "searchWord": "ache" }
items.problem: The verb sense — 아프다, 쑤시다 ('My head aches', 'My feet ached for days') — is missing, and for the noun the precise word is 통증 (a continued dull physical pain); bare 아픔 in Korean reads first as emotional hurt (마음의 아픔). The same lesson mv3-26 glosses its other noun/verb words both ways ("sigh=한숨 쉬다; 한숨", "hate=미워하다; 증오", "bear=곰; 참다, 견디다", "beat=이기다; 치다"), so the single-sense gloss here is an inconsistency inside one 30-word list.
items.correction: "아프다; 통증, 아픔"

items.locator: voca_dictionary.json line 12186 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 59); lessons mv1-34, mv2-01
items.original: "act": { "meaning": "행위", "searchWord": "act" }
items.problem: 행위 is a correct noun gloss, but `act` is met by beginners far more often as a verb — 행동하다 ('act quickly', 'act like a child', 'Don't act surprised') and 연기하다 ('She acts in films'). These are mv1/mv2 lists, the lowest levels in the course. The file's own convention in the very same lessons is to give both parts of speech when both matter: mv1-34 has "taste=맛이 나다; 맛", "wave=파도; 손을 흔들다", "quarrel=말다툼하다; 말다툼"; mv2-01 has "work=일하다; 일". `act` is left noun-only, and 행위 is also the stiffest of the noun readings (행동 is the everyday one, but that string is already used by `action`, line 60).
items.correction: "행동하다; 연기하다; 행위"

items.original: "admission": { "meaning": "입학", "searchWord": "admission" }
items.problem: 입학 is a real but narrow sense. The primary sense is 입장/입장 허가, and 입장료 ('Admission is $10', 'free admission') is what learners meet on signs and in listening passages; 인정/시인 ('an admission of guilt') is the third. It also breaks the root pairing the lesson is built on: hv-44 is the mit/miss (send) lesson and glosses `admit` as 인정하다 (line 84), so a learner has no way to connect admit=인정하다 with admission=입학.
items.correction: "입장, 입장료; 입학; 인정, 시인"

items.original: "adopt": { "meaning": "채택하다", "searchWord": "adopt" }
items.problem: 채택하다 is correct for 'adopt a policy/method' and fits the opt- (choose) root lesson, but it omits 입양하다, which is the first sense in general dictionaries and the one that appears constantly in school reading passages about families and pets. Nothing in 채택하다 lets a learner reach 입양하다 on their own — the two are unrelated words in Korean.
items.correction: "채택하다; 입양하다"

items.locator: voca_dictionary.json line 550 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 132); lessons hv-05, mv2-10
items.original: "alike": { "meaning": "똑같이", "searchWord": "alike" }
items.problem: 똑같이 gives only the adverb ('treat everyone alike', 'young and old alike'). The form learners actually meet is the predicative ADJECTIVE — 'They look alike', 'The twins are alike' — which is 서로 닮은/비슷한, not 똑같이; and 'alike' means similar, not identical, so 똑같이 also overstates it. The file glosses `alike`'s a- prefix siblings as adjectives (alive=살아 있는 line 133, asleep=잠든, 자고 있는, awake=깨어 있는; 깨우다), so this entry is the odd one out.
items.correction: "서로 닮은, 비슷한; 똑같이"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 202; voca_dictionary.json line 1438, key "appearance"; used by lessons hv-13, hv-48, mv2-31
items.original: "appearance": { "meaning": "외관", "searchWord": "appearance" }
items.problem: 외관 is normally said of buildings and objects; for a person Korean uses 외모 or 겉모습, and mv2-31 places the word among body and person words (ankle, chest, neck, athlete). The other main sense, 나타남·출현, is missing entirely, although hv-48 is the appear family lesson (appear 나타나다, apparent 명백한) where that is exactly what the noun is derived from.
items.correction: "외모, 겉모습; 나타남, 출현"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 211; voca_dictionary.json line 5850, key "apply"; used by lessons hv-51 and mv2-22
items.original: "apply": { "meaning": "적용하다", "searchWord": "apply" }
items.problem: 적용하다 is a correct sense, but the entry omits 'apply for/to' = 지원하다, 신청하다 - the sense the same lesson's own derivatives already use. hv-51 teaches applicant 지원자 and application 신청 side by side with apply 적용하다, so the word family contradicts itself on the card.
items.correction: "적용하다; (일자리·학교에) 지원하다, 신청하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 237; voca_dictionary.json line 7158, key "arrest"; used by lessons hv-63, mv2-22, mv3-11
items.original: "arrest": { "meaning": "체포", "searchWord": "arrest" }
items.problem: The file's own convention marks verbs with -하다 (announce 발표하다 vs announcement 발표; capture 붙잡다 on line 515), so a bare 체포 presents arrest as a noun, while learners meet it as a verb ('The police arrested the man'). hv-63 is the 'stop/stand' root lesson, where arrest also carries the 저지하다 sense ('arrest the spread of the disease') that is absent too.
items.correction: "체포하다; 체포; (진행을) 막다, 저지하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 247; voca_dictionary.json line 8682, key "as"; used by lesson mv1-01
items.original: "as": { "meaning": "~로", "searchWord": "as" }
items.problem: No main use of 'as' reduces to ~로. The closest is 'in the role of' = ~로서, and the particle ~로 on its own reads as 'with/by/to' in Korean. mv1-01 is a bare word grid of basic function words with no sentence context, so this one-particle gloss is the entire teaching for the word.
items.correction: "~처럼, ~만큼; ~로서; ~할 때; ~때문에"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 249; voca_dictionary.json line 6470, key "ascent"; used by lesson hv-57
items.original: "ascent": { "meaning": "오르막", "searchWord": "ascent" }
items.problem: The primary sense is the act of going up (상승, 올라감, 등반); 오르막 renders only the secondary 'upward slope' sense. It also breaks two pairs the dictionary itself sets up: ascend 상승하다 (line 248) and descent 하강 (line 979).
items.correction: "상승, 올라감; 오르막(길)"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 253; voca_dictionary.json line 554, key "aside"; used by lesson hv-05
items.original: "aside": { "meaning": "제쳐두고", "searchWord": "aside" }
items.problem: The adverb's core sense is 'to or on one side, out of the way' = 옆으로, 한쪽으로. 제쳐두고 renders only the idioms 'aside from' and 'put aside' and is a connective phrase, not a standalone adverb gloss. hv-05 is the a- + noun position lesson (aboard (탈것에) 타고, abreast 나란히, ashore 해안으로), so this entry is the only one that abandons the pattern the lesson teaches.
items.correction: "옆으로, 한쪽으로; (~은) 제쳐두고"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 259; voca_dictionary.json line 6746, key "assemble"; used by lesson hv-59
items.original: "assemble": { "meaning": "조립하다", "searchWord": "assemble" }
items.problem: 조립하다 is correct for 'assemble a model ship', but the gather sense ('The parents assembled in the school hall') is missing, and that is the sense school texts use. The same lesson glosses assembly as '집회, 의회; 조립' (line 260), so the noun leads with a meaning its own verb never teaches.
items.correction: "모이다, 모으다; 조립하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 266; voca_dictionary.json line 6778, key "associate"; used by lesson hv-59
items.original: "associate": { "meaning": "동료", "searchWord": "associate" }
items.problem: Only the noun is given. The verb 'associate A with B' (연관짓다, 연상하다) is the form that appears in reading passages and in the 'associate ... with' pattern tested at this level; without it the entry also cannot explain 'association'.
items.correction: "연관짓다, 연상하다; (명사) 동료"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 267; voca_dictionary.json line 6770, key "association"; used by lesson hv-59
items.original: "association": { "meaning": "협회", "searchWord": "association" }
items.problem: 협회 is a correct primary sense, but the abstract sense 연관, 관련, 연상 ('the association between smoking and cancer') is missing, and it is the sense that actually turns up in reading passages. With 'associate' glossed 동료 in the same lesson, neither entry teaches the connect-in-the-mind meaning anywhere.
items.correction: "협회, 단체; 연관, 연상"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 289; voca_dictionary.json line 7830, key "attentive"; used by lesson hv-68
items.original: "attentive": { "meaning": "세심한", "searchWord": "attentive" }

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 307; voca_dictionary.json lines 14642-14645, key "autumn(=fall)"; used by lesson mv3-12 (word grid, content/lessons/phonics/mv3-12.json line 54)
items.original: "autumn(=fall)": { "meaning": "가을", "searchWord": "autumn=fall" }
items.problem: The meaning 가을 is right and the spoken form is already handled (VOCA_SPEECH_FORMS maps this headword to 'autumn' in src/lib/vocaSpeech.ts), but searchWord is the non-word 'autumn=fall'. searchWord's only runtime use is getCollocation (src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:256), which lower-cases and strips parentheses but not '='; the key therefore stays 'autumn=fall' and can never match a preset, unlike the plain 'autumn' entry on line 306. It is one of only two bracketed headwords whose searchWord is not a real word (the other, gray(grey) -> graygrey, is outside this slice; colo(u)r -> colour and the rest are fine). Today COLLOCATION_PRESETS holds no entry for autumn, so nothing is visibly broken - this is a latent defect, not a live one.
items.correction: "searchWord": "autumn"

items.original: "back": {"meaning":"뒤로","searchWord":"back"}
items.problem: 부사 뜻 '뒤로'만 있고, 기초 단계에서 반드시 배우는 명사 뜻 '등'(신체 부위)과 '뒤쪽'이 없다. Longman 명사 1번 뜻이 BODY(등)다. mv1-03은 과정 맨 앞이라 body·bone 같은 신체 단어와 함께 쓰이는 자리인데도 '등'을 배울 길이 없다.
items.correction: "뒤로, 다시; 등; 뒤쪽"

items.original: "bank": {"meaning":"은행","searchWord":"bank"}
items.problem: 학교 영어에서 반드시 짚는 동음이의어인 '둑, 제방, (강)기슭'(the river bank, sat on the bank)이 빠져 있다. Longman도 RIVER/LAKE를 두 번째 뜻으로 싣는다. 이 사전은 같은 성격의 단어(bar=막대; 술집, bear=곰; 참다)에 두 뜻을 다 주고 있어 처리 기준이 일관되지 않다.
items.correction: "은행; 둑, (강)기슭"

items.original: "bargain": {"meaning":"흥정하다","searchWord":"bargain"}
items.problem: 동사 뜻만 주고, 실제로 더 자주 만나는 명사 뜻 '싼 물건, 특가품'(What a bargain! / a real bargain)과 '거래, 합의'(make a bargain)가 빠졌다. 영어 사전들도 명사 뜻을 먼저 싣는다.
items.correction: "싼 물건, 특가품; 거래, 합의; 흥정하다"

items.original: "bark": {"meaning":"짖다","searchWord":"bark"}
items.problem: 명사 뜻 '나무껍질'이 빠졌다. Longman 명사 2번 뜻이며 환경·자연 소재 지문에 꾸준히 나오는 동음이의어다. bear·bar·band 항목처럼 세미콜론으로 한 뜻만 더하면 해결된다.
items.correction: "짖다; 나무껍질"

items.original: "bay": {"meaning":"만","searchWord":"bay"}
items.problem: 뜻풀이가 한 글자 '만'뿐이다. 한국어에서 '만'은 숫자 10,000, 조사 '~만' 등으로 먼저 읽히는 말이라, 카드에 'bay — 만'만 뜨면 지리 용어 灣이라는 것을 알아보기 어렵다. 문장 없는 단어판이라 문맥으로 풀 수도 없다. 같은 mv3-32에는 bankrupt·beach·bone이 함께 있어 바다 맥락이 있긴 하나 뜻풀이 자체로 읽히지 않는다.
items.correction: "만(灣), 바닷가의 후미"

items.original: "because": {"meaning":"왜냐하면","searchWord":"because"}
items.problem: 한국어 '왜냐하면'은 문장 앞에 놓여 '~때문이다'로 끝맺는 호응 부사라, because가 실제로 쓰이는 자리(I was late because it rained)에는 그대로 대입되지 않는다. because의 기본 대응어는 종속접속사 '~때문에, ~해서'다. 영어 사실관계가 아니라 한국어 대응어 선택 문제다.
items.correction: "~때문에, ~해서 (왜냐하면 ~이기 때문이다)"

items.original: "beg": {"meaning":"구걸하다","searchWord":"beg"}
items.problem: Longman이 첫 번째로 싣는 뜻(간절히 부탁하다, 간청·애원하다 — She begged Helen to stay)이 빠지고, 두 번째 뜻인 '구걸하다'만 있다. beg somebody to do / I beg you / beg for mercy 형태가 독해에서 훨씬 자주 나온다. mv2-13은 bank·bill·beggar·blind가 같이 나오는 단어판이라 '구걸하다'가 편집 맥락상 선택된 것으로 보이지만, 이 뜻풀이는 전 과정 공통으로 쓰인다.
items.correction: "간청하다, 애원하다; 구걸하다"

items.original: "behold": {"meaning":"보다","searchWord":"behold"}
items.problem: '보다'는 see·look·watch와 구분이 전혀 없다. behold는 문어체·고어체로 '(감탄하며) 바라보다, 주시하다'이며 주로 명령형(Behold! / lo and behold)으로 쓰인다. hv-11은 고등 어휘 단어판이라 등록 수준(register) 정보가 뜻풀이에 없으면 학습자가 알 길이 없다.
items.correction: "(문어) 바라보다, 주시하다"

items.original: "bell": {"meaning":"벨","searchWord":"bell"}
items.problem: 영어 단어를 한글로 소리만 옮긴 '벨'이라 뜻풀이가 정보를 거의 주지 않는다('벨'은 국어사전에 있는 말이지만 초인종 뜻에 치우친다). bell의 기본 뜻은 '종'이고 학교 종·교회 종·방울이 모두 여기에 든다. 같은 과정의 bench(벤치)·belt(벨트)와 달리 bell은 한국어 고유 대응어 '종'이 분명히 있다.
items.correction: "종, 방울; 초인종"

items.original: "below": {"meaning":"아래","searchWord":"below"}
items.problem: below는 전치사·부사인데 뜻풀이 '아래'는 명사형이라 품사가 어긋난다. 같은 계열 단어들은 모두 조사를 붙여 전치사임을 드러내고 있다 — behind(뒤에), beside(옆에), between(사이에), beyond(~을 넘어서). below만 형식이 다르다.
items.correction: "~아래에, 밑에"

items.original: "bid": {"meaning":"명령하다; 입찰","searchWord":"bid"}
items.problem: 두 가지가 겹쳐 있다. (1) Longman이 literary(문어체)로 표시한 뜻 '명령하다'를 맨 앞에 놓고, 현대 영어의 주된 동사 뜻 '(값을) 부르다, 입찰하다'는 명사 '입찰'로만 처리했다. (2) '명령하다'(동사) + '입찰'(명사)로 품사가 섞여 있어, 학습자가 bid를 동사로 쓸 때 문어체 뜻만 손에 쥐게 된다. 참고로 이 사전은 bear·beat·break에서는 같은 품사끼리 묶어 주고 있다.
items.correction: "입찰하다, (값을) 부르다; 입찰; (bid farewell) 작별을 고하다"
