items.original: "bill": {"meaning":"계산서","searchWord":"bill"}
items.problem: '계산서'는 Longman 기준 두 번째(식당, 영국식) 뜻이다. 첫 번째 뜻인 '청구서'(the bill for the repairs = 수리비 청구서)와, 미국식 '지폐'(a five-dollar bill), 그리고 '법안'(pass a gun-control bill)이 모두 빠졌다. 특히 '지폐'와 '법안'은 중·고등 독해에서 흔하고 '계산서'와 전혀 겹치지 않는 뜻이다.
items.correction: "청구서, 계산서; 지폐; 법안"

items.locator: key "biography" (voca-dictionary.tsv line 406; lessons hv-20, mv2-37, mv3-22)
items.original: "biography": {"meaning":"전기","searchWord":"biography"}
items.problem: '전기'는 電氣(electricity)로 먼저 읽히는 동음이의어다. 같은 항목의 biographer는 '전기 작가'라 문맥이 붙어 구분되지만, biography는 '전기' 한 낱말뿐이라 문장 없는 단어판·플래시카드에서 電氣로 오해될 소지가 크다.
items.correction: "전기(傳記), 위인전"

items.original: "blaze": {"meaning":"불꽃","searchWord":"blaze"}
items.problem: blaze는 '활활 타오르는 큰 불, 화재'(Longman: a big dangerous fire)이고 동사로는 '활활 타다'다. 한국어 '불꽃'은 보통 flame 또는 spark에 대응하는 말이라, blaze를 flame과 같은 단어로 묶어 버린다. 규모와 기세라는 핵심 뉘앙스가 사라진다.
items.correction: "활활 타는 불, 화재; 활활 타오르다"

items.original: "block": {"meaning":"블록","searchWord":"block"}
items.problem: 뜻풀이가 영어 발음을 한글로 옮겨 적은 '블록' 하나뿐이라 사실상 뜻을 알려주지 않는다. 학교 영어에서 block이 가장 많이 쓰이는 용법인 동사 '막다, 차단하다'(block the road / block the sun)가 없고, 명사 '덩어리', '구역'도 '블록'만으로는 어느 쪽인지 알 수 없다.
items.correction: "막다, 차단하다; 덩어리; (도시의) 구역, 블록"

items.original: "board": {"meaning":"판자; 게시판","searchWord":"board"}
items.problem: 명사 두 뜻은 맞지만, 중3 수준 독해·듣기에서 자주 나오는 동사 '(배·비행기·버스에) 타다, 탑승하다'(board the plane, now boarding)와 명사 '이사회, 위원회'(the board of directors)가 빠졌다. 이 사전은 다의어에 세미콜론으로 여러 뜻을 주는 방식을 쓰고 있으므로 한 항목만 늘리면 된다.
items.correction: "판자; 게시판; (배·비행기에) 타다, 탑승하다; 이사회"

items.original: "bow": {"meaning":"활","searchWord":"bow"}
items.problem: bow의 가장 흔한 뜻인 동사 /baʊ/ '(허리 굽혀) 절하다, 인사하다'가 통째로 빠지고 /bəʊ/ '활' 하나만 있다. Longman은 bow¹(절하다, /baʊ/)를 첫 표제어로, '활'은 bow³로 싣는다. 이 사전에서 band(악단; 띠), bar(막대; 술집), bear(곰; 참다), beat(이기다; 치다)처럼 동음이의어는 세미콜론으로 두 뜻을 주고 있는데 bow만 한쪽이 없다. 게다가 mv1-39·mv2-03은 문장 없이 단어만 늘어놓은 wordgrid라 학습자에게는 뜻풀이 말고 단서가 전혀 없고, 이 두 뜻은 발음 자체가 다르다(/bəʊ/ vs /baʊ/).
items.correction: "활; (허리 굽혀) 절하다, 인사하다"

items.original: "brilliant": {"meaning":"빛나는","searchWord":"brilliant"}
items.problem: '빛나는'은 Longman 1번 뜻(BRIGHT)에 해당하므로 틀린 말은 아니지만, 독해에서 훨씬 자주 만나는 2번 뜻 '아주 뛰어난, 훌륭한'(a brilliant scientist, a brilliant idea)이 빠졌다. 문장 없는 단어판에서는 학습자가 이 뜻을 만날 통로가 없다.
items.correction: "빛나는; 아주 뛰어난, 훌륭한"

items.original: "bud": {"meaning":"새싹","searchWord":"bud"}
items.problem: bud는 '피기 전에 단단히 말려 있는 꽃봉오리 또는 잎눈'(rose buds, in bud)이다. 한국어 '새싹'은 씨에서 갓 돋아난 sprout/shoot 쪽이라 가리키는 대상이 다르다. 같은 단어판 계열의 blossom(꽃이 피다), bloom(개화하다)과 함께 쓰일 때 구분이 무너진다.
items.correction: "꽃봉오리, (나무의) 눈, 싹"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 491; content/voca_dictionary.json line 8893-8894 (key "by"); lesson mv1-03
items.original: "by": { "meaning": "에 의해" }
items.problem: mv1-03 is the third beginner lesson; its grid is mother, friend, house, home, live, month, year, people… The one sense given, "에 의해", is the passive-voice agent marker — a construction a learner at this level has not met and will not meet for a long time. The senses they need first (~옆에, ~까지, ~로/~을 타고, by the way) are all absent. The other function words in the same grid are given the beginner-useful sense (into '안으로', back '뒤로', after '이후'), and the file elsewhere lists several senses for one preposition (since '~이후로; ~때문에', right '옳은; 오른쪽; 권리').
items.correction: "by": "~옆에; ~까지; ~로(수단); ~에 의해"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 537; content/voca_dictionary.json line 13101-13102 (key "cause"); lessons mv2-16, mv3-17
items.original: "cause": { "meaning": "원인" }
items.problem: 원인 is the correct primary noun, but the verb sense 야기하다/일으키다 is missing and, unlike most Sino-Korean glosses in this file, it cannot be derived by adding -하다: 원인하다 is not a Korean word, so the learner has no route from this card to "Smoking causes cancer" — a sentence type they meet in every middle-school reading unit. The file's own convention supplies both where both exist (in the same mv2-16 grid: slip '미끄러지다; 실수', flow '흐르다; 흐름', claw '발톱; 할퀴다').
items.correction: "cause": "원인; 일으키다, 야기하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 551; content/voca_dictionary.json line 2617-2618 (key "certificate"); lesson hv-23
items.original: "certificate": { "meaning": "인증서" }
items.problem: The standard, and for a school learner the only useful, gloss is 증명서 (and 자격증 / 수료증 for the qualification sense): birth certificate 출생증명서, marriage certificate 혼인관계증명서, certificate of completion 수료증. In present-day Korean, 인증서 on its own is read as a digital authentication certificate (공동인증서/공인인증서), a sense of the English word that a middle- or high-school learner will never meet. hv-23 teaches the cert- root family (certain, certainly, certainty, certificate), so the gloss should show the 'document certifying that something is true' idea the root carries.
items.correction: "certificate": "증명서; 자격증"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 556; content/voca_dictionary.json line 10329-10330 (key "change"); lessons mv1-16, mv2-09, mv3-30
items.original: "change": { "meaning": "변화" }
items.problem: Only the abstract noun is given for one of the most common verbs in beginner English. At the mv1-16 level the word is met as a verb far more often than as a noun (change your clothes / change your mind / change trains), and 변화 does not cover those: 옷을 변화하다 is not Korean. The everyday noun sense 거스름돈 is also missing. This file's own convention is to list both parts of speech with a semicolon, and mv1-16 does exactly that for the grid-mates sound ('소리; ~처럼 들리다'), break ('깨다, 부수다; 휴식') and close ('닫다; 가까운') — change is the exception.
items.correction: "change": "바꾸다, 변하다; 변화; 거스름돈"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 558; content/voca_dictionary.json line 12025-12026 (key "character"); lessons mv1-32, mv2-25
items.original: "character": { "meaning": "성격" }
items.problem: 성격 is correct but is only one of three senses a Korean secondary-school learner meets constantly, and arguably not the most frequent: 등장인물 (a character in a story or film) and 문자/글자 (Chinese characters, 200 characters) are missing entirely. These are not shades of one meaning — a learner cannot infer 등장인물 from 성격. The file gives multiple senses with a semicolon everywhere else (in mv1-32 alone: tear '찢다; 눈물', natural '자연의; 자연스러운').
items.correction: "character": "성격; 등장인물; 문자, 글자"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 559; content/voca_dictionary.json line 2393-2394 (key "charge"); lessons hv-21, mv1-39, mv2-34, mv3-11
items.original: "charge": { "meaning": "요금" }
items.problem: The word is taught in four separate lessons and gets one noun gloss. Missing: 충전하다 (charge a phone — the sense Korean teenagers meet daily), 청구하다 (they charged me $20), and 책임/담당 in the fixed phrase in charge of, which is standard middle-school material. In the mv3-11 grid every other polysemous word is given both senses (review '복습; 검토', upset '속상한; 뒤엎다', leak '새다; 누출', locate '위치를 찾다; ~에 두다').
items.correction: "charge": "요금; 청구하다; 충전하다; 책임 (in charge of ~을 맡은)"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 599; content/voca_dictionary.json line 13989-13990 (key "clap"); lessons mv2-37, mv3-26
items.original: "clap": { "meaning": "박수" }
items.problem: clap is primarily a verb (to strike the hands together), and "박수" is a noun. Worse, the course glosses applause with the identical string "박수" (key "applause", lesson hv-49), so the two words become indistinguishable on the card even though one is a verb and the other a noun. The file's convention for verbs is the -다 form, which its mv2-37 grid-mates follow (mention 언급하다, scold 꾸짖다).
items.correction: "clap": "박수를 치다; 박수" (leaving applause as "박수, 박수갈채")

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 608; content/voca_dictionary.json line 14617-14618 (key "cleave"); lesson mv3-11
items.original: "cleave": { "meaning": "쪼개지다" }
items.problem: Wrong voice, and the word's second meaning is missing. The splitting sense of cleave is chiefly transitive — you cleave something (cleave the bone) — so the gloss should be 쪼개다, 가르다; "쪼개지다" is the intransitive/passive reading and is the minority use. Separately, cleave is a contranym: the other cleave means to cling or adhere (cleave to tradition), which is the opposite of what the entry says. This matters inside this very course, because cling is taught as "달라붙다" at line 614 (mv3-04) with no hint that cleave can mean the same thing. In the mv3-11 grid every other transitive verb gets an active gloss (bend 굽히다, wrap 감싸다, surround 둘러싸다, collect 수집하다), so this entry is also inconsistent with its neighbours.
items.correction: "cleave": "쪼개다, 가르다; (~에) 달라붙다, 고수하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 637; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9637-9640 (key "colo(u)r"); lesson mv1-10
items.original: "colo(u)r": { "meaning": "색깔", "searchWord": "colour" }
items.problem: The meaning 색깔 is right and the bracketed key is a reasonable way to show the two spellings, but searchWord is set to the British "colour" while the rest of the course uses American spelling — colorful (line 641, "colorful"), favorite (hv-15), neighbor-type entries aside. searchWord is what is sent to Azure TTS (scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs:284) and what keys the collocation lookup (src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:256, which strips the parentheses), so the one spelling the system actually uses for this word is the one the course does not teach. Impact is limited — the two spellings are pronounced identically so no audio is wrong, and I confirmed COLLOCATION_PRESETS contains neither 'color' nor 'colour', so no collocation card is lost — but the inconsistency is real and would bite if a 'color' collocation is ever authored.
items.correction: "searchWord": "color" (keep the key "colo(u)r" so both spellings stay visible). Note that changing searchWord changes the TTS clip key, so the clip must be regenerated with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: "compose": { "meaning": "작곡하다", "searchWord": "compose" }
items.problem: content/lessons/phonics/hv-10.json presents the trio compose | composer | composition in one row, and this dictionary glosses them 작곡하다 / 작곡가 / 구성 (lines 698-700). The noun card says 구성 but the verb card offers no 구성하다, so the derivation does not line up and the learner is left with an unexplained 구성. More importantly, the "be composed of ~로 구성되다" pattern — standard Korean middle/high-school exam material and the first sense in learner dictionaries — is not covered anywhere in the trio.
items.correction: "compose": "구성하다 (be composed of ~로 구성되다); 작곡하다"

items.original: "concerned": { "meaning": "우려되는", "searchWord": "concerned" }
items.problem: The voice is reversed. Korean 우려되는 is passive and describes the thing that causes worry (우려되는 상황 = a worrying situation) — it renders "concerning", not "concerned". English "concerned" describes the person who feels the worry (Cambridge: "worried"; "I'm a little concerned about your health"). 우려되는 시민들 is ungrammatical for "concerned citizens"; the active 우려하는/걱정하는 is required. The error is compounded by the lesson: content/lessons/phonics/hv-23.json opens with the pair concerned | concerning, and the sibling card concerning is glossed "~에 관하여", so the adjective meaning that 우려되는 actually expresses is attached to the wrong headword of the pair. This same dictionary handles the identical trap correctly two rows later — "confused": "(사람이) 혼란스러워하는" (line 744).
items.correction: "concerned": "(사람이) 걱정하는, 염려하는; ~에 관계된" — and, to keep the hv-23 pair honest, extend "concerning" to "~에 관하여; 걱정스러운".

items.original: "confer": { "meaning": "수여하다", "searchWord": "confer" }
items.problem: confer has two senses — to bestow/award (수여하다) and to discuss together, confer with somebody (상의하다, 협의하다) — and only the first is given. content/lessons/phonics/hv-31.json is the -fer root lesson, built explicitly out of verb/noun pairs in one row: refer | reference, prefer | preference, confer | conference, infer | inference. This dictionary glosses conference "회의" (line 729), and 회의 comes from the discuss sense, not the award sense. With only 수여하다 the confer/conference pair — the whole reason both words are in the row — is unexplainable.
items.correction: "confer": "상의하다, 협의하다 (confer with ~와 상의하다); (상·학위를) 수여하다"

items.original: "confirmed": { "meaning": "확고한, 상습적인", "searchWord": "confirmed" }
items.problem: Both glosses are defensible for the fixed adjective collocations (a confirmed bachelor = 확고한 독신주의자, a confirmed smoker = 상습적인 흡연자), so this is not a wrong meaning — but it is the only gloss offered, and it omits the sense a learner meets in nearly every real encounter: the participle 확인된/확정된 (a confirmed case, a confirmed reservation, confirmed cases of the disease). The dictionary's own confirm card says "확인하다" (line 737), so the learner who has just learned confirm = 확인하다 is then shown confirmed = 상습적인 with no bridge between them. content/lessons/phonics/mv3-03.json gives no disambiguating context either — the grid around it is patriot, famine, authority, precious, advertise.
items.correction: "confirmed": "확인된, 확정된; (신념·습관이) 확고한, 상습적인"

items.original: "conscious": { "meaning": "의식이 있는", "searchWord": "conscious" }
items.problem: 의식이 있는 is the medical "awake, not unconscious" sense. OALD gives sense 1 as "aware of something; noticing something", used as be conscious of something / conscious that... ("She's very conscious of the problems involved"). The be conscious of ~ pattern is standard Korean middle/high-school exam material and is not covered by 의식이 있는, which cannot take an object in Korean the way the English needs. content/lessons/phonics/hv-57.json groups conscious | consciousness | conscience, and the file glosses consciousness 의식 and conscience 양심, so the aware sense is the only thing missing from the cluster.
items.correction: "conscious": "~을 의식하는, 알고 있는 (be conscious of ~을 의식하다); 의식이 있는"

items.original: "conserve": { "meaning": "절약하다", "searchWord": "conserve" }
items.problem: OALD gives conserve sense 1 as "to protect something and prevent it from being changed or destroyed" (new laws to conserve wildlife) — 보존하다, 보호하다. 절약하다 covers only the energy/water use (conserve energy). content/lessons/phonics/hv-58.json groups conservation | conservative | conserve with preserve | reservation | reserve, and this dictionary glosses conservation "(자원·자연의) 보호, 보존" (line 762) and preserve "보존하다" — so the noun on the card next to it says 보존 while its own verb says 절약, which does not hold together.
items.correction: "conserve": "보존하다, 보호하다; (자원을) 아끼다, 절약하다"

items.original: "construct": { "meaning": "구성하다", "searchWord": "construct" }
items.problem: Two defects at once. (1) The primary sense is missing: OALD gives sense 1 as "to build or make something such as a road, building or machine" (건설하다, 짓다); 구성하다 is sense 2 (construct an argument). content/lessons/phonics/hv-64.json is the -struct root lesson, where construct sits in a row with structure, structural and construction, and this dictionary glosses structure 구조, construction 건설, constructive 건설적인 — so the building sense is unmistakably the one taught, and it is the one omitted. (2) "구성하다" is character-for-character identical to the gloss of constitute (line 775) — the only exact duplicate meaning string in the whole 160-entry range (verified by scripted comparison). A quiz or drill that shows 구성하다 and asks for the word therefore has two equally correct answers and no way to mark either wrong.
items.correction: "construct": "건설하다, 짓다; 구성하다". Leave constitute as "구성하다" (or tighten it to "구성하다, ~을 이루다") so the two headwords stop colliding.

items.original: "contain": { "meaning": "함유하다", "searchWord": "contain" }
items.problem: 함유하다 is a narrow Korean verb used of substances and ingredients (비타민을 함유하다, 나트륨을 함유한 식품). English contain is general: OALD defines it as having something inside it or as part of it, with examples ranging from drinks to documents ("The documents contain sensitive information"). "The box contains books" cannot be rendered 상자가 책을 함유하다 — it needs 담고 있다/포함하다. Giving only 함유하다 as the single gloss therefore makes the card wrong for most uses. content/lessons/phonics/hv-65.json is the -tain (hold) root lesson — contain | container | entertain | retain | sustain — and this dictionary glosses retain 보유하다, 간직하다 and container 용기, 그릇, so the narrow gloss also breaks the root link the lesson is built on.
items.correction: "contain": "포함하다, 담고 있다; (성분을) 함유하다"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 788; JSON key "content" (lessons hv-66, mv2-24)
items.original: "content": { "meaning": "내용", "searchWord": "content" }
items.problem: content is a heteronym with two parts of speech and two stress patterns: noun /ˈkɑːntent/ = 내용, adjective /kənˈtent/ = 만족한. Only the noun is given. In content/lessons/phonics/hv-66.json the grid runs ... | content | contentment | continent | ..., i.e. content is placed immediately before contentment, which this same dictionary glosses "만족" (line 789) — so the lesson is presenting the satisfaction sense while the card shows only 내용. Because VOCA lessons are audio wordgrids with a dictation block, the learner may hear the second-syllable stress /kənˈtent/ and see a gloss that does not correspond to it.
items.correction: "content": "내용, (복수형) 목차; (kənˈtent) 만족한"

items.original: "contract": { "meaning": "계약", "searchWord": "contract" }
items.problem: 계약 is correct and is the commonest noun sense, so this is an omission rather than an error — but it leaves the lesson broken. content/lessons/phonics/hv-69.json is the tract- (pull/draw) root lesson and opens with abstract | extract | contract | contraction, which this file glosses 추상적인 / 추출하다 / 계약 / 수축. The learner is therefore given a noun contraction = 수축 whose verb is nowhere to be found, and a headword whose gloss does not explain the card sitting next to it. contract also carries the stress-shift pattern (noun ˈcontract 계약 vs verb conˈtract 수축하다), which is material in an audio dictation lesson.
items.correction: "contract": "계약; (conˈtract) 수축하다, 줄어들다"

items.original: "contradict": { "meaning": "모순되다", "searchWord": "contradict" }
items.problem: Transitivity mismatch. contradict is transitive — OALD sense 1 is "to say that something that somebody else has said is wrong, and that the opposite is true", with the patterns contradict somebody / contradict something ("All evening her husband contradicted everything she said"; "You've just contradicted yourself"). Korean 모순되다 is intransitive and stative, so it cannot take that object: "He contradicted me" cannot be 그는 나를 모순되었다 — it requires 반박하다. The gloss covers only OALD's sense 2 (statements conflicting with each other). content/lessons/phonics/hv-07.json is the "against" prefix lesson — contrary | contradict | contradiction | contradictory, alongside counterattack, disagree, disapprove — where the speaking-against sense is exactly the point.
items.correction: "contradict": "반박하다, 부정하다 (contradict somebody ~의 말을 반박하다); (~와) 모순되다"

items.original: contrary	contrary	반대로	hv-07 mv2-35
items.problem: 반대로 is an adverb form in Korean, so the gloss implies 'contrary' is an adverb. The headword senses are adjective (반대되는, 반대의) and noun (the contrary = 정반대); 반대로 only renders the fixed phrases 'contrary to ~' and 'on the contrary'. In hv-07 the word sits with contradict / contradiction / contradictory / counterattack (content/lessons/phonics/hv-07.json), i.e. it is being taught as the contra- prefix adjective, and the adjective reading is the one the entry never shows.
items.correction: 반대되는, 반대의; (the ~) 정반대 (contrary to ~: ~와는 반대로 / on the contrary: 그와는 반대로)

items.original: convict	convict	죄수	hv-73
items.problem: 죄수 is a correct noun gloss, but the verb sense '유죄를 선고하다' is missing, and that is the sense that makes the lesson coherent: hv-73 groups convince / conviction / convict together (content/lessons/phonics/hv-73.json). With convince=설득하다, conviction=신념 and convict=죄수, the three related entries share no visible thread. 'convict' is also a stress-shift pair (noun ˈcon·vict vs verb con·ˈvict), which a noun-only gloss hides.
items.correction: 유죄를 선고하다; (명사) 죄수, 기결수

items.original: cooky	cooky	쿠키	mv3-06
items.problem: The gloss 쿠키 is right, but the headword 'cooky' is an archaic/rare variant of the standard spelling 'cookie', and the entry carries no note saying so. 'cookie' does not exist anywhere in voca_dictionary.json (checked: key absent), so the standard spelling of this very common everyday word is never shown to the learner. The word comes from the mv3-06 dictation wordgrid (content/lessons/phonics/mv3-06.json line 43), where it is presented for listening and spelling practice.
items.correction: 쿠키 (표준 철자는 cookie; cooky 는 드물게 쓰이는 옛 변이형)

items.original: corporation	corporation	법인	hv-25
items.problem: 법인 is a narrow legal-register term and is the only gloss given. The everyday sense a school learner meets — (대)기업, 회사, 주식회사, as in 'multinational corporations' — is missing, and it clashes with the sibling entry in the very same lesson, corporate => 기업의. hv-25 teaches the corp- (body) root: core / corps / corporate / corporation (content/lessons/phonics/hv-25.json).
items.correction: 기업, 회사, 주식회사; (법률) 법인

items.original: correspond	correspond	대응하다	hv-10
items.problem: Two of the three senses learners actually meet are missing: '일치하다, 부합하다' (correspond to/with the facts) and '서신을 주고받다'. The second omission is visible inside the dictionary itself, because the sibling entry correspondence is glossed 서신 — the noun is given a sense its own verb does not have. The single gloss chosen, 대응하다, is also the most ambiguous option in Korean: its ordinary reading is 'to respond to / cope with', which is 'respond' (already glossed 응답하다 in this file), not 'correspond'.
items.correction: 일치하다, 부합하다; 해당하다; 서신을 주고받다

items.original: cotton	cotton	면화	mv3-29
items.problem: 면화 is the raw crop/fibre (the plant), while in mv3-29 'cotton' sits directly beside 'silk' in the wordgrid (…strategy, silk, cotton, preface), i.e. it is being taught as a fabric. The dictionary glosses silk as 비단, 실크; the parallel gloss for cotton would be 면, 무명, and that sense is absent.
items.correction: 면, 무명; 목화, 면화

items.original: cure	cure	치료법	hv-26
items.problem: Noun-only gloss. The verb sense 치료하다, 낫게 하다 is co-primary and is what the adjacent entry in the same lesson is derived from: hv-26 pairs cure with curable (치료할 수 있는), an adjective formed from the verb.
items.correction: 치료하다, 낫게 하다; (명사) 치료법, 치료약

items.original: cylinder	cylinder	실린더	mv2-21
items.problem: mv2-21 is a geometric-shapes lesson. Its wordgrid is pyramid / square / circle / rectangle / cylinder / oval / spiral / sphere / cube / triangle, and every other shape in that grid is glossed with a Korean shape name (square=정사각형; 광장, circle=원, rectangle=직사각형, triangle=삼각형, sphere=구체, oval=타원형, spiral=나선형). Only 'cylinder' is glossed with the transliteration 실린더, which in Korean names the engine/hydraulic part, not the solid. The geometric sense the lesson actually teaches (원기둥/원통) is absent from the entry.
items.correction: 원기둥, 원통 (기계 부품: 실린더)

items.original: degree	degree	정도	hv-34 mv2-40 mv3-22
items.problem: Only the 'extent' sense is given. The two senses a Korean middle/high-school learner meets most often are missing: 학위 (academic degree) and (온도·각도의) 도. hv-34 is the grad-/gress- root lesson (graduate, graduation, gradual, progress, congress, degree), where 학위 is precisely the sense that ties 'degree' to 'graduate' — and the dictionary already glosses graduate as 졸업하다 and temperature as 온도, so the link is left broken.
items.correction: 정도; 학위; (온도·각도의) 도

items.original: delegate	delegate	대리인	hv-37
items.problem: The verb sense — (권한·일을) 위임하다, 맡기다 — is missing entirely, and it is the sense that appears most in reading ('delegate tasks to your team'). The noun gloss chosen is also the weakest of the standard set: a delegate is primarily a 대표(자)·사절 sent to a conference, whereas 대리인 means a legal agent/proxy. The same dictionary already assigns 대리인 to 'agent' and 대표 to 'representative', so this entry collides with 'agent' and leaves the true gloss 대표 attached to a different word. Like 'convict', delegate is a noun/verb stress pair, which a noun-only gloss hides.
items.correction: (권한·일을) 위임하다, 맡기다; (명사) 대표(자), 사절

items.original: "desperate": { "meaning": "절망적인", "searchWord": "desperate" }
items.problem: 절망적인 is correct, but the dominant modern sense - 필사적인 / 절박한 (be desperate to do, a desperate attempt, desperate need) - is missing. Dictionaries list 절망적인, 필사적인, 자포자기의 together.
items.correction: "절망적인; 필사적인, 절박한"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1004; JSON keys "detective" (lessons hv-66, mv2-32, mv3-22)
items.original: "detective": { "meaning": "형사", "searchWord": "detective" }
items.problem: 형사 is not wrong, but 탐정 is missing, and 탐정 is the sense Korean middle-schoolers overwhelmingly meet first (detective story/novel, Sherlock Holmes). Dictionaries list both (형사, 수사관, 탐정).
items.correction: "탐정, 형사"

items.original: "diagram": { "meaning": "다이어그램", "searchWord": "diagram" }
items.problem: The 'meaning' is a Hangul transliteration of the English headword, not a Korean meaning - the card answers 'diagram' with 'diagram'. Standard glosses are 도표, 도식, 도해. (Same non-gloss pattern exists elsewhere in the file, e.g. table=테이블, restaurant=레스토랑, so it is worth a sweep beyond this slice.)
items.correction: "도표, 도식"

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv lines 1016 and 1017; JSON keys "dialog(ue)" (lesson mv3-14) and "dialogue" (lesson hv-06)
items.original: "dialog(ue)": { "meaning": "대화", "searchWord": "dialogue" }  …  "dialogue": { "meaning": "대화", "searchWord": "dialogue" }
items.problem: Two dictionary entries for the same word with the same meaning and the same searchWord. Both are live: content/lessons/phonics/mv3-14.json prints the headword as "dialog(ue)" while content/lessons/phonics/hv-06.json prints it as "dialogue". Meanings are currently identical, so nothing displays wrong today - the risk is drift (editing one gloss silently leaves the other stale) and an inconsistent headword across courses.
items.correction: Keep one canonical entry - "dialogue" - and have mv3-14 use the same headword, or, if the mv3 wordgrid text must stay as "dialog(ue)" (changing lesson English text destroys that clip's Azure audio per AGENTS.md), leave both keys but add a sync check to the dictionary lint so the two glosses can never diverge.

items.original: "dining-room": { "meaning": "식당", "searchWord": "dining-room" }
items.problem: The hyphenated headword is a dated/British form. Merriam-Webster and current usage head the word as two words, "dining room"; the hyphen survives mainly in older OED-style British printing. The learner is being drilled - including in dictation - on a spelling that is now marked in exams and writing.
items.correction: Headword "dining room"; gloss "(집 안의) 식당". Caution: content/lessons/phonics/mv3-31.json prints the word as "dining-room", so the lesson text must change too, and per AGENTS.md changing English lesson text invalidates that clip's hash - regenerate with scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: "disappearance": { "meaning": "실종", "searchWord": "disappearance" }
items.problem: 실종 is only the missing-person sense. The general noun is 사라짐/소멸/소실. hv-07.json places disappear and disappearance side by side to drill the verb-to-noun pair, and the verb is glossed 사라지다 (line 1050) - so the noun gloss breaks the pair it is supposed to teach.
items.correction: "사라짐, 소멸; (사람의) 실종"

items.original: "distinct": { "meaning": "별개의", "searchWord": "distinct" }
items.problem: 별개의 is a genuine but secondary sense. Dictionaries lead with 뚜렷한 / 분명한 / 명백한 (a distinct smell, a distinct improvement), which is the sense a middle/high-school learner meets most often. The 'separate' ground is already covered elsewhere in this same file (distinction=구별, separate="분리하다; 별도의"), so the perceptual sense is exactly the one left out.
items.correction: "뚜렷한, 분명한; 별개의"

items.original: "distress": { "meaning": "고민", "searchWord": "distress" }
items.problem: 고민 means worrying/agonising over a problem. distress is severe mental or physical 고통·괴로움, and secondarily 곤경/조난 (a ship in distress, a distress signal). Dictionaries lead with (정신적) 고통, 괴로움; 고민 appears only far down the list. The gloss badly understates the word's strength.
items.correction: "(정신적) 고통, 괴로움; 곤경"

items.original: "distribution": { "meaning": "유통", "searchWord": "distribution" }
items.problem: 유통 is a narrow commerce/logistics sense. The core senses for a school learner are 분배 (distribution of wealth), 배포, and 분포 (population distribution). It also contradicts its own verb entry in the same lesson: distribute = 배포하다 (line 1097), so the noun and verb look unrelated.
items.correction: "분배, 배포; 분포"

items.original: "district": { "meaning": "지구", "searchWord": "district" }
items.problem: 지구(地區) is technically correct, but as a bare one-word gloss with no hanja and no context it reads as 지구(地球, the Earth) to a Korean school learner - and this very file glosses earth as "지구" (key "earth"). Two different English words then carry the identical answer string in the same card/quiz pool.
items.correction: "지역, 구역"

items.original: "division": { "meaning": "구분", "searchWord": "division" }
items.problem: 구분 is not a standard gloss for division (dictionaries give 분할, 분배, 분열, 구획, 나눗셈, 부서/학부), and in this same file it is visually indistinguishable from distinction = "구별" (line 1089). It also drops the verb link to its own lesson partner divide = 나누다 (line 1105).
items.correction: "분할, 나누기(나눗셈); 부서"

items.original: downstairs	downstairs	아래층	mv1-38
items.problem: 롱맨은 downstairs 를 부사부터 싣습니다('towards or on a lower floor of a building'). 명사 용법(the downstairs)도 있으므로 '아래층'이 틀린 것은 아니지만, 주된 품사인 부사 뜻이 없고 같은 파일의 동류 단어 처리(abroad 해외에서, indoors 실내에서, aboard (탈것에) 타고)와도 어긋납니다. mv1 은 가장 초급 단계라 첫인상이 그대로 굳습니다.
items.correction: 아래층에(서), 아래층으로; 아래층

items.original: downtown	downtown	시내	mv3-37
items.problem: downtown 은 부사('to or in the centre or main business area of a town')와 명사 앞에만 쓰는 형용사이며, 롱맨에는 명사 용법 자체가 없습니다. 그런데 뜻이 명사 '시내' 하나뿐입니다. 같은 파일이 이 부류의 부사는 부사답게 풀고 있습니다(abroad 해외에서, indoors 실내에서, aboard (탈것에) 타고, overseas 해외의; 해외로).
items.correction: 시내로, 시내에; 시내의 (go downtown 시내에 가다)

items.original: dread	dread	공포	mv3-05
items.problem: 롱맨은 dread 를 동사('to feel anxious or worried about something that is going to happen')부터 싣고 빈도 표시도 동사에만 붙어 있는데, 뜻풀이는 명사 '공포' 하나뿐입니다. mv3-05 격자의 같은 줄은 gamble(도박하다)·reverse(뒤집다)·scream(비명을 지르다)·dash(돌진하다)처럼 동사 위주이고, 이 파일은 두 품사를 함께 쓰는 단어를 '동사; 명사' 순으로 적는 관례(scream '비명을 지르다; 비명', reverse '뒤집다; 반대의')를 이미 갖고 있습니다.
items.correction: 몹시 두려워하다; 공포, 두려움

items.original: due	due	~하기로 되어 있는; ~때문에	hv-27
items.problem: 둘째 뜻 '~때문에'는 단어 due 가 아니라 숙어 due to 의 뜻입니다. due 단독으로는 '때문에'라는 뜻이 없습니다(롱맨 형용사 뜻: 예정된, (돈을) 지불해야 하는, 정당한 — '때문에'는 due to 라는 별도 표제항). 표제어 뜻으로 그냥 '~때문에'를 병기하면 to 가 필수라는 정보가 사라집니다. 또 hv-27 은 due·duty·duty-free 가 한 줄에 모인 어근 묶음인데, 돈을 지불해야 한다는 due 의 뜻이 빠져 duty(세금)와의 연결도 끊깁니다.
items.correction: ~할 예정인, ~하기로 되어 있는; (돈을) 지불해야 하는; [due to] ~때문에

items.original: dull	dull	둔한	mv2-15 mv3-01
items.problem: 유일한 뜻 '둔한'은 롱맨 사전에서 old-fashioned(옛투)로 표시된 '머리가 둔한' 뜻입니다. 빈도 표시(●●○)가 붙은 주된 뜻 두 가지 — '지루한, 따분한(not interesting or exciting)'과 '(색·빛이) 흐릿한(not bright or shiny)' — 그리고 '(칼날이) 무딘'이 모두 빠졌습니다. 특히 mv3-01 은 형용사 격자이고 같은 격자 안에 sharp(날카로운)가 함께 들어 있어, 여기서 학습자가 만나는 dull 은 sharp 의 반대인 '무딘' 쪽인데 그 뜻이 없습니다.
items.correction: 지루한, 따분한; (칼날이) 무딘; (색·빛이) 흐릿한

items.original: dumb	dumb	어리석은; 말을 못 하는	mv2-01 mv3-01
items.problem: 두 뜻 모두 사용역(register) 표시가 없습니다. Wiktionary 기준 '말을 못 하는'은 dated(옛투)이며 오늘날 사람에게 쓰면 모욕으로 받아들여집니다(현대어는 mute). '어리석은'에 해당하는 뜻도 informal, derogatory(구어·비하) 표시가 붙은 말입니다. 중·고등학생이 예문 없이 이 두 줄만 보고 외우는 구조여서 경고가 필요합니다.
items.correction: (구어) 멍청한, 바보 같은; (옛투) 말을 못 하는 ※ 사람에게 쓰면 모욕적

items.original: duplicate	duplicate	중복	hv-10 mv3-19
items.problem: duplicate 의 핵심 뜻인 '복제하다/복사하다'(동사)와 '사본, 복제품'(명사)이 통째로 빠지고, 유일한 뜻이 '중복'입니다. 영어 duplicate 에는 '겹침·중복(redundancy/overlap)'이라는 명사 뜻이 없습니다(Wiktionary: 명사 'an identical copy', 동사 'to make a copy of'). 게다가 hv-10 은 billion·dual·twist·twilight·tribe·triple·trivial 처럼 '둘/여럿'을 뜻하는 어근 묶음이라, du-(둘) → '똑같이 하나 더 만든다'는 연결이 '중복'이라는 뜻풀이로는 전혀 드러나지 않습니다.
items.correction: 복제하다, 복사하다; 사본, 복제품; 똑같은

items.original: dye	dye	염료	mv2-38 mv3-16
items.problem: 롱맨에서 명사(a substance you use to change the colour)와 동사(to give something a different colour using a dye)의 빈도 표시가 ●●○ 로 동일한데, 뜻풀이에는 명사 '염료'만 있고 동사 '염색하다'가 없습니다. 특히 mv3-16 에서 dye 가 들어간 줄은 scratch(긁다)·stare(응시하다)·gaze(응시하다)·scare(겁주다)로 동사가 대부분이라, 그 자리에서 요구되는 품사가 빠져 있습니다.
items.correction: 염색하다; 염료, 염색약

items.original: either	either	어느 쪽이든	mv1-11 mv3-08
items.problem: mv3-08 은 together·rather·hastily·suddenly·perhaps·probably 처럼 전부 부사만 모은 격자이고, either 는 그 안에서 neither·besides 와 나란히 제시됩니다. 즉 이 레슨에서 학습자가 만나는 either 는 부정문 끝에 붙는 부사 '~도 또한 (아니다)'(I haven't seen it either)입니다. 그런데 뜻은 한정사·대명사 뜻인 '어느 쪽이든' 하나뿐이라 정작 레슨이 가르치는 용법이 없습니다.
items.correction: (둘 중) 어느 하나(의); [부정문 끝에서] ~도 또한 (아니다)

items.original: embarrassing	embarrassing	창피한	hv-19
items.problem: embarrassing 은 '남을 창피하게 만드는(making you feel ashamed, nervous, or uncomfortable)' 쪽인데, 한국어 '창피한'은 창피함을 느끼는 사람 쪽(embarrassed)으로 먼저 읽힙니다. 같은 파일은 이 -ing/-ed 구분을 다른 단어에서는 정확히 지키고 있습니다: confusing '헷갈리게 하는' / confused '(사람이) 혼란스러워하는'. 또 hv-19 한 레슨 안의 세 파생어가 서로 다른 어근으로 풀려 연결이 보이지 않습니다(embarrass 난처하게 하다 / embarrassing 창피한 / embarrassment 당혹스러움).
items.correction: 창피하게 만드는, 난처하게 하는

items.original: emigrate	emigrate	이주하다	hv-42
items.problem: emigrate 의 정의는 '자기 나라를 떠나 다른 나라에 살러 가다(to leave your own country in order to live in another country)'로, '떠나는 방향'이 뜻의 핵심입니다. '이주하다'만으로는 방향이 사라지고, 같은 사전 파일의 immigrate('이민하다')와 한국어로 구별이 전혀 되지 않습니다. 같은 가족인 emigrant 는 '(다른 나라로 떠나는) 이민자', immigrant 는 '(다른 나라에서 온) 이민자, 이주민'처럼 괄호로 방향을 명시해 두었으므로, 동사만 관례에서 벗어나 있습니다.
items.correction: (자기 나라를 떠나 다른 나라로) 이민 가다, 이주하다

items.original: emigration	emigration	이주	hv-42
items.problem: emigrate 와 같은 문제입니다. '이주'만으로는 '자국을 떠나 나가는 것'이라는 방향이 드러나지 않고, 같은 파일의 immigration('이민')과 한국어로 구분되지 않습니다. hv-42 격자에는 emigrant, emigration, emigrate 가 모두 들어 있는데 명사 emigrant 만 방향 표시가 있어 한 레슨 안에서도 표기가 어긋납니다.
items.correction: (자국을 떠나는) 이민, 국외 이주

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 5534-5536 (key "expedition", meaning on line 5535); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1345; lesson hv-49
items.problem: 원정대 names the GROUP of people. The primary senses are the journey itself: "An important or long journey, for example a march or a voyage" and "A trip, especially a long one, made by a person or a group of people for a specific purpose"; "the group of people making such excursion" is only the fourth sense. The gloss substitutes a secondary, collective-noun reading for the core one and gives the learner no way back to it — the word stands alone in the hv-49 ped-/pel- root grid (pedestrian, compel, expel) with no sentence context.
items.correction: 탐험, 원정(여행)  (원정대는 부차적 의미)

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 438-440 (key "exposition", meaning on line 439); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1363; lesson hv-04
items.problem: 박람회 is a real but later sense ("An exhibition, especially of goods, artwork or cultural displays to the public"). The sense that ties the word to its own hv-04 word family — the grid is expose / exposure / exposition — and that a high-school reader meets in expository writing is "the act or process of declaring or describing something through either speech or writing" = 설명, 해설. That sense is missing, so the family card teaches 노출하다 / 노출 / 박람회 as if they were related.
items.correction: 설명, 해설; 박람회

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 474-476 (key "extraordinarily", meaning on line 475); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1378; lesson hv-04
items.problem: The adjective and its adverb sit side by side in the same hv-04 grid (extraordinary, extraordinarily) but their glosses do not correspond: 특별한 vs 유난히. 유난히 also understates "to an extraordinary degree" — the natural adverb glosses are 엄청나게, 대단히, 비범하게. Not wrong enough to mislead on its own, but it breaks the derivation the lesson exists to teach.
items.correction: 엄청나게, 대단히  (extraordinary를 "비범한, 대단한"으로 고칠 때 한 쌍으로 함께 수정)

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 470-472 (key "extraordinary", meaning on line 471); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1379; lesson hv-04
items.problem: 특별한 is the Korean for "special" — and this same dictionary glosses `special` as 특별한 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 3305), so the two English words are presented as interchangeable. extraordinary means "out of the ordinary; exceptional; unusual" and "remarkably good": 비범한, 보통이 아닌, 대단한. The force of the word (well beyond ordinary) is lost, and 특별한 matches only the marginal "special or supernumerary" reading (as in "ambassador extraordinary").
items.correction: 비범한, 보통이 아닌; 대단한

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 13614-13616 (key "faint", meaning on line 13615); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1394; lesson mv2-28
items.problem: 희미한 is a genuine adjective sense ("barely perceptible; not bright, or loud, or sharp"), so this is not an error of fact — but the verb "to lose consciousness" (기절하다) is the use a Korean middle schooler overwhelmingly meets ("She fainted."), and the card never shows it. The mv2-28 grid gives no sentence context to disambiguate, so the learner has no other route to the verb.
items.correction: 희미한; 기절하다

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 13758-13760 (key "fasten", meaning on line 13759); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1417; lesson mv2-32
items.problem: 고정하다 is a defensible reading of "to attach or connect in a secure manner", but it does not produce natural Korean for the use every learner meets — "Fasten your seat belt" is 안전벨트를 매다, never 안전벨트를 고정하다. The dictionary's own example use is the seat belt one, and the gloss omits 매다/잠그다 entirely.
items.correction: 매다, 잠그다; 단단히 고정하다

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 12126-12128 (key "favo(u)r", meaning on line 12127); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1425; lesson mv1-34
items.problem: 호의 is the "goodwill; benevolent regard" sense, which is the SECOND sense. The first is "A kind or helpful deed; an instance of voluntarily assisting (someone)" — 부탁 / 도움 — the one in "Can you do me a favor?", a fixed phrase in Korean middle-school textbooks. The gloss is not wrong, but it omits the sense the lesson's learners actually meet. (The key/searchWord pair itself is fine: favo(u)r -> favour follows the file's convention, cf. colo(u)r->colour line 637, hono(u)r->honour line 1717.)
items.correction: 부탁; 호의

items.locator: content/voca_dictionary.json lines 12978-12980 (key "favor", meaning on line 12979); voca-dictionary.tsv line 1426; lesson mv2-13
items.problem: Same gap as the favo(u)r entry, in the American-spelling twin used by mv2-13: the gloss gives only 호의 (goodwill, the second sense) and omits the primary "a kind or helpful deed" = 부탁, the sense in "do me a favor". Filed separately because it is a separate record in the JSON — fixing one spelling and not the other would leave mv1-34 and mv2-13 teaching different things.
items.correction: 부탁; 호의

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1443; JSON key "few", meaning field; lesson mv1-12
items.original: (수가) 적은, 몇몇의
items.problem: The second gloss 몇몇의 belongs to 'a few', not to bare 'few'. Bare 'few' is semantically negative — 'not many / hardly any' — while 'a few' is affirmative ('some'). Wiktionary's usage note states it directly: 'Few alone emphasises smallness of number, while a few emphasises some', with the contrast 'He's a dull man with few ideas' vs 'He's a clever man with a few ideas'. The card in mv1-12 shows the word alone (grid row: life, near, week, few, often, room), with no article and no note, so the learner has no way to see that 몇몇의 requires 'a'. The first gloss '(수가) 적은' is right; the trouble is that the entry also hands the learner the opposite-polarity reading.
items.correction: (수가) 적은, 거의 없는  ※ a few = 몇몇의, 조금 있는

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1476; JSON key "floor", meaning field; lessons mv1-19, mv2-08
items.original: 바닥
items.problem: 바닥 is correct but is only half the word. Wiktionary sense 8 is 'A storey/story of a building. For years we lived on the third floor.' — the 층 sense, which is the one Korean learners meet in 'the third floor', 'What floor?', lift announcements and every building description. The mv1-19 grid is explicitly a house/building lesson (living room, build, office, clean, wash, telephone … floor), which is where 층 belongs. The dictionary has ceiling=천장 (line 541), roof=지붕 (line 3050) and stair=계단 (line 3339) but no other entry supplying 층, so the sense is missing from the course entirely.
items.correction: 바닥; (건물의) 층

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1492; JSON key "force", meaning field; lessons hv-33, mv2-37, mv3-09
items.original: 힘
items.problem: The verb sense is missing. Wiktionary's first verb sense is 'To make someone or something do something, often regardless of their will' — 강요하다, the force + 목적어 + to부정사 pattern that middle/high-school reading and grammar drills lean on. As it stands the gloss is also non-discriminating inside this very dictionary: power (line 2684) = 힘 and strength (line 3385) = 힘, so three different headwords carry the identical one-word gloss and the card tells the learner nothing about what makes 'force' different from the other two. Adding 강요하다 both fills the real gap and separates it from power/strength.
items.correction: 힘; 강요하다

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1515; JSON key "found", meaning field; lessons hv-33, mv2-37
items.original: 설립하다
items.problem: 'found' is the highest-traffic homograph in this whole range and the entry carries no note about it. Wiktionary lists two separate etymologies: Etymology 1 is 'simple past and past participle of find', Etymology 2 is the verb 'to start (an institution or organization)'. 설립하다 is right for hv-33, which is the fund-/found- root lesson (profound, found, foundation, fund, fundamental), but the word also appears in mv2-37, a general list whose neighbours are ordinary base-form content words (handle, ancestor, found, section, sacrifice, flame). 'find' is itself taught in this course at mv1-02 (line 1455, '찾다, 발견하다'), so the learner already owns the other reading and gets no signal connecting the two.
items.correction: 설립하다 (※ find의 과거·과거분사형인 found와 철자가 같음)

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1530; JSON key "from", meaning field; lesson mv1-01
items.original: 에서
items.problem: Not wrong, but thin and inconsistently formatted for a preposition. Korean 에서 renders both 'from' (서울에서 왔다) and 'at/in' (학교에서 공부한다), so the bare particle does not pin down which English preposition it is teaching; adding 로부터 does. The formatting is also inconsistent with how this same file marks other prepositions: about (line 10) '~에 대하여; 약' and over (line 2470) '~위에; 끝난' carry the ~ placeholder, while from (1530), by (491) '에 의해', with (3872) '와', under (3689) '아래' and into (1922) '안으로' do not. from is in mv1-01, the very first lesson of the course, so it is the first thing a paying learner sees.
items.correction: ~에서, ~로부터

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1540; JSON key "fur", meaning field; lessons mv2-40, mv3-32
items.original: 모피
items.problem: 모피 is the processed-pelt/clothing-material sense only, and in Korean it connotes a fur coat almost exclusively. The primary sense of 'fur' — the hairy coat on a living animal, i.e. (동물의) 털 — is absent. Wiktionary gives first 'The hairy coat of various mammal species, especially when fine, soft and thick', and only then 'The hairy skins of animals used as a material for clothing'. The mv3-32 grid is full of animals (bone, wolf, lamb, turtle, owl in row 1; fur in row 3), so the lesson's own word list points at the animal-coat sense the gloss omits.
items.correction: (동물의) 털; 모피

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1576; JSON key "German", meaning field; lesson mv1-02
items.original: 독일의; 독일인
items.problem: The language sense 독일어 is missing. Wiktionary gives both: common noun 'A native or inhabitant of Germany' and proper noun 'An Indo-European language, primarily spoken in Germany, Austria …'. The omission is visible inside a single grid row: mv1-02 row 5 is 'much, if, English, Korean, German, Japanese', and in the same dictionary English (line 1235) is glossed 영어 — the language and nothing else — while German (1576), Japanese (1956) and Korean (1990) are glossed '…의; …인' with no language. Four nationality words taught side by side in one row, split across two incompatible gloss patterns.
items.correction: 독일의; 독일인; 독일어

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 1598; JSON key "good-bye", meaning field; lesson mv1-07
items.original: 안녕
items.problem: 안녕 is bidirectional in Korean — Wiktionary lists it as both '(informal, casual) hello, hey' and '(informal, casual) good-bye' — so as a one-word gloss it does not actually tell the learner that this word is the parting greeting. The ambiguity is made worse by the neighbouring entry: hello (line 1688) is glossed 안녕하세요. Side by side, 안녕하세요 / 안녕 reads as a formal-vs-casual pair of the SAME greeting rather than as hello vs goodbye, which is the distinction the two cards are supposed to teach. mv1-07 shows the word alone in a grid (music, trip, thousand, hundred, ten, good-bye), so nothing disambiguates it.
items.correction: 잘 가, 안녕히 가세요 (헤어질 때 하는 인사)

items.original: grade	grade	등급	mv1-39 mv2-36 mv3-21
items.problem: The gloss gives only 등급 (a class/rating). The two school senses — 학년 (a year of schooling) and 성적 (a mark for work) — are absent, and those are the senses a Korean middle/high-school learner actually meets. mv3-21's grid row is entirely school vocabulary: "stress, grade, semester, score, danger, exclaim" (content/lessons/phonics/mv3-21.json), where grade can only be 성적/학년. Phonics lessons are word grids with no sentence context, so this one line is the whole meaning the card teaches.
items.correction: 학년; 성적; 등급

items.original: grass	grass	잔디	mv1-23 mv2-07
items.problem: 잔디 is turf or a mown lawn specifically. The primary sense of grass is the plant in general — 풀 — which is what the word means in the sentences beginners meet (Cows eat grass; grass grows). Both lessons are beginner grids (mv1-23 "grass, meaning, leg, cousin, amount, neighbo(u)r"; mv2-07 "thank, fall, half, wish, begin, grass") with no context to recover the wider sense from.
items.correction: 풀; 잔디

items.original: grave	grave	무덤	hv-35 mv2-34 mv3-18
items.problem: Only the noun 무덤 is given; the adjective sense 중대한/심각한 is missing, yet two of the three lessons need the adjective. hv-35's row is "disgrace, grave, gravity, grieve, grief, habit" (content/lessons/phonics/hv-35.json) — an hv root-family grid in which grave stands next to gravity, both from Latin gravis "heavy, serious"; the burial-place noun is an unrelated homograph from Old English græf. mv3-18's row is "religious, valuable, harmful, grave, elementary, charming" — every other word in it is an adjective.
items.correction: 중대한, 심각한; 무덤

items.original: gray(grey)	graygrey	회색	mv3-01
items.problem: The searchWord is "graygrey", which is not a word — the brackets were simply deleted. Every other bracketed headword in this range carries a real alternative spelling in that field (hono(u)r→honour line 1717, humo(u)r→humour line 1744), as do colo(u)r→colour and dialog(ue)→dialogue elsewhere in the file. The stored non-word has already had an effect: scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs:284 adds entry.searchWord to the Azure clip list, and src/lib/vocaSpeech.ts rewrites only the bracketed headword, not "graygrey" — so an Ava clip of the non-word was synthesized and is on disk at public/audio/azure-ava/v1/8-13da5e45d3fb7bdb.mp3. The same string is also the collocation lookup key (src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:256 via src/components/PhonicsLearningView.tsx:429).
items.correction: searchWord should be "gray", matching VOCA_SPEECH_FORMS["gray(grey)"] = "gray" in src/lib/vocaSpeech.ts:41. (The neighbouring entry autumn(=fall)→"autumn=fall" has the same defect but falls outside this line range.)

items.original: hate	hate	미워하다; 증오	mv2-26 mv3-26
items.problem: 미워하다 and 증오 are hatred directed at a person. The everyday sense — 몹시 싫어하다, used of things and activities (I hate carrots / I hate waiting) — is the one a middle-school learner meets and produces far more often, and it is missing. The mv2-26 row is "similar, trick, hate, fear, blaze, means" and mv3-26 is "hate, frighten, entire, primary, prohibition, participate"; neither forces the person-directed reading.
items.correction: 몹시 싫어하다, 미워하다; 증오

items.original: heart	heart	심장	mv1-17 mv2-19 mv3-28
items.problem: Only the organ 심장 is given; the figurative 마음 sense is missing even though it is the more frequent one in ordinary English and in the mv3-28 row, "security, heart, nature, coast, tongue, trust", where heart sits with trust. The same entry also supports heartily (line 1683, 진심으로), whose connection to heart is invisible if heart means only 심장.
items.correction: 심장; 마음

items.locator: key "historical" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 1704 (pair partner "historic" on line 1703)
items.original: historical	historical	역사적인	hv-17
items.problem: hv-17 is a confusable-pairs lesson — its rows are "healthful, healthy, disinterested, uninterested, envious, enviable" and "momentary, momentous, historic, historical, intelligible, intelligent" (content/lessons/phonics/hv-17.json). The dictionary glosses historic as 역사적으로 중요한 and historical as 역사적인. But 역사적인 is the ordinary Korean rendering of *historic* (역사적인 순간 = a historic moment), so the two cards do not draw the distinction the lesson exists to teach, and the label of the stronger word is handed to the weaker one. historical means "of recorded history / that actually existed in the past", with no implication of importance.
items.correction: 역사(상)의, 역사에 관한; 실제 역사에 있었던

items.locator: keys "hono(u)r" and "honor" — voca-dictionary.tsv lines 1717-1718; keys "humo(u)r" and "humor" — lines 1744-1745
items.original: hono(u)r	honour	명예	mv3-13 / honor	honor	명예	mv1-36 mv2-36 ||| humo(u)r	humour	유머	mv1-37 / humor	humor	유머	mv2-19
items.problem: Each of these two words exists as two separate headwords with identical Korean glosses, because the lesson grids spell the word two ways: "honor" in mv1-36 ("death, knock, excellent, attack, enemy, honor") and mv2-36, but "hono(u)r" in mv3-13; "humor" in mv2-19, but "humo(u)r" in mv1-37. The dictionary faithfully mirrors an inconsistency in the content, so the same word reaches the learner as two different cards.
items.correction: Settle one spelling convention per word across the phonics grids — the bracketed form is the one src/lib/vocaSpeech.ts already supports (VOCA_SPEECH_FORMS has "hono(u)r" and "humo(u)r") — and keep a single dictionary entry for each.

items.locator: key "hostess" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 1728 (pair partner "host" on line 1727)
items.original: hostess	hostess	안주인	hv-36
items.problem: host is glossed "주인, 주최자" but hostess only "안주인" (the lady of the house). The 여성 주최자/진행자 half of the meaning is dropped, and 안주인 reads as dated Korean. The two words sit side by side in the same hv-36 row — "inheritance, heritage, heir, host, hostess, hostile" (content/lessons/phonics/hv-36.json) — so the mismatch is visible within one grid.
items.correction: 여주인; (여성) 주최자

items.original: hot	hot	뜨거운	mv1-09 mv2-06
items.problem: Only 뜨거운 (of an object) is given. The weather/body sense — 더운 — is missing, and it cannot be derived from 뜨거운, because 날씨가 뜨겁다 is not Korean. mv2-06's row is "pretty, hot, ice, wet, sound, clock", a temperature-and-weather context where 더운 is at least as likely as 뜨거운.
items.correction: 뜨거운; (날씨가) 더운

items.original: human	human	인간의	mv1-40
items.problem: The gloss 인간의 marks the word as an adjective only. The noun 인간/사람 is missing, although it is at least as common and is the form beginners use. The file's own convention elsewhere in this range is to carry both parts of speech in one gloss — "guard 지키다; 경비원" (line 1637), "handle 다루다; 손잡이" (1654), "horn 뿔; 경적" (1722) — so this entry is also inconsistent with its neighbours.
items.correction: 인간, 사람; 인간의

items.original: reproduction | 재생산
items.problem: The main senses of 'reproduction' are biological reproduction (번식, 생식) and copying or a copy (복제, 복제품). '재생산' is a narrow economics term. The etymology card for 'reproduce' in the same lesson says '복제하다/번식하다' (vocaUtils.ts:105), so the gloss and the card disagree, and the most frequent exam sense (biology) is absent.
items.correction: 번식, 생식; 복제(품)

items.locator: hv-05 row 4 col 1 alike (Q19, English-to-Korean) and row 4 col 5 akin; dictionary keys "alike" (line 550) and "akin" (line 566); alike also appears in mv2-10
items.original: alike | 똑같이 ; akin | 비슷한
items.problem: 'alike' is first an adjective meaning similar ('The twins look alike'). The adverb sense ('똑같이', as in 'employees and customers alike') comes second, and the gloss gives only that. In the same lesson akin is glossed '비슷한', which is exactly alike's adjective meaning. Q19 asks for the best Korean meaning of 'alike' and can offer '비슷한' as a distractor. A learner who knows the main sense picks it and is marked wrong. The Step 4 drill can also show 'alike = 비슷한' and expect '불일치'.
items.correction: alike: 비슷한; 똑같이. akin: (~와) 유사한, 관련된 (akin to). If both glosses keep 비슷한, the shared segment trips the R-7 rule, so either reword akin or make the distractor filter work on segments.

items.locator: hv-05 row 4 col 3 (quiz Q21, English-to-Korean); dictionary key "accustom" (line 558)
items.original: accustom | 익숙해지다
items.problem: 'accustom' is transitive: 'to make familiar', used as 'accustom oneself/someone to' or 'be accustomed to'. The gloss '익숙해지다' is an intransitive 'become used to', which invites the error '*I accustomed to the noise'.
items.correction: 익숙하게 하다 (accustom oneself to / be accustomed to: ~에 익숙해지다)

items.original: array | 배열
items.problem: Learner dictionaries give the main sense of 'array' as 'a group or collection of things or people, often one that is large or impressive', as in 'a wide/vast array of' (다양한, 다수의). '배열' (an ordered arrangement, or the IT/maths term) is secondary.
items.correction: 다수, 모음 (a wide array of: 다양한 ~); 배열

items.original: disappearance | 실종
items.problem: The main senses are vanishing or ceasing to exist (사라짐, 소멸), as in 'the disappearance of species' or 'of coiled phone cords'. '실종' (a person going missing) is Wiktionary sense 3. The verb above it is glossed 사라지다, so the noun should carry that sense too.
items.correction: 사라짐, 소멸; 실종

items.locator: hv-10 row 1 col 2 (quiz Q2, Korean-to-English); dictionary key "duplicate" (voca_dictionary.json line 1082); the same gloss appears in mv3-19 row 5 col 6
items.original: duplicate | 중복
items.problem: 'duplicate' is a verb (복제하다, 복사하다), an adjective (똑같은, 사본의) and a count noun meaning an identical copy (사본). The abstract noun '중복' (overlap, redundancy) translates 'duplication', not 'duplicate'. Q2 shows '[ 중복 ]' and expects 'duplicate', which reinforces the mismatch.
items.correction: 복제하다; 사본; 똑같은. Because the dictionary is shared, this also fixes mv3-19.

items.locator: hv-10 row 2 col 3 compose (Q9) next to row 2 col 5 composition; dictionary key "compose" (line 1110)
items.original: compose | 작곡하다 ; composition | 구성
items.problem: Wiktionary's first senses of 'compose' are to make up or constitute (구성하다), as in the very common 'be composed of ~로 구성되다'. The gloss gives only 작곡하다, while the derived word in the same row is glossed 구성, so the family link is lost.
items.correction: 구성하다; 작곡하다 (be composed of: ~로 구성되다)

items.locator: hv-13 row 1 col 1 (content/lessons/phonics/hv-13.json). Dictionary key "appearance". The same gloss is shown in hv-48 row 1 col 2 and mv2-31 row 2 col 3.
items.original: appearance = 외관
items.problem: 외관 (external look, mostly of objects and buildings) is correct but narrow. It leaves out the two senses learners meet most: 외모/겉모습 (a person's looks) and 출현/등장/출연 (the act of appearing, as in 'the appearance of new species' or 'make an appearance'). Engoo lists both '외모, 모습' and '출연, 출현, 등장'.
items.correction: appearance = 외모, 겉모습; 출현, 등장

items.locator: hv-15 row 1 col 3 (lucky) and row 2 col 2 (fortunate). Distractor filters are in src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:280-282, 323-331 and 431-434.
items.original: lucky = 운이 좋은 / fortunate = 다행스러운, 복 받은 (code comment at vocaUtils.ts:329: "e.g. hv-15 \"운이 좋은\" would otherwise list both `lucky` and `fortunate`.")
items.problem: lucky and fortunate are true synonyms: Engoo glosses fortunate '행운의, 운 좋은, 다행스러운'. The quiz and speed drill exclude a distractor only when its meaning string is exactly identical. Because the two glosses are now different strings, the KIG-019/V-04 guard never fires for this pair, even though the code comment names this very pair as handled. So the graded quiz can offer fortunate as a wrong option, and lucky can appear as a wrong option on the '[ 다행스러운, 복 받은 ]' question. The speed drill can also show 'fortunate = 운이 좋은' and expect 불일치 (no match), which is really a match.
items.correction: Add a same-sense exclusion list (for example lucky↔fortunate) that the quiz and speed-drill distractor filters check in addition to the exact-string rule. Or gloss fortunate as '운 좋은, 다행스러운' and let the existing guard treat the shared sense as the same meaning. Update the misleading comment at vocaUtils.ts:329.

items.locator: hv-15 row 4 col 2 (content/lessons/phonics/hv-15.json). Dictionary key "childlike". It sits next to childish at row 4 col 1.
items.original: childlike = 어린애 같은 (next to it: childish = 유치한)
items.problem: The pair childish/childlike exists to contrast a negative word (유치한) with a positive one (순진한, 천진난만한). 어린애 같은 carries no positive tone, and Korean dictionaries also use it for childish (Engoo: childish '유치한, 어린애 같은'). So the gloss does not show what makes childlike different. It is not wrong, because Longman and Engoo give 어린애 같은 with a positive-sense note, but on the card it confuses.
items.correction: childlike = (좋은 뜻으로) 어린아이 같은, 순진한, 천진난만한

items.locator: hv-15 row 5 col 1 (lesson file content/lessons/phonics/hv-15.json, wordgrid). Meaning comes from dictionary key "continual". The same word and gloss also appear in hv-66 row 3 col 3.
items.original: continual = 지속적인 (next to it: continuous = 연속적인)
items.problem: The lesson places continual and continuous side by side to teach their difference: continual = happening again and again with breaks; continuous = without a break. The gloss 지속적인 says 'lasting without a break', and Korean dictionaries give it as a gloss of continuous (Engoo: continuous '꾸준한, 지속적인, 계속되는'). So the gloss erases, and nearly reverses, the one distinction the pair exists to teach. The gloss is not flatly wrong, because Merriam-Webster keeps an older sense of continual meaning 'without interruption'. That is why this is Medium, not High. The quiz's ko-to-en item '[ 지속적인 ]' can also offer continuous as a 'wrong' option, and a learner who knows continuous = 지속적인 would pick it.
items.correction: continual = 거듭되는, 반복되는 (끊겼다 이어지는); continuous = 끊임없는, 연속적인

items.locator: hv-15 row 5 col 3 (content/lessons/phonics/hv-15.json). Dictionary key "economic". It sits next to economical at row 5 col 4.
items.original: economic = 경제의, 경제적인 (next to it: economical = 절약하는)
items.problem: This confusable pair teaches economic = 'relating to the economy' against economical = 'cost-saving'. In Korean teaching, 경제적인 is the standard gloss for economical, as in '경제적인 차' for 'an economical car'. The OWL Dictionary explainer glosses economic as 경제의 and economical as 경제적인. Putting 경제적인 in the economic gloss gives economic the Korean word learners attach to economical. The quiz and speed drill then treat economic as the right answer for a sense that belongs to economical.
items.correction: economic = 경제의, 경제(학)상의; economical = 경제적인, 절약하는, 알뜰한

items.original: agency = 대리점
items.problem: The only sense given is 대리점 (dealership or branch agency). In high-school and exam reading, the most common senses are (정부) 기관/청, as in government agency, space agency or EPA, and 대행사, as in advertising agency or travel agency (여행사). Engoo lists '대행사, 대리점, 관청, 기관'. With only 대리점, learners will misread 'federal agencies' or 'a government agency'.
items.correction: agency = (정부) 기관, 청; 대행사, 대리점

items.original: apt = 적절한
items.problem: The gloss leaves out the sense 'be apt to do = ~하는 경향이 있다, ~하기 쉽다'. That is the most heavily tested use of apt in Korean high-school English, and Cambridge lists it as a main sense. A learner who sees 'People are apt to forget...' will read it as '적절하다'.
items.correction: apt = ~하는 경향이 있는 (be apt to ~하기 쉽다); 적절한

items.locator: hv-21 row4 col2 'concept' + row4 col3 'conception'; voca_dictionary.json keys "concept", "conception"
items.original: concept = "개념"; conception = "개념, 구상"
items.problem: Two words in the same lesson share the sense '개념'. Quiz and speed-drill distractors are excluded only when the whole meaning string is identical (src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:282 and :434), so the shared sense is not caught. In the speed drill, 'concept = 개념, 구상' expects ❌ 불일치 even though 개념 is concept's own meaning. In the 4-choice quiz for concept, '개념, 구상' can appear as a wrong option that is actually correct. This pair is already listed as R-7 in maps/voca.md:82 but is still unfixed.
items.correction: conception → "구상, 착상; 임신" (drop 개념), or add a code-side exclusion for any shared sense segment.

items.original: exceptional = "예외적인"
items.problem: The very common sense 'unusually excellent' (dictionary.com sense 2; British sense 2: 'having much more than average … ability') is missing. 'exceptional talent/quality' would be read as 예외적인 재능.
items.correction: exceptional → "예외적인; 특출한, 뛰어난".

items.locator: hv-21 row5 col3 'deception' + row5 col4 'deceit'; voca_dictionary.json keys "deception", "deceit"
items.original: deception = "속임, 기만"; deceit = "사기, 거짓 (속이는 짓)"
items.problem: deceit and deception are synonyms. Dictionary.com lists deception as a synonym of deceit, and Korean Wiktionary glosses deceit as '속임수, 사기, 기만'. So deception's card '속임, 기만' is a correct meaning of deceit, and deceit's '(속이는 짓)' is a correct meaning of deception. Because the full strings differ, the speed drill and the quiz can use each one as a 'wrong' meaning for the other.
items.correction: Separate the nuance, e.g. deceit → "속임수, 부정직 (성향)" and deception → "기만 (행위), 속임", and add a synonym-pair exclusion in the distractor filters (vocaUtils.ts:282/:330/:434).

items.original: access = "접근하다"
items.problem: The gloss presents access only as a verb. Access is listed first as a noun ('the ability, right, or permission to approach, enter … or use'), and the core high-school pattern is 'have access to' (~에 접근/이용할 수 있다).
items.correction: access → "접근, 이용 (권한); 접근하다".

items.locator: hv-22 row3 col2 'succeed'; voca_dictionary.json key "succeed" (also mv2-30, mv3-32)
items.original: succeed = "성공하다"
items.problem: The lesson groups succeed with succession 계승, successive 연속적인 and successor 후임, which all come from succeed's other sense, 뒤를 잇다/계승하다 (Korean Wiktionary sense 2: 물려받다, 승계하다). With only 성공하다, the family link is invisible, and 'succeed A as CEO' or 'succeed to the throne' will be misread.
items.correction: succeed → "성공하다; 뒤를 잇다, 계승하다". No identical segment appears in hv-22, mv2-30 or mv3-32; succession '계승' is noun vs verb.

items.locator: hv-22 row4 col3 'ceaseless' + row4 col4 'incessant'; voca_dictionary.json keys "ceaseless", "incessant"
items.original: ceaseless = "끊임없는"; incessant = "쉴 새 없는"
items.problem: These are synonyms. Dictionary.com defines incessant as 'continuing without interruption; unending; ceaseless', and Korean Wiktionary glosses incessant as 끊임없는, which is word for word the gloss this lesson gives ceaseless. The strings differ, so the code treats them as different meanings. The speed drill can show 'incessant = 끊임없는' and expect ❌, and the en-to-ko quiz for incessant can offer 끊임없는 as a 'wrong' option.
items.correction: Give the nuance: incessant → "(짜증스러울 정도로) 쉴 새 없는, 끊임없는". Also add a synonym-pair exclusion (ceaseless/incessant) to the distractor filters in src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:282/:330/:434, because any correct glosses of the two words will overlap.

items.locator: hv-23 row2 col3 'certain'; voca_dictionary.json key "certain" (also mv1-36, mv2-16, mv3-02)
items.original: certain = "확실한"
items.problem: The sense 'definite or particular, but not named' (어떤, 특정한; dictionary.com sense 6) is missing. It is the sense in 'a certain man' and 'certain people', a classic misreading point for Korean learners.
items.correction: certain → "확실한; 어떤, 특정한". No collision in the four lessons that use it was found.

items.original: certificate = "인증서"
items.problem: In current Korean, 인증서 mostly means a digital or quality-certification certificate. The general sense is 증명서/증서/자격증, as in birth certificate = 출생증명서 and teaching certificate = 교사 자격증. Korean Wiktionary gives '증서, 증명서'.
items.correction: certificate → "증명서, 자격증".

items.original: discriminate = "차별하다"
items.problem: The sense 'to note or observe a difference; distinguish accurately' (구별하다, 식별하다; dictionary.com intransitive sense 2 and both transitive senses) is missing. That sense is common in academic reading, e.g. 'discriminate between two sounds'.
items.correction: discriminate → "차별하다; 구별하다, 식별하다".

items.original: exclusively = "독점적으로"
items.problem: The first sense of exclusively is 'solely; only' (오로지, 전적으로; dictionary.com sense 1), as in 'focused exclusively on…' or 'exclusively for members'. 독점적으로 covers only the 'sold exclusively at' sense.
items.correction: exclusively → "오로지, 전적으로; 독점적으로".

items.locator: hv-25 row3 col2 'accord' + row3 col3 'accordance'; voca_dictionary.json keys "accord", "accordance"
items.original: accord = "합의, 협정; 일치"; accordance = "일치 (in accordance with ~에 따라)"
items.problem: Both glosses contain the sense 일치. The check behind R-7 missed this pair because accordance's segment includes the parenthetical, so it is not in maps/voca.md:82. In the speed drill (vocaUtils.ts:434), word 'accordance' shown with '합의, 협정; 일치' expects ❌ 불일치, although accordance does mean 일치.
items.correction: accord → "합의, 협정" and accordance → "일치, 부합", with the phrase note kept outside the graded meaning string (see the separate Low finding). Alternatively, exclude shared segments in code with parentheticals stripped before comparing.

items.locator: hv-25 row3 col3 'accordance'; voca_dictionary.json key "accordance"; prompt built at src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:344
items.original: accordance = "일치 (in accordance with ~에 따라)"
items.problem: The graded meaning string contains the English headword. The ko-to-en quiz prompt becomes '[ 일치 (in accordance with ~에 따라) ] 에 해당하는 올바른 영단어를 고르세요.', which shows the answer. In en-to-ko the correct option is the only one containing 'accordance'. The item tests nothing.
items.correction: Keep the graded gloss free of English ("일치, 부합"). Show the phrase 'in accordance with ~에 따라' in a non-graded note, or remove the parenthetical before the string is used as a quiz prompt or option.

items.original: colonial = "식민지 시대의"
items.problem: The primary sense is 'of, concerning, or pertaining to a colony or colonies' (식민지의); dictionary.com sense 1. '식민지 시대의' is a narrower, period sense. 'colonial rule' and 'colonial powers' mean 식민 지배 and 식민 강대국, not 식민지 시대의 ….
items.correction: colonial → "식민지의; 식민지 시대의".

items.original: due = "~하기로 되어 있는; ~때문에"
items.problem: '~때문에' is the meaning of the compound preposition 'due to', not of the headword due. The adjective's first senses, 'owed at present; having reached the date for payment' (지불 기한이 된, 만기인), as in 'The rent is due' or 'due date', are missing.
items.correction: due → "(지불) 기한이 된; ~할 예정인; (due to) ~때문에".

items.original: duty = "의무"
items.problem: The next card, duty-free = 면세의, only makes sense through duty = 관세/세금, and that sense is missing. Korean Wiktionary lists 관세 as a sense of duty. As it stands, the lesson implies duty-free = 의무가 없는.
items.correction: duty → "의무; 관세, 세금".

items.original: rent = "임대하다; 집세"
items.problem: 임대하다 is only the landlord's side (to let out). The main sense for learners, paying to use something (rent a car, rent an apartment), is 빌리다/세내다/임차하다, which Korean Wiktionary lists first. With the current gloss, 'I rented an apartment' reads as 'I leased out an apartment'.
items.correction: rent → "(돈을 내고) 빌리다, 임차하다; 임대하다; 집세".

items.locator: hv-29 row1 col2 'present'; voca_dictionary.json key "present" (also mv1-07, mv2-04, mv3-40)
items.original: present = "현재의; 선물; 발표하다"
items.problem: The first adjective sense in Korean Wiktionary, '(사람이) 있는, 존재하는; 출석한, 참석한', is missing. In this lesson present sits right after absent 결석한/absence 부재 and before presence, so the absent/present opposition is exactly what the grid sets up. 'be present at', 'those present' and 'all present' cannot be read with the current gloss.
items.correction: present → "현재의; 출석한, 있는; 선물; 제시하다, 발표하다".

items.locator: hv-30 row2 col3 'profit' + row3 col2 'benefit'; voca_dictionary.json keys "profit", "benefit" (benefit also appears in mv3-39)
items.original: profit = "이익"; benefit = "혜택"
items.problem: 이익 is the standard Korean gloss for benefit as well; Korean Wiktionary gives benefit (n.) = 이익. So the speed drill item 'benefit = 이익' expects ❌ 불일치, and the en-to-ko quiz for benefit can offer 이익 as a 'wrong' option. A learner who knows benefit = 이익, 혜택 is marked wrong.
items.correction: profit → "이윤, 수익". This is specific to financial gain and no longer collides; profit appears only in hv-30.

items.locator: hv-30 row5 col3 'fault'; voca_dictionary.json key "fault" (same gloss shown in mv1-39 r2c2, mv2-25 r5c4, mv3-16 r1c3)
items.original: fault = "결점"
items.problem: The most frequent sense, 잘못/책임 as in 'It's my fault' or 'not your fault', is missing. Korean Wiktionary lists '잘못, 흠' first and '결점, 결함' second. With only 결점, 'It's not your fault' reads as '네 결점이 아니야'. The same gloss is used in three mv lessons, where the 잘못 sense matters even more.
items.correction: fault → "잘못, 책임; 결점". Checked: this creates no identical segment in hv-30, mv1-39, mv2-25 or mv3-16. faulty '잘못된' is a derivation pair.

items.locator: hv-31 grid r2c1 'offensive' (voca-lessons.tsv line 908); dictionary key 'offensive' (voca_dictionary.json line 3514); used only in hv-31
items.original: offensive | 공격적인
items.problem: The card leaves out the first and most common sense of the adjective: 'causing offence', i.e. 불쾌한, 모욕적인 (an offensive remark/joke). The attack sense ('공격의', military or sports) comes third in dictionaries. Two cells earlier the same grid teaches offend = '기분을 상하게 하다', so the derivative is shown with no visible link to its verb. The gloss is also identical to aggressive '공격적인' (hv-34 r4c3), so the learner cannot tell offensive from aggressive. '공격적인' as a personality trait is a meaning offensive rarely has.
items.correction: 불쾌한, 모욕적인; 공격(용)의

items.locator: hv-31 grid r3c3 'confer' (tsv line 916), next to conference; dictionary key 'confer' line 3546 (used only in hv-31)
items.original: confer | 수여하다
items.problem: confer has two current core senses: transitive 'bestow' (수여하다) and intransitive 'consult, discuss' (confer with = 상의하다, 협의하다). The second is the sense that conference ('회의', next cell) comes from, and it is common in advanced reading. The card gives only 수여하다.
items.correction: 수여하다; 상의하다, 협의하다

items.locator: hv-35 grid r3c2 'grave' (tsv line 1035), next to gravity, grieve, grief; dictionary key 'grave' line 4002 (shared with mv2-34 r3c1 and mv3-18 r5c4)
items.original: grave | 무덤
items.problem: hv-35 groups grave with gravity, grieve and grief, the Latin gravis ('heavy') family. The member of that family is the adjective grave, '심각한, 중대한' (from Latin gravis). The noun grave, '무덤', is a different word, from Old English græf ('dig'). Showing only 무덤 teaches a false link (무덤 ↔ 중력/슬픔) and leaves out the high-school sense (grave danger / grave concern).
items.correction: 무덤; 심각한, 중대한 (this combined gloss still fits mv2-34 and mv3-18, which share the key). Alternatively, a per-lesson override for hv-35: 심각한, 중대한

items.locator: hv-36 grid r1c1 'inheritance' (quiz index 0, English→Korean item) and r1c2 'heritage' (quiz index 1, Korean→English item) (tsv lines 1052-1053); dictionary keys 'inheritance' line 4070 and 'heritage' line 4074
items.original: inheritance | 상속 / heritage | 유산
items.problem: inheritance is glossed '유산' just as commonly as '상속' (money or property one inherits). In the quiz: (a) heritage's Korean→English item '[ 유산 ]' can draw inheritance as a 'wrong' option (about 3 in 29); (b) inheritance's English→Korean item can draw '유산' as a 'wrong' option; (c) the speed drill can show inheritance with '유산' and expect 불일치. A learner who knows inheritance = 유산 is marked wrong. The identical-string guard (vocaUtils.ts:282, 330, 434) does not catch this because the strings differ. Separately, heritage '유산' is identical to legacy '유산' in the next lesson (hv-37 r3c4), so the three words cannot be told apart from their cards.
items.correction: heritage → (문화적) 유산, 전통. Keep inheritance 상속 (or 상속(재산)) and consider legacy → (후대에 남긴) 유산, 유물.

items.locator: hv-37 grid r1c2 'relation' and r5c5 'relationship' (tsv lines 1083, 1110); dictionary keys 'relation' line 4182 and 'relationship' line 4290
items.original: relation | 관련, 관계; 친척 / relationship | (사람·집단 사이의) 관계
items.problem: relation(s) also means the way people, groups or states deal with each other (foreign relations, race relations). The speed drill can show relation with '(사람·집단 사이의) 관계' and expect 불일치, which is not true. With the current grid order the four-choice quiz stays fair: relation is asked Korean→English with a prompt that contains 친척, and relationship is asked English→Korean. So only the drill is affected (about 1.6% per run).
items.correction: relation → (사물 사이의) 관련, 관계; 친척, or exclude relation and relationship as each other's non-match meaning.

items.locator: hv-37 grid r3c2 'just' (tsv line 1095); dictionary key 'just' line 4230 (same gloss already taught in mv1-04 r3c1)
items.original: just | 단지, 그저
items.problem: In this advanced-series lesson, just sits in the jus/jur ('right, law') family: injurious in the same grid, and justice, justify, justification, judg(e)ment, prejudice, injure and injury in hv-38. The family sense is the adjective '공정한, 정당한' (a just cause / just society). The card shows only the adverb '단지, 그저', a middle-school sense already taught with the identical gloss in mv1-04. So the hv card teaches nothing new and hides the link to justice.
items.correction: 단지, 그저; 공정한, 정당한 (this shared entry still works for mv1-04). Alternatively, a per-lesson override for hv-37: 공정한, 정당한

items.locator: hv-38 grid r4c4 'translate': on-screen etymology box (also shown as the quiz etymologyHint), PREFIX_RULES entry at src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:112. The same rule serves hv-06 r5c4.
items.original: trans(바꾸어) + late(옮기다) ➔ 한 언어를 다른 언어로 건네주다, 번역하다
items.problem: trans- means 'across, beyond', not 'change'. translate comes from Latin translatus, 'carried over', the past participle of transferre (trans 'across' + latus 'carried'). The box's own paraphrase ('건네주다') describes carrying across, but the morpheme gloss '바꾸어' is wrong and conflicts with the transport/transfer rules in the same table (trans = 가로질러/건너서).
items.correction: trans(건너서) + late(옮겨진; ferre '나르다'의 과거분사) ➔ 한 언어에서 다른 언어로 건너 옮기다, 번역하다

items.locator: hv-40 grid r1c5 'lengthen' (quiz index 4) and r2c5 'prolong' (quiz index 10), both English→Korean items (tsv lines 1176, 1182); dictionary keys 'lengthen' line 4534 and 'prolong' line 4558
items.original: lengthen | 길게 하다 / prolong | 연장하다
items.problem: Korean 연장하다 means making time or distance longer, so it is an equally valid gloss for lengthen. prolong literally means to make longer in time, i.e. 길게 하다. In each word's English→Korean item, the other word's gloss can be drawn as a 'wrong' option although it is a defensible answer. The same happens in the speed drill.
items.correction: prolong → (기간을) 연장하다, 오래 끌다; lengthen → 길게 하다, 길어지다. Also exclude the pair from each other's distractors.

items.locator: hv-40 grid r2c3 'limit' (quiz index 8, English→Korean item) and r2c1 'limitation' (tsv lines 1180, 1178); dictionary keys 'limit' line 4550 (shared with mv1-30, mv2-21, mv3-19) and 'limitation' line 4542
items.original: limit | 한도 / limitation | 제한
items.problem: '제한' is the standard Korean gloss of limit itself (speed limit = 제한 속도, age limit = 연령 제한). When limit's English→Korean item draws limitation's '제한' as a distractor (about 3 in 29), two options are correct but only '한도' is accepted. In the 60-second drill, limit shown with '제한' expects 불일치, which is false. The whole-string equality guard does not catch this.
items.correction: limit → 한도, 한계; 제한하다. In addition, never use limit and limitation as each other's distractor or non-match meaning (extend the KIG-019/V-04 guard to this pair).

items.original: reminder	알림
items.problem: In modern Korean, 알림 mostly means a notification. A reminder is something that makes you remember ('a reminder of the war', 'a painful reminder'). The general sense, which links to 'remind 생각나게 하다' in the same lesson, is missing.
items.correction: 생각나게 하는 것, 상기시키는 것; (잊지 않도록 보내는) 알림

items.locator: hv-41 row 4 col 2 immigrate (also row 3 col 6 immigration)
items.original: immigrate	이민하다  /  immigration	이민
items.problem: The lesson uses the noun immigrant to teach the direction ('(다른 나라에서 온) 이민자'), but the verb and the -ation noun lose it. 이민하다 does not say whether the person is coming in or going out. Next lesson, emigrate is glossed as the equally undirected 이주하다, so the two verbs look like synonyms. The in/out direction is the whole point of the im-/e- root pair.
items.correction: immigrate '(다른 나라로) 이민 오다, 이주해 오다'; immigration '(외국에서 들어오는) 이민, 이주; 출입국 관리'

items.locator: hv-42 row 5 col 3 emigrate (also row 5 col 1 emigration)
items.original: emigrate	이주하다  /  emigration	이주
items.problem: The emigrant card in the same lesson says '(다른 나라로 떠나는) 이민자', but emigrate and emigration are glossed with the generic 이주하다 and 이주, which also cover moving within a country and do not show 'leaving one's country'. Next to hv-41's immigrate 이민하다, the pair reads as synonyms.
items.correction: emigrate '(다른 나라로) 이민 가다, 이주해 나가다'; emigration '(타국으로의) 이민, 이주'

items.original: admire	감탄하다
items.problem: admire has two main senses: to respect someone for their qualities (존경하다) and to look at something with pleasure (감탄하다). The first is the most frequent and the most tested ('I admire her courage'). The card shows only 감탄하다, which gives an unnatural translation of the common usage.
items.correction: 존경하다; 감탄하다, 감탄하며 바라보다

items.original: diminish	감소시키다
items.problem: diminish is used both intransitively (to become smaller) and transitively (to make smaller), and the intransitive use is very common ('Their enthusiasm diminished'). The gloss gives only the causative 감소시키다, so the learner is taught that the word always needs an object.
items.correction: 줄어들다, 감소하다; 줄이다

items.original: admiration	감탄
items.problem: This has the same gap as admire in hv-43: the 존경 sense, which is the primary one ('deep admiration for her teacher'), is missing.
items.correction: 존경; 감탄

items.original: admission	입학
items.problem: The card shows only the narrow sense 입학. The main senses are 입장(허가) and 입장료, and 인정, 시인 ('an admission of guilt'). The 인정 sense ties directly to 'admit 인정하다' in row 5 col 6 of the same lesson.
items.correction: 입장(허가), 입학; 입장료; 인정, 시인

items.original: comic	만화
