items.problem: comic is placed with comedy (and tragic/tragedy in hv-45), where its core role is the adjective 웃기는, 희극의 (the counterpart of tragic 비극적인). The gloss gives only the noun 만화 (comic book), which loses the root pairing and the adjective use ('comic relief', 'a comic actor').
items.correction: 웃기는, 희극의; 만화(책); 코미디언

items.original: orient	동양
items.problem: The headword is lower-case 'orient' but it is taught only as the noun 동양. That sense belongs to the capitalised proper noun 'the Orient', which dictionaries describe as dated. In current English, lower-case orient is chiefly a verb: to position or direct toward, to adapt, to familiarise ('career-oriented', 'orient yourself'). This verb is the base of 'orientation 방향, 성향' in row 3 col 1 of the same lesson, so the root link is broken.
items.correction: (~쪽으로) 향하게 하다, 지향하게 하다; 적응시키다; (the Orient) 동양 (옛 표현)

items.original: oriental	동양의
items.problem: The gloss is correct, but the card has no usage note. Merriam-Webster and American Heritage mark 'Oriental' as usually offensive when used of people, and as dated even for cultural objects; 'Asian' is preferred. A paid course for learners who may use English abroad should warn them.
items.correction: 동양의 (주로 사물·문화에 쓰는 옛 표현; 사람에게 쓰면 모욕적 — Asian 사용)

items.original: passage	통로
items.problem: The gloss shows only 통로. For an advanced high-school learner, the most frequent sense in exam material is '(글의) 구절, 지문' ('Read the passage').
items.correction: 통로, 복도; (글의) 구절; 통과

items.original: expedition	원정대
items.problem: The gloss shows only the secondary 'group of people' sense. The primary sense is the journey itself (원정, 탐험): 'go on an expedition' means 탐험을 떠나다, not 원정대를 떠나다.
items.correction: 원정, 탐험; 원정대, 탐험대

items.locator: hv-49 row 2 col 3 penalty vs row 2 col 6 punishment
items.original: penalty	처벌, 벌금  /  punishment	처벌
items.problem: punishment (index 11, odd) is asked Korean-to-English: '[ 처벌 ]', and 'penalty' (glossed '처벌, 벌금') can be drawn as a 'wrong' option. penalty (index 8, even) is asked English-to-Korean, and '처벌' (punishment's gloss) can be drawn as a 'wrong' option. Both are correct meanings. The overlap seems to come from the 2026-09-15 correction that changed penalty from 페널티 to 처벌, 벌금 (docs/qa-2026-09-15/evidence/voca-corrections.md:179).
items.correction: penalty '벌금, 과태료; (규칙 위반에 대한) 불이익' and punishment '처벌, 벌'. Alternatively, extend the quiz filter to reject distractors that share a gloss token with the answer.

items.locator: hv-50 row 3 col 6 fancy (vs row 5 col 5 fantastic)
items.original: fancy	멋진  /  fantastic	환상적인
items.problem: fancy is glossed only with the vague 멋진. Its core senses are 화려한, 장식이 많은, 고급의 (adjective) and 공상, 좋아함 (noun), which link it to phantom and fantasy in this root lesson. In everyday Korean, 멋진 is also a natural translation of fantastic (굉장한, 멋진). fancy (index 17, odd) is asked '[ 멋진 ]' Korean-to-English, and fantastic may appear as a 'wrong' option. fantastic (index 28, even) may show '멋진' as a 'wrong' option. Both are defensible choices.
items.correction: fancy '화려한, 고급의; 공상, (일시적) 좋아함'

items.locator: row 2 col 4 'pleasing' (idx 9, ko-to-en) and row 2 col 5 'pleasant' (idx 10, en-to-ko); dictionary lines 5806, 1682
items.original: pleasing = 기분 좋은 / pleasant = 즐거운
items.problem: pleasant and pleasing are near-synonyms (a pleasant day = 기분 좋은 날). On pleasing's ko-to-en item "[ 기분 좋은 ]", 'pleasant' can be drawn as a 'wrong' option although it is a valid translation. For pleasant's en-to-ko item, '기분 좋은' can be the 'wrong' option.
items.correction: Give distinguishing glosses, e.g. pleasant = '(날씨·경험이) 즐거운, 쾌적한' and pleasing = '(보기·듣기에) 흡족한, 만족스러운'. Or put the pair on the synonym-exclusion list. The pleasant entry is shared with hv-15.

items.locator: row 3 col 2 'plea' (next to row 3 col 3 'plead = 간청하다'); dictionary line 5818
items.original: plea = 항변
items.problem: The primary sense of plea is 'an appeal, petition, urgent prayer or entreaty' (a plea for help/mercy = 간청, 탄원). '항변' only corresponds to the secondary defence or legal sense. Placed next to plead = 간청하다, the gloss hides the direct noun-verb relationship (plead → plea = 간청).
items.correction: plea = '간청, 탄원; (법정) 답변, 항변'

items.locator: row 4 col 1 'complicated' (idx 18, en-to-ko) and row 4 col 2 'complex' (idx 19, ko-to-en); dictionary lines 5834-5839
items.original: complicated = (이해하기) 까다로운, 복잡한 / complex = 복합적인, 복잡한
items.problem: Both glosses contain the identical segment 복잡한, and the exact-string filter does not exclude the other word (R-7, maps/voca.md:82). The qualifiers (이해하기)/복합적인 partly tell them apart, so this is less severe than prime/primary. Still, complex is equally 'hard to understand' (a complex problem), so on complex's ko-to-en item 'complicated' is arguably also correct, and in the speed drill 'complex = (이해하기) 까다로운, 복잡한' expects 불일치.
items.correction: Drop the shared segment, e.g. complicated = '(이해하기) 까다로운, 뒤얽힌' and complex = '복합적인, 여러 부분으로 된; (명) 복합 단지'. Or apply the segment-level distractor exclusion.

items.locator: row 4 col 5 'apply' (with row 4 col 6 'application', row 5 col 2 'applicant'); dictionary lines 5850-5855
items.original: apply = 적용하다 / application = 신청 / applicant = 지원자
items.problem: apply shows only 적용하다, while its derivatives on the same grid are glossed with the other core sense (신청, 지원자). The high-frequency sense 'apply for' = 지원하다/신청하다 (Wiktionary sense 7, 'submit oneself as a candidate') is missing. As a result the word family the lesson is built around does not connect: apply (적용) → application (신청) → applicant (지원자).
items.correction: apply = '지원하다, 신청하다; 적용하다; (크림 등을) 바르다'. application could be '신청(서), 지원; 적용, 응용'.

items.locator: row 5 col 1 'import' etymology box, src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:116 (same pattern for export at :115)
items.original: im/in(안으로) + port(항구/나르다) ➔ 항구 안으로 물건을 들여오다, 수입하다
items.problem: The box teaches port = 항구 and explains import as bringing goods into a harbour. Latin importare comes from in- + portare 'to carry', not from portus 'harbour'. The harbour story is a folk etymology presented as the word's origin.
items.correction: im/in(안으로) + port(나르다) ➔ 안으로 실어 들여오다, 수입하다 (and the same fix for export: ex(밖으로) + port(나르다))

items.locator: row 2 col 5 'repute' (idx 10, en-to-ko) and row 3 col 3 'reputation' (idx 14, en-to-ko); dictionary lines 6262, 6278
items.original: repute = 명성, 세평 / reputation = 평판
items.problem: repute is defined as 'reputation, especially a good reputation' (Wiktionary), so the words are synonyms. Because the strings differ, '명성, 세평' can be a 'wrong' option on reputation's item (reputation = 명성 is correct) and '평판' can be a 'wrong' option on repute's item (a person of good repute = 평판이 좋은).
items.correction: Mark repute as the formal synonym and keep the pair out of each other's distractors, e.g. repute = '(격식) 평판, 명성 (= reputation)' plus a synonym-exclusion entry, and reputation = '평판, 명성'.

items.locator: row 5 col 4 'arrangement', row 5 col 5 'arrange'; dictionary lines 6330-6335
items.original: arrangement = 배열 / arrange = 배열하다
items.problem: The glosses are correct but omit the second core sense, 'to plan; to prepare in advance' (arrange a meeting, make arrangements = 준비하다, 마련하다, (일정을) 정하다), which is very frequent at high-school level.
items.correction: arrange = '배열하다, 정리하다; 준비하다, 마련하다', arrangement = '배열, 정리; 준비, 합의'

items.original: ascribe = 귀속하다
items.problem: ascribe is transitive: 'to regard as arising from a specified cause or source' (ascribe X to Y), i.e. ~의 탓/덕으로 돌리다, (작품을) ~의 것으로 보다. The Korean 귀속하다 is defined as 재산이나 영토, 권리 따위가 특정 주체에 붙거나 딸리다, an intransitive 'belong to' meaning about property or rights. The gloss therefore suggests 'to belong to', with the wrong direction and voice, and it is an obscure legal word for a high-school learner.
items.correction: ascribe = '(원인·책임을) ~의 탓으로 돌리다, ~에 귀속시키다'

items.original: sensational = 선정적인
items.problem: Only the pejorative sense is given. In Korean, 선정적인 strongly connotes lurid or sexually provocative content. The main modern senses are 'provoking a reaction of interest or excitement' and 'exceptionally great' (Wiktionary senses 3-4), i.e. 선풍적인, 세상을 놀라게 하는, 굉장한.
items.correction: sensational = '선풍적인, 세상을 떠들썩하게 하는; 굉장한; 선정적인'

items.locator: row 2 col 3 'subsequently' (vs row 3 col 3 'subsequent = 다음의, 그 후의'); dictionary line 6606
items.original: subsequently = 이후
items.problem: subsequently is an adverb, but '이후(以後)' is a noun in 표준국어대사전 ('기준이 되는 때를 포함하여 그보다 뒤'). Every other adverb in these lessons is glossed adverbially (primarily = 주로, consequently = 결과적으로, privately = 개인적으로).
items.correction: subsequently = '그 후에, 이후에, 나중에'

items.locator: row 4 col 3 'conserve' (idx 20, en-to-ko) and row 4 col 4 'preserve' (idx 21, ko-to-en); dictionary lines 6650-6655
items.original: conserve = 절약하다 / preserve = 보존하다 (same grid: conservation = (자원·자연의) 보호, 보존)
items.problem: conserve's second core sense is 'to protect an environment, heritage' (Wiktionary sense 2), which is 보존하다/보호하다, the sense its own noun 'conservation' shows on the same grid. Showing only '절약하다' hides it. On preserve's ko-to-en item "[ 보존하다 ]", 'conserve' can be drawn as a 'wrong' option although it is a correct translation. On conserve's en-to-ko item, '보존하다' can be a 'wrong' option.
items.correction: conserve = '(자원을) 아끼다, 절약하다; (자연·유산을) 보존하다' and preserve = '(원래 상태로) 보존하다, 지키다'. Also exclude the pair from each other's distractors.

items.original: spectacular = 장관의
items.problem: '장관의' is ambiguous: a learner will most naturally read it as 長官 (minister), 'of the minister', rather than 壯觀 (grand sight). The English sense is 'amazing or worthy of special notice'.
items.correction: spectacular = '장관을 이루는, 극적인, 굉장한'

items.original: associate = 동료
items.problem: Only the noun sense is shown. The dominant exam sense is the verb: associate A with B = A를 B와 연관 짓다/연상하다, and (be) associated with = ~와 관련된; associate with sb = 어울리다. The same grid shows association = 협회, so the learner never meets the connect/associate-in-mind meaning in this lesson.
items.correction: associate = '연관 짓다, 연상하다; 어울리다; (명) 동료'

items.locator: row 2 col 2 'respect'; dictionary line 6834; etymology box src/lib/vocaUtils.ts:119
items.original: respect = 존경 (etymology box on the same screen: "re(다시) + spect(돌아보다) ➔ 훌륭한 사람을 다시 돌아보다, 존경하다")
items.problem: The card gives only the noun, while the etymology box shown for this word concludes with the verb 존경하다. respect is equally common as a verb, and the lesson's other spect verbs (expect, suspect, inspect) are glossed as verbs.
items.correction: respect = '존경하다; 존경, 존중; (측)면'

items.locator: row 2 col 4 'respectful' (after row 2 col 3 'respectable = 존경할 만한'); dictionary line 1806
items.original: respectful = 존경하는
items.problem: respectful means 'marked by respect', i.e. 공손한, 예의 바른, 존경심을 보이는. The Korean modifier '존경하는' is ambiguous and is most often read as 'respected' (존경하는 선생님 = a teacher whom one respects), which is the meaning of respectable/respected. The lesson deliberately pairs respectable/respectful, a classic exam confusable, and this gloss blurs the contrast it is meant to teach.
items.correction: respectful = '공손한, 존경심을 보이는' (keep respectable = '존경할 만한, 훌륭한'). The entry is shared with hv-16.

items.original: desperate	절망적인
items.problem: Only the despair sense is given. The dominant sense in use is 'in dire need; willing to try anything' (필사적인, 절박한, 간절히 원하는), as in 'desperate for help', 'desperate to win', 'a desperate attempt'. That sense is missing.
items.correction: "desperate": { "meaning": "필사적인, 절박한; 절망적인" }

items.original: statement	성명서
items.problem: '성명서' names only the written-document form of an official statement. The core sense is 진술, 말, 서술 (something stated), which also connects to 'state 진술하다' in hv-61. It is missing.
items.correction: "statement": { "meaning": "진술, 성명; (은행) 명세서" }

items.original: substantial	실질적인
items.problem: The primary modern sense 'large in amount, value or importance' (상당한) is missing. Only the secondary sense 실질적인 is shown.
items.correction: "substantial": { "meaning": "상당한, 많은; 실질적인" }

items.original: district	지구
items.problem: '지구' written in hangul alone is read by Korean learners as 地球 (Earth), its dominant meaning. The intended 地區 (district) is the rarer reading. The card gives no hanja and no second gloss, so it can mislead.
items.correction: "district": { "meaning": "지역, 구역, (행정) 지구" }

items.original: construct	구성하다
items.problem: The primary sense 'build' (건설하다) is missing, even though the next card 'construction 건설' and 'constructive 건설적인' depend on it. '구성하다' is also exactly the gloss of 'constitute' (hv-63), which blurs the two words.
items.correction: "construct": { "meaning": "건설하다; (이론·문장 등을) 구성하다" }

items.original: stake	말뚝
items.problem: Only the literal 'wooden post' sense is given. For advanced high-school level the useful senses are 'share or interest' (지분, 이해관계) and 'something risked or wagered' (판돈), which give 'at stake' (위태로운, 걸려 있는) and 'stakeholder'. None of these are shown.
items.correction: "stake": { "meaning": "지분, 이해관계; (내기의) 판돈; 말뚝 (at stake: 위태로운)" }

items.original: contain	함유하다
items.problem: '함유하다' is limited to substances or ingredients. The primary senses 포함하다/담고 있다 and the frequent 'keep under control' sense 억제하다 (contain anger, contain the spread) are missing.
items.correction: "contain": { "meaning": "포함하다, 담고 있다; 억제하다" }

items.locator: grid r1c4 content (voca-lessons.tsv line 1955) next to r1c5 contentment (line 1956); content/voca_dictionary.json key "content" (also used by mv2-24)
items.original: content	내용 / contentment	만족
items.problem: 'content' is shown only as the noun 내용. The very next card, 'contentment 만족', derives from the adjective 'content' (만족하는), which is not shown, so the pairing looks arbitrary. Because the key is shared with mv2-24, a hv-only fix should be checked against that lesson.
items.correction: "content": { "meaning": "내용; 만족하는" } (acceptable for mv2-24 as well)

items.locator: grid r5c4 (voca-lessons.tsv line 1979); content/voca_dictionary.json key "contemporary" (also used by mv3-21)
items.original: contemporary	현대의
items.problem: The base sense 'of the same time period' (동시대의; noun 동시대인) is missing. That sense explains the con+tempor root this lesson is teaching (temporary, temporarily) and is common in reading passages ('Shakespeare's contemporaries').
items.correction: "contemporary": { "meaning": "동시대의; 현대의" }

items.original: distribution	유통
items.problem: '유통' covers only the commerce sense (goods reaching consumers). The primary senses are 분배 (act of distributing) and 분포 (how something is spread, e.g. species or income distribution), and both are missing. The card also no longer matches the neighbouring card 'distribute 배포하다'.
items.correction: "distribution": { "meaning": "분배, 배포; 분포; 유통" }

items.original: attribute	속성
items.problem: Only the noun sense is given. The verb 'attribute A to B' (~을 …의 탓/덕분으로 돌리다) is a core advanced-level item and is missing. The same row teaches the verbs contribute/distribute, so learners will assume 'attribute' is only a noun.
items.correction: "attribute": { "meaning": "(~의) 탓[덕분]으로 돌리다; 속성, 특성" }

items.original: avail	소용이 있다
items.problem: The intransitive verb sense 'to be of use' is correct but uncommon in current English. The forms a learner actually meets are the noun idiom 'to no avail / to little avail' (헛되이, 소용없이) and 'avail oneself of' (~을 이용하다). The gloss teaches neither.
items.correction: (명) 소용, 이익 (to no avail 헛되이); (동) 도움이 되다; avail oneself of ~을 이용하다

items.locator: r5c3 'prevent' (content/lessons/phonics/hv-71.json:60; content/voca_dictionary.json:8182-8184; entry also used by mv2-26)
items.original: prevent	예방하다
items.problem: 예방하다 covers only the disease/accident context. The core sense of prevent is 'to stop (an outcome); to keep from (doing something)' (막다, 방지하다), which the key pattern 'prevent A from -ing' uses. That pattern is a staple of Korean high-school English.
items.correction: 막다, 방지하다; 예방하다

items.original: convince	설득하다
items.problem: The gloss gives only the secondary sense 'persuade'. Sense 1 of convince is 'to make someone believe or feel sure' (확신시키다, 납득시키다), which also underlies the frequent 'be convinced that ~' (~라고 확신하다). The site uses the identical gloss 설득하다 for 'persuade' (hv-11, mv3-34), so the learner is taught that convince = persuade. The 확신 meaning that links convince to conviction is lost.
items.correction: 확신시키다, 납득시키다; 설득하다

items.original: conviction	신념
items.problem: 신념 is correct, but the second primary sense 'a judgement of guilt in a court of law' (유죄 판결) is missing. The lesson places conviction right next to convict and convince, and conviction is the noun of both. Only the 신념 half is taught, so neither family link is visible.
items.correction: 확신, 신념; 유죄 판결

items.original: convict	죄수
items.problem: The gloss gives only the noun sense (prisoner). The verb 'convict' (to find guilty, stressed /kənˈvɪkt/) is the first sense in Wiktionary, and 'be convicted of ~' is the common reading pattern. The noun is stressed differently (/ˈkɒnvɪkt/). The site also glosses 'prisoner' as 죄수 (hv-54), so convict and prisoner look like the same word to the learner. The grid places convict next to conviction, but without the verb sense the learner cannot see the convict → conviction (유죄 판결) link.
items.correction: 유죄를 선고하다; 죄수, 기결수

items.original: view	경치; 견해  /  viewpoint	관점
items.problem: In the ko-to-en quiz the distractors are lesson words whose meaning string differs from the prompt (docs/qa-2026-09-18/maps/voca.md:219). '경치; 견해' ≠ '관점', so for the prompt 관점 the options can include both 'viewpoint' and 'view'. 'view' genuinely means 관점/견해 ('point of view', 'in my view'). A learner who picks 'view' is marked wrong and the card drops to Leitner Box 1. It happens only when 'view' is drawn as one of the 3 distractors (about 3 in 29 runs), but the item is unfair when it does.
items.correction: Keep view and viewpoint from being distractors for each other (a per-lesson exclusion pair). Or make viewpoint's gloss clearly distinct, e.g. 'viewpoint = 관점(보는 입장), 전망 지점', and review the pair in the quiz.

items.original: advocate	옹호자
items.problem: The gloss gives only the noun. The verb 'advocate' (to support publicly, 옹호하다/주장하다) is equally common in academic and 수능-style texts ('experts advocate ~'). The verb is pronounced differently (/ˈædvəkeɪt/ vs noun /ˈædvəkət/).
items.correction: 옹호하다, 지지하다; 옹호자

items.locator: r5c2 'volume' (content/lessons/phonics/hv-74.json:59; content/voca_dictionary.json:8534-8536; entry also used by mv3-34)
items.original: volume	책, 권; 음량
items.problem: The gloss leaves out the quantity senses: 부피 (three-dimensional measure, Wiktionary sense 1) and 양 (amount, as in 'a large volume of data/traffic'). These are the senses high-school and science texts use most. The book sense is listed first although it is the least frequent of the three in modern use.
items.correction: 양, 부피; 음량; (책의) 권

items.original: award	수상
items.problem: 'award' as a noun is the prize itself (상), and as a verb it means to give it (수여하다; 'be awarded ~'). 수상 usually reads as 受賞, the act of receiving a prize, which is neither the noun's referent nor the verb sense. Some Korean word lists do include 수상, so it is not wrong, but it is the least precise of the usual glosses.
items.correction: 상; (상을) 수여하다

items.original: impersonal	impersonal	비인격적인	hv-08
items.problem: 비인격적인 corresponds only to the narrow 'not having personality / not representing a person' sense, and in current Korean it reads as '인격을 무시하는' (dehumanising), which is not what English 'impersonal' conveys. The everyday sense — Wiktionary's 'lacking warmth or emotion; cold' (an impersonal email, an impersonal hotel room) — is absent. hv-08 is a negative-prefix lesson (impersonal, irrelevant, uneasy, unfair, unlucky, untidy...), and this same dictionary glosses 'personal' as 개인의, 개인적인, so im- + personal should land on 비개인적인/인간미 없는; 비인격적인 breaks the prefix logic the lesson is built on.
items.correction: 인간미 없는, 사무적인; 개인적 감정이 섞이지 않은

items.original: inflict	inflict	가하다	hv-32
items.problem: '가하다' with no object hint is ambiguous in Korean: read on its own it is as easily taken as 더하다 ('add') as 'impose/deal out'. 'inflict' only means the latter, and only of something unwelcome — pain, injury, damage, punishment. This file uses a parenthetical object hint precisely for this situation elsewhere in the same range (line 1917 'interrupt — (말·일을) 가로막다, 중단시키다'; line 1776 'immigrant — (다른 나라에서 온) 이민자'; line 1903 'intent — (굳은) 의도, 목적'), so the hint is missing rather than stylistically excluded.
items.correction: (고통·상처·벌 등을) 가하다, 입히다

items.original: ingredient	ingredient	성분	hv-34
items.problem: 성분 alone captures the chemical-constituent reading. Wiktionary's first noun sense is 'one of the substances present in a mixture, especially food' (the ingredients of a Spanish omelette are potatoes, eggs, onion...), i.e. 재료 — by far the commonest use and the one that appears in recipe/food reading passages. The second, figurative sense ('a necessary element to achieve a certain goal') is also normally rendered 요소.
items.correction: (요리) 재료, 성분; (성공 등의) 요소

items.original: inside	inside	내부	mv1-20
items.problem: The gloss gives only the noun sense (the interior). 'inside' is overwhelmingly met as a preposition/adverb ('come inside', 'inside the box'), which is 안에 / 안으로 — Wiktionary lists the adverb ('within or towards the interior of something', 'indoors') and preposition ('within the interior of', 'to the interior of') senses separately from the noun 'the interior or inner part'. mv1-20 is a first-level word grid (ear, mom, village, quiet, wood, bear...), so the beginner sense is exactly the one omitted. Note the same gap exists at 'outside' => 외부 (outside my line range), so this looks systematic rather than a one-off typo.
items.correction: 안에, 안으로; 내부

items.original: insult	insult	모욕	hv-64
items.problem: Only the noun is glossed, so the card implies insult is a noun. The verb 모욕하다 ('he insulted her') is at least as common for learners at this level. The file's own convention expresses a dual part of speech with a semicolon and does so repeatedly in this very range — line 1786 'implement — 실행하다; 도구', line 1788 'import — 수입하다; 수입', line 1802 'incline — 기울다; 경사', line 1895 'intellectual — 지적인; 지식인', line 1907 'interest — 관심; 이자' — so the omission is inconsistent with neighbouring entries rather than a deliberate noun-only policy.
items.correction: 모욕하다; 모욕

items.original: interpret	interpret	해석하다	hv-53 mv3-34
items.problem: Only 해석하다 is given; the equally core sense 통역하다 (to convey in real time what a speaker of one language says to a speaker of another) is missing — Wiktionary lists it as a distinct verb sense. The gap is self-evident inside this same dictionary: 'interpreter' (line 1916) is glossed 통역사 and 'interpretation' (line 1915) 해석, and both hv-53 and mv3-34 present the family together (mv3-34's grid holds interpretation and interpret in adjacent rows).
items.correction: 해석하다; 통역하다

items.original: involvement	involvement	참여	hv-74
items.problem: 참여 is the gloss this dictionary gives to participation (line 2519). In hv-74 the word is taught in the volv- root row "revolve | revolution | revolutionary | involve | involvement | evolve", where the sense being built from involve (포함하다, 말려들게 하다) is 관여 / 개입 / 연루, not 참여.
items.correction: 관여, 개입; 참여

items.original: issue	issue	문제	hv-36
items.problem: 문제 alone is thin for a high-school entry, and it is the same single word this dictionary gives to matter (2156) and problem (2761). hv-36 teaches issue inside the -it-/ire ("go out") root cluster — its row is "initiate | initiative | transit | transition | perish | issue", in a lesson with exit and initial — where the senses that make the word worth teaching (쟁점, and the verb 발행하다 / (간행물의) 호) are exactly the ones omitted.
items.correction: 문제, 쟁점; 발행하다; (잡지의) 호

items.original: Japanese	Japanese	일본의; 일본인	mv1-02
items.problem: Same defect as Korean and in the same row ("much | if | English | Korean | German | Japanese"): the language sense 일본어 is missing, while the neighbouring English is glossed 영어 (line 1235) and nothing else in the lesson supplies the missing reading.
items.correction: 일본의; 일본인; 일본어

items.original: jump	jump	뛰다	mv1-19 mv2-06
items.problem: 뛰다 in everyday Korean is read first as "run", and this dictionary separately teaches run	run	달리다 (line 3069), so the learner has no way to tell from the Korean side which English verb is wanted. The word appears bare in the grids ("care | jump | reach | hole | tape | floor"; "kill | pair | dead | sell | jump | bicycle"), and the Korean→English quiz in src/lib/vocaUtils.ts asks precisely in that direction.
items.correction: 뛰어오르다, 점프하다

items.locator: key "justice" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 1973 (lessons hv-38, mv1-25, mv2-35)
items.original: justice	justice	정의	hv-38 mv1-25 mv2-35
items.problem: 정의 is a Korean homonym — 正義 (justice) and 定義 (definition) — and this dictionary gives the identical string to the other one: definition	definition	정의 (line 952). Nothing on the card says which is meant. The file already solves this with hanja elsewhere: edition	판(版) (line 1168).
items.correction: 정의(正義), 공정

items.original: keep	keep	유지하다	mv1-15 mv2-06
items.problem: 유지하다 is the gloss given to maintain (line 2116) — an abstract, higher-level verb — while the beginner senses 계속 가지고 있다 / 간직하다 / 보관하다 are absent. The lessons are elementary: mv1-15's row is "sea | able | usually | catch | keep | while" and mv2-06's is "wide | note | keep | like | need | know".
items.correction: 계속 가지고 있다, 간직하다; 유지하다

items.original: Korean	Korean	한국의; 한국인	mv1-02
items.problem: The language sense 한국어 is missing, and the omission is inconsistent inside a single word-grid row. The mv1-02 row is "much | if | English | Korean | German | Japanese", and in that same row English is glossed as the language only — English	English	영어 (line 1235) — while Korean and Japanese are glossed as adjective+person only. The row plainly teaches languages/nationalities, and no card covers both.
items.correction: 한국의; 한국인; 한국어

items.locator: key "labour" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 1995 (lesson mv3-04); compare key "labor" line 1992 (hv-37)
items.original: labour	labour	노동	mv3-04
items.problem: The Commonwealth spelling is kept as its own entry with a gloss identical to labor	labor	노동 (line 1992), and neither card mentions the other. Every other US/UK pair in this same file is handled with one combined key instead: colo(u)r (637), favo(u)r (1425), hono(u)r (1717), humo(u)r (1744), neighbo(u)r (2323), dialog(ue) (1016), enrol(l) (1241), marvel(l)ous (2150), medi(a)eval (2174), judg(e)ment (1965). The mv3-04 row even mixes the conventions: "labour | struggle | endeavor | slave | cling | press" — British labour beside American endeavor.
items.correction: 노동 (= labor, 영국식 철자)

items.locator: key "letter" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 2038 (lessons mv1-12, mv2-03, mv3-37)
items.original: letter	letter	편지	mv1-12 mv2-03 mv3-37
items.problem: Only 편지. The other core sense 글자 / 문자 is missing, in a course whose lessons are listening and dictation drills where 글자 is exactly what a learner works with. The word appears bare in all three grids ("around | over | nice | letter | another | bedroom"; "rice | sad | road | letter | bottle | area"; "explosion | blanket | investment | scene | letter | store"), so no context supplies it. The related entry alphabet	alphabet	알파벳 (line 142) is taught in mv3-10 with no link to letter.
items.correction: 편지; 글자, 문자

items.original: liability	liability	책임	hv-39
items.problem: 책임 is the same single word this dictionary gives to responsibility (line 3009), so the two cards are interchangeable, and the legal/financial colour that makes liability a separate high-school word (법적 책임; 부채, 부담) is lost. hv-39 teaches it beside obligation and oblige, where that colour is the point.
items.correction: (법적) 책임; 부채, 부담

items.original: light	light	빛	mv1-08 mv2-02
items.problem: Only the noun 빛. The equally basic adjective 가벼운 is missing, and the word is shown alone in a grid ("history | light | second | flower | farm | dear" in mv1-08; "tooth | light | tea | drink | room | think" in mv2-02) so nothing else can supply the sense. Its antonym is taught as a full entry — heavy	heavy	무거운	mv1-24 mv2-07 (line 1686) — and this dictionary's own convention is to carry both senses of such words (kind 친절한; 종류 / last 마지막의; 지속되다 / lie 거짓말; 눕다 / fall 떨어지다; 가을).
items.correction: 빛; 가벼운

items.locator: key "limit" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 2056 (lessons hv-40, mv1-30, mv2-21, mv3-19)
items.original: limit	limit	한도	hv-40 mv1-30 mv2-21 mv3-19
items.problem: 한도 (a cap/ceiling, as in a credit limit) is the narrowest of this word's senses, and it is the only one given for a word that appears in four lessons. The ordinary noun 한계 / 제한 and the verb 제한하다 are missing. hv-40 teaches it inside the limen root cluster — "limitation | limited | limit | preliminary | prolong | eliminate" — where limitation	제한 (2057) and limited	제한된 (2058) both use 제한, so the head word is the odd one out. The file's own convention for noun+verb words is the (하다) form: control 통제(하다) (806), demand 요구(하다); 수요 (962), estimate 추정(하다) (1283), design 설계(하다) (985).
items.correction: 한계, 제한(하다)

items.original: linger	linger	머무르다	hv-40
items.problem: 머무르다 is plain "stay" — and it is literally the same string this dictionary gives to stay	stay	머무르다 (line 3357). The defining part of linger, that something stays longer than expected or is slow to disappear, is gone. hv-40 groups it with prolong and permanent, so duration is the point of the lesson.
items.correction: (예상보다 오래) 머무르다, 좀처럼 사라지지 않다

items.original: listen	listen	듣다	mv1-14 mv2-02
items.problem: The gloss is the identical single word given to a different head word — hear	hear	듣다 (line 1681) — so the two cards are indistinguishable and the hear/listen contrast, one of the most heavily taught points at this level, is invisible. This dictionary already uses a parenthetical qualifier exactly for this purpose elsewhere: solve (문제를) 풀다 (3275), interrupt (말·일을) 가로막다 (1917), celebrate (행사를 열어) 기념하다 (542).
items.correction: (귀 기울여) 듣다

items.original: literate	literate	글을 읽을 줄 아는	hv-16 hv-40
items.problem: The definition is half the word: literate means able to read AND write. Precision matters especially here because hv-16 is a confusable-adjective lesson that puts the three side by side in one row — "imaginary | industrial | industrious | literal | literary | literate" — so the gloss is what the learner uses to keep them apart.
items.correction: 읽고 쓸 줄 아는, 글을 깨친

items.original: loaf	loaf	덩어리	mv3-28
items.problem: 덩어리 is any lump or mass, which is not what "loaf" denotes: it is specifically a shaped block of baked bread (and by extension a moulded block of food such as meat loaf). The grid row gives no help — "blood | prison | loaf | passport | list | distort". The dictionary already carries bread	빵 (line 458), so the bread link is available and simply not made.
items.correction: (빵) 한 덩이, 덩어리로 구운 빵

items.original: lock	lock	자물쇠	mv2-15 mv3-06
items.problem: Noun only; the verb 잠그다 — the far more frequent use for this level — is missing. In the very same mv2-15 row the neighbouring word is glossed as a verb: "surprise | couple | course | knock | ceiling | lock", and knock	knock	두드리다 (line 1988). The dictionary elsewhere marks noun+verb words explicitly (judge 판사; 판단하다, line 1966; lay 놓다; 낳다, 2012; leak 새다; 누출, 2019).
items.correction: 자물쇠; 잠그다

items.problem: Both senses given are correct, but the third core sense — 성냥 — is missing, and the lesson context points straight at it. The mv3-16 word grid (content/lessons/phonics/mv3-16.json) is an everyday-object list: jewel, lantern, powder, flood, bush, wagon, garage, suitcase, hut, log, mail. "Match" sitting in that company alongside lantern and log reads as 성냥, not 경기. The word also appears in mv1-28 and mv2-28, likewise bare word grids with no sentences, so nothing anywhere disambiguates it. A learner given only 경기; 어울리다 has no entry point for "a box of matches" or "strike a match".
items.correction: "경기; 성냥; 어울리다" — adds the missing noun without disturbing the two senses already there.

items.problem: 구조 is defensible, but the primary concrete sense — 기계 장치 — is missing entirely, and 기제 is an opaque academic 한자어 that a Korean middle/high-school student meets only inside 방어기제. The lesson context makes the omission worse, not better: the hv-42 word grid (content/lessons/phonics/hv-42.json) is a machine/hand cluster — mechanic, mechanism, machinery, manipulate, manipulation, manage, management — so the word is plainly being taught next to its 기계 relatives, and the gloss is the only meaning the learner gets, because that lesson is a bare word grid with no sentences. Worse, this meaning string is also the answer text in the 4-choice quiz and the speed drill (src/lib/vocaUtils.ts), so "구조, 기제" is what the learner must recall under time pressure.
items.correction: "기계 장치; 구조, 방법" — leads with the concrete sense the hv-42 cluster is teaching, keeps 구조, and replaces 기제 with 방법, which a school learner can actually use.

items.problem: 마음 is correct as the noun, but the verb sense 꺼리다 / 신경 쓰다 is missing, and that verb is the form Korean learners meet first and most often: "Do you mind…?", "Would you mind…?", "I don't mind", "Never mind". The word is taught in mv1-18, mv2-03 and mv3-24, all confirmed to be bare word grids with no sentences, so 마음 is the whole lesson. The verb is also the one that is actively counter-intuitive for Korean learners, because "No, I don't mind" means yes — exactly the trap a one-word noun gloss leaves them in.
items.correction: "마음; 꺼리다, 신경 쓰다" — noun first, then the verb, matching the noun;verb pattern already used in this slice ("mean → 의미하다; 비열한", "might → ~일지도 모른다; 힘").

items.original: mortal	mortal	필멸의	hv-43
items.problem: Two issues in one gloss. First, the very common sense 치명적인 (mortal wound, mortal danger, mortal blow) is missing entirely. Second, 필멸(必滅) is a rare literary Sino-Korean word that a Korean middle/high-school student is unlikely to know; it explains an unfamiliar English word with an unfamiliar Korean one. hv-43 is a root-based grid (mort-/mov-/mit-) with no sentences, so nothing else on screen conveys the meaning.
items.correction: 죽을 운명의, 죽게 마련인; 치명적인

items.original: most	most	가장	mv1-12 mv3-08
items.problem: 가장 covers only the superlative adverb. The determiner sense 대부분의 ('most people', 'most of the time') is a separate core sense and is missing. The entry is cited by two lessons with different profiles: mv3-08 is an adverb list (together, rather, hastily, forward, ahead, most, correctly, suddenly, almost, exactly...) where 가장 fits, but mv1-12 places 'most' among few, each, another - quantifiers - where 가장 does not fit.
items.correction: 가장; 대부분의

items.original: much	much	많이	mv1-02
items.problem: 많이 is a Korean adverb, so the gloss presents 'much' as adverb-only. But mv1-02 teaches 'many' and 'much' in the same word grid (many in row 3, much in row 5), and 'many' is glossed 많은 (determiner). The countable/uncountable determiner pair many/much is exactly what that pairing exists to teach, and the mismatched parts of speech hide it. 'much' as a determiner (much money, much time, How much?) is the form a first-year learner meets most.
items.correction: 많은; 많이

items.original: with | 와
items.problem: The card shows a bare particle syllable with no tilde and no '함께'. Out of context it reads like the interjection '와!'. It also covers only vowel-final nouns (~과 is needed after consonants). Other particle-type glosses in the same lesson do use the tilde (as ~로, about ~에 대하여, like ~처럼), but this one and from | 에서 do not.
items.correction: ~와 함께, ~을 가지고

items.original: as | ~로
items.problem: Korean '~로' most naturally reads as direction or means (to, toward, by). That misleads for 'as', whose core senses are ~로서 (role), ~처럼 (manner), ~만큼 (as...as) and, as a conjunction, ~할 때 / ~때문에. Only the role sense survives, and only if the learner mentally expands ~로 into ~로서.
items.correction: ~로서; ~처럼; ~만큼

items.original: some | 일부
items.problem: '일부' is a noun/pronoun gloss (some of them = 그들 중 일부). The use learners meet first and most often is the determiner, as in some water or some friends (약간의, 몇몇의). The card never shows it, so "Would you like some tea?" gets mapped to '차 일부'.
items.correction: 약간의, 몇몇의; 일부

items.locator: row 5, col 4-6 (Korean, German, Japanese); dictionary keys "Korean", "German", "Japanese"
items.original: Korean | 한국의; 한국인 ; German | 독일의; 독일인 ; Japanese | 일본의; 일본인
items.problem: The language sense (한국어 / 독일어 / 일본어) is missing from all three nationality words, although it is one of their most frequent uses at this level ("I speak Korean"). The same row shows English | 영어 with only the language sense. A learner can therefore conclude that Korean means only 한국의/한국인 and has no gloss that fits "Can you speak Japanese?". The same pattern applies to American and British elsewhere in mv1, but those are outside this scope.
items.correction: Korean: 한국의; 한국인; 한국어 / German: 독일의; 독일인; 독일어 / Japanese: 일본의; 일본인; 일본어

items.locator: mv1-03 row 4, col 4 (useful) repeated in mv1-11 row 5, col 4; mv1-05 row 1, col 3 (next) repeated in mv1-40 row 3, col 3
items.original: useful | 유용한 (mv1-03, mv1-11); next | 다음 (mv1-05, mv1-40)
items.problem: Each headword repeats with an identical meaning inside the same mv1 series. These are two of the only 8 within-series repeats, so they are probably unintended.
items.correction: Keep the first occurrence and replace the later one (mv1-11 useful, mv1-40 next) with an unused mv1-level word, then regenerate its audio clip.

items.locator: row 1, col 5 (hope); dictionary key "hope" (also shown in mv2-06)
items.original: hope | 희망
items.problem: Only the noun is given. The verb (I hope ~ = 바라다, 희망하다) is the more frequent use at this level. The same dictionary gives both parts of speech for comparable words: start 시작하다; 시작, help 돕다; 도움, work 일하다; 일.
items.correction: 바라다, 희망하다; 희망

items.locator: row 3, col 3 (teacher), repeating mv1-04 row 5, col 1
items.original: mv1-04: teacher | 선生님 ; mv1-06: teacher | 선생님
items.problem: The same headword, with the same meaning, appears in two lessons of the same series only two lessons apart. Within mv1 (1,200 cells) only 8 headwords repeat, so this looks like an authoring slip rather than planned spiral review. It wastes one of the 30 slots in mv1-06.
items.correction: Replace teacher in mv1-06 r3c3 with an unused mv1-level word (the replacement needs a new audio clip via node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.original: nothing | 아무것도
items.problem: In Korean, '아무것도' needs a negative predicate, while English 'nothing' carries the negation itself. The bare gloss hides this, and it invites the double-negative error "I don't have nothing". Compare mv1-04's never | 결코 ~않다, which does show the negation.
items.correction: 아무것도 ~ 없음(않음)

items.locator: row 1, col 1 (travel); dictionary key "travel" (also shown in mv2-08, mv3-15)
items.original: travel | 여행
items.problem: The gloss is noun-only and is exactly the same string as trip | 여행 (mv1-07 r2c2) and journey | 여행. Learners get no way to tell travel from trip, and the main verb use (travel to Busan = 여행하다) is missing.
items.correction: 여행하다; 여행

items.original: outside | 외부
items.problem: '외부' is a formal Sino-Korean noun. The dominant use at this level is the adverb or preposition (go/play outside = 밖에, 밖으로; outside the house = ~ 밖에). The same series glosses out | 밖으로 and into | 안으로, so this entry is inconsistent with them. inside | 내부 has the same pattern.
items.correction: 밖에, 밖으로; 바깥(쪽)

items.original: shall | ~할 것이다
items.problem: The only sense shown is the plain first-person future. That use is formal or archaic in modern (especially American) English. The sense a middle-school learner actually meets is the offer or suggestion question "Shall I/we ~?" = ~할까요?, and it is missing. With this gloss, "Shall we dance?" reads as "우리는 춤출 것이다", which is the wrong function.
items.correction: ~할까요? (Shall I/we ~?); ~할 것이다

items.locator: grid row 3 col 2 'either'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9802-9803; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2546
items.original: either	어느 쪽이든
items.problem: '어느 쪽이든' is correct but covers only the determiner sense. Two uses that middle-school-1 learners need are missing: 'either A or B' (A든지 B든지) and the adverb in negative sentences (I don't like it either = ~도 역시 (아니다)). Longman English-Korean lists both. The same entry is shown in mv3-08.
items.correction: (둘 중) 어느 하나(의), 어느 쪽이든; (부정문에서) ~도 역시; either A or B: A든지 B든지

items.locator: grid row 4 col 1 'excuse'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9818-9819; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2551
items.original: excuse	변명하다
items.problem: The card gives only the verb '변명하다'. That is not the main sense of the verb. The main sense is 'forgive / pardon' (용서하다, 양해하다), which is the one in 'Excuse me', the first place a middle-school-1 learner meets this word. The very common noun sense (변명, 핑계) is missing too. Longman English-Korean lists the verb as 봐주다/양해해 주다 first, and the noun as 변명, 해명 / 핑계, 구실. It does not list a plain '변명하다' verb sense; the closest is '⋯에 대한 변명이 되다' (serve as an excuse for). The same entry is shown in mv3-14.
items.correction: 용서하다, 양해하다; 변명, 핑계 (Excuse me. 실례합니다)

items.locator: grid row 4 col 4 'player'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9830-9831; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2554
items.original: player	플레이어
items.problem: The gloss is a transliteration and never gives the core meaning '선수' (athlete). Longman English-Korean lists 운동선수 first and 연주자 second. 'CD/DVD 플레이어' (the device) is only its 4th sense. The same grid teaches football, baseball and basketball, where 'player' means 선수.
items.correction: 선수; 연주자; (CD 등) 재생기, 플레이어

items.locator: grid row 4 col 5 'picture'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9942-9943; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2585
items.original: picture	그림
items.problem: '그림' is correct, but '사진' (photograph) is missing. That sense drives the extremely common phrase 'take a picture'. Longman English-Korean lists 그림 first and 사진 second. The same entry is shown in mv2-04.
items.correction: 그림; 사진

items.locator: grid row 5 col 3 'most'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 9958-9959; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2589
items.original: most	가장
items.problem: The card gives only the superlative sense '가장' (the most). The determiner/pronoun sense '대부분(의)' (most people, most of them) is missing, although it is at least as frequent. Cambridge Grammar treats 'most' as both the superlative marker and a determiner meaning 'the majority of'. The same entry is shown in mv3-08.
items.correction: 가장; 대부분(의)

items.locator: grid row 2 col 5 'England'; content/voca_dictionary.json line 10014-10015; dump voca-lessons.tsv line 2603
items.original: England	영국
items.problem: England is 잉글랜드, the largest of the four countries of the United Kingdom. It is not the UK (영국) as a whole. Longman English-Korean translates it as 잉글랜드 and describes it as the largest country in the U.K. Calling England '영국' is common casual Korean, but a vocabulary card should be accurate.
items.correction: 잉글랜드 (영국을 이루는 나라 중 하나; 흔히 '영국'으로도 부름)

Longman English-Korean lists the verb first (변하다, 바뀌다 / 바꾸다) and has 거스름돈/잔돈 among the noun senses. The same entry is shown in mv2-09 and mv3-30.
items.correction: 바꾸다, 변하다; 변화; 잔돈

items.original: lose	잃다
items.problem: '잃다' is correct, but the core sense '(경기에서) 지다' (lose a game, the opposite of win) is missing. Longman English-Korean lists '<경기·선거·전쟁 등>에서 지다' as a main sense. mv1-19 teaches 'win 승리하다', so the matching antonym sense is absent. The same entry is shown in mv2-10 and mv3-15.
