items.locator: row 4, col 5 (bury); content/voca_dictionary.json:13606-13607 (the entry is shared with mv3-21 r3c2)
items.original: bury	묻다
items.problem: The Korean '묻다' has several meanings: '(질문을) 묻다' (ask), '(땅에) 묻다' (bury) and '(얼룩이) 묻다' (stain). The dictionary uses exactly the same string, '묻다', for ask (content/voca_dictionary.json:8754-8755, taught in mv1-02 and mv2-08). On the card, and in the Leitner review list and the wrong-answer list, bury and ask look identical. The lesson is a list of unrelated words, so nothing around the card helps the learner tell which '묻다' is meant. The most common reading of '묻다' is 'ask'.
items.correction: bury → "(땅에) 묻다, 매장하다" (a similar clarification could be added to ask → "(질문을) 묻다"). Only the Korean meaning changes, so the English audio clip is unaffected.

items.original: appearance	외관
items.problem: 외관 is correct but mostly describes buildings or objects. The two senses most useful at this level are missing: 외모 (a person's looks, as in 'judge by appearance') and 출현/등장 ('make an appearance').
items.correction: 외모, 겉모습; 출현, 등장

items.locator: mv2-31 row 2 col 4 'neck' and row 5 col 6 'throat' (same lesson)
items.original: neck	목 / throat	목구멍
items.problem: Both glosses are correct on their own, but they sit in the same lesson and Korean 목 also means throat (목이 아프다 = sore throat). In the Korean-to-English quiz, the prompt '목' can list both neck and throat, and only neck counts. In the speed drill, 'throat = 목' may appear as a planned mismatch and be scored wrong when the learner marks it a match. The drill and quiz exclude only identical meaning strings (voca.md R-7), so this pair is not caught.
items.correction: Keep the glosses. Add neck/throat to the drill and quiz distractor exclusions that are planned for R-7, or sharpen the neck gloss to '목 (머리와 몸통을 잇는 부분)'.

items.original: vacation	휴가
items.problem: For Korean students the most frequent sense is 방학 (summer vacation = 여름 방학), and it is missing.
items.correction: 방학, 휴가

items.locator: mv2-32 row 1 col 3 'jaw' and row 1 col 4 'chin' (same lesson)
items.original: jaw	턱, 턱뼈 / chin	턱 끝
items.problem: Both are in the same lesson and chin is very commonly glossed simply as 턱. In the speed drill, 'chin = 턱, 턱뼈' can appear as a planned mismatch that many learners would reasonably mark a match. The glosses separate the words better than neck/throat do, so the risk is smaller.
items.correction: Keep the glosses and add jaw/chin to the drill distractor exclusions, or write chin as '턱 (얼굴 아래 끝부분)'.

items.locator: mv2-35 row 3 col 1 'contrary' (dictionary key 'contrary'; also hv-07 r2c3)
items.original: contrary	반대로
items.problem: The adverb-like gloss 반대로 fits only the phrases 'on the contrary' and 'contrary to'. The headword is mainly an adjective (반대의, 상반된) and a noun (the contrary, 반대), and those senses are missing.
items.correction: 반대의; 반대 (on the contrary 반대로)

items.locator: mv2-36 'export' etymology box (PREFIX_RULES entry 'export'; the same rule shows in hv-04; the 'import' rule has the same pattern)
items.original: ex(밖으로) + port(항구/나르다) ➔ 항구 밖으로 물건을 내보내다, 수출하다
items.problem: export comes from Latin exportare = ex 'out' + portare 'to carry'. 'Harbour' (portus) is only a related word, not a part of export. The explanation '항구 밖으로' teaches the folk etymology. The file's own V-11 note says a wrong breakdown is learnt like a right one.
items.correction: ex(밖으로) + port(나르다) ➔ 밖으로 실어 나르다, 수출하다

items.locator: mv2-36 row 1 col 3 'admire' (dictionary key 'admire'; also hv-43 r4c1)
items.original: admire	감탄하다
items.problem: The core sense at middle-school level is 존경하다 (to hold someone in high esteem, as in 'I admire my father'). That sense is missing; only 감탄하다 is shown.
items.correction: 존경하다, 감탄하다

items.original: sow	뿌리다
items.problem: 뿌리다 on its own also means spray or sprinkle (water, perfume). sow means specifically to sow seed, and the object is missing from the gloss.
items.correction: (씨를) 뿌리다

items.locator: mv2-36 row 5 col 5 'grade' (dictionary key 'grade'; also mv1-39 r5c2, mv3-21 r1c2)
items.original: grade	등급
items.problem: Only 등급 (rating) is given. The two senses a Korean middle-school learner needs most are missing: 학년 (school year: 'the eighth grade') and 성적 (mark: 'get good grades').
items.correction: 학년; 성적; 등급

items.locator: mv2-37 row 4 col 2 'biography' (dictionary key 'biography'; also mv3-22 r4c6, hv-20 r1c6)
items.original: biography	전기
items.problem: The bare Korean 전기 is a homograph. Five lessons earlier the same series teaches electricity with the identical string (mv2-32 r2c6 'electricity	전기'). Nothing on the card tells the learner that this 전기 is 傳記 (a life story) and not 電氣.
items.correction: (인물의) 전기(傳記), 일대기

items.original: force	힘
items.problem: Only the noun is given. The verb 강요하다 ('force A to do B') is a core middle-school pattern and is missing.
items.correction: 힘; 강요하다

items.locator: mv2-37 row 4 col 6 'clap' (dictionary key 'clap'; also mv3-26 r1c6)
items.original: clap	박수
items.problem: The gloss is noun-only. clap is mainly used as a verb ('clap your hands', 손뼉을 치다).
items.correction: 손뼉을 치다, 박수를 치다; 박수 (소리)

items.locator: mv2-37 row 5 col 3 'forecast' (dictionary key 'forecast'; also hv-21 r3c3, mv3-31 r3c4)
items.original: forecast	예측
items.problem: The key collocation 'weather forecast' means 일기 예보, and the sense 예보 is missing. The word is also a verb (예측하다, 예보하다).
items.correction: 예보, 예측; 예보하다

items.original: immigrate	이민하다
items.problem: The gloss has no direction, yet direction is the only thing that separates immigrate (이민 오다, moving into a country) from emigrate (이민 가다). The dictionary glosses emigrate as '이주하다', so the pair is never contrasted.
items.correction: (다른 나라로) 이민 오다, 이주해 오다

items.locator: mv2-40 row 4 col 2 'degree' (dictionary key 'degree'; also mv3-22 r1c5, hv-34 r4c5)
items.original: degree	정도
items.problem: Only 정도 (extent) is given. The unit sense (온도·각도의 '도', as in 'It's 30 degrees') and the academic sense (학위) are missing. The unit sense is among the most frequent uses at this level, especially in weather listening items.
items.correction: 정도; (온도·각도의) 도; 학위

items.original: dumb = "어리석은; 말을 못 하는"
items.problem: The 'unable to speak' sense is dated and widely considered offensive, and the 'stupid' sense is informal and derogatory. Neither sense carries a register note, so a paid course is teaching children to use this word neutrally.
items.correction: dumb → "(구어·비하) 멍청한; (옛·모욕적) 말을 못 하는"

items.original: dull = "둔한"
items.problem: The most frequent sense of dull, 'boring, not interesting' (지루한), is missing. So is 'not sharp or not bright' (무딘, 흐릿한). With only 둔한, 'a dull movie' reads as '둔한 영화'.
items.correction: dull → "지루한; 둔한, 무딘"

items.original: certain = "확실한"
items.problem: The determiner sense 'particular' (어떤, 특정한: a certain person, in certain cases) is missing, and it is very frequent in school texts.
items.correction: certain → "확실한; 어떤, 특정한"

items.original: fairly = "상당히"
items.problem: The 'in a fair way' sense, 공정하게 (treat everyone fairly), is missing. It is the sense learners arrive at directly from fair = 공정한.
items.correction: fairly → "상당히, 꽤; 공정하게"

items.locator: mv3-03 r3c1 'succeeding' (same lesson has r3c5 'lasting' = 지속적인)
items.original: succeeding = "다음의, 계속되는"
items.problem: 'succeeding' means 'following, next in order' (succeeding generations = 후대). The Korean 계속되는 reads as 'continuing', which is the meaning of 'lasting' (지속적인) in the same lesson. The gloss therefore blurs two different words and invites confusion with succeed (성공하다).
items.correction: succeeding → "뒤이은, 다음의"

items.original: confirmed = "확고한, 상습적인"
items.problem: The headword is also the past tense and past participle of confirm, and that is how middle-school learners nearly always meet it ('The news was confirmed' = 확인되었다). The gloss gives only the formal adjective sense (a confirmed liar = 상습적인 거짓말쟁이) and leaves out 확인된. A learner will read 'confirmed' in a passive sentence as 확고한/상습적인.
items.correction: Replace the headword with the lemma 'confirm' (확인하다), which the dictionary already has as '확인하다'. If 'confirmed' is kept, gloss it as "확인된; 확고한, 상습적인". If the headword changes, regenerate its clip.

items.original: abuse = "남용"
items.problem: The gloss covers only misuse (drug abuse). It leaves out the equally common 'cruel treatment' sense, 학대 (child abuse, animal abuse), and the verb use.
items.correction: abuse → "남용; 학대(하다)"

items.original: labour = "노동"
items.problem: The British spelling is shown with no marker, next to the American 'endeavor' in the same lesson. Everywhere else the course marks British variants with brackets (colo(u)r, hono(u)r, neighbo(u)r), and hv-37 uses 'labor'. The checker also lists labor/labour as a 'possible typo' pair.
items.correction: Show it as 'labo(u)r', following the existing bracket convention and adding 'labo(u)r' → 'labor' to VOCA_SPEECH_FORMS, or use 'labor'. Either choice changes the spoken text, so regenerate the clip.

items.original: peasant = "농부"
items.problem: The gloss is identical to farmer = "농부" (mv1-21). 'Peasant' means a member of the poor, low-status rural class (농민, 소작농), usually in a historical setting, and it can be insulting. Glossing it 농부 teaches that it means the same as farmer.
items.correction: peasant → "(가난한) 농민, 소작농"

items.original: brilliant = "빛나는"
items.problem: The gloss gives only the literal 'shining' sense. It leaves out the senses learners meet most, 'excellent' and 'very clever' (a brilliant idea = 기발한 생각, a brilliant scientist = 뛰어난 과학자).
items.correction: brilliant → "훌륭한, 뛰어난; 빛나는"

items.original: block = "블록"
items.problem: The gloss is just the loanword 블록, which does not explain the word. It leaves out the very common verb sense 'to obstruct' (막다, 차단하다: The road is blocked) and the city sense 구역.
items.correction: block → "막다, 차단하다; (도시의) 구역, 블록"

items.file: content/lessons/phonics/mv3-06.json (wordgrid) and content/voca_dictionary.json (key 'cooky'; there is no 'cookie' entry)
items.original: cooky = "쿠키"
items.problem: 'cooky' is a dated spelling. The standard spelling is 'cookie', and the dictionary has no 'cookie' entry at all, so this is the only form of the word learners ever see. The ko-to-en question also teaches them to produce 'cooky'. It is easily confused with 'kooky' (괴짜 같은).
items.correction: Change the headword to 'cookie' (meaning 쿠키) in mv3-06.json and rename the dictionary key. Because the English text changes, regenerate its clip in the same task with `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs`, as the project's CLAUDE.md requires.

items.original: most = "가장"
items.problem: The determiner sense 'the majority of' (대부분의: most students, most of the time) is missing. It is at least as frequent as the superlative 가장. Mixing up most, almost and most of is a classic mistake for Korean learners, and 'almost' sits in the same lesson.
items.correction: most → "대부분(의); 가장"

items.locator: mv3-08 r2c1 'correctly' (quiz #7, en-to-ko) and r3c2 'exactly' (quiz #14, ko-to-en)
items.original: exactly = "정확히, 꼭" ; correctly = "올바르게, 정확하게"
items.problem: 정확히 and 정확하게 are the same Korean adverb in two forms, so the glosses overlap in meaning even though the strings differ. The existing overlap check misses them. On '[ 정확히, 꼭 ] 에 해당하는 올바른 영단어', 'correctly' can be offered as a wrong option, and a learner who goes by the Korean has no way to tell the two apart.
items.correction: Give correctly only "올바르게, 바르게" and exactly "정확히, 꼭 (딱)", or add the pair to the synonym list used by the distractor filter.

items.original: either = "어느 쪽이든"
items.problem: mv3-08 is an adverb lesson (rather, quite, indeed, besides, anyway...), but the gloss gives only the determiner/pronoun sense. The adverb sense, '(in a negative sentence) also' (I don't like it either = 나도 역시 좋아하지 않는다), is a core middle-school grammar point and is missing. The paired 'neither 둘 다 아닌' makes the gap more noticeable.
items.correction: either → "(부정문에서) ~도 또한; 어느 한쪽(의)"

items.original: jar = "항아리"
items.problem: 항아리 suggests a large earthenware crock. In modern English a jar is usually a small glass container with a lid (a jar of jam = 잼 한 병), and the gloss does not cover that everyday sense.
items.correction: jar → "(유리)병, 단지; 항아리"

items.original: nephew = "조카 (남자), 생질"
items.problem: 생질 means only a sister's son (누이의 아들). A nephew can be the son of a brother or a sister, so offering 생질 as an equivalent is too narrow. It is also an uncommon Sino-Korean kinship term for this level.
items.correction: nephew → "(남자) 조카"

items.original: arrest	체포
items.problem: Only the noun is given. arrest is used mainly as a verb ('be arrested', 'arrest a suspect'), and the other five words in the same row (remain, prove, locate, replace, halt) are all glossed as verbs. The noun gloss is not wrong, but it hides the more frequent verb use.
items.correction: arrest: 체포하다; 체포

items.original: cleave	쪼개지다
items.problem: There are two problems. (1) The gloss gives only the intransitive '쪼개지다'. The main sense of cleave is transitive, to split something with a sharp instrument (쪼개다), and the word also has a rare opposite sense, 'cleave to' (to cling to). (2) cleave is a rare, largely literary verb with irregular forms (cleft/clove/cloven). It appears in no other lesson of the 195-lesson mv/hv corpus (checked against the full voca-lessons dump), which suggests it does not belong in a Middle School 3 core list. Whether to keep it at this level needs expert review against the curriculum word list.
items.correction: Either replace cleave with a word at mv3 level, or gloss it as 'cleave: (날붙이로) 쪼개다, 가르다'.

items.locator: row 3 col 3 'excuse'; content/voca_dictionary.json key 'excuse' (line 9818). The same entry is also shown in mv1-11.
items.original: excuse	변명하다
items.problem: The only gloss is the verb '변명하다'. The verb's first senses are to forgive or pardon (용서하다/봐주다, as in 'Excuse me') and to let someone leave. The justify sense comes third. The sense learners use most, 'make an excuse', is the noun (변명/핑계), which is also pronounced differently (/-s/ for the noun vs /-z/ for the verb). A learner guided by '변명하다' may write '*He excused that he was late' and will not connect the word to 'Excuse me'.
items.correction: excuse: 변명, 핑계 (명사); 용서하다, 봐주다 (동사)

items.original: expect	기대하다
items.problem: The first sense of expect is neutral prediction ('to predict or believe that something will happen' = 예상하다). The Korean 기대하다 suggests hopeful anticipation, so a learner with only this gloss misreads 'We expect heavy rain' or 'I expected him to fail'. This is a well-known confusion for Korean learners.
items.correction: expect: 예상하다, 기대하다

items.original: common	공통의
items.problem: Only the 'shared' sense is given. The 'frequent, usual' sense (흔한, as in 'a common mistake' or 'common cold') is at least as frequent and is standard at middle-school level, but it is missing.
items.correction: common: 흔한; 공통의

items.original: fault	결점
items.problem: The only gloss is 결점 (flaw). The first and most used sense is responsibility for something that went wrong ('It's my fault' = 내 잘못이야), and that sense is missing.
items.correction: fault: 잘못, 책임; 결점

items.locator: row 5 col 4 'grave'; content/voca_dictionary.json key 'grave' (line 4002). The same entry is also shown in mv2-34 and hv-35.
items.original: grave	무덤
items.problem: mv3-18 is an adjective set: 28 of its 30 words are adjectives (fresh, empty, boring ... elementary, charming). grave is shown only as the noun 무덤. Its adjective sense, serious or grave in consequence ('grave danger', 'a grave mistake'), is the one this lesson places it with, and it is a frequent exam sense. The noun gloss is correct but it is not the whole word, and the adjective sense is missing.
items.correction: grave: 무덤; 심각한, 중대한

items.original: appointment	약속
items.problem: The bare 약속 does not tell appointment (an arranged meeting, e.g. a doctor's appointment) apart from promise, which mv3-20 also glosses as 약속. This gap causes the typical Korean learner error '*I have a promise with my friend'. The other main senses, 예약 (booking) and 임명 (appointing to a post), are also missing.
items.correction: appointment: (만날) 약속, 예약; 임명

items.original: sophomore	2학년
items.problem: The bare '2학년' is imprecise. A sophomore is a second-year student at a US four-year high school or college (US high school sophomore = 10th grade), not any 2nd grader. It is also a person noun (2학년생), not a school year.
items.correction: sophomore: (미국 4년제 고교·대학의) 2학년생

items.locator: row 5 col 6 'duplicate'; content/voca_dictionary.json key 'duplicate' (line 1082). The same entry is shown in hv-10 row 1 col 2.
items.original: duplicate	중복
items.problem: '중복' means overlap or redundancy, which translates the noun 'duplication' (as in software labels like '중복 항목'). The headword 'duplicate' has three core senses: verb, to make a copy (복사하다/복제하다); noun, an identical copy (사본); adjective, identical (똑같은). The card shows none of these, so a learner who reads 'make a duplicate of the key' with this gloss gets it wrong.
items.correction: duplicate: 복제하다, 복사하다; 사본; 똑같은

items.original: junior	손아래의
items.problem: junior sits next to senior ('연장자, 선배; 고위의'), but it is glossed only with the adjective 손아래의. Its common senses are missing: lower in rank (하급의), the noun 후배/연소자 ('He is my junior'), and US third-year student (as in 'junior high'). The glosses of the pair are lopsided.
items.correction: junior: 손아래의, 하급의; 후배; (미국 고교·대학) 3학년생

items.locator: row 1 col 2 'grade'; dictionary key 'grade' (the same card also appears in mv1-39 and mv2-36)
items.original: grade | 등급
items.problem: The card shows only 등급 (rank or quality level). The senses a middle-school learner meets most are 학년 ('I'm in the ninth grade') and 성적 or 점수 ('get good grades'), which learner dictionaries list first. The same row is about school (semester 학기, score 점수), which points to the school senses. The card also appears in mv1-39, where it matters even more for beginners.
items.correction: 학년; 성적; 등급

items.locator: row 3 col 2 'bury'; dictionary key 'bury' (also in mv2-28)
items.original: bury | 묻다
items.problem: 묻다 is a Korean homonym: 'ask', 'bury' and 'get stained'. The site's own dictionary gives the identical string to 'ask' (ask = 묻다, taught in the free preview lesson mv1-02 and in mv2-08). A card has no context, so a learner who has already learned 'ask = 묻다' reads 'bury = 묻다' as 'ask'.
items.correction: (땅에) 묻다, 매장하다

items.locator: row 1 col 5 'degree'; dictionary key 'degree' (also in mv2-40 and hv-34)
items.original: degree | 정도
items.problem: The card shows only 정도. It leaves out the measurement sense (온도 or 각도의) 도, as in '30 degrees', which middle-school texts use constantly, and the academic sense 학위.
items.correction: 정도; (온도·각도의) 도; 학위

items.locator: row 4 col 1 'type'; dictionary key 'type' (also in mv2-40)
items.original: type | 유형; 타자치다
items.problem: '타자치다' is not one word in standard Korean. The National Institute of Korean Language says '타자 치다' is written with a space. 'Typing' today is also more naturally 입력하다.
items.correction: 유형; (타자를) 치다, 입력하다

items.locator: row 4 col 6 'biography'; dictionary key 'biography' (also in mv2-37 and hv-20)
items.original: biography | 전기
items.problem: The most common reading of 전기 is 'electricity'. The site's dictionary gives the identical string to electricity (electricity = 전기, taught in mv2-32 and mv3-03, just before this lesson). With no context, 'biography = 전기' reads as 'electricity'.
items.correction: 전기(傳記), 일대기

items.locator: row 5 col 1 'detective'; dictionary key 'detective' (also in mv2-32 and hv-66)
items.original: detective | 형사
items.problem: detective covers both 탐정 (a private or fictional detective, as in detective stories and Sherlock Holmes) and 형사 (a police detective). The card shows only 형사, which leaves out the sense young readers meet most.
items.correction: 탐정; 형사

items.locator: row 5 col 6 'ceremony'; dictionary key 'ceremony' (also in mv2-38)
items.original: ceremony | 의식
items.problem: 의식 is a homonym: 儀式 (ceremony) and 意識 (consciousness). The site's dictionary gives the identical string to consciousness (consciousness = 의식, in hv-57). Middle-school learners are less exposed to the 'consciousness' sense, so the risk is lower than for bury, biography and mayor.
items.correction: 식, 의식(儀式)

items.locator: row 1 col 5 'vacation'; dictionary key 'vacation' (also in mv1-22 and mv2-31)
items.original: vacation | 휴가
items.problem: For Korean students, vacation usually means 방학 ('summer vacation' = 여름 방학). 휴가 is the sense for work leave. The card shows only 휴가.
items.correction: 방학; 휴가

items.locator: row 5 col 3 'puzzle' (quiz Q27, en-to-ko) and row 5 col 4 'riddle' (quiz Q28, ko-to-en)
items.original: puzzle | 퍼즐   /   riddle | 수수께끼
items.problem: Standard English-Korean dictionaries give puzzle as '퍼즐, 수수께끼'. Q28 '[ 수수께끼 ]' can offer puzzle as a wrong option, and Q27 ('puzzle') can offer 수수께끼 as a wrong option. The loanword 퍼즐 does help the learner separate the two, so the risk is limited.
items.correction: Keep 퍼즐 for puzzle (it may become '퍼즐; 난제') and make riddle '수수께끼 (말로 내는 문제)'. Or rely on the segment-aware or synonym-aware distractor fix.

items.original: chase | 추적
items.problem: chase is mainly a verb (뒤쫓다), and every other word in its row is a verb (introduce, produce, float, discuss, shrug). The card gives only the noun 추적.
items.correction: 뒤쫓다, 추적하다; 추적

items.locator: row 5 col 4 'deal'; dictionary key 'deal' (also in mv2-25)
items.original: deal | 거래
items.problem: Row 5 is all verbs (slide, suck, bother, treat, destroy), but deal is glossed only as the noun 거래. The verb sense that middle-school learners need, 'deal with = 다루다, 처리하다', is missing.
items.correction: 거래; (deal with) 다루다, 처리하다

items.locator: row 1 col 6 'clap'; dictionary key 'clap' (also in mv2-37)
items.original: clap | 박수
items.problem: clap is mainly a verb ('clap your hands' = 손뼉을 치다). The card gives only the noun 박수, which is also the exact string the dictionary uses for applause, so the verb and the noun are blurred together.
items.correction: 손뼉을 치다, 박수를 치다; 박수

items.locator: row 2 col 6 'mayor'; dictionary key 'mayor' (also in mv1-28, mv2-40 and hv-39)
items.original: mayor | 시장
items.problem: The most common reading of 시장 is 'market'. The site's dictionary gives the identical string to market (market = 시장, taught in mv1-35 and mv2-19). On a card with no context, 'mayor = 시장' reads as 'market'.
items.correction: (시의) 시장, 시장(市長)

items.locator: row 3 col 6 'stupid' (quiz Q18, ko-to-en) and row 4 col 1 'silly' (quiz Q19, en-to-ko)
items.original: stupid | 어리석은   /   silly | 바보 같은
items.problem: Dictionaries give silly as 어리석은 as well as 바보 같은. The strings differ, so the distractor filter lets them face each other. (1) Q18 '[ 어리석은 ] 에 해당하는 올바른 영단어를 고르세요.' can offer silly as a wrong option. (2) Q19 ('silly') can offer 어리석은 as a wrong option. (3) The speed drill can show 'silly = 어리석은' and expect 불일치. All three answers are lexically correct.
items.correction: Give the pair glosses that do not overlap and still guide the learner, e.g. stupid 어리석은, 멍청한 and silly 우스꽝스러운, 철없는 (바보 같은). Or apply the same segment-aware or synonym-aware exclusion as in the firm/company fix.

items.original: loaf | 덩어리
items.problem: loaf specifically means a shaped loaf of baked bread ('a loaf of bread' = 빵 한 덩이). A bare 덩어리 reads as any lump, which is closer to 'lump' or 'chunk'.
items.correction: (빵 한) 덩어리, 덩이

items.locator: mv3-32 wordgrid row 3 col 1 (operator), next to row 3 col 2 operate 작동하다; content/voca_dictionary.json line 5278-5281 (the same entry is shown in hv-46 and mv2-40)
items.original: operator → "meaning": "운영자"
items.problem: Learner dictionaries list first 'a person who uses and controls a machine or vehicle' and 'a person who connects telephone calls'. 'A company that runs a business' (tour operator) comes after these. 운영자 in current Korean usually suggests a website or community administrator, which is not what 'operator' means. The card sits next to 'operate 작동하다' but does not show the link between the two words.
items.correction: (기계) 조작자, 기사; (전화) 교환원; 운영 업체·운영자

items.locator: mv3-32 wordgrid row 3 col 4 (fur); content/voca_dictionary.json line 14142-14145 (the same entry is shown in mv2-40)
items.original: fur → "meaning": "모피"
items.problem: The primary sense is the thick hair on a living animal (털). 모피 (processed pelt or fur garment) is the secondary sense. 'The cat's fur is soft' cannot be read as 모피.
items.correction: (동물의) 털; 모피

items.locator: mv3-32 wordgrid row 3 col 5 (shore 해안) and row 5 col 1 (beach 해변); dictionary lines 15230 and 11502; quiz distractor rule at src/lib/vocaUtils.ts lines 280-282
items.original: shore → "해안"; beach → "해변" (same lesson); poolMeanings filter `.filter((m) => m && m !== correctMeaning)`
items.problem: shore and beach are near-synonyms in one lesson, and their Korean glosses (해안 / 해변) are near-synonyms too. Both words sit at even positions (16 and 24), so both are English-to-Korean items. The distractor filter removes only identical meanings, so in about 1 of 10 runs (3 of 29 meanings drawn) the 'shore' item offers both 해안 and 해변, or the 'beach' item offers both. 해변 is an acceptable rendering of 'shore' in many Korean-English glossaries.
items.correction: Leave the glosses as they are but make them distinct: shore '(바다·호수의) 물가, 해안' and beach '해변, 바닷가(모래사장)'. Or add this pair to a near-synonym exclusion so each meaning is never used as a distractor for the other.

items.locator: mv3-32 wordgrid row 5 col 4 (subsequently); content/voca_dictionary.json line 6606-6609 (the same entry is shown in hv-58)
items.original: subsequently → "meaning": "이후"
items.problem: 'subsequently' is an adverb. 이후 is a Korean noun ('the period after'), so the gloss implies the wrong part of speech. Other adverbs in this set are glossed as adverbs (steadily 꾸준히, relatively 상대적으로, ultimately 궁극적으로).
items.correction: 그 후에, 이후에, 나중에

items.locator: mv3-35 wordgrid row 4 col 4 (handicap); content/voca_dictionary.json line 13942-13945 (the same entry is shown in mv2-36)
items.original: handicap → "meaning": "장애"
items.problem: The disability sense of 'handicap' is labelled old-fashioned and usually offensive by Oxford, Cambridge and Collins, which recommend 'disability' / 'disabled'. The card teaches that sense as the only meaning and gives no warning. The neutral senses (a disadvantage; a golf or racing handicap) are missing.
items.correction: 불리한 조건, 핸디캡(경기의 핸디캡); (구식·모욕적 표현) 장애 → 장애는 disability로 표현

items.locator: mv3-36 wordgrid row 4 col 5 (bitterly); content/voca_dictionary.json line 15422-15425
items.original: bitterly → "meaning": "씁쓸하게"
items.problem: 씁쓸하게 is a mild, wry feeling. The main uses of 'bitterly' are strong: 'weep/complain bitterly' (비통하게, 격렬하게) and 'extremely' ('bitterly disappointed' 몹시 실망한, 'bitterly cold' 몹시 추운). The gloss covers only a weakened form of the emotional sense and leaves out the intensifier sense, which is the one learners meet most often.
items.correction: 몹시, 비통하게, 격렬하게 (예: bitterly cold 몹시 추운, bitterly disappointed 몹시 실망한)

items.locator: mv3-38 wordgrid row 1 col 6 (tear); content/voca_dictionary.json line 11966-11969 (the same entry is shown in mv1-32 and mv2-07)
items.original: tear → "meaning": "찢다; 눈물"
items.problem: 'tear' is a heteronym: 찢다 is /ter/ (rhymes with 'bear') and 눈물 is /tɪr/ (rhymes with 'ear'). The card audio (speakText(vocaSpeechForm(word))) plays one pronunciation, and the gloss gives two meanings with no note that they are said differently. Which pronunciation the clip uses was not checked.
items.correction: 찢다 [teər]; 눈물 [tɪər] (뜻에 따라 발음이 다름)

items.locator: mv3-38 wordgrid row 4 col 2 (wake); content/voca_dictionary.json line 11702-11705 (the same entry is shown in mv1-29 and mv2-20)
items.original: wake → "meaning": "일어나다"
items.problem: 'wake' means to stop sleeping (깨다) or to rouse someone (깨우다). 일어나다 is the usual gloss for 'get up', the phrasal verb this word is most often confused with. The same Korean gloss 일어나다 is also used for 'happen' (mv3-39) and 'arise' (mv3-35), so three different verbs share one card meaning.
items.correction: (잠에서) 깨다; 깨우다

items.locator: mv3-40 wordgrid row 1 col 5 (inherit); dictionary key "inherit" at content/voca_dictionary.json line 4066-4069 (the same entry is shown in hv-35)
items.original: inherit → "meaning": "상속하다"
items.problem: 'inherit' means to RECEIVE property, a title or a trait from someone. 표준국어대사전 defines 상속하다 sense 2 from the giver's side: "한 사람이 사망한 후에 다른 사람에게 재산에 관한 권리와 의무의 일체를 이어 주다". Korean speakers also say '재산을 자녀에게 상속하다' (bequeath). The gloss therefore does not tell the learner which direction the verb goes, and it can teach the opposite one. It also leaves out the everyday non-legal sense (inherit a trait = 물려받다).
items.correction: 물려받다, 상속받다

items.locator: mv3-40 wordgrid row 3 col 6 (British); content/voca_dictionary.json line 15490-15493
items.original: British → "meaning": "영국의; 영국인"
items.problem: 'British' is an adjective. The noun use is only the plural 'the British'. There is no singular noun 'a British'; the singular is 'a Briton' (formal) or 'a Brit' (informal). A bare '영국인' gloss invites the classic error 'He is a British.'
items.correction: 영국의, 영국 사람의; (the British) 영국 사람들

items.original: mystery	mystery	미스터리	mv2-24 mv3-19
items.problem: The gloss is a transliteration of the headword, not a translation. 미스터리 is a real Korean loanword, so this is not wrong, but it conveys no meaning to a learner who does not already know the English word - and in Korean the loanword is narrower than the English, being used mainly of genre fiction (미스터리 소설). The everyday senses 수수께끼 and 신비 are not reachable from it. Compare the neighbouring entry myth = 신화, which does translate.
items.correction: 수수께끼, 신비; 미스터리(소설)

items.original: neglect	neglect	방치하다	hv-37
items.problem: 방치하다 means to leave something abandoned and unattended. That renders only the narrow 'neglect a child / neglect a building' use. The primary sense of 'neglect' - to fail to give proper care or attention to a duty, a task or a person - is 소홀히 하다 / 등한히 하다, and 'neglect one's duty' cannot be said as 의무를 방치하다 in natural Korean. The sense that fails to do something through carelessness ('he neglected to mention it') is also unreachable from 방치하다.
items.correction: 소홀히 하다, 등한히 하다; 방치하다

items.locator: TSV lines 2323 and 2324; JSON keys "neighbo(u)r" and "neighbor"
items.original:
neighbo(u)r	neighbour	이웃	mv1-23
neighbor	neighbor	이웃	mv2-15 mv3-29
items.problem: The same word has two separate dictionary entries with identical meanings, because the lesson files spell it two ways: content/lessons/phonics/mv1-23.json prints "neighbo(u)r" in its wordgrid while mv2-15.json and mv3-29.json print "neighbor". The searchWord for the parenthetical key is "neighbour" (British only), so that card is not reachable by searching the American spelling - it resolves to the other entry instead, with separate quiz/progress identity. This is systemic rather than a one-off: the same split exists for favo(u)r/favor, humo(u)r/humor, hono(u)r/honor, autumn(=fall)/autumn and dialog(ue)/dialogue, though only the neighbour pair falls in this line range.
items.correction: Keep one entry per word. Either spell the word the same way in all three lesson grids and delete the redundant key, or keep the "neighbo(u)r" key and give it a searchWord that matches both spellings so the American form resolves to the same card. Apply the same rule to the five other parenthetical/plain pairs listed above.

items.original: nephew	nephew	조카 (남자), 생질	mv3-10
items.problem: The secondary gloss 생질 is narrower than the English word. 표준국어대사전 defines 생질(甥姪) as 누이의 아들 - specifically a sister's son - whereas 'nephew' covers a brother's son equally. It is also an archaic kinship term that mv3-10's middle-school audience will not know. The paired entry niece = "조카딸, 질녀" (line 2339) does not have the same defect, since 질녀 is defined as 형제자매의 딸 and so matches 'niece' exactly; the asymmetry makes the nephew card the odd one out.
items.correction: 조카 (남자) — drop 생질, or replace it with 조카아들

items.original: nobility	nobility	귀족	hv-25
items.problem: The abstract sense 고귀함, 고결함 (nobility of character/spirit) is missing, and it is the sense the lesson's own structure points at. hv-25 is built on adjective + derived abstract noun pairs: ignorant/ignorance (무지한/무지), courageous/courage (용감한/용기), and noble/nobility. Every other pair in that grid keeps the morphological link, but noble is glossed 고귀한 while nobility jumps to 귀족, a class of people. 귀족 is a real sense of the word, but as the sole gloss it breaks the pattern the lesson is teaching.
items.correction: 고귀함, 고결함; 귀족(계급)

items.locator: TSV lines 2343 and 2360; JSON keys "nobody" and "nothing"
items.original:
nobody	nobody	아무도	mv1-28
nothing	nothing	아무것도	mv1-07
items.problem: 아무도 and 아무것도 are negative-polarity items in Korean: they are ungrammatical without a following negative (아무도 없다 / 아무도 오지 않았다). As standalone glosses they are incomplete fragments. The dictionary already uses the correct style for the same class of word elsewhere - none = "아무것도 ~없다" (line 2347), never = "결코 ~않다" (line 2332), neither = "둘 다 아닌" (line 2326) - so this is an internal inconsistency, not a house style.
items.correction: nobody: 아무도 ~않다, 아무도 없다 / nothing: 아무것도 ~않다, 아무것도 없다

items.original: note	note	메모, 쪽지	hv-45 mv1-24 mv2-06
items.problem: The gloss gives only the 'short written message' noun. The verb sense 주목하다 / 주의하다 / 언급하다 is missing, and it is the sense the surrounding lesson depends on: the hv-45 word grid contains both 'note' and 'notable' (glossed 주목할 만한, TSV line 2356), and hv-46 adds 'noted' (유명한, 저명한). Both derived words come from the verb sense that the headword does not list. The common noun senses 음표 (music) and (영) 지폐 are also absent.
items.correction: 메모, 쪽지; 주목하다, 주의하다; 음표

items.original: obey	obey	복종하다	hv-20 mv2-22 mv3-39
items.problem: 복종하다 is a defensible gloss for obeying a person or an order, but it is the only gloss given and it is too narrow for the lessons that cite it. mv3-39 is a basic-verb grid (hide, guess, carry, smell, roll, pull, bring, belong, fight, fear, shoot, obey, ride, need...) and mv2-22 likewise, where the collocations a Korean middle-schooler meets are 'obey the rules / obey the law / obey your parents'. In Korean those are 규칙을 지키다 / 법을 따르다, not 규칙에 복종하다, which is unnatural and carries a submission nuance the English does not.
items.correction: (명령에) 복종하다; (규칙·법을) 따르다, 지키다

items.original: observe	observe	관찰하다	hv-06 mv2-22
items.problem: 'observe' is given only the sense 관찰하다, but its second core sense - (규칙·법·관습을) 지키다, 준수하다 - is missing. This is not an abstract omission: the hv-06 word grid contains observe, observer, observation, observatory AND observance in the same five-row screen, and observance is glossed 준수 (TSV line 2389). The learner is shown 준수 as the noun of a verb they have just been told means 관찰하다, with nothing in the lesson to bridge the two.
items.correction: 관찰하다; (규칙·약속을) 지키다, 준수하다

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2411; key "offensive" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-31)
items.original: offensive	offensive	공격적인	hv-31
items.problem: Only 공격적인 is given. Wiktionary lists "Causing offense; arousing a visceral reaction of disgust, anger, hatred, sadness, or indignation" as sense 1 and the attack-related sense as sense 2 — so the omitted sense (불쾌한, 모욕적인) is the primary one. The omission is inconsistent within its own word family: the same hv-31 lesson glosses offend as 기분을 상하게 하다 and offense with two senses (위반, 범죄; 공격), so the adjective built on 기분을 상하게 하다 is the only member of the family whose emotional sense has been dropped.
items.correction: 불쾌한, 모욕적인; 공격적인

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2428; key "operator" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lessons hv-46, mv2-40, mv3-32)
items.original: operator	operator	운영자	hv-46 mv2-40 mv3-32
items.problem: 운영자 gives only the business/service-provider sense and omits the two senses a middle-school learner is far likelier to meet: the person who operates a machine (조작자, 기사) and the telephone operator (교환원). The gap is visible inside the lessons themselves — in the mv3-32 wordgrid "operator" and "operate" sit side by side in the same row, and operate is glossed 작동하다, so the derived noun ought to be 작동시키는 사람; in mv2-40 it appears among stamp, passenger, mayor, nation (everyday civic vocabulary), where 전화 교환원 is the expected reading.
items.correction: (기계) 조작자, 기사; (전화) 교환원; 운영자

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2444; key "orient" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-47)
items.original: orient	orient	동양	hv-47
items.problem: The headword is lowercase "orient", which in English is a VERB (to orient, orient yourself, orient the map). The noun meaning 동양 belongs to the capitalized proper noun "the Orient", which is a different, article-requiring form that the learner is not being taught. Wiktionary lists seven verb senses under the lowercase English headword, and marks the East/Asia noun sense as "usually preceded by the" and an alternative letter-case form of capitalized "Orient". The entry is also internally inconsistent with its own lesson: in the same hv-47 wordgrid, orientation is glossed 방향, 성향 — which derives from the verb sense that this entry omits entirely.
items.correction: 방향을 정하다, ~로 향하게 하다; (새 환경에) 적응시키다  (※ the Orient = 동양)

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2445; key "oriental" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-47)
items.original: oriental	oriental	동양의	hv-47
items.problem: 동양의 is a correct translation, but the entry carries no usage warning, and this is a word modern dictionaries flag. Wiktionary's English entry for Oriental labels both the adjective sense and the person-noun sense "dated" and "offensive", with the usage note: "Use of the term Oriental to describe a person is considered dated and potentially offensive in North America." (Merriam-Webster marks the noun "usually offensive"; Oxford Learner's calls it old-fashioned and possibly offensive.) A paid site teaching the word to Korean learners as a bare equivalent of 동양의 gives them no way to know this.
items.correction: 동양의 (※ 사람을 가리킬 때는 쓰지 말 것 — 모욕적으로 들림. 사람은 Asian)

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2464; key "output" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-05)
items.original: output	output	출력	hv-05
items.problem: Only the computing sense 출력 is given. Wiktionary lists production first — "That which is produced by something, especially that within a particular time period or from a particular effort" (생산량, 산출량) — with the computer-data sense second. The production sense is also the one that is transparent from the out- + put derivation that hv-05 exists to teach (the grid is outstanding, outline, outskirts, outcome, outlook, output, outlaw, outlet, outdo, outnumber, outgrow, outweigh).
items.correction: 생산량, 산출; 출력

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2482; key "overwork" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-03)
items.original: overwork	overwork	과로	hv-03
items.problem: The gloss is noun-only. Wiktionary gives the verb first — "To make (someone or something) work too hard" and "To work too hard" — with the noun "Excessive work" alongside. The noun-only gloss is also out of step with its own lesson row: every sibling over-/up- word in hv-03 is glossed as a verb (overtake 추월하다, overthrow 전복하다, uphold, upset).
items.correction: 혹사시키다, 과로하다; 과로

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2526; key "passage" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-48)
items.original: passage	passage	통로	hv-48
items.problem: The gloss gives only the corridor sense and omits "(글의) 구절, 지문", which Wiktionary lists as the FIRST English noun sense ("A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning"); 통로 is its seventh sense. For Korean middle/high-school learners, 지문/구절 is overwhelmingly the sense they meet, because it is the standard word on every English reading test ("Read the passage and answer the questions").
items.correction: (글의) 구절, 지문; 통로, 복도; 통행

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2534; key "pathetic" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson hv-47)
items.original: pathetic	pathetic	한심한	hv-47
items.problem: 한심한 is Wiktionary's sense 2 ("Arousing scorn or contempt, often due to miserable inadequacy"); sense 1 is "Arousing pity, sympathy, or compassion; exciting pathos" (불쌍한, 애처로운), and it is missing. This also severs the root family the lesson is built on: hv-47's grid groups pathetic with passion, passionate, patience, patient and compassion (the pat-/pass- "feel, suffer" root), and 한심한 is the one sense that does not show that link, while 애처로운 does.
items.correction: 불쌍한, 애처로운; 한심한, 형편없는

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2540; key "patrolman" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson mv3-19)
items.original: patrolman	patrolman	순찰대원	mv3-19
items.problem: 순찰대원 drops the defining element: a patrolman is specifically a police officer. Wiktionary: "A police officer, especially a junior officer assigned patrol duty instead of detection or supervision." 순찰대원 reads as any patrol/security team member. The mv3-19 lesson context is unambiguously law enforcement — the grid holds uniform, evidence, identify, oath, clue, debt, traffic, appointment.
items.correction: 순찰 경관, 순경

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2550; key "peasant" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson mv3-04)
items.original: peasant	peasant	농부	mv3-04
items.problem: peasant is glossed 농부 — the identical gloss already given to "farmer" at line 1414 (farmer	farmer	농부	mv1-21). The two English words are not synonyms: Wiktionary defines peasant as "A member of the lowly social class that toils on the land, constituted by small farmers and tenants, sharecroppers, farmhands and other laborers", i.e. a historical/poor rural class, not an occupation. The mv3-04 lesson context confirms that class sense — peasant sits in a grid with slave, struggle, labour, endeavor, press, bundle, burden-type vocabulary.
items.correction: 소작농, (가난한) 농민

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2551; key "pebbles" in content/voca_dictionary.json (lesson mv2-27)
items.original: pebbles	pebbles	조약돌(들)	mv2-27
items.problem: The headword is a bare plural, unlike every other count noun in this range (pea, pear, pen, pencil, parcel are all singular). The plural comes from the mv2-27 wordgrid, which does print "pebbles", so the key itself is defensible — but two consequences are not. (1) The gloss 조약돌(들) carries a parenthetical plural marker that Korean does not use and that looks like a conversion artifact; no other entry in the slice does this. (2) searchWord is also "pebbles" and no "pebble" entry exists anywhere in the dictionary, so a learner who looks up the singular — the form they will actually meet in reading — gets nothing.
items.correction: Gloss: 조약돌. Keep key "pebbles" to match the mv2-27 grid, but add "pebble" as a searchable singular (either a second entry or an alias in searchWord) so the dictionary answers the form learners look up.

items.original: "perception": {"meaning":"지각","searchWord":"perception"}
items.problem: The one-word gloss 지각 is a Korean homograph, and for the target age group the overwhelmingly dominant reading is 지각(遲刻) = being late for school, not 지각(知覺) = perception. Nothing on the card disambiguates it. The entry is also inconsistent with its own lesson partner: the same file glosses 'perceive' (line 2564, also hv-21) as 인지하다, so the verb is 인지 but the noun is 지각.
items.correction: 인식, 지각 (사물을 알아차리는 것)

items.original: "perform": {"meaning":"수행하다","searchWord":"perform"}
items.problem: 수행하다 covers only the 'carry out a task' sense. The entertain-an-audience sense ('To do something in front of an audience, such as acting or music' — Wiktionary sense 4) is the one Korean middle-school textbooks use most (perform a play, perform on stage, the band performed), and it is absent. The mv2-21 grid contains 'comedy', which points at exactly that sense.
items.correction: 수행하다, 행하다; 공연하다, 연주하다

items.original: "perish": {"meaning":"멸망하다","searchWord":"perish"}
items.problem: 멸망하다 in Korean requires a nation, dynasty or civilisation as its subject. Perish's core senses are to die (of people/animals), to be destroyed or waste away, and (of food/rubber) to spoil or degrade — Wiktionary gives 'break down and vanish', 'deteriorate...unusable', and 'to pass from life; to cease living' as senses 1-3, with no nation-specific restriction. hv-36 is a root lesson (exit, transit, initiate, issue, perish from the 'go' root) with nothing suggesting the fall-of-a-nation reading.
items.correction: 죽다, 목숨을 잃다; 소멸하다, 사라지다; (음식 등이) 상하다

items.original: "pity": {"meaning":"동정심","searchWord":"pity"}
items.problem: 동정심 is correct for the feeling, but the exclamatory sense — 유감스러운 일, 안타까운 일 ('What a pity!', 'It's a pity you can't come') — is missing, and that is the form middle-school learners meet most in dialogue. The verb use (불쌍히 여기다) is also absent.
items.correction: 동정, 연민; 유감스러운 일, 안타까운 일; 불쌍히 여기다

items.original: "player": {"meaning":"플레이어","searchWord":"player"}
items.problem: The gloss is a bare Hangul transliteration of the English word, so the card teaches nothing — and it is actively misleading, because in Korean 플레이어 is normally a playback device (CD 플레이어) or a game player, which is Wiktionary sense 7, not sense 1. The mv1-11 grid pins the intended sense down: football, baseball, basketball all appear in the same lesson, so 'player' here is 선수. Note the same file glosses 'play' (line 2625) as 놀다; 연극, so the derivation player < play is also lost.
items.correction: 선수; 연주자; (게임) 참가자

items.locator: key "post"; voca-dictionary.tsv line 2675; lessons mv1-35 mv2-29 mv3-40
items.original: "post": {"meaning":"우편; 기둥","searchWord":"post"}
items.problem: Both glosses are correct but the set is incomplete for a 2026 learner: the verb/noun sense 'publish a message online; a message on a forum or social media' is missing, as is 'to display a notice publicly' — Wiktionary lists both ('To hang notices conspicuously for public viewing' under the pole etymology, 'To publish content online' / 'A message published on forums, blogs, or social media'). 우편 is also the British-leaning sense; a Korean learner meets post far more often as 게시하다/올리다.
items.correction: 우편; 기둥, 말뚝; (인터넷에) 올리다, 게시하다; 게시물

items.original: "precision": {"meaning":"정밀도","searchWord":"precision"}
items.problem: 정밀도 is an engineering/measurement term meaning 'degree of precision'. The general noun sense is 정확성, 정밀함 ('with great precision' = 매우 정확하게). The gloss is also out of step with its own word family in the same lesson hv-23, where precise = 정확한 and precisely = 정확하게, so the noun alone jumps to a technical register.
items.correction: 정확성, 정밀함, 정확도

items.original: "premium": {"meaning":"보험료; 할증금","searchWord":"premium"}
items.problem: Both glosses are specialist finance senses (Wiktionary noun sense 4 is labelled Insurance; the surcharge sense is noun sense 3/5). The everyday adjective sense a middle/high-school learner actually meets — 'Superior in quality; higher in price or value' (premium service, premium product) — is listed first among the adjective senses and is entirely absent here. mv3-19 is a mixed general-vocabulary grid (series, mystery, uniform, evidence, furniture, novice, burden…), not an insurance lesson, so there is no context that justifies restricting the card to 보험료.
items.correction: 고급의, 우수한; 할증금, 추가 요금; (보험) 보험료

items.locator: key "present"; voca-dictionary.tsv line 2718; lessons hv-29 mv1-07 mv2-04 mv3-40
items.original: "present": {"meaning":"현재의; 선물; 발표하다","searchWord":"present"}
items.problem: Three senses are given but the attendance sense (있는, 참석한, 출석한) is missing — Wiktionary adjective sense 2, 'Located in the immediate vicinity', example 'present at the meeting'. hv-29 is a word-family lesson whose grid runs absence, present, presently, presence: the entry is placed there precisely for the absent/present contrast, and that is the one sense the gloss omits.
items.correction: 현재의; (그 자리에) 있는, 참석한; 선물; 발표하다, 제시하다

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2731; JSON key "prevent" at content/voca_dictionary.json line 8182; lessons hv-71, mv2-26
items.original: prevent	prevent	예방하다	hv-71 mv2-26
items.problem: 예방하다 covers only the narrow "prevent a disease/an accident" subsense. LDOCE defines prevent as "to stop something from happening, or stop someone from doing something", with the headline pattern prevent somebody from doing something ("His back injury may prevent him from playing in tomorrow's game", "We were prevented from entering the site"). That pattern is the single most-drilled use of the word in Korean middle/high-school English, and 예방하다 cannot express it: 비가 우리가 나가는 것을 예방했다 is not Korean. Neither lesson supplies a sentence to repair this — hv-71 is the vent/vail root grid (prevent, prevention, prevail, prevalent, invent, event) and mv2-26 lists it bare beside promote/feast/wood/hill. The companion entry prevention=예방 is fine, which is exactly why the verb needs the wider gloss.
items.correction: 막다, ~하지 못하게 하다; 예방하다

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2783; JSON key "progress" at content/voca_dictionary.json line 3902; lessons hv-34, mv2-24
items.original: progress	progress	진행	hv-34 mv2-24
items.problem: The gloss gives only the secondary "in progress / 계속 이어짐" sense and omits the primary one. LDOCE lists noun sense 1 as "the process of getting better at doing something, or getting closer to finishing or achieving something" (= 진전, 발전) and verb sense 1 as "to improve, develop, or achieve things so that you are then at a more advanced stage" (= 발전하다, 나아가다). Two things make 진행 actively misleading here rather than merely narrow. (1) In mv2-24 the word sits in a verb run — "mistake, boil, examine, applaud, wound, progress" in a grid otherwise full of pour/ignore/gain/advise/earn/harvest/solve/deliver/aim — but the gloss is a bare noun, and the Korean verb it points to, 진행하다, is transitive ("회의를 진행하다") while English progress in this sense is intransitive, so the learner is steered into *"I progressed the meeting". (2) In hv-34 the word is taught as part of the gress/grad root family — "graduate, graduation, gradual, gradually, progress, progressive" — where the root idea is "step forward", and the derived entry progressive is already glossed 진보적인, so the base word contradicts its own derivative. 진행 is also already the gloss for proceeding, and 진행하다 for proceed, so the entry adds nothing to distinguish them.
items.correction: 진전, 발전; 나아가다, 발전하다 (예: make progress 진전을 보이다 / in progress 진행 중)

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2837; JSON key "purse" at content/voca_dictionary.json line 14058; lesson mv2-38
items.original: purse	purse	지갑	mv2-38
items.problem: 지갑 is not wrong — it is LDOCE's British sense 1, "a small bag in which women keep paper money, coins, cards etc" — but the entry omits the American sense, which LDOCE lists separately as "a bag in which a woman carries her money and personal things", i.e. 핸드백. The course is delivered in American English (the site's synthesized voice is the US Azure Ava), so in the material learners will actually hear, purse usually means a handbag rather than a fold-up wallet. mv2-38 shows the word bare (uniform, grip, unite, information, shrink, instance, purse, trust, twinkle, ugly), so there is no picture or sentence to disambiguate.
items.correction: (여성용) 손지갑; (미) 핸드백

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 2871; JSON key "rather" at content/voca_dictionary.json line 11642; lessons mv1-28, mv3-08, mv3-38
items.original: rather	rather	오히려	mv1-28 mv3-08 mv3-38
items.problem: 오히려 corresponds to the lower-frequency "not … but rather / or rather" senses. LDOCE gives sense 1 as "fairly or to some degree" ("I was rather surprised to see him") and groups rather in its thesaurus with quite, fairly and pretty as meaning "more than a little, but less than very" — i.e. 꽤, 다소. The other high-frequency school items, would rather (차라리) and rather than (~보다는), are missing too. The lesson context makes the omission worse: mv3-08 is an adverb drill whose grid contains quite, indeed, almost, exactly, badly, correctly — and this same dictionary glosses quite=꽤, pretty=예쁜; 꽤, fairly=상당히, so rather is the one degree adverb in the family without its degree sense. mv3-08 also contains instead, glossed 대신, which already occupies the slot 오히려 is pointing at, so the two cards look like near-synonyms when they are not.
items.correction: 꽤, 다소; 오히려 (would rather 차라리, rather than ~보다는)

items.original: 기르다; 뒤쪽
items.problem: Both senses are correct, but they are ordered with the rare one first. Longman marks the `rear` verb ("to look after a person or animal until they are fully grown") as less common (●○○) while the adjective and noun 뒤쪽 are ●●○. The mv3-24 grid row is noun-heavy — "amateur nation puzzle riddle rear atom" — so 뒤쪽 is the reading the lesson points at, yet the card leads with 기르다. Everywhere else in this slice the primary sense is placed first (rest 휴식; 나머지, right 옳은; 오른쪽; 권리).
items.correction: 뒤쪽, 뒷부분; 기르다, 양육하다

items.original: 기록
items.problem: `record` is glossed noun-only. The verb sense — above all 녹음하다/녹화하다 — is absent, and so is the noun 음반. Longman lists the verb senses "to write down information so that it can be looked at in the future" and "to store music, sound, television programmes etc on a disc or tape", and marks the stress difference explicitly: noun /ˈrekɔːd/ vs verb /rɪˈkɔːd/. This matters more here than in an ordinary word list because the course is a listening/dictation program (제목: 영어듣기훈련프로그램) and the audio pronounces one stress pattern or the other; a card reading only 기록 gives the learner no way to connect what they hear to what they see. Note the sibling entry `recorder` (line 2900) is already glossed 녹음기; 리코더(악기), so the 녹음 sense is acknowledged for the derivative but missing from the base word.
items.correction: [명] 기록; 음반, 레코드 / [동] 기록하다; 녹음(녹화)하다 (명사 /ˈrekɔːd/, 동사 /rɪˈkɔːd/ 강세 위치가 다름)

items.original: 반사
items.problem: `reflection` is given only the physics sense 반사 — which Longman lists LAST of its four senses (1 image in a mirror/water, 2 careful thought, 3 a sign of something, 4 the throwing back of light/heat/sound). The two senses a Korean middle/high-school learner actually meets in reading passages, (거울·물에 비친) 상 and 반영/성찰, are both absent. This is also internally inconsistent: the verb `reflect` two lines earlier (line 2915, same lesson hv-32) is correctly glossed 반사하다; 반영하다, so the noun drops a sense its own verb already carries.
items.correction: (거울·물에 비친) 상, 모습; 반사; 반영; 성찰, 숙고

items.original: 임대하다; 집세
items.problem: The verb gloss gives only the landlord side. Korean 임대하다 means to let property OUT; the tenant side is 임차하다/빌리다. English `rent` covers both directions — Wiktionary lists "To take a lease of premises in exchange for rent" (tenant), "To grant a lease in return for rent" (landlord), and "To obtain or have temporary possession of an object (e.g. a movie) in exchange for money". The direction the learner overwhelmingly meets — rent a car, rent a room, rent a bike — is the tenant/빌리다 one, and it is the one missing. The noun 집세 is also narrower than the word: 임대료/사용료 covers cars and equipment, 집세 only covers housing.
items.correction: (돈을 내고) 빌리다, 임차하다; 임대하다, 세를 놓다; [명] 집세, 임대료

items.original: 답장하다
items.problem: The single gloss 답장하다 restricts `reply` to written correspondence. Longman defines the verb as "to answer someone by saying or writing something" and gives spoken examples first — "I asked Clive where he was going, but he didn't reply", "'Of course,' Nathalie replied with a smile". The core sense 대답하다 is missing, and mv3-38 is a bare word grid ("burn sink flow policy reply tear") with no sentence to supply it.
items.correction: 대답하다, 답하다; 답장하다; [명] 대답, 답장

items.original: 재현하다
items.problem: 재현하다 is a real but low-ranked sense. Longman orders the verb: 1 "if an animal or plant reproduces... it produces young plants or animals" (번식하다), 2 "to make a photograph or printed copy of something" (복제하다), 3 replicate a result, 4 recreate a quality. The biology sense 번식하다/생식하다 — the one Korean students meet constantly in science reading and in 수능-style passages — is listed first in the dictionary and is absent from the card, as is 복제하다.
items.correction: 번식하다, 생식하다; 복제(복사)하다; 재현하다

items.original: 재생산
items.problem: 재생산 is a narrow economics/sociology term in Korean (사회적 재생산) and is the only gloss offered. Wiktionary orders the noun: "The act of reproducing new individuals biologically" first, then "The act of making copies" and "A copy of something, as in a piece of art; a duplicate". The two senses a middle/high-school learner meets — 번식/생식 (biology) and 복제(품) (art/printing) — are both missing. The card is also out of step with its own verb `reproduce` (line 2977, same lesson hv-02, adjacent in the same grid row), which is glossed 재현하다.
items.correction: 번식, 생식; 복제, 복사(품); 재생

items.original: 돌아오다
items.problem: Only the intransitive sense is given. Longman lists the transitive sense second, immediately after "go back": "to give or send something back, or to put something back in its place". 돌려주다/반납하다 is the sense in the sentences beginners actually produce — return a book to the library, return the money — and it is absent. The word carries three lessons (mv1-18, mv2-09, mv3-39), so the gap is repeated across all three levels.
items.correction: 돌아오다, 돌아가다; 돌려주다, 반납하다; [명] 귀환; 반납

items.original: 반지
items.problem: `ring` is a homograph and only the jewellery noun is given. Longman lists two verb senses — the bell sense first ("to make a bell make a sound") and the telephone sense — plus the noun senses 고리/원 and 소리. The mv2-04 grid row is "prepare river sun ring die cool", a mix of verbs and nouns with no context, so the verb reading is live there and the learner has nothing to tell them which is meant. The file handles other homographs in this same range properly — rest 휴식; 나머지 (line 3011), right 옳은; 오른쪽; 권리 (line 3038), relative 상대적인; 친척 (line 2942) — so `ring` is inconsistent with the file's own standard.
items.correction: 반지; 고리, 원 / (종·전화가) 울리다, 울리게 하다

items.original: {"meaning":"장미","searchWord":"rose"}  (TSV: rose / rose / 장미 / mv1-35)
items.problem: 장미 is right as the primary sense, but the entry does not note that "rose" is also the simple past of the irregular verb "rise" (rise – rose – risen). This is inconsistent with how the same file handles the identical situation four dozen lines later: `saw` at line 3096 is glossed "톱; see의 과거형", explicitly flagging the past-tense homograph. The convention exists in the file; it is just not applied here.
items.correction: 장미; rise의 과거형

items.original: {"meaning":"왕족","searchWord":"royalty"}  (TSV: royalty / royalty / 왕족 / hv-56)
items.problem: 왕족 is correct and is the right primary sense for the hv-56 royal/royalty pair, but the entry omits the payment sense — 인세, 로열티, 저작권 사용료 ("payment given to a writer, composer, inventor etc for the sale or use of intellectual property"). This sense is common in the business and technology reading that hv-level learners meet, and the Korean loanword 로열티 makes it easy to teach in one extra phrase.
items.correction: 왕족; (저작권) 사용료, 인세

items.original: {"meaning":"안전한","searchWord":"secure"}  (TSV: secure / secure / 안전한 / hv-09)
items.problem: The adjective gloss 안전한 is correct, but the entry omits the verb entirely. "Secure" as a verb meaning 확보하다 ("to get possession of; to acquire certainly") is extremely common in the academic and news English that high-school learners meet — secure funding, secure a job, secure a deal. The neighbouring entries in the same slice do give two parts of speech where both matter (e.g. separate "분리하다; 별도의" at line 3153, sentence "문장; 형벌, 선고" at line 3150), so this entry is inconsistent with the file's own convention. hv-09 presents it in a bare grid with secretary/security and no sentence, so the part of speech is never demonstrated.
items.correction: 안전한; 확보하다

items.locator: key "seed" — voca-dictionary.tsv line 3128; lessons mv1-38, mv2-40, mv3-36
items.original: {"meaning":"종자","searchWord":"seed"}  (TSV: seed / seed / 종자 / mv1-38 mv2-40 mv3-36)
items.problem: 종자 is not wrong, but it is the agricultural/technical register (as in 종자 개량, 우량 종자) rather than the everyday word. Korean learner dictionaries lead with 씨, 씨앗 and list 종자 after it. The word first appears in mv1-38, a beginner-level grid (luck, lip, nation, downstairs, serious, foolish, fool, abroad, visitor, energy, steak, seed), so the gloss is aimed at a learner who is more likely to know 씨앗 than 종자.
items.correction: 씨앗, 씨

items.original: {"meaning":"선정적인","searchWord":"sensational"}  (TSV: sensational / sensational / 선정적인 / hv-57)
items.problem: The gloss gives ONLY the pejorative media sense (선정적인 = sensationalist, shock-seeking), which is a secondary sense. The core, far more frequent meaning of the adjective is "provoking a reaction of interest or excitement / exceptionally great" — 굉장한, 대단한, 선풍적인. Wiktionary lists "Provoking a reaction of interest or excitement" and "Exceptionally great" as the live senses; the Korean learner dictionary gives 선풍적인, 환상적인, 아주 훌륭한 alongside 선정적인. The error is compounded by the lesson design: in hv-57 the word sits in a bare word grid immediately after "sensation" (glossed 감각) and "sense" (감각; 의미), so the morphological family is 감각 → 감각 → 선정적인, which breaks the link the grid is teaching, and there is no example sentence anywhere in the lesson to correct the impression.
items.correction: 굉장한, 선풍적인; (보도가) 선정적인

items.original: {"meaning":"정착","searchWord":"settlement"}  (TSV: settlement / settlement / 정착 / hv-59)
items.problem: 정착 is correct but incomplete in two ways. (1) The concrete noun sense 정착지/취락 ("a community of people living together, such as a hamlet, village, town") is the one that actually appears in history and geography reading passages, and 정착 (the abstract act) does not cover it. (2) The dispute-resolution sense 합의, 해결 ("a resolution of a dispute"; "a mutual agreement to end a dispute without resorting to legal proceedings") is missing altogether and is common in news English. The related entries settle (line 3164, 정착하다) and settler (line 3166, 정착민) are consistently built on the 정착 root, so nothing elsewhere in the course supplies the missing senses.
items.correction: 정착, 정착지; 합의, 해결

items.original: {"meaning":"샤워","searchWord":"shower"}  (TSV: shower / shower / 샤워 / mv3-25)
items.problem: Only the bathing sense is given. The precipitation sense 소나기 is listed first among the noun senses in Wiktionary ("A brief fall of precipitation") and is a standard Korean middle-school test item, appearing constantly in weather descriptions and in the compound meteor shower (유성우). mv3-25 is a middle-3 word grid (laundry, shower, guest, gallery, Mars, navy) with no sentence, so the single gloss is all the learner gets.
items.correction: 샤워; 소나기

items.original: side	side	측면	mv1-09

items.problem: 접속 용법 '그래서'만 있고 정도 부사 용법이 빠졌습니다. Longman은 so의 첫 번째 뜻을 'VERY'(아주, 너무: It was so embarrassing! / He was so weak that he could hardly stand up.)로 싣습니다. mv1-01은 중등 과정 첫 과라 이 뜻 하나가 곧 학습자의 so 전체 지식이 됩니다.
