items.original: some	some	일부	mv1-02
items.problem: '일부'는 명사적인 풀이라 한정사 용법(some water, some books)과 맞지 않습니다. mv1-02는 중등 과정 2과로, 이 단계의 some은 '약간의, 몇몇의'로 쓰입니다. 뜻이 틀린 것은 아니지만(some people = 일부 사람들) 가장 먼저 만나는 용법이 빠져 있습니다.
items.correction: 약간의, 몇몇의; 일부

items.original: sophisticated	sophisticated	정교한	hv-60
items.problem: 기계·시스템에 쓰는 2번 뜻만 주었습니다. Longman은 ① (사람이) 세련된·교양 있는(a sophisticated, witty American) ② (기계·기술이) 정교한·첨단의 ③ (이해가) 수준 높은 순으로 싣습니다. 사람을 묘사하는 1번 뜻이 빠져 있습니다.
items.correction: 세련된, 교양 있는; (기계·기술이) 정교한, 첨단의

items.original: sovereign	sovereign	주권자	hv-03
items.problem: 명사 뜻 하나만 주어 형용사 용법이 통째로 빠졌습니다. Longman은 형용사(① 최고 권한을 가진 ② 주권을 가진·독립된)를 먼저 싣고, 명사 뜻은 '왕·여왕(군주)'와 '옛 영국 금화'입니다. '주권자'는 Longman이 명사 뜻으로 싣지 않는 풀이이고, 학습자가 실제로 만나는 sovereign state / sovereign nation(주권 국가)은 형용사입니다.
items.correction: 주권을 가진, 자주 독립의; (명사) 군주, 국왕

items.original: sow	sow	뿌리다	mv2-36
items.problem: '뿌리다'만 있으면 물·소금을 뿌리는 sprinkle/scatter와 구분되지 않습니다. sow는 '씨를 뿌리다(파종하다)'라는 한정된 뜻이어서 괄호 보충이 필요합니다.
items.correction: (씨를) 뿌리다, 파종하다

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 3301 / JSON key "space" (lessons: mv1-23, mv2-20, mv3-09)
items.original: space	space	공간	mv1-23 mv2-20 mv3-09
items.problem: '우주' 뜻이 빠졌습니다. Longman은 '지구 밖 별과 행성이 있는 영역'을 명사 4번 뜻으로 싣습니다. 한국어 '공간'은 이 뜻을 포함하지 않습니다. 이 단어는 세 개 과(mv1-23, mv2-20, mv3-09)에 반복 출제되는데 세 과 모두 같은 한 줄 뜻만 보여 줍니다.
items.correction: 공간; 우주

items.original: specialize	specialize	전문화하다	hv-61
items.problem: '전문화하다'는 목적어를 받는 타동사('무엇을 전문화하다')로 읽히지만, Longman은 이 동사를 사실상 한 가지 뜻으로 싣고 전형적인 형태가 자동사 specialize in(Simmons specialized in contract law / The chef specializes in Hunan cuisine)임을 명시합니다. 학습자가 만나는 구문과 품사 감각이 어긋납니다.
items.correction: (specialize in) ~을 전문으로 하다, 전공하다

items.original: stake	stake	말뚝	hv-65
items.problem: '말뚝'은 stake의 가장 빈도가 낮은 뜻입니다. Longman 사전은 명사 뜻을 ① at stake(성패가 걸린·위태로운) ② (사업의) 지분·투자 ③ (도박에) 건 돈 ④ 말뚝 순으로 싣고 있어, 이 사전이 유일하게 준 뜻이 사전 순서상 맨 마지막 항목입니다. 고등 수준 독해에서 stake는 사실상 'at stake' 관용구와 '지분·이해관계'로 만나는데 그 뜻이 전혀 없습니다.
items.correction: 말뚝; (사업의) 지분, 이해관계 — at stake: 위태로운, 성패가 걸린

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 3343 / JSON key "stand" (lessons: hv-61, mv2-18)
items.original: stand	stand	서다	hv-61 mv2-18
items.problem: '서다'는 올바른 주된 뜻이지만, 고등 어휘 과(hv-61)에 넣으면서 can't stand(참다·견디다) 뜻을 빼 두었습니다. Longman에서 이 뜻은 동사 6~7번으로, 별도 표제어(can't stand)까지 있을 만큼 빈출입니다.
items.correction: 서다; (can't stand) 참다, 견디다

items.original: statement	statement	성명서	hv-62
items.problem: '성명서'는 공식 발표문이라는 좁은 뜻만 가리킵니다. Longman은 ① 공식적·공개적으로 말하거나 쓴 것(진술·발언) ② bank statement(입출금 명세서) ③ 의사 표현 순으로 싣습니다. 같은 사전이 state를 '상태; 국가; 진술하다'(3349행)로 풀어 놓았으면서 그 명사형만 '성명서'로 좁혀 둔 내부 불일치이기도 합니다.
items.correction: 진술, 말; 성명(서); (은행) 명세서

items.original: 난로
items.problem: 난로 (a heating stove) is a legitimate sense, and the mv2-21 grid does sit next to coal/brick, but in present-day English — especially American English — stove most often means the kitchen cooking appliance (가스레인지 / (요리용) 레인지): Collins labels this use 'mainly US … a large box-shaped device that is used to cook and heat food'. The card gives only the heating sense.
items.correction: (요리용) 레인지, 가스레인지; 난로

items.original: 실질적인
items.problem: '실질적인' is a real but peripheral sense of substantial (the 'real/actual' sense, as in substantial evidence). The sense learners overwhelmingly meet — Longman's sense 1, 'large in amount or number' — is missing entirely, and Longman's sense 2 is 'large and strongly made'. A learner who has only 실질적인 will misread the standard collocations (a substantial increase / a substantial amount of money = 상당한 증가 / 상당한 액수, not 실질적인).
items.correction: 상당한, 많은; (크고) 튼튼한; 실질적인

items.locator: key "succeed" (voca-dictionary.tsv line 3414; lessons hv-22, mv2-30, mv3-32)
items.original: 성공하다
items.problem: succeed also means '뒤를 잇다, 계승하다' (Longman senses 4-5: 'to be the next person to take a position or job after someone else'). This sense is essential here, because hv-22 (content/lessons/phonics/hv-22.json) is a cede/cess root grid that teaches succeed next to succession, successor and predecessor — and the dictionary glosses those as 계승 and 후임. With only 성공하다 on the succeed card, the learner cannot connect the family the lesson is built on.
items.correction: 성공하다; (~의) 뒤를 잇다, 계승하다

items.original: 계승
items.problem: Longman lists the 'one after another' senses first — 'in succession' (We lost four important games in succession) and 'a succession of something' — with the official-position sense only third. The card gives only 계승, dropping 연속/잇따름, which is the more frequent sense and the one that pairs with successive (연속적인) taught in the same hv-22 grid.
items.correction: 연속, 잇따름; 계승, 승계

items.original: 후원자
items.problem: 후원자 means backer/patron/sponsor (someone who gives money). Longman gives supporter only as (1) 'someone who supports a particular person, group, or plan' and (2) BrE 'someone who likes a particular sports team' — i.e. 지지자 / 팬. The money-giving sense is not the word's core meaning, and the card omits 지지자 altogether.
items.correction: 지지자, 지지하는 사람; (스포츠 팀의) 팬, 서포터; 후원자

items.original: 일시 중지하다
items.problem: Longman gives three senses: stop temporarily, 'make someone leave their school or job for a short time' (정학/정직시키다), and 'attach something to a high place so that it hangs down' (매달다). Only the first is glossed. The hanging sense is the pend root sense that hv-49 (content/lessons/phonics/hv-49.json) is built around — the same grid contains suspension and suspense — and the 정학 sense is what suspension (glossed 정지, 보류) usually refers to for a school-age reader.
items.correction: 일시 중지하다, 중단하다; 정학[정직]시키다; 매달다

items.original: 서스펜스
items.problem: The gloss is a transliteration of the English word, so the card teaches nothing new, and the Korean loanword 서스펜스 only covers the film/novel-genre use. Longman defines suspense as 'a feeling of excitement or anxiety when you do not know what will happen next' — 조마조마함, 불안, 긴장감 — which is the sense in 'keep someone in suspense' and 'the suspense is killing me'. Unlike 텔레파시 (3520) or 시스템 (3492), where the Korean loanword covers the full English meaning, 서스펜스 here leaves the core meaning unexplained.
items.correction: 조마조마함, 불안, 긴장감; (영화·소설의) 서스펜스

items.original: tiptoe	tiptoe	발끝	mv3-29
items.problem: The card gives only the bare noun 발끝. The noun "tiptoe" is almost never used on its own — it survives essentially only inside the phrase "on tiptoe / on one's tiptoes" — while the form learners actually meet standing alone in a text is the verb (to walk quietly on the tips of one's toes). The gloss therefore teaches the one use of the word a learner will almost never encounter, and gives no clue how to read "She tiptoed out of the room." The mv3-29 lesson is a bare word grid (content/lessons/phonics/mv3-29.json) with no sentence, so nothing else supplies the verb sense.
items.correction: 발끝; 발끝으로 살금살금 걷다  (or "(on tiptoe) 발끝으로; 발끝으로 걷다")

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 3616; JSON key "town" (lessons mv1-13, mv3-40)
items.original: town	town	마을	mv1-13 mv3-40
items.problem: "town" is glossed 마을, which is the ordinary Korean word for village — and the same dictionary glosses "village" (line 3778, lessons mv1-20 mv3-34) with the identical string 마을. The defining fact about a town, that it is larger than a village and smaller than a city, is lost, and the two headwords become indistinguishable on the card. The card carries no example sentence or part of speech, so 마을 is all the learner gets.
items.correction: 마을보다 큰 (작은) 도시, 읍; 시내  — or at minimum "읍, 소도시", keeping 마을 for village only.

items.original: transportation	transportation	교통	hv-52
items.problem: 교통 is a listed Korean equivalent, so this is not an error, but it is the least discriminating choice available: "traffic" (line 3623, lessons mv1-23 mv2-34 mv3-19) carries the identical gloss 교통, and the closely related "transport" two lines above (line 3641, hv-52) is glossed 수송 — so the same dictionary tells the learner that transport = 수송 while transportation = 교통, and that transportation and traffic are the same word. The act-of-conveying / means-of-conveying sense that hv-52 actually needs is not visible.
items.correction: 교통수단, 수송 (운송)  — and leave 교통(량), 차량 통행 to traffic.

items.locator: voca-dictionary.tsv line 3681; JSON key "type" (lessons mv2-40, mv3-22)
items.original: type	type	유형; 타자치다	mv2-40 mv3-22
items.problem: 타자치다 is written closed up. 타자 is a noun and 치다 a verb, so the two are not one word and must be spaced: 타자 치다. (The noun sense 유형 is correct and needs no change.)
items.correction: 유형; 타자 치다  (a modern alternative for the verb: 유형; 입력하다, 타자 치다)

items.original: "unity": { "meaning": "화합", "searchWord": "unity" }   (TSV row: unity / unity / 화합 / hv-09)
items.problem: 화합 renders only Wiktionary's SECOND sense ("Agreement; harmony"). The first and defining sense - "Oneness: the state or fact of being one undivided entity" (단결, 통합, 통일성) - is missing. hv-09 is precisely the uni- = 'one' root family: its wordgrid runs unique, union, unify, unification, unity, unit, unite, universe, universal, university, and the sibling glosses are unify = 통일하다 and unification = 통일. So unity is the one member whose gloss hides the root meaning the lesson exists to teach. 화합 also collides with 'harmony', glossed 조화 at voca-dictionary.tsv line 1667.
items.correction: "통일성, 단결"

items.original: "utterance": { "meaning": "발화", "searchWord": "utterance" }   (TSV row: utterance / utterance / 발화 / hv-05)
items.problem: 발화 is the specialist Korean linguistics term. It matches only the parenthesised "(especially linguistics)" part of Wiktionary's sense 2; the senses that come first are the everyday ones - "An act of, or the process of, uttering" and "something spoken (e.g., syllables, words, phrases)", i.e. 말 or 발언. Two further problems: 발화 is a Korean homograph (발화 發火 = catching fire / ignition) and the single-word gloss gives no disambiguation; and hv-05 is not a linguistics lesson - its wordgrid is the out-/ut- prefix family (outstanding, outline, outcome, output, outdo, outweigh, utter, utterance, utterly, utmost).
items.correction: "말, 발언"

items.original: "vacation": { "meaning": "휴가", "searchWord": "vacation" }   (TSV row: vacation / vacation / 휴가 / mv1-22 mv2-31 mv3-24)
items.problem: 휴가 is leave from work - the adult sense. The school sense (방학) is missing, although it is the first noun sense listed: "An extended period of leisure time away from work or school", illustrated with "Schoolchildren are on vacation this week", plus a separate sense "an official holiday from university, law courts etc." The dictionary already covers the general day-off space with 'holiday' = 휴일 (voca-dictionary.tsv line 1710), so 휴가 adds no coverage that is missing while 방학 is left out entirely.
items.correction: "방학; 휴가"

items.original: "volume": { "meaning": "책, 권; 음량", "searchWord": "volume" }   (TSV row: volume / volume / 책, 권; 음량 / hv-74 mv3-34)
items.problem: The 부피/용량 sense is absent, although it is the first noun sense listed: "A three-dimensional measure of space that comprises a length, a width and a height" (loudness is second, bound book fourth). Leading with 책, 권 is motivated inside hv-74, whose wordgrid is the volvere='roll' family (revolve, revolution, involve, evolve, revolt) where a volume is a rolled scroll - but because voca_dictionary.json is a flat map with one gloss per word, the mv3-34 learner gets that same etymology-driven ordering with the everyday science sense missing.
items.correction: "부피; 음량; 책, 권"

items.original: "wagon": { "meaning": "마차", "searchWord": "wagon" }   (TSV row: wagon / wagon / 마차 / mv3-16)
items.problem: A wagon is defined as "A heavier four-wheeled (normally horse-drawn) vehicle designed to carry goods (or sometimes people)" - the goods-carrying element is what distinguishes it, and the Korean for that is 짐마차 or 수레. 마차 is the passenger vehicle, and this dictionary already uses 마차 as the entire gloss for "carriage" (voca-dictionary.tsv line 523, 'carriage / carriage / 마차'). Two distinct headwords therefore carry one identical gloss, and the one that is imprecise is 'wagon'. The mv3-16 wordgrid (lantern, flood, bush, wagon, garage, suitcase, hut, log, mail) is a goods/rural-object set, which fits 짐마차, not a passenger coach.
items.correction: "짐마차, 수레"

items.original: "way": { "meaning": "방법", "searchWord": "way" }   (TSV row: way / way / 방법 / mv1-03)
items.problem: 방법 gives only the method-or-manner sense. The road/path/direction sense (길) is absent even though Wiktionary lists it FIRST: "A road, a direction, a (physical or conceptual) path from one place to another", with the method sense only at number 3. Worse, 방법 is already the entire gloss for "method" (voca-dictionary.tsv line 2203, 'method / method / 방법'), so on a card or a 한글-to-English quiz prompt the two headwords are indistinguishable.
items.correction: "길; 방법"

items.original: "wear": { "meaning": "입다", "searchWord": "wear" }   (TSV row: wear / wear / 입다 / mv1-20 mv2-07)
items.problem: English 'wear' covers everything carried on the body: "To carry or have equipped on or about one's body, as an item of clothing, equipment, decoration, perfume, etc.", with cited examples spanning clothes, a seatbelt, medals, makeup, eyeglasses. Korean splits this one verb across 입다 (clothes) / 쓰다 (hat, glasses) / 신다 (shoes) / 끼다 (ring, gloves), and the gloss supplies only 입다. This is a one-to-many mapping where the gloss teaches one of four branches with no signal that the others exist.
items.correction: "(옷을) 입다, (모자·안경을) 쓰다, (신발을) 신다; 착용하다"

items.original: 어디서
items.problem: 어디서 is the locative-of-action form ("at/from where"), which fits "Where do you live?" but not the equally basic "Where is my bag?" (어디에 있어요, not 어디서 있어요). Every sibling wh-word in the same mv1-01 set is glossed bare without a particle — what 무엇, when 언제, why 왜, which 어느, whose 누구의 — so this entry is also the odd one out in its own group. This is a Korean-usage wording judgement, not a disputed English sense, so there is no dictionary URL to cite; a Korean-language editor can confirm it in seconds.
items.correction: 어디(에)

items.original: 와
items.problem: The gloss is a single bare Korean particle covering only Longman's sense 1 (together / in the company of). Senses 2 (possession: "a tall gentleman with a beard") and 3 (instrument: "Chop the onions with a sharp knife") are both core and both missing. Two further problems with the bare form: 와 is only the post-vowel allomorph (과 after a consonant), and as a standalone one-syllable card it is also readable as the imperative of 오다 ("come"). Note for the owner: bare-particle glosses are the house style for prepositions here (from "에서", by "에 의해", under "아래", during "동안"), but comparable entries already use the fuller tilde form (about "~에 대하여; 약", through "~을 통해", among "~중에, ~사이에"), so the fix stays in style.
items.correction: ~와 함께; ~을 가지고, ~으로

items.original: 철수하다
items.problem: The card gives only the narrow military sense ("pull troops out"). Longman lists the senses of the verb withdraw in this order: 1 not take part, 2 stop supporting, 3 change your mind, 4 say something is not true, 5 product/service, 6 leave a place (military), 7 money. The gloss picks sense 6 of 10 and omits every sense above it, including 철회하다 (retract) and (돈을) 인출하다, which are the ones Korean study sources lead with (dokjongban TOEIC voca: "withdraw - 철회하다, 철수하다"). hv-02 is a prefix drill (postwar/propose/replace/withdraw/overcome) that shows the word in isolation with no sentence, so this one gloss is the learner's whole definition.
items.correction: 철회하다; 물러나다, 철수하다; (돈을) 인출하다 — multi-sense glosses separated by ";" are already the house style in this range (western "서양의; 서쪽의", whistle "휘파람을 불다; 호루라기", wish "바라다; 소원").

items.original: 증인
items.problem: 증인 is the courtroom sense, which Longman lists as noun sense 2. Noun sense 1 is "someone who sees a crime or an accident and can describe what happened" (목격자), and verb sense 1 is "to see something happen, especially a crime or accident" (목격하다). Wiktionary likewise puts the observer sense ahead of the court sense. The entry omits both the primary noun sense and the verb entirely, even though neighbouring entries in this same range routinely carry a noun+verb pair (wonder "궁금해하다; 경이", work "일하다; 일", whole "전체의; 전체").
items.correction: 목격자; 증인; 목격하다

items.original: For example, in a healthy environment, the amount of _______ food is just right for the number of fish in a river.  (only accepted answer: plant)
items.problem: 'fish' appears as an option in 10.2% of loads. 'the amount of fish food is just right for the number of fish in a river' is grammatical and plausible on its own, yet it is graded wrong. Only the later sentence ('too much plant life') tips the balance toward 'plant'.
items.correction: Exclude 'fish' (and 'river', which gives the odd but grammatical 'river food') from this item's distractors, or blank 'amount' or 'healthy' instead.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-004-s001, reading-004-s002, reading-004-s003 (EN and KO)
items.original: Two Colombian rhythms have a foreign origin. / The 'cumbia' was created by African slaves who were brought to the hot regions of the country to work in the gold mines. / It was a sad song of these people who missed their families.
items.problem: The passage states as fact that cumbia was created by African slaves who had been brought to work in gold mines, and that it was a sad song about missing their families. Standard accounts describe cumbia differently. It developed on the Caribbean coast (lower Magdalena River, Cartagena area) as a fusion of Indigenous (gaita flutes, maracas), African (drums, rhythms) and Spanish (language, dress) elements, and the dance is traditionally a courtship dance. These sources say nothing about gold mines or a lament for families. Colombia's gold-mining slave labor was concentrated in the Pacific and Antioquia regions, not on the Caribbean coast where cumbia arose. The opening claim that both rhythms have a 'foreign origin' is also questionable, since both genres took shape in Colombia. The 2026-09-17 audit (R-16) hedged only the bambuco sentence and left the cumbia claims unchanged.
items.correction: Rewrite as hedged, verifiable statements, e.g. 'Two Colombian rhythms have roots outside the country. The cumbia grew up on the hot Caribbean coast, where the drums and rhythms of African slaves mixed with Indigenous flutes and Spanish songs. In contrast, the bambuco of the colder Andean region is often said to have Spanish roots, and it was often used for love songs.' Then update the KO translation, the cards (e.g. 'missed' and 'families' if those words are dropped) and the audio clips (the English text hash changes).

items.original: It was a sad song of these people who missed their _______.  (only accepted answer: families)
items.problem: 'country' (7 letters vs 8) appears as an option in 18.3% of loads. 'It was a sad song of these people who missed their country.' is natural and fits the context (enslaved Africans taken from their homeland), but it is graded wrong.
items.correction: Exclude 'country' from this item's distractors, or blank a different word (e.g. 'missed').

items.original: Two Colombian rhythms have a _______ origin.  (options drawn from: rhythms, regions, foreign, bambuco, express, created, brought, spanish, country, african; item 3 pool also has colombian)
items.problem: Distractors are lower-cased, so learners see the proper adjectives 'spanish', 'african' and 'colombian' misspelled as answer choices. 'spanish' shows up in 32.8% of loads for item 1.
items.correction: Keep the original case for proper nouns and adjectives in the distractor pool, or exclude capitalized words from it.

items.original: As you become a teenager, however, you may sometimes begin to question adults' ideas, instead of blindly accepting their ideas as you did when you were a small child.  / KO: 그러나, 당신이 10대가 됨에 따라, …
items.problem: The passage opens with the contrast marker 'however' (그러나), but nothing comes before it to contrast with. It is a mid-text excerpt, since the textbook original (docs/qa-2026-09-15/evidence/reading-q1-answer-keys.txt) starts the same way. Learners are taught that 'however' links back to a previous statement, and here there is none.
items.correction: Drop the connector: 'As you become a teenager, you may sometimes begin to question adults' ideas…' / KO: '10대가 되면서 당신은 …' (regenerate the S1 audio), or add a short lead-in sentence about childhood acceptance.

items.original: S1: …때때로 어른들의 생각에 의문을 갖기 시작할 지도 모른다. / S4: …당신의 삶을 꾸려가고 싶어한다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.
items.problem: Korean spacing errors. In '-ㄹ지도 모른다' the '지' is an ending and attaches to the verb: 시작할지도. The auxiliary construction '-어 하다' is written with a space: 싶어 한다는.
items.correction: S1: 시작할지도 모른다. / S4: 꾸려 가고 싶어 한다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.

items.original: This means that a human law is a set of rules that are valid only for a _______ number of people over a certain period of time.  (answer: certain)
items.problem: Only the first occurrence of the answer is masked, so 'certain' is still visible later in the same sentence ('over a certain period'). The item can be answered by copying (the same issue the map records for pr100).
items.correction: Mask every occurrence of the target, or skip targets that occur more than once in the sentence and pick the next valid word.

items.original: My belief is that all _______ has an expressive power, some more and some less, but that all music has a certain meaning behind the notes.  (answer: music)
items.problem: The answer 'music' is still visible later in the same sentence ('but that all music has'), so the item gives itself away.
items.correction: Mask all occurrences of the target, or choose a target that occurs only once (e.g. 'expressive').

items.original: This whole problem can be stated quite simply by _______, "Is there a meaning to music?" My answer to that would be, "Yes."  (only accepted answer: asking)
items.problem: 'saying' has the same length as 'asking' and appears as an option in 49.5% of loads. 'can be stated quite simply by saying, "Is there a meaning to music?"' is grammatical and natural English, so a defensible choice is graded wrong.
items.correction: Exclude 'saying' from this item's distractors, or blank another word (e.g. 'simply' or 'stated').

items.original: It takes the Earth a little less than 365 and a quarter days to travel once around the Sun.  / KO: 지구가 태양 둘레를 한 바퀴 도는 데는 365와 4분의 1일보다 조금 짧은 시간이 걸린다.
items.problem: One orbit of the Sun (the sidereal year) takes 365.256 days, which is slightly more than 365¼, not less. The period that is a little less than 365¼ days (365.2422 days, which matches the 'a little less than six hours' in S5) is the tropical year, the cycle of the seasons, and that is what the calendar follows. The passage was newly written for R-01 on a promise of 'verified facts only', and its first premise conflates the two years. The leap-year rule it goes on to explain is correct.
items.correction: 'It takes a little less than 365 and a quarter days for the seasons to come round again (from one spring to the next).' / KO: '계절이 한 바퀴 돌아 다시 같은 계절이 오기까지는 365와 4분의 1일보다 조금 짧은 시간이 걸린다.' Regenerate the S1 audio clip.

items.original: divided | divide | v. | 나누다 (be divided by ~으로 나누어떨어지다)
items.problem: 'be divided by' simply means '~으로 나누어지다' (e.g. 10 divided by 3 = 3.33 is not evenly divisible). The 'divisible evenly' sense in S6 comes from 'can be divided by' in this context (standard term: 'be divisible by'). The gloss teaches that 'be divided by' itself means 나누어떨어지다.
items.correction: 나누다 (can be divided by 400: 400으로 나누어떨어지다 ≒ be divisible by)

items.original: To fix this, an extra day, _______ 29, is added every four years.  (answer: February; distractors such as divided, slightly, calendar, because, quarter, seasons)
items.problem: The answer keeps its original case, while distractors are lower-cased from the passage pool. 'February' is therefore the only capitalized option, and a month name before '29' is the only sensible choice anyway.
items.correction: Do not blank proper nouns or dates (skip capitalized words that are not sentence-initial), or blank 'extra' or 'added' in this sentence.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr011.json readingSentences #1 (reading-011-s001) EN + KO and the passage as a whole; same in pr011-1.json
items.original: The Crane could help us in many ways in the future. / KO: Crane은 앞으로 여러 면에서 우리에게 도움이 될 수 있을 것이다.
items.problem: The passage is the ending of a longer text that has lost its opening. 'The Crane' is never introduced, so a learner cannot tell whether it is a bird, a construction crane or a spacecraft until sentence #4. The Korean translation leaves the name as Latin letters ('Crane은'), so it does not help either. I could not find the source by web search, so I cannot confirm whether 'the Crane' is a real or a fictional spacecraft, or check the claim that it would let us see 'seven times further into space'.
items.correction: Add a one-line introduction that says what the Crane is, or at least gloss it in Korean, e.g. KO '크레인호(우주 비행체)는 앞으로 ...'. Before writing the introduction, find the original source to confirm what the Crane is. If an English sentence is added or changed, regenerate its voice clip.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 generated from content/lessons/reading/pr011.json readingSentences #1
items.original: The Crane could help us in many ways in the future.
items.problem: The cloze blanks the modal 'could' ('The Crane _______ help us in many ways in the future.'). The distractor pool of 5-letter words includes 'would', and it is drawn on about 3 visits in 13 (23%). 'The Crane would help us in many ways in the future' is grammatical and says nearly the same thing, but it is marked wrong. Blanking a modal verb as the 'core keyword' also teaches little. Item 2 ('a _______ telescope') can also offer 'solar', and 'a solar telescope' is a real kind of instrument, though the next sentence favours 'giant'.
items.correction: Choose a content word from the lesson's cards as the target, e.g. 'future' in #1 or 'telescope' in #2, or curate this lesson's cloze.

items.locator: TSV line 154; readingVocabulary entry word "station" (pr011.json line 235); same entry in src/lib/readingVocabulary.json key pr011
items.original: station	n.	발전소 (solar power station 태양광 발전소)  — context: also help build a solar power [station] in space.
items.problem: The headline gloss gives the headword 'station' a meaning it has only in the compound 'power station'. 'Station' on its own never means 발전소. It means a facility or place set up for a particular service (시설, ~소, ~국, 기지, 역). Wiktionary lists 15 noun senses and none of them is a power plant; 'power station' is listed separately as a derived term. The same range shows the correct pattern: 'waggle n. 흔들기 (waggle dance 8자 춤)' glosses the word alone and puts the compound meaning in parentheses. This card does the opposite.
items.correction: n. (특정 목적의) 시설, ~소(所), 기지 (power station 발전소; solar power station 태양광 발전소)

items.lesson: pr011-pr021 (37 of the 150 cards in lines 152-301)
items.original: e.g. pr014 "spent	v.	(시간을) 보내다" (lemma spend); pr013 "earlier	adv.	더 일찍, 그 이전에" (lemma early); pr021 "setting	v.	두다, 배치하다" (lemma set); pr021 "leads	v.	이끌다, ~하게 하다" (lemma lead)
items.problem: The lemma data is correct for all 37 inflected cards. The card, however, shows the inflected surface form as the headword next to a dictionary-form Korean gloss (…하다), and the lemma the learner needs is never shown. This matters most for irregular forms: spent→spend, earlier→early, and setting→set. A learner also knows 'setting' as a noun (배경, 설정), so a card reading 'setting v. 두다' looks like a wrong POS unless the base form set is shown. This is a site-wide rendering choice, so it probably affects cards outside this range too.
items.correction: Show the lemma as the headword and the passage form as a secondary note, e.g. 'spend (본문: spent)', 'set (본문: setting)', 'early (본문: earlier)'. Or show 'spent ← spend' whenever lemma differs from word.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 generated from content/lessons/reading/pr013.json readingSentences #1 (src/lib/readingUtils.ts generateClozeItems)
items.original: Person A: Since people generally like what they are good at, I propose that our children focus on areas in which they excel.
items.problem: The graded cloze blanks 'children' ('... I propose that our _______ focus on areas in which they excel.'). The three distractors are drawn at random from the passage words of the same length (8 letters): students, requires, aptitude, limiting, required, subjects, graduate. So on about 3 visits in 7 (43%) the option 'students' appears. 'I propose that our students focus on areas in which they excel' is fully correct and natural, but it is marked wrong ('❌ 정답은 'children' 입니다'). I worked this out by re-running the generator's logic in node.
items.correction: Keep distractors from being words that fit the blank, for example by using this sentence's card word 'excel' as the target, or by curating this lesson's cloze. Otherwise, exclude 'students' as a distractor for 'children'.

items.original: Secondary school should be a time for expanding horizons―not limiting them. / I abandoned the medical profession with relief but I do not regret the five years I spent at the hospital - far from it. / The great loneliness―like the loneliness a caterpillar ...
items.problem: Dashes are typed with the wrong characters. pr013 #9 and pr019 #2 use U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR (―), which is common in Korean typesetting, instead of an English em dash. pr014 #1 uses a spaced hyphen ' - '. These are what learners copy and read as models of English punctuation.
items.correction: Use an em dash, e.g. 'expanding horizons—not limiting them', 'at the hospital—far from it'. pr019 #2 is rewritten anyway by the cocoon finding. After the edit, confirm that the speech-clip key (unifiedSpeechKey) still resolves, or regenerate the clips.

items.original: Most of us spend 59 minutes an hour living in the past with regret for lost joys, or shame for things badly done or in a future which we either long for or dread.
items.problem: Cutting Jameson's parenthetical and dash left no break before 'or in a future'. The sentence can now be parsed as 'things badly done or [done] in a future', which hides its real structure ('living in the past ... or in a future ...'). The Korean translation has the correct structure, so the English and Korean seem to disagree.
items.correction: "Most of us spend 59 minutes an hour living in the past, with regret for lost joys or shame for things badly done, or in a future which we either long for or dread." This changes the English, so regenerate the voice clip.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 3 generated from content/lessons/reading/pr016.json readingSentences #3
items.original: The only way to live is to accept each minute as an unrepeatable miracle.
items.problem: The blank is 'as an _______ miracle' and the target is 'unrepeatable'. The distractors are always 'thousand' plus two of believe, present, minutes, miracle, all starting with a consonant. The article 'an' therefore gives the answer away on every visit, and the item tests nothing.
items.correction: Mask the article together with the word ('as _______ miracle', answer 'an unrepeatable'), or choose another target in this sentence, e.g. 'accept'.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr018.json readingSentences #2, #3, #5 KO (reading-018-s002/s003/s005); same in pr018-1.json
items.original: #3 EN: Nowadays, many young people seem to prefer surfing the Internet to reading books. / KO: 요즈음 많은 젊은이들은 책을 읽는 것보다 인터넷을 검색하는 것을 더 좋아한다. ; #5 EN: One may wonder if literary fiction is destined to become ... / KO: ... 구식 장르가 될 운명이 아닌지 사람들은 궁금해한다. ; #2 KO: ... 컴퓨터 게임이 더 영향력있게 됨에 따라 ...
items.problem: #3: the Korean drops 'seem to', so a hedged observation becomes a flat statement of fact. #5: 'One may wonder' becomes '사람들은 궁금해한다' ('people wonder'), which loses 'may'. The passage's tentative stance is a point readers are often asked about in reading exams. #2: '영향력있게' should be spaced as '영향력 있게'.
items.correction: #3 KO: '요즈음 많은 젊은이들은 책을 읽는 것보다 인터넷 검색을 더 좋아하는 것 같다.' #5 KO: '... 구식 장르가 될 운명인 것은 아닌지 궁금해질 수도 있다.' #2 KO: '영향력 있게'. Update pr018-1.json too.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr019.json readingSentences #1 (reading-019-s001) EN + KO; same in pr019-1.json
items.original: An Eskimo once told European visitors that the only true wisdom lives far from mankind, out in the great loneliness, and can be reached only through suffering. / KO: 한 에스키모인이 유럽에서 온 방문객들에게, ...
items.problem: Many Inuit and Yupik people consider 'Eskimo' pejorative, and it has been replaced by 'Inuit' in Canada and Greenland (Inuit Circumpolar Council, 1977). The speaker was Igjugarjuk, a Caribou Inuit (Paallirmiut) shaman whose words Knud Rasmussen recorded in 1922, so 'Inuit' is also more accurate. A paid product in 2026 should not present the term without comment.
items.correction: EN: "An Inuit shaman once told European visitors that ..." KO: "한 이누이트 주술사가 유럽에서 온 방문객들에게, ..." Regenerate the voice clip for the changed English sentence. Also update pr019-1.json and src/lib.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr019.json readingSentences #2 (reading-019-s002), EN + KO; same in pr019-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: The great loneliness―like the loneliness a caterpillar endures when she wraps herself in a silky cocoon and begins the long transformation to butterfly. / KO: 거대한 고독이란, 애벌레가 비단 같은 고치로 몸을 감싸고 나비가 되는 긴 변화를 시작할 때 견디는 외로움과 같다.
items.problem: Butterfly caterpillars do not wrap themselves in a silk cocoon. They form a chrysalis, which is their own hardened pupal skin, and it hangs from a small silk pad. Silk cocoons are made by moths. The author's original sentence (Elizabeth Lesser, Broken Open) reads 'silky shroud ... from chrysalis to butterfly'. The course version changed that to 'silky cocoon', which teaches a common misconception as fact, and the Korean ('비단 같은 고치') repeats it. The English is also a sentence with no main verb, and 'transformation to butterfly' has no article, which is unnatural. The Korean has to add '~과 같다' to make it a sentence.
items.correction: EN: "The great loneliness is like the loneliness a caterpillar endures when it hangs inside its chrysalis and begins the long transformation into a butterfly." KO: "거대한 고독이란 애벌레가 번데기 속에서 나비가 되는 긴 변화를 시작할 때 견디는 외로움과 같다." Changing the English removes this sentence's voice clip, so regenerate it in the same change (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs). Also update pr019-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze items 1-3 generated from content/lessons/reading/pr020.json readingSentences #1, #2, #3
items.original: Water, soil, and the earth's green mantle of plants make up the world that supports the animal life of the earth. / Although modern man seldom remembers the fact, he could not exist without the plants that harness the sun's energy and manufacture the basic foodstuff he depends upon for life. / Our attitude toward plants is a singularly narrow one.
items.problem: All three cloze items in this lesson have the same answer, 'plants'. Once a learner has answered item 1, items 2 and 3 are trivial ('plants' is the only option that repeats), so the lesson's whole cloze practises one word. The lesson has 14 cards (mantle, harness, utility, undesirable and others) that go unused.
items.correction: Do not reuse a target word within one lesson. Pick the next valid word or a card word instead, e.g. 'mantle' in #1, 'harness' in #2, 'narrow' in #3.

items.locator: TSV line 290; readingVocabulary entry word "according" (pr021.json line 160); same entry in src/lib/readingVocabulary.json key pr021
items.original: according	adv.	(according to) ~에 따라  — context: conscience leads him to act [according] to the good of this organism
items.problem: The word is used here only inside 'according to', which learner dictionaries and Korean school grammar treat as a compound preposition, not as an adverb. The Korean gloss (~에 따라) is correct. The adv. tag and the bare headword 'according' are wrong. The generated reason string on the same entry also calls it '문장 구조를 결정하는 핵심 동사', which is wrong as well, if that string is ever shown to learners.
items.correction: Headword 'according to', pos 'prep.', gloss '~에 따라'

items.locator: readingSentences #2 (reading-024-s002) korean; same text in pr024-1 readingSentences #2 and pr024-1 instruction block
items.original: 예를 들어, 많은 중국 학생들은 더 좋은 기회와 봉급을 주는 한국 회사를 위해 일할 것을 계획함에 따라 한국에 관심을 갖게 되었다.
items.problem: The English is 'many Chinese students have become interested in Korean', and here 'Korean' means the Korean language, which is the topic of the whole passage (#1 'interested in the Korean language', #3 'Korean language programs'). The Korean translation says 한국에 관심 (interested in the country Korea) instead of 한국어에. 'work for Korean firms' is also rendered as the literal translationese 한국 회사를 위해 일할 (work on behalf of) instead of 한국 회사에서 일할.
items.correction: 예를 들어, 많은 중국 학생들은 더 좋은 기회와 봉급을 주는 한국 회사에서 일할 계획을 세우면서 한국어에 관심을 갖게 되었다. (Update pr024.json, pr024-1.json readingSentences #2 and the pr024-1 instruction text. The English is unchanged, so no clip needs regenerating.)

items.locator: readingSentences #3 (reading-024-s003) english/korean, with #1 'over the past few years'; pr024-1 same
items.original: The total number of foreign students attending Korean language programs has increased to more than 30,000 in Seoul alone this year from about 4,700 at the end of last year.
items.problem: This undated news statistic, from an article that could not be located, is presented as current ('this year', 'last year', and in #1 'over the past few years'). The numbers claim a more than sixfold rise in Seoul alone within less than a year. That does not fit any period of national data: all of South Korea had 22,526 international students in 2005 and 49,270 in 2007. Nor does it describe today: Seoul alone had more than 82,000 foreign students in March 2026. #2's claim that Korean firms 'offer better opportunities and pay' to Chinese students is the same dated framing. A 2026 learner reads all of this as present-day fact.
items.correction: Needs a decision. Either (a) date the passage by finding the original article and putting the real year in the text (e.g. 'In 2005, ...' / '... from about 4,700 in [year]'), or (b) drop the specific numbers (e.g. '... has risen sharply, especially in Seoul.'). Any English change needs `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs` in the same change, because clip keys are text hashes, and the -1 page Korean must be updated to match.

items.original: 펜을 들면 당신은 삶 속의 고마운 사람들을 떠올릴 만큼 충분히 속도를 늦추게 된다.
items.problem: 'the beautiful people in your life' is rendered as 고마운 사람들 ('people you are grateful to'). That changes the adjective. The idea of gratitude comes later in the passage (#4, #6), not in this sentence.
items.correction: 펜을 들면 당신은 삶 속의 소중한(멋진) 사람들을 떠올릴 만큼 충분히 속도를 늦추게 된다.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-031-s002 korean; same text in the pr031-1.json instruction block and readingSentences, and in src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 좋은 양심 만큼 좋은 친구는 없다.
items.problem: Korean spacing error. After a noun, '만큼' is a particle and attaches to it ('양심만큼'). The next sentence of the same passage already writes '나쁜 양심만큼 위험한 적도 없다.', so the two rows are inconsistent.
items.correction: 좋은 양심만큼 좋은 친구는 없다. (Korean text is not voiced, so no audio regeneration is needed.)

items.original: can	v.	~할 수 있다 (조동사)	The best equipment the young [can] have for the battle of life / have	v.	가지다	The best equipment the young can [have] for the battle of life is
items.problem: The passage has only three sentences. To fill the fixed 14-card set, the list includes a modal auxiliary ('can', score 35) and the most basic verb ('have', score 35). Both carry no vocabulary-learning value for a high-school learner. The same padding pulls in good/bad/best/life/friend. 'can' is also tagged 'v.' although the gloss itself calls it 조동사 (aux.). The glosses are correct; the problem is card selection and the inconsistent POS tag for 'can'.
items.correction: Replace 'can' and 'have' with passage words that carry meaning for learners, e.g. 'the battle of life' as a phrase card (인생이라는 싸움) or the 'no ~ so ... as' comparison pattern. If 'can' is kept, tag it 'aux.' (조동사) instead of 'v.'.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1, built from readingSentences[0] (reading-034-s001) by src/lib/readingUtils.ts generateClozeItems lines 731-733
items.original: Common sense aside, the most important asset in business is a sense of humor, an ability to laugh at yourself or the situation.
items.problem: The generator picks 'sense' as the target and masks only its first occurrence: the RegExp has flag 'i' but not 'g'. The learner sees 'Common _______ aside, the most important asset in business is a sense of humor…', so the answer is printed in the same sentence and the graded item tests nothing. The same code gives the same leak in 18 cloze items across the course (pr006#3, pr007#1, pr024#2, pr034#1, pr054#1, pr058#1, pr100#1, pr105#3, pr107#1, pr134#3, pr141#3, pr143#3, pr145#3, pr153#3, pr177#3, pr193#1, pr198#2, pr232#2). I counted these by running the generator's own target rule over src/lib/readingSentences.json.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, either mask every occurrence (new RegExp(`\\b${escapeRegExp(target)}\\b`, 'gi')) or skip target words that appear more than once in the sentence. No content change is needed.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2, built from readingSentences[1] (reading-034-s002); target 'force'
items.original: Laughter is the most powerful and constructive force for calming tension.
items.problem: The wrong options come from the passage's other five-letter words (sense, aside, asset, humor, laugh, point, party, share, upper). In 1 of 3 loads 'asset' is offered. 'Laughter is the most powerful and constructive asset for calming tension' is grammatical and sensible, especially since the previous sentence calls humor 'the most important asset'. It would be marked wrong.
items.correction: Code side: filter distractors that fit the blank, or choose a different target in this sentence (e.g. 'calming').

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-040-s002 (EN and KO), also pr040-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: Parents first teach us essential ways of living by cautioning, “Don’t touch” or “It’s not nice to do that.” We may think that we learn these lessons through independent efforts, but it’s not the way we obtain them at all.
items.problem: One sentence row holds two English sentences and two Korean sentences; the split failed at the closing quote before 'We'. As a result, the header says '11개 핵심 문장' but the passage has 12 sentences. The Step 4 1:1 view, the per-sentence audio and the Step 3 cloze item each treat two sentences as one unit. The map's merged-sentence check (`[a-z][.?!] [A-Z]`) does not catch this because of the quote mark, and the 2026-09-17 fix script rewrote this row without splitting it.
items.correction: Split the row into s002: 'Parents first teach us essential ways of living by cautioning, “Don’t touch” or “It’s not nice to do that.”' / '부모는 먼저 “만지지 마라”, “그러면 못써” 하고 주의를 주며 기본적인 생활 방식을 가르친다.' and s003: 'We may think that we learn these lessons through independent efforts, but it’s not the way we obtain them at all.' / '우리는 이런 교훈을 스스로의 노력으로 배운다고 생각할지 모르지만, 결코 그렇게 얻는 것이 아니다.' Renumber the following ids, update the -1 page and src/lib/readingSentences.json, and regenerate the two new sentence clips with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs, because clip keys are text hashes.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2, built from readingSentences[1] (reading-040-s002); target 'touch'
items.original: Parents first teach us essential ways of living by cautioning, “Don’t touch” or “It’s not nice to do that.”
items.problem: The blank shows as 'cautioning, “Don’t _______”'. The three wrong options are drawn at random from the passage's other five-letter words: lives, aware, teach, don’t, learn, sense, right, wrong, leave, homes, carry, hands, whole, light. 'Don’t leave', 'Don’t carry', 'Don’t teach' and 'Don’t learn' are all grammatical imperatives, and 'Don’t leave' is a very natural parental warning. Nothing in the sentence favors 'touch'. About 2 in 3 page loads offer at least one of these four (1 − C(10,3)/C(14,3) ≈ 0.67), and about 1 in 5 offer 'leave' (3/14). A learner who picks one is marked wrong.
items.correction: Code side: do not pick a target inside quoted speech, or keep wrong options that cannot complete the frame (for example, exclude verbs when the target follows 'Don’t'). An alternative is to take the pr040 cloze from a sentence where context decides the word, e.g. 'right and _______' (wrong).

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-044-s003 .korean (pr044.json and pr044-1.json; pr044-1 instruction block)
items.original: 결국 아이들은 자신의 부모와 같은 방식으로 먹는다.
items.problem: In 'After all, children eat the same way as their parents do.', 'after all' gives the reason for the previous sentence (children of poor eaters also eat poorly, because children copy their parents). '결국' reads as 'in the end / eventually', which is the other sense of 'after all'. The discourse relation changes from reason to conclusion.
items.correction: 따지고 보면 아이들은 부모와 같은 방식으로 먹기 마련이니까. (or: 어쨌든 아이들은 부모가 먹는 대로 먹기 때문이다.)

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-045-s006 (and the passage premise in s001/s005); pr045.json and pr045-1.json
items.original: Remember that it is shared by several people who have an equal right to its use.
items.problem: The passage presents telephone etiquette for a single telephone shared by a household ('Do not keep the telephone to yourself' / 'it is shared by several people') as current, general advice. In 2026 almost every adult Korean learner owns a personal phone (Pew: 98% smartphone ownership in South Korea), so the premise is outdated and puzzling without context. The English itself is correct.
items.correction: Keep the English (changing it would require regenerating its Ava clips). Make the context clear in the Korean, e.g. s006 KO '(집) 전화는 그것을 쓸 동등한 권리를 가진 여러 사람이 함께 쓴다는 것을 기억하라.' Or replace the passage in a later content revision.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-047-s002 .korean (pr047.json and pr047-1.json; pr047-1 instruction block)
items.original: 정부는 경제가 강하게 유지되어야 한다는 점을 인식하고 이러한 우수성을 성취하기 위해 필요로 하는 것은 무엇이든지 기꺼이 제공하고 있다.
items.problem: 'is willing to provide whatever is needed' states a willingness (the government is prepared to provide). The Korean '기꺼이 제공하고 있다' ('is gladly providing') turns it into an ongoing action. The meaning of 'be willing to' (~할 용의가 있다) is lost.
items.correction: 정부는 경제가 강하게 유지되어야 한다는 점을 인식하고 있으며, 이러한 우수성을 이루는 데 필요한 것이라면 무엇이든 기꺼이 제공하려 한다.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-049-s005 .korean (pr049.json and pr049-1.json; pr049-1 instruction block)
items.original: 시인이라면 시도 잘 쓸 것이다.
items.problem: The English is 'If one is a poet, poetry will be easy to write.' The Korean gives 'will also write poetry well'. The meaning of 'easy' is missing, and '도' (also) is added. The Step 2 card 'easy — 쉬운' comes from this sentence, so the aligned translation does not show the carded word.
items.correction: 시인이라면 시를 쓰는 것이 쉬울 것이다.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-050-s001 .korean (pr050.json and pr050-1.json; also the pr050-1 instruction block, which joins the sentence KO)
items.original: 언어가 없는 사회는 가장 단순한 협동 작업 말고는 어떤 일도 할 수 없을 것이다.
items.problem: The English says the society could not take part in any cooperative enterprise except the simplest ones ('incapable of engaging in any but the simplest of cooperative enterprises'). The Korean '어떤 일도' widens this to 'could do nothing at all except the simplest cooperative tasks'. That contradicts sentence #3, where each individual still acts on 'his own strength and ability'.
items.correction: 언어가 없는 사회는 가장 단순한 협동 작업 말고는 어떤 협동 작업에도 참여할 수 없을 것이다.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] reading-051-s004 english; card readingVocabulary[13] 'obtain' (얻다, 이루다)
items.original: He who gets all he can honestly, and saves all he gets will certainly obtain his goal.
items.problem: This is an adaptation of Franklin's 'He that gets all he can honestly, and saves all he gets (necessary expenses excepted) will certainly become rich.' The rewrite introduced 'obtain his goal', which is not a standard collocation (achieve/attain/reach a goal). The obtain card then teaches it with the meaning '이루다'. The comma before 'and saves' has no matching comma after 'gets', which leaves a single comma inside the subject.
items.correction: 'He who gets all he can honestly and saves all he gets will certainly achieve his goal.' (or restore Franklin's 'will certainly become rich'). Swap the card for 'achieve = 이루다, 달성하다', or keep obtain but gloss it 얻다, 획득하다 only. Changing the English deletes its audio clip, so regenerate it with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: {"word":"right","lemma":"right","partOfSpeech":"adj.","korean":"옳은 (right from wrong 옳고 그름)"}
items.problem: In 'know good from bad, and right from wrong' and 'distinguish right from wrong' (2 of the 3 occurrences, including the card's context sentence), 'right' is a noun ('what is morally correct'). The card labels it adj. and uses that very noun phrase as its example.
items.correction: partOfSpeech 'n.', korean '옳은 것, 선 (right from wrong 옳고 그름)'. Or keep adj. and use the adjective example '(the right path 올바른 길)'.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 728; content/lessons/reading/pr052.json readingVocabulary[12] (word 'right', freq 3); context sentence reading-052-s002 (also s007 'distinguish right from wrong')
items.original: {"word":"right","lemma":"right","partOfSpeech":"adj.","korean":"옳은 (right from wrong 옳고 그름)"} — context: "We want our children to know good from bad, and right from wrong."
items.problem: The card is built from 'know good from bad, and right from wrong', and the gloss's own example is 'right from wrong'. In that phrase 'right' is a noun meaning what is morally correct. It is the object of know/distinguish A from B, parallel to the nouns good/bad and paired with the noun 'wrong'. The card labels it adj. and glosses it with the adjective form 옳은, so the tag contradicts the card's own example 옳고 그름. The passage uses the same noun in s007 ('distinguish right from wrong'). Only s004 ('the right path') uses 'right' as an adjective, and that is not the card's context.
items.correction: partOfSpeech "n.", korean "옳은 것, 옳음 (know/distinguish right from wrong 옳고 그름을 구별하다)". If the card should also cover s004, add "· adj. 올바른 (the right path)" after the noun gloss rather than tagging the whole card adj.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] reading-052-s004 english (+ passage block, pr052-1.json, src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: In short, we want our children to develop a conscience―a powerful inner voice that will keep them on the right path.
items.problem: The dash is U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR (a Korean/HWP typesetting glyph), not an English em dash (U+2014). It shows as a long bar in some fonts. It also glues 'conscience―a' into one token for the whitespace-based cloze/pool code (this is not the current cloze target). The same glyph appears in 12 READING passages (pr013 pr019 pr048 pr052 pr074 pr149 pr165 pr168 pr187 pr222 pr235 pr237).
items.correction: Replace ― (U+2015) with — (U+2014). Audio clip keys are text hashes, so regenerate the audio for the changed sentences (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs), or first confirm that the key normalizes this character.

items.original: 그러면 결국 우리 자녀들은 우리들이 의도하는 뜻을 완전히 받아들이게 될 것이고, 그러한 뜻은 그들의 성격의 바탕이 될 것이다.
items.problem: The passage is about moral character (card: character = 인격, 성품), but here 'the essence of their character' is rendered 성격 ('personality/temperament'), and essence (card: 본질, 핵심) as 바탕. The sentence and the lesson's own cards disagree.
items.correction: …그러한 메시지는 그들 인격의 본질이 될 것이다.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] reading-053-s002 english + korean (+ pr053-1.json, src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: Albert Einstein remarked, “There is no chance that nuclear energy will ever be obtainable.”
items.problem: The sentence is shown as a direct quotation, but it is a paraphrase. Einstein's recorded words (Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, 29 Dec 1934) were 'There is not the slightest indication that [nuclear energy] will ever be obtainable.' The paraphrase turns 'no evidence yet' into a flat claim that it is impossible.
items.correction: Use the recorded wording: 'In 1934 Albert Einstein remarked, “There is not the slightest indication that nuclear energy will ever be obtainable.”' KO: 'Albert Einstein은 1934년에 “핵에너지를 얻을 수 있으리라는 조짐은 조금도 없다.”라고 말했다.' Alternatively, drop the quotation marks (reported speech). Regenerate the sentence audio after the English change.

items.locator: readingSentences[0] reading-054-s001 korean (same text in pr054-1.json readingSentences + instruction block, src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: 성공적인 데이터베이스 마케팅 솔루션을 수행하기 위해, 여러분은 고객과 잠재 고객에 대한 적절한 데이터를 구별하고 수집하는 방법을 알고 원자료를 강력한 마케팅 정보로 바꾸기 위하여 데이터 창고 기술을 사용해서 행동을 분석하기 위해 통계 기술을 고객과 잠재 고객 데이터베이스 적용하고 그들의 반응의 가능성의 각도에서 개인을 점수를 매기는 것이 필요하다.
items.problem: The English lists four things you need to know how to do (identify/gather data; use data-warehousing techniques to transform raw data; apply statistical techniques to databases to analyze behavior; score individuals by response probability). The Korean attaches 'know how to' only to the first, and it merges the 2nd and 3rd into one clause, so it reads as 'using data-warehousing techniques, apply statistical techniques'. It also drops a particle ('데이터베이스 적용하고' → 데이터베이스에). It mistranslates identify as 구별하고 and implement as 수행하기. 'in terms of the probability of their response' becomes the unreadable '그들의 반응의 가능성의 각도에서 개인을 점수를 매기는'. The R-30 'Korean mistranslations only' fix left this sentence as it was.
items.correction: 성공적인 데이터베이스 마케팅 솔루션을 구현하려면, 고객과 잠재 고객에 관한 적절한 데이터를 식별하고 수집하는 법, 데이터 웨어하우징 기법으로 원자료를 강력한 마케팅 정보로 바꾸는 법, 고객·잠재 고객 데이터베이스에 통계 기법을 적용해 행동을 분석하는 법, 그리고 응답 가능성에 따라 개인별 점수를 매기는 법을 알아야 한다. (Only relevant if the owner keeps pr054 under R-30.)

items.original: 우리가 여러분에게 데이터베이스 마케팅을 위한 유일한 끝과 끝을 잇는 소프트웨어 솔류션을 여러분에게 소개함으로써 데이터베이스 마케팅 세미나에서 우리는 이러한 주제와 그 이상을 발표할 것이다.
items.problem: 'end-to-end' is translated literally as 끝과 끝을 잇는 ('connecting end and end'). In context it means a solution covering the whole process (통합/엔드투엔드). 'address these topics' (다루다) becomes 발표할 것이다 (announce/present). 여러분에게 appears twice. 솔류션 is misspelled; S1 of the same passage spells it 솔루션.
items.correction: 데이터베이스 마케팅 세미나에서는 데이터베이스 마케팅을 위한 유일한 엔드투엔드(전 과정 통합) 소프트웨어 솔루션을 소개하면서 이러한 주제와 그 밖의 내용을 다룰 것이다.

items.original: 데이터 베이스 마케팅 능력을 적용함으로써 여러분은 비용을 감소하면서 이윤을 증가할 수 있다.
items.problem: 감소하다/증가하다 are intransitive, so they cannot take 비용을/이윤을 as objects (감소시키면서/늘릴 is needed). 데이터 베이스 is spaced differently from 데이터베이스 elsewhere in the passage.
items.correction: 데이터베이스 마케팅 역량을 활용하면 비용은 줄이면서 이익은 늘릴 수 있다.

items.original: 응용 분석의 선구자인 SAS 연구소와 깊이있는 중요한 주제를 와서 체험하십시오.
items.problem: 'explore this important topic in depth' is mistranslated. 'in depth' becomes an adjective on the topic (깊이있는 중요한 주제), 'this' is dropped, and explore becomes 체험하십시오 ('experience'), which contradicts the lesson's own card (explore = 탐구하다). 'leader' becomes 선구자 ('pioneer'). 'SAS Institute' is a software company's proper name, not a research institute (연구소).
items.correction: 응용 분석 분야의 선도 기업인 SAS Institute와 함께 이 중요한 주제를 깊이 있게 탐구해 보십시오.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 (readingSentences[0] reading-054-s001); masking at src/lib/readingUtils.ts:732-733 replaces only the first match
items.original: In order to implement successful database marketing solutions, you need to know how to identify and gather relevant data about customers and prospects, use data warehousing techniques to transform raw data into powerful marketing information, …
items.problem: The blank is 'marketing' ('successful database _______ solutions'). The regex replaces only the first occurrence, so the answer is still printed later in the same masked sentence ('into powerful marketing information'). The item tests nothing.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, prefer a target word that occurs only once in the sentence, or mask every occurrence (use the 'gi' flag). The same code fix also fixes pr058 item 1 and pr100 (already noted in maps/reading.md). pr054 as a whole is still pending under R-30.

items.original: 교사들이 학생들을 효율적으로 가르칠 수 있으려면 학생들을 잘 알 필요가 있다.
items.problem: 'effectively' (효과적으로, producing the intended result) is translated as 효율적으로 ('efficiently'). Korean learners often confuse this pair.
items.correction: 교사들이 학생들을 효과적으로 가르칠 수 있으려면 학생들을 잘 알 필요가 있다.

items.original: 뿐만 아니라, 교사들은 그 부모들과도 좋은 관계를 유지해야만 하는데, 그 부모들도 또한 전공동체의 중요한 일부분이다.
items.problem: 'the total community' is written as 전공동체, which can also be read as 前공동체 ('former community'). It should be 전체 공동체.
items.correction: …그 부모들 또한 공동체 전체의 중요한 일부이다.

items.original: 학생들이 그들의 선생님과 다른 성인들과 의미있는 관계를 맺을 때, 학생들은 그들을 실제적인 사람들로 더 잘 볼 수 있다.
items.problem: 'see them as real people' means seeing teachers as real human beings, not just roles. 실제적인 means 'practical/actual', so 실제적인 사람들 does not convey this. 의미있는 should be spaced 의미 있는.
items.correction: 학생들이 교사나 다른 어른들과 의미 있는 관계를 맺으면, 그들을 (역할이 아닌) 한 사람의 인간으로 더 잘 보게 된다.

items.original: 그 학교 공동체의 모든 구성원들은 소속감을 느끼고, 그 학교에 적극적인 공헌을 할 수 있다.
items.problem: 'positive contribution' means a beneficial/constructive contribution (긍정적인/유익한), not an active one (적극적인). The Korean also turns 'can make a positive contribution' into a separate factual claim, when in the English it is part of what members feel ('feel as though they belong and can make…').
items.correction: 학교 공동체의 모든 구성원이 자신이 그곳에 속해 있으며 학교에 긍정적인 기여를 할 수 있다고 느낀다.

items.locator: TSV line 772; content/lessons/reading/pr056.json readingVocabulary[0] (word 'young'); same entry in src/lib/readingVocabulary.json['pr056']
items.original: young | adj. | 젊은 (the young 젊은이들) | context: The [young] should learn that no one can win all the time
items.problem: In this passage, 'the young' means children. The next sentences are 'A child who doesn't make the baseball team feels terrible.' and 'The youngster should be allowed to experience disappointment.', and the same lesson's 'youngster' card reads '아이, 청소년'. In Korean, 젊은/젊은이 means young adults in their prime (synonym 청년), so the gloss gives the wrong picture of who the sentence is about. It is a dictionary sense, but not the right sense for this sentence.
items.correction: adj. 어린, 젊은 (the young 어린 사람들, 젊은이들: 여기서는 아이들)

items.original: 적당한 보험 증권은 휴가 전이나 휴가 동안 질병이나 사고로부터 발생하는 의료비용과 휴가비의 손해, 그리고 휴일의 취소에 대한 보상을 제공해야 한다.
items.problem: The passage is British English ('travellers'). 'cancellation of the holiday' means cancellation of the trip/vacation (BrE holiday = AmE vacation), not of a 휴일 (day off / public holiday). '휴일의 취소' makes no sense and teaches the wrong meaning of holiday in exactly the context where the BrE sense matters. 'loss of vacation money' (losing one's travel money) is also vaguely rendered as 휴가비의 손해.
items.correction: 적합한 보험 증권은 휴가 전이나 휴가 중의 질병이나 사고로 생기는 의료비, 여행 경비 분실, 그리고 여행(휴가) 취소에 대한 보장을 제공해야 한다.

items.original: In educating students for adult work and adult life, American schools try, above all, to be practical.
items.problem: Target is 'adult'. Only the first occurrence is masked, so the learner sees 'In educating students for _______ work and adult life', with the answer two words after the blank.
items.correction: Same code fix as pr054: skip targets that occur more than once in the sentence, or mask all occurrences. With the skip rule this sentence's target becomes another eligible word (e.g. 'schools' or 'American').

items.locator: readingSentences[3] reading-059-s004 english + korean (+ pr059-1.json, src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: The blind must get the corneas from people with healthy eyes—people who agree to let blind people use their eyes after they die.
items.problem: This implies only people with 'healthy eyes' can donate corneas. Eye-bank associations say the opposite: poor eyesight, glasses, cataracts, LASIK and many eye diseases do not stop cornea donation, and eligibility depends on corneal tissue quality and a few systemic conditions. The sentence can mislead learners, and could discourage potential donors.
items.correction: 'The blind can get corneas from donors—people who agree to let blind people use their corneas after they die.' Update the KO to match (…기증자, 즉 자신이 죽은 뒤 시각장애인이 자기 각막을 쓰도록 허락한 사람들에게서 각막을 받을 수 있다). Regenerate the audio after the English change.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 968; content/lessons/reading/pr070.json:79 and pr070-1.json:79 (readingVocabulary word 'safe'); src/lib/readingVocabulary.json:11805
items.original: safe	adj.	(it is not safe to conclude) 섣불리 ~라고 결론 내릴 수 없다	| context: So it is not [safe] to conclude that what you say
items.problem: The card for the adjective 'safe' never says what 'safe' means here, which is 틀릴 염려가 없는, 무방한. The whole gloss translates the clause, and its core '결론 내릴 수 없다' is really the meaning of 'not ... conclude'. That meaning already has its own card in the same lesson (conclude v. 결론 내리다, line 980). A student who reveals the card sees no meaning for 'safe' itself, so the frequent exam pattern 'It is safe to say/assume that ~' (~라고 해도 무방하다) is not learned. The same site already handles this better elsewhere: pr023 glosses it as '(it is safe to say) ~라고 해도 틀리지 않다'.
items.correction: (판단·말이) 틀릴 염려가 없는, 무방한 (it is not safe to conclude ~ 섣불리 ~라고 결론 내릴 수 없다). Apply in pr070.json, pr070-1.json and src/lib/readingVocabulary.json.

items.original: A famous psychology experiment is often said to show that your appearance makes up 55% of a first impression. / The experiment, however, was not about first impressions. / It looked at how listeners judge a speaker's feelings when the words, the tone of voice, and the facial expression do not match. / In that special case, facial expression counted for 55%, tone of voice for 38%, and the actual words for only 7%.
items.problem: The passage exists to correct a myth, but it describes one experiment that tested words, tone and face together. The 7/38/55 figures come from two separate small 1967 studies: Mehrabian & Wiener compared words with tone, and Mehrabian & Ferris compared face with tone (spoken on a neutral word). The percentages were calculated by combining the two. No single experiment put all three channels in conflict. The judgments were about liking/attitude toward the speaker.
items.correction: Suggested EN: s001 "Famous psychology research from 1967 is often said to show that ..."; s002 "The research, however, was not about first impressions."; s003 "Two small experiments looked at how listeners judge a speaker's feelings when the words, the tone of voice, or the facial expression do not match."; s004 "When the two results were combined, facial expression counted for 55%, ...". Update the KO lines to match, then the cards (experiment freq) and both files. Regenerate the changed sentence clips with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: "word": "safe", "lemma": "safe", "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "(it is not safe to conclude) 섣불리 ~라고 결론 내릴 수 없다"
items.problem: The meaning shown for the adjective 'safe' is a negative clause for the whole phrase. It never says what 'safe' means here (reasonable, certain not to be wrong). Learners can take 'safe' to mean '섣불리 / ~할 수 없다'.
items.correction: "korean": "(판단·결론이) 무리가 없는, 틀릴 염려가 없는 (it is not safe to conclude ~ 섣불리 ~라고 결론 내릴 수 없다)"

items.problem: The headword 'representative' is glossed as '직원' (employee), and no English dictionary gives that sense. On its own the noun means 대표(자) or 대리인: someone who speaks or acts for a person or organisation. The sales sense is 'a company agent who visits potential purchasers' (판매 대리인, 영업 담당자). The student would then misread phrases like 'a representative of the students' (학생 대표) or 'House of Representatives' (하원). The phrase gloss '영업 사원' is fine; only the headword sense is wrong.

items.original: "They say best men are molded out of faults," wrote Shakespeare in Measure for Measure, "and, for the most part, become much more the better for being a little bad."
items.problem: The passage puts this line in quotation marks and credits it to Shakespeare, but it does not match the text. In Measure for Measure, Act 5 Scene 1, Mariana says 'And, for the most, become much more the better / For being a little bad'. The play has 'for the most', not 'for the most part'. The meaning is the same, but a direct quotation is misworded. Separately, the line belongs to the character Mariana, so 'wrote Shakespeare' presents a character's plea as the author's own view. This is common in quote collections and I do not treat it as an error by itself. The card glosses on this sentence are all correct.
items.correction: Either quote exactly ('..."and, for the most, become much more the better for being a little bad."') or leave the quotation marks as they are and gloss 'for the most' as 대개 in a note. If the English sentence is changed, the audio clip must be regenerated in the same change with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs, because clip keys are hashes of the text. Update pr074.json, pr074-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json.

If the headword text changes, regenerate its audio clip in the same change (clip keys are text hashes).

items.original: 효과가 얼마나 심각할지에 의문을 제기하는 비판자도 일부 있지만, 지구 온난화의 증거는 이제 매우 확실하다.
items.problem: 'the effects' here are the harmful impacts of warming. 효과 usually means an intended or beneficial result, and '효과가 심각하다' is an odd collocation. The next sentence (s004) translates the same word 'effects' as 영향.
items.correction: 영향이 얼마나 심각할지에 의문을 제기하는 비판자도 일부 있지만, 지구 온난화의 증거는 이제 매우 확실하다.

items.original: But although they had looked attractive separately, the entire assembly shocked him, for he found that he had been changed into an ugly camel.
items.problem: The blank is 'assembly'. The distance-0 pool is merciful, creature, features, although, remember; 3 are drawn, so 'creature' appears 60% of the time. 'the entire creature shocked him' is grammatical and makes sense: the whole new animal shocked him. It is graded wrong.
items.correction: Exclude 'creature' for this item, or pick another target word. No English change.

items.locator: readingSentences s004 / s008 / s013 / s014 / s015 korean (also pr080-1 instruction block)
items.original: “Mays씨, 사인 좀 받을 수 있을까요?” / 굴러 떨어지기 시작했고, 울음을 그치게 할 수 있는 건 아무 것도 없었다. / Willie Mays 보다 / 그 날 밤 이후에 / 있는지 없는 지를 꼭 확인하는 것은
items.problem: Korean spacing errors. 씨 is a dependent noun and takes a space. 보다 is a particle and attaches. 아무것, 그날 and 굴러떨어지다 are single dictionary words. 'N는지' is an ending and attaches. In s015, '집을 떠날 때마다' also means leaving home for good; 나설 is meant.
items.correction: “Mays 씨, …” / 굴러떨어지기 … 아무것도 / Willie Mays보다 / 그날 밤 이후에 / 있는지 없는지를 (and 집을 나설 때마다)

items.original: I rushed to him and said, “Mr. Mays, could I please have your autograph?” He said, “Sure, kid. | You got a pencil?” I didn’t have one in my pocket.
items.problem: The row break falls inside Mays's quotation. s004 ends with an unclosed quote, and s005 starts with a closing quote and then switches to narration. On the per-sentence hover or Step 4 view, and in per-sentence audio, each row shows a half quotation. The Korean mirrors this ('“물론이지, 꼬마야.' / '연필 있니?” 내 주머니에는…').
items.correction: Re-segment as: 'I rushed to him and said, “Mr. Mays, could I please have your autograph?”' / 'He said, “Sure, kid. You got a pencil?”' / 'I didn’t have one in my pocket.' Adjust the Korean rows the same way. Because the English row text changes, regenerate audio with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: readingSentences[11] reading-080-s012 korean (same text in pr080-1.json readingSentences and pr080-1 instruction block)
items.original: 그 팀을 생각하면, 더 이상 존재하지 않는 지금에도 나는 그 팀의 거의 모든 야구 선수들의 이름을 암송할 수 있다.
items.problem: In the English, 'which no longer exists' modifies 'that team': the New York Giants moved away in 1958. The Korean attaches '더 이상 존재하지 않는' to '지금' (now), which gives 'even now, which no longer exists'. That garbles who or what no longer exists.
items.correction: 지금도 나는 이제는 존재하지 않는 그 팀을 떠올리면 그 팀의 거의 모든 선수 이름을 줄줄이 욀 수 있다. Update pr080.json, pr080-1.json readingSentences and the pr080-1 instruction text together. This is a Korean-only change, so there is no audio impact.

items.locator: readingSentences[0] id reading-084-s001, korean (same in pr084-1)
items.original: 사람들은 그들의 첫인상이 잘못된 것일 지라도 그것에 집착하는 경향이 있다.
items.problem: '-ㄹ지라도' is a connective ending and must be written attached: '것일지라도'. The space is a Korean spelling error.
items.correction: 사람들은 첫인상이 잘못된 것일지라도 그것을 고수하는 경향이 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-084-s002, korean (same in pr084-1)
items.original: 당신이 당신의 이웃 사람의 이름을 어떤 친구에게 언급했다고 가정해보자.
items.problem: The English is 'your new neighbor', but 'new' is not translated. It matters to the argument: you have no impression of a new neighbour yet, so the friend's judgment becomes your first impression.
items.correction: 새로 이사 온 이웃의 이름을 친구에게 말했다고 가정해 보자.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] id reading-084-s004, korean (same in pr084-1)
items.original: “그는 처음에는 멋진 것처럼 보이지만, 그것은 전부 꾸민 것이야.” 아마 이 평가는 근거 없는 것일 수도 있다.
items.problem: 'He seems nice at first' is about character: the neighbour seems kind or a good person. '멋진' means cool or stylish, which shifts the judgment to looks or impressiveness. The whole passage is about judging a person's character.
items.correction: “처음엔 좋은 사람처럼 보이지만, 다 연기야.” 어쩌면 이 평가는 근거가 없을 수도 있다.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 1187; content/lessons/reading/pr085.json readingVocabulary[9] (JSON lines 203-214, word "according")
items.original: according	adv.	(according to) ~에 따르면	[According] to ancient superstitions, moles reveal a
items.problem: Same defect as pr077. 'According to ancient superstitions' is the compound preposition 'according to', but the card is tagged 'adv.' while the gloss gives the prepositional meaning '~에 따르면'.
items.correction: word/lemma "according to", partOfSpeech "prep.", korean "~에 따르면". Regenerate the headword audio clip if the text changes.

items.original: according | adv. | (according to) ~에 따르면
items.problem: In 'According to ancient superstitions, moles reveal a person’s character', 'according to' is a compound preposition. Learner dictionaries list it as a preposition. The card labels it adv. The same label appears on the 'according' cards in pr021, pr077, pr091, pr117 and pr124, so it is a course-wide choice.
items.correction: Show the card as 'according to' with partOfSpeech 'prep.' and meaning '~에 따르면'. Apply the same change course-wide.

items.locator: readingSentences[0] id reading-087-s001, korean (same in pr087-1)
items.original: 십대들은 상상(허상)의 관객들로 둘러싸여 있다.
items.problem: The parenthetical '(허상)' looks like a translator's leftover note inside a translation meant to be complete. The passive '둘러싸여 있다' also loses the reflexive 'surround themselves': the teens themselves create the imaginary audience.
items.correction: 십대들은 상상 속의 관객들로 자신을 둘러싼다.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] id reading-087-s004 (EN + KO; same in pr087-1)
items.original: A young boy, for example, may believe that he is unattractive because of his nose. Nothing can convince him that other people are paying no attention to his nose at all.
items.problem: Two English sentences are stored as one unit (the map flagged pr087#4). The Korean fuses them into a single restructured sentence ('예를 들면, 자신의 코가 못생겼다고 생각하는 소년에게 … 설득하는 것은 불가능하다.'), so neither English sentence has its own Korean counterpart.
items.correction: Split into two units: 'A young boy, for example, may believe that he is unattractive because of his nose.' / '예를 들어 어떤 소년은 코 때문에 자신이 못생겼다고 믿을지도 모른다.' and 'Nothing can convince him that other people are paying no attention to his nose at all.' / '다른 사람들은 그의 코에 전혀 신경 쓰지 않는다고 아무리 말해도 그를 납득시킬 수 없다.' Regenerate Ava clips.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] id reading-087-s005, korean (same in pr087-1.json and in the pr087-1 Korean instruction block)
items.original: 또한, 십대 소녀들이 친구들과 얘기를 할 때면, 그들은 과장되게 표현하거나, 크게 웃고 얘기하며 가상의 청중들이 있는 것처럼 행동한다.
items.problem: The English says 'some teenage girls are too expressive'. The Korean drops 'some' (일부), so it says that teenage girls as a group behave this way. That changes the meaning and turns a limited example into a gender stereotype. 'too expressive' (지나치게) is also softened to a plain '과장되게 표현하거나'.
items.correction: 또한 일부 십대 소녀들은 친구들과 이야기할 때 지나치게 표현이 과해서, 큰 소리로 떠들고 웃으며 있지도 않은 청중을 의식해 행동한다.

items.locator: readingSentences[6] id reading-087-s007, korean (same in pr087-1)
items.original: 십대들의 행동은 남들이 자신들을 지켜보기엔 남들의 삶이 아주 바쁘다는 것을 깨달으면서 변하게 된다.
items.problem: 'too busy with their own lives to be watching them' is the too…to construction, meaning so busy that they cannot watch. '아주 바쁘다' (very busy) weakens it, and repeating '남들이 … 남들의' makes the Korean awkward.
items.correction: 십대들은 남들이 자기 삶에 너무 바빠서 자신들을 지켜볼 겨를이 없다는 것을 깨달으면서 행동이 달라진다.

items.locator: readingSentences[2] id reading-088-s003, english (same in pr088-1 and in the English instruction block)
items.original: Because of this change, shop owners are changing store designs to make shopping and consumer service easier.
items.problem: 'consumer service' is not the idiomatic term for the service a store gives its shoppers. The standard collocation is 'customer service', and the passage's own Korean translation already says '고객 서비스'.
items.correction: Because of this change, shop owners are changing store designs to make shopping and customer service easier. Changing the English removes this sentence's Ava clip, so regenerate it with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze items #2 and #3, generated from readingSentences[1] reading-090-s002 and readingSentences[2] reading-090-s003 (the same items appear on pr090-1)
items.original: The husband influences his wife and child. / The wife influences her husband and child.
items.problem: Distractors are chosen only by closeness in word length. Item #2 masks 'influences' (10 letters). The only other 10-letter word in the passage pool is 'influenced', so it appears as a distractor on every load, and 'The husband influenced his wife and child.' is a correct English sentence that the item marks wrong. Item #3 masks 'husband' (7 letters). The only 7-letter pool words are friends, society and network, so all three always appear, and 'The wife influences her friends and child.' is also grammatical and plausible. Only the exact passage word is graded correct.
items.correction: For this lesson, stop offering another form of the answer word as a distractor (exclude influence, influenced, influences when the target is 'influences'). Also check that no distractor forms a valid sentence, or choose a different target word for s002 and s003. A general fix in generateClozeItems would exclude words that share the target's lemma.

items.locator: readingVocabulary[10] word "according" (TSV line 1272); passage sentence reading-091-s002
items.original: according	adv.	(according to) ~에 따르면  — context: "For example, [according] to American law, if someone is accused of a crime..."
items.problem: The card has an adv. badge, but its gloss explains the phrase 'according to', and that is the only way the word appears in the passage. 'According to' is a preposition (a two-word preposition, 구전치사). 'According' by itself is only an adjective ('in agreement') or an obsolete adverb meaning 'accordingly'. Neither sense is used here. So the badge gives the wrong part of speech for the phrase the card teaches. The same adv. tag appears on 'according' cards in pr021, pr077, pr085, pr117 and pr124 (outside this scope), so the fix should be applied to all of them.
items.correction: partOfSpeech "prep." with word/gloss shown as the phrase: "according to" prep. ~에 따르면. At minimum, change the badge from adv. to prep. (구전치사). Apply the same change to the other 'according' cards in pr021, pr077, pr085, pr117 and pr124.

items.locator: readingSentences[5] (reading-103-s006) korean; mirrored in pr103-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 두 번째로 부유한 사람뿐만 아니라 가난한 사람들도 이용할 수 있는 새로운 작물의 경작, 저장 및 판매 방식이 개발될 것이다.
items.problem: In the English, 'new' modifies 'ways' (new ways of growing, storing and selling crops). Placed before '작물의', the Korean '새로운' most naturally reads as 'new crops' (cultivation, storage and sale of new crops), which changes the meaning.
items.correction: '두 번째로 부유한 사람뿐만 아니라 가난한 사람들도 이용할 수 있는, 작물을 기르고 저장하고 파는 새로운 방식이 개발될 것이다.'

items.original: "word": "different", "lemma": "different", "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "다른"  — context: "Mexico attracts [different] types of visitors."
items.problem: In "different types of visitors" the adjective carries the 'various / several of the same basic kind' sense, not the contrastive 'not the same as something else' sense that 다른 expresses. Longman lists this as a separate numbered sense ("used to talk about two or more separate things of the same basic kind", synonym "various") with the structurally identical example "There are many different types of fabric"; Wiktionary lists it as sense 4, "Various, assorted, diverse." The gloss 다른 also contradicts the lesson's own sentence translation in the same file (reading-104-s001, line 51): "멕시코에는 여러 부류의 방문객이 모여든다." There is no antecedent in the passage for anything the visitors could be 'different from' — the sentence is the topic sentence introducing three groups. (By contrast the same gloss 다른 is correct at TSV line 1354, pr097 "vastly different from one another", so the card set is applying one fixed gloss without checking the sentence.)
items.correction: "korean": "여러 가지의, 다양한" (optionally "여러 가지의 (different types of ~ 여러 부류의)" to match the collocation convention already used elsewhere in this data set).

items.original: One group is composed of artists. As admirers of the Mexican culture, they want to be close to the subjects they are writing about or painting.
items.problem: One sentence entry holds two sentences, and the KO does too ('한 부류는 예술가들이다. 멕시코 문화를 동경하는 그들은 …'). Every other entry in pr101–pr110 is one sentence. The 1:1 numbering, the per-sentence audio and the speaking tester therefore treat two sentences as one unit, unlike the rest of the course. The alignment itself is correct.
items.correction: Split into two entries: 'One group is composed of artists.' / '한 부류는 예술가들이다.' and 'As admirers of Mexican culture, they want to be close to the subjects they are writing about or painting.' / '멕시코 문화를 동경하는 그들은 자신이 글로 쓰거나 그리는 대상 가까이에 있고 싶어 한다.' Renumber the ids, update pr104-1.json and src/lib, and regenerate both EN clips. Dropping 'the' before 'Mexican culture' is optional.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] (reading-104-s004) english + korean; mirrored in pr104-1.json, instruction blocks, src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: They like the unhurried way of life with its long afternoon nap and they enjoy the temperate climate.
items.problem: The sentence presents 'the long afternoon nap' (siesta) as a feature of Mexican life.
