The napping, unhurried Mexican is a well-known negative stereotype ('sleepy/lazy Mexican'), and the siesta is not a common practice in modern Mexico (a 1998 J Sleep Res study of urban Mexicans found the 'siesta culture' concept unsupported). The Korean repeats it: '긴 낮잠을 즐기는 느긋한 생활 방식'. This is a reputational risk for a commercial product.
items.correction: EN: 'They like the unhurried way of life and they enjoy the temperate climate.' KO: '그들은 느긋한 생활 방식을 좋아하고 온화한 기후를 즐긴다.' The 'unhurried' card stays valid. Regenerate the EN clip.

items.locator: readingSentences[3] (reading-106-s004) english + korean; mirrored in pr106-1.json, instruction blocks, src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: There is also a quantity discount, which is offered to individuals who order large quantities of a product.
items.problem: A quantity discount is a price reduction for volume purchases by any buyer, including businesses. 'Individuals' (KO '개인에게') wrongly narrows it to private persons and sets up a false contrast with the trade discount in #3. The next sentence already calls them 'these buyers'.
items.correction: EN: '…which is offered to buyers who order large quantities of a product.' KO: '수량 할인도 있는데, 이는 한 제품을 대량으로 주문하는 구매자에게 제공된다.' Regenerate the EN clip.

items.locator: readingSentences[5] (reading-106-s006) english + korean; mirrored in pr106-1.json, instruction blocks, src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: Finally, a cash discount is a lower price offered to people who pay in cash.
items.problem: The passage teaches business pricing terms (trade discount, quantity discount, cash discount). In marketing and accounting, the standard meaning of 'cash discount' is a discount for prompt payment of an invoice (e.g. 2/10, net 30), not only for paying with banknotes. The Korean term 현금할인 has the same accounting meaning (조기 결제 할인). The passage gives only the colloquial retail sense, so learners get the business term wrong.
items.correction: EN: 'Finally, a cash discount is a lower price offered to buyers who pay promptly, for example in cash or before the bill is due.' KO: '마지막으로 현금 할인은 현금 결제나 기한 전 결제처럼 대금을 빨리 치르는 구매자에게 제공되는 낮은 가격이다.' Regenerate the EN clip.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] (reading-108-s005) korean (also #6, #7 term); mirrored in pr108-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 대조적으로 비물질적 문화는 눈에 보이지 않는 인간의 창조로 이루어진다.
items.problem: (1) 'human creations' (things created) is rendered '인간의 창조' (the act of creating), while the card for 'creations' says 창조물. (2) 'not physical' is rendered '눈에 보이지 않는' (invisible), but 'not physical' means having no material form, and written language, for example, is visible. (3) The term is inconsistent: #2 uses the standard sociology term '물질문화', while #5–#7 use '비물질적 문화' / '비물질적인 문화' instead of the paired term '비물질문화'.
items.correction: #5: '대조적으로 비물질문화는 물리적 형태가 없는 인간의 창조물로 이루어진다.' #6: '비물질문화의 예로는 가치관과 관습이 있다.' #7: '… 또한 비물질문화의 일부이다.'

items.locator: readingSentences[1] (reading-109-s002) korean and readingSentences[2] (reading-109-s003) korean; mirrored in pr109-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 한가지 예로 직업을 가질 수도 있지만, 도시 생활은 흔히 돈이 많이 들기에, 급료가 높은 직업이 아니면 많은 것을 향유할 여유가 없을 것이다. / 더구나 대중 교통은 때때로 혼잡하고 지저분한데, 특히 출퇴근 시간에 그러하다.
items.problem: (1) '한가지' written without a space is a different word (한가지 = 'the same'). The count phrase needs a space: '한 가지'. (2) 'For one thing' introduces the first of several drawbacks (the passage continues with 'What is more' and 'Last of all'), so '우선/첫째로' fits better than '한 가지 예로' (as one example). (3) 'afford many things' means being able to pay for things, so '향유할' (enjoy/possess) is off. (4) '대중 교통' should be the single word '대중교통', which the transportation card itself uses.
items.correction: #2: '우선, 직업을 가질 수는 있겠지만, 도시 생활은 흔히 돈이 많이 들기에, 보수가 아주 좋은 직업이 아니면 많은 것을 살 여유가 없을 것이다.' #3: '더구나 대중교통은 때때로 혼잡하고 지저분한데, 특히 출퇴근 시간에 그러하다.'

items.locator: readingSentences[0] (reading-110-s001) korean and readingSentences[3] (reading-110-s004) korean; mirrored in pr110-1.json and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 또 다른 신체적 이점은 얻기에 시간이 더 걸리지만, 노력할 만한 가치가 있는 것들이고 특히 여성들에게는 더 그렇다. / 실질적으로 규칙적인 운동은 뼈의 질량을 높이는 데 도움이 되고 골다공증을 피할 수 있는 가장 좋은 조처라고 말하여진다.
items.problem: #1: the subject is a single benefit ('Another physical benefit … it is') but the Korean uses the plural '것들이고', and 'well worth' loses 'well'. #4: 'actually' is rendered '실질적으로' (substantively) where '실제로' is meant, and '말하여진다' is an awkward literal passive; '~라고 한다' is the natural form.
items.correction: #1: '또 다른 신체적 이점은 얻기까지 시간이 더 걸리지만 충분히 노력할 가치가 있으며, 특히 여성에게 그렇다.' #4: '실제로 규칙적인 운동은 골량을 늘리는 데 도움이 되며, 골다공증을 피하는 가장 좋은 예방책이라고 한다.'

items.locator: readingSentences[1] (reading-110-s002) english + korean; same text in pr110-1.json, both instruction blocks, src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: If done regularly and over a long period of time, exercise can help prevent osteoporosis, a gradual process of bone loss that occurs naturally as people age.
items.problem: The appositive defines osteoporosis as a normal age-related process. The NIH consensus statement says osteoporosis is a skeletal disorder that is 'no longer considered to be a natural part of aging'. The sentence also contradicts itself: it calls a natural process something exercise can prevent. The Korean repeats the error ('나이가 들어감에 따라 자연적으로 발생되는 … 골다공증').
items.correction: EN: 'If done regularly and over a long period of time, exercise can help prevent osteoporosis, a disease of gradual bone loss that becomes more common as people age.' KO: '규칙적으로 오랫동안 꾸준히 하면, 운동은 나이가 들수록 흔해지는, 뼈가 점차 소실되는 질환인 골다공증을 예방하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.' Optional: make #3 'Bone loss can be slowed by regular exercise.' / '뼈 소실은 규칙적인 운동으로 늦출 수 있다.' Removing 'naturally' leaves the card 'naturally' (adv., 자연스럽게, 저절로) with no word in the passage, so replace that card. Regenerate the EN clip (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.locator: readingSentences[1] (reading-110-s002) korean; mirrored in pr110-1.json instruction and src/lib/readingSentences.json
items.original: 규칙적으로 오랫동안 꾸준히 하면, 운동은 나이가 들어감에 따라 자연적으로 발생되는 뼈의 점진적인 손상인 골다공증을 예방할 수 있다.
items.problem: This is a separate problem from the factual one above. (1) 'can help prevent' is rendered '예방할 수 있다', which drops 'help' and overstates the health claim. (2) 'bone loss' (loss of bone mass) is rendered '뼈의 손상' (bone damage), which is a different concept. (3) '발생되는' is an unnecessary passive of the intransitive verb 발생하다.
items.correction: If the EN is fixed per the Medium finding, use that KO. Otherwise: '규칙적으로 오랫동안 꾸준히 하면, 운동은 나이가 들면서 뼈가 점차 소실되는 골다공증을 예방하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.'

items.original: {"word":"workday","lemma":"workday","partOfSpeech":"n.","korean":"근무일","freq":1}  — context sentence: "...to reduce the stress you experience during your [workday]."
items.problem: workday has two senses: (a) the part of a day during which work is done, and (b) a day on which work is done, as opposed to a day off. "during your workday" is sense (a) — 근무 시간, 하루 일과 — and the lesson's own Korean translation of that sentence renders it "일하는 동안 받은 스트레스". The gloss 근무일 is sense (b), the day-as-a-calendar-unit reading, so the card and the lesson's own translation do not match.
items.correction: korean: "근무 시간, 하루 일과 (during your workday 일하는 동안)"

items.locator: readingSentences reading-115-s002 .korean. Also in the pr115-1.json instruction block and its readingSentences s002
items.original: 손은 팔 전체와, 팔은 몸통과 이어져 있고, 몸통은 바닥을 딛은 발이 받쳐 준다.
items.problem: '딛은' is nonstandard Korean. '딛다' is the short form (준말) of '디디다'. Under 표준어 규정 제16항, a short form's conjugation is not accepted before a vowel-initial ending, so the adnominal form must be '디딘'. The English sentence is fine.
items.correction: 손은 팔 전체와, 팔은 몸통과 이어져 있고, 몸통은 바닥을 디딘 발이 받쳐 준다.

items.locator: readingVocabulary card #5 'low' (same card in pr116-1.json). Passage sentence reading-116-s003
items.original: "word": "low", "lemma": "low", "partOfSpeech": "adv.", "korean": "작게 (as low as practical 가능한 한 작게)"
items.problem: The sentence is 'Keep your wireless ringer as low as practical to avoid disturbing others.' Here 'low' is the object complement of 'keep' (keep + object + complement: 'keep the ringer low'). That makes it a predicative adjective meaning quiet or not loud, not an adverb. Korean school grammar drills exactly this point: an object complement must be an adjective, never an adverb. So labelling it 'adv.' and glossing it with the adverb form '작게' teaches the wrong analysis.
items.correction: "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "(소리가) 작은, 낮은 (keep ~ as low as practical ~을 가능한 한 작게 해 두다)"

items.original: {"word":"low","lemma":"low","partOfSpeech":"adv.","korean":"작게 (as low as practical 가능한 한 작게)","freq":1}  — context sentence: "Keep your wireless ringer as low as practical to avoid disturbing others."
items.problem: In the only occurrence of the word in this passage (freq 1), low is the adjective complement of keep — keep + 목적어 + 형용사 ("Keep your wireless ringer ... low") — not an adverb. The Korean gloss 작게 is idiomatic Korean and reads fine, which is why the error is easy to miss, but the adv. tag misdescribes the structure of the sentence the card came from.
items.correction: partOfSpeech: "adj.", korean: "(소리가) 작은, 낮은 (keep ~ as low as practical 가능한 한 작게 해 두다)"

items.original: {"word":"damage","lemma":"damage","partOfSpeech":"n.","korean":"손상, 해","freq":2}  — context sentence: "...always [staring] at computer screens is likely to damage our eyes." (TSV context for this card: "at computer screens is likely to [damage] our eyes.")
items.problem: The sentence this card was built from uses damage as a transitive verb — "is likely to damage our eyes" (passage sentence 2, whose own Korean line reads "눈이 상하기 쉬우므로"). The card tags it n. and glosses it with noun-only Korean (손상, 해), which cannot be substituted into the to-infinitive: a learner gets "우리 눈을 손상". The noun occurrence does exist (sentence 3, "can also cause damage to our backs"), but that one is already glossed on the neighbouring card — "cause v. 일으키다 (cause damage 해를 끼치다)" — so the deck spends this slot duplicating the noun sense and leaves the verb use, which is the word's first and more prominent appearance, unglossed.
items.correction: partOfSpeech: "v.", korean: "손상시키다, 해치다 (cause damage 해를 끼치다)"

items.locator: readingSentences reading-120-s003 .korean. Also in the pr120-1.json instruction block
items.original: 17세기쯤에 갈릴레오와 파스칼을 포함한 일부 천재들이 더 좋은 시계에 대한 이론을 만들었지만 그것을 만드는데는 실패했다.
items.problem: (1) Spacing error: '만드는데는' should be '만드는 데는', because '데' is a dependent noun and takes a space. (2) The English 'By the 17th century ... had theorized' (past perfect with 'by') means 'by the time of / up to the 17th century'. '17세기쯤에' ('around the 17th century') loses that. (3) '이론을 만들었지만 ... 만드는 데는' repeats 만들다 awkwardly.
items.correction: 17세기 무렵까지 갈릴레오와 파스칼을 비롯한 몇몇 천재들이 더 나은 시계에 대한 이론을 세웠지만, 실제로 만드는 데는 실패했다.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-121-s002 korean, pr121.json and pr121-1.json; pr121-1.json instruction block
items.original: "다른 일을 하는데 에너지를 소모하지 않으면 어떤 손상도 더 빨리 치유될 수 있다."
items.problem: This is a Korean spacing error. 데 here is the dependent noun meaning '일/것' (using energy on doing other things), so it must be written separately: 하는 데. Written as '하는데', it reads as the connective ending -는데.
items.correction: "다른 일을 하는 데 에너지를 소모하지 않으면 어떤 손상이든 더 빨리 치유될 수 있다." The required fix is the spacing. 어떤 손상이든 is optional and reads more naturally with a positive verb.

items.locator: reading-123-s001 and reading-123-s002 (english + korean), pr123.json and pr123-1.json
items.original: "Television is partly blamed for a sharp slide in traditional learning." / "Since television became nearly universal in the early 1960s, average scores for high school students taking the Scholastic Aptitude test, the broadest measure of academic ability, have declined from 478 to 424 on the verbal exam"
items.problem: This is an early-1980s news text, but it is written in the present tense and present perfect with no end date. A 2026 reader will take it that scores have been falling from the 1960s until now and that the 'Scholastic Aptitude Test' with a 'verbal exam' still exists. The figures stop at 1980. The test was renamed in 1990, its scores were recentered in 1995, and the verbal section was replaced in 2005. Other outdated passages were given a time anchor in the 09-17 fixes (R-45: pr122, pr128), but this one was not.
items.correction: Anchor it in time, e.g. S1 "In the early 1980s, television was partly blamed for a sharp slide in traditional learning." S2 "Between the early 1960s, when television became nearly universal, and 1980, average scores for high school students taking the Scholastic Aptitude Test, then the broadest measure of academic ability, declined from 478 to 424 on the verbal exam and from 502 to 466 in mathematics." KO: "1980년대 초 텔레비전은 전통적인 학습 능력이 급격히 떨어진 원인 가운데 하나로 지목되었다." / "텔레비전이 거의 모든 가정에 보급된 1960년대 초부터 1980년까지 ... 떨어졌다." Regenerate the speech clips for the changed English sentences.

items.locator: reading-123-s002 english, pr123.json and pr123-1.json (and the pr123.json instruction block)
items.original: "taking the Scholastic Aptitude test, the broadest measure"
items.problem: This is the proper name of the exam, so every word is capitalized ("Scholastic Aptitude Test"). The lower-case "test" is inconsistent with "Scholastic Aptitude".
items.correction: "taking the Scholastic Aptitude Test, ...". Fold this into the same edit as the two pr123 findings above, since regenerating the clip is needed anyway.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-123-s002, english + korean, in both content/lessons/reading/pr123.json and pr123-1.json; also the instruction block of pr123.json (EN) and pr123-1.json (KO)
items.original: EN: "from 503 to 466 in mathematics" / KO: "수학에서 503점에서 466점으로 떨어졌다"
items.problem: The 1963 starting value of the SAT mathematics average is wrong. The College Board average cited at the time was 502 (verbal 478 → 424 and math 502 → 466, 1963 to 1980). The verbal figures and the 466 are correct. The math starting point is off by one in both the English and the Korean.
items.correction: EN: "...and from 502 to 466 in mathematics." / KO: "...수학에서 502점에서 466점으로 떨어졌다." Apply to readingSentences in pr123.json and pr123-1.json and to both instruction blocks. The English text changes, so regenerate its speech clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.locator: reading-124-s001 english + korean, pr124.json and pr124-1.json
items.original: EN: "according to a new study, they do a lot more than give shade." / KO: "한 새로운 연구에 따르면"
items.problem: The study behind this passage is Kuo & Sullivan's Chicago public-housing vegetation and crime study, published in 2001. Calling it "a new study" in 2026 is inaccurate.
items.correction: EN "according to one study" (or "a 2001 study"); KO "한 연구에 따르면" (or "2001년의 한 연구에 따르면"). Regenerate the clip if the English changes.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] id reading-124-s005 korean, pr124.json and pr124-1.json; also the pr124-1.json instruction block
items.original: "푸른 나무들은 이웃사람들을 자연스럽게 모일 수 있는 곳을 만들고, 궁극적으로 공동체 내에 보다 강한 유대를 만들어 낸다."
items.problem: The Korean is ungrammatical. '이웃사람들을 ... 모일 수 있는 곳' takes the object particle 을, but 이웃 사람들 is the subject of 모일 수 있는, so it needs 이.
items.correction: "초목은 이웃 사람들이 자연스럽게 모일 수 있는 곳을 만들고, 궁극적으로 공동체 내에 보다 강한 유대를 만들어 낸다." (Keep 푸른 나무들은 if preferred. The required fix is 을 → 이.) Apply to both files and the -1 instruction block.

items.locator: menuLabel of pr126-1: content/lessons/reading/pr126-1.json line 9 and content/courses/reading.json line 3572
items.original: "menuLabel": "[ pr 126-1 ]"
items.problem: There is a stray space inside the id. Every other entry is "[ <id> ]" (e.g. "[ pr125-1 ]"). Per the map it is visible only in <meta name="description"> of /reading/pr126-1.
items.correction: "menuLabel": "[ pr126-1 ]" in both files.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] id reading-128-s005 korean, pr128.json and pr128-1.json; pr128-1.json instruction block
items.original: "이 격차는 2005년 이전에는 좁혀지지 않을 것으로 예상되었다."
items.problem: The English is "This gap was not expected to close before 2005". To close a gap means it is eliminated (해소되다/메워지다). 좁혀지다 means it narrows. The Korean therefore says the gap would not even narrow before 2005, which is a stronger claim than the English. The 09-17 fix note R-45 itself describes the intended meaning as "2005년 전 해소 안 될 것".
items.correction: "이 격차는 2005년 이전에는 해소되지 않을 것으로 예상되었다." Apply to both files and the -1 instruction block.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] id reading-130-s002 korean, pr130.json and pr130-1.json; pr130-1.json instruction block
items.original: "일을 하면 휴일이 왔을 때 그 휴일이 훨씬 더 즐겁다는 것이다."
items.problem: The English sentence says "it makes holidays more delicious", with no 'much'. The Korean adds the intensifier 훨씬, apparently carried over from Russell's original 'much more delicious', which was edited out of the English. The Step 4 1:1 pairing then shows a word that the English does not have.
items.correction: "일을 하면 휴일이 왔을 때 그 휴일이 더 즐겁다는 것이다." This keeps the English as is and needs no clip regeneration. Apply to both files and the -1 instruction block.

items.original: "word": "because", "lemma": "because", "partOfSpeech": "adv.", "korean": "(because of) ~ 때문에"
items.problem: In 'because of their false belief', 'because of' is a two-word (phrasal) preposition taking a noun phrase. Korean learners are taught 'because (접속사) + 절 / because of (전치사) + 명사'. Labelling 'because' as adv. matches neither that convention nor this course's own practice: pr131's 'because' card is conj., and other phrasal/prepositional uses in the course are tagged prep. (despite, during, regarding).
items.correction: word 'because of' (or keep 'because'), partOfSpeech 'prep.', korean '(because of + 명사) ~ 때문에'. Mirror in pr132-1.json.

items.original: {"word":"because","lemma":"because","partOfSpeech":"adv.","korean":"(because of) ~ 때문에","freq":1}
items.problem: In this passage the word appears only inside "...dialect differentiation because of their false belief that...", i.e. as part of the complex preposition "because of", which takes a noun phrase. It is not an adverb. The gloss text itself names "(because of)", so the Korean is right and only the badge is wrong. The same dataset tags plain "because" correctly as conj. in pr131 (TSV line 1833), so the card grid shows the same word with two different and one wrong label.
items.correction: "partOfSpeech":"prep.", "korean":"(because of + 명사(구)) ~ 때문에 (cf. because + 절)"

items.locator: readingSentences reading-134-s005 korean (and the pr134-1.json instruction block)
items.original: 그러나 우주의 모든 존재들처럼, 우리는 속도의 한계, 초당 30만km인 광속의 한계에 직면해 있다.
items.problem: The EN says 'about 300,000 kilometers per second'. The KO leaves out 'about' (약) and so states an approximate figure as exact. The real value is 299,792.458 km/s.
items.correction: 그러나 우주의 모든 존재들처럼, 우리도 속도의 한계, 즉 초당 약 30만 km인 광속이라는 한계에 직면해 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-134-s006 korean (and the same text in the pr134-1.json instruction block)
items.original: 오늘날 우리의 우주선은 광속 1%이하만 가능하다.
items.problem: The EN is 'less than one percent of the speed of light', which means 1% 미만, but the KO says '1%이하' (1% or less). The Korean sentence is also incomplete: it does not say what is 'possible' (the speed the ships can reach), and it is missing '의' and a space.
items.correction: 오늘날 우리의 우주선은 광속의 1%에도 못 미치는 속도밖에 내지 못한다. (Update the pr134-1 instruction text too, since it must equal the joined KO sentences.)

items.locator: readingVocabulary card 'care' (card #08); first occurrence in s001
items.original: "word": "care", "lemma": "care", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "(care for) 돌보다", "freq": 2 — first occurrence: "how to take care of their water supply"
items.problem: The card counts two occurrences with different parts of speech. In 'take care of their water supply' care is a NOUN (take care of = 관리하다/돌보다). In 'how to better care for their farms' it is a verb. The card shows only 'v. (care for)', and the QA context dump anchors it to the noun use.
items.correction: korean: '(care for) 돌보다 (v.); take care of ~을 관리하다·돌보다 (n.)'. Or keep v. but gloss both phrases. Mirror in pr137-1.json.

items.original: "word": "hiding", "lemma": "hiding", "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "숨는 (hiding place 숨는 곳)"
items.problem: In 'the best hiding place' the word 'hiding' is a gerund used as a noun modifier ('a place for hiding'; 'hiding place' is a compound noun). It is not an adjective or present participle. Korean school grammar explicitly contrasts 동명사 (a sleeping bag / a hiding place = 용도) with 현재분사 (a sleeping baby). Tagging it adj. with '숨는' teaches the wrong side of that contrast.
items.correction: partOfSpeech 'n.' (동명사), korean '숨기, 숨는 것 (hiding place 숨을 곳, 은신처)'. Mirror in pr138-1.json.

items.original: "word": "demands", "lemma": "demand", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "요구", "freq": 2 — first occurrence: "The social order demands unity and widespread agreement, both characteristics that are destructive to creativity."
items.problem: 'demands' occurs twice with two parts of speech. In s005 it is the main VERB ('The social order demands unity' = 요구한다). In s006 it is a noun ('the demands of society'). The card counts both (freq=2) but shows only 'n. 요구'. The QA context dump anchors it to the verb use in s005. A learner who sees 'n. 요구' can misparse s005 as a noun phrase 'social order demands' with no main verb. Finding the main verb is the key parsing skill for this sentence.
items.correction: Keep the card, but gloss both uses, e.g. partOfSpeech 'v./n.', korean '요구하다 (s5); 요구 (the demands of society, s6)'. Alternatively make it 'v. 요구하다' anchored to s005. Mirror the change in pr139-1.json.

items.original: {"word":"demands","lemma":"demand","partOfSpeech":"n.","korean":"요구","freq":2}
items.problem: "demands" occurs twice in the passage and the card teaches only the second, easier one. The first occurrence is the main VERB of the passage's thesis sentence - "The social order demands unity and widespread agreement, both characteristics that are destructive to creativity." - which the lesson itself translates "사회 질서는 통일성과 폭넓은 합의를 요구하는데" (reading-139-s005). The second is the noun in "conflict between the demands of society" (reading-139-s006, KO "사회의 요구"). The card tags n. and glosses the noun 요구 only; freq=2 asserts it covers both. The audit dump pairs this very card with the verb sentence, so the tag contradicts the sentence it was extracted from.
items.correction: Cover the verb sense that carries the thesis sentence, e.g. "partOfSpeech":"v.", "korean":"요구하다 (The social order demands ~ 사회 질서는 ~을 요구한다) / n. 요구" - or at minimum "v./n." with both glosses.

items.locator: reading-140-s001 (`readingSentences[0].english`) in pr140.json and pr140-1.json; it is the context sentence printed on reading-vocab-context.tsv lines 1952, 1953, 1954, 1955, 1957, 1958 and 1959 (7 of the 10 cards in this lesson)
items.original: Recognizing the healing power of humor, many hospitals are starting to take laughing matter seriously.
items.problem: "laughing matter" is a singular countable noun and cannot stand bare in English. It needs a determiner (a laughing matter) or must be plural (laughing matters). As written, "take laughing matter seriously" is ungrammatical. Dictionaries record the expression only in the determined idiom "no laughing matter" / "be no laughing matter"; the bare singular is not an attested pattern. I found this while checking the card on line 1953, and it matters for that card specifically: the card teaches "laughing matter 웃을 일" as a phrase, but the only sentence the learner ever sees it in is a sentence where the phrase is used incorrectly, so the learner has no correct model to copy. It also sits in the passage's thesis sentence, which is the one sentence of this lesson learners shadow and memorise, and it is the context for 7 of the lesson's 10 vocabulary cards.
items.correction: "Recognizing the healing power of humor, many hospitals are starting to take laughing matters seriously." (plural — preserves the intended play on "no laughing matter" and needs no other change; the existing Korean translation 「유머의 치유력을 인정한 많은 병원이 웃음을 진지하게 받아들이기 시작했다」 still fits). Apply the same fix to pr140-1.json. IMPORTANT per AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md: this edits English text, so the Azure Ava clip keyed on the old text hash disappears — run `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs` in the same task, and re-check the seven TSV context strings, which are generated from this sentence.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 1953 — card word "laughing"; source entry readingVocabulary[] {"word":"laughing"} in pr140.json AND the paired variant pr140-1.json (both carry the identical gloss)
items.original: laughing	adj.	웃기는 (laughing matter 웃을 일)	many hospitals are starting to take [laughing] matter seriously.
items.problem: The headword gloss 웃기는 is wrong. 웃기는 means "funny / amusing", which is the meaning of funny or amusing, not of laughing. As an adjective, laughing means "that laughs, or that appears to laugh" — 웃는, 웃고 있는 (a laughing child = 웃고 있는 아이). It never means "funny": a funny movie is not *a laughing movie. The parenthetical (laughing matter 웃을 일) is correct for the phrase, but it is the primary gloss 웃기는 that the learner reads first and memorises, and the card's own context sentence gives the learner no way to notice the difference, because in "laughing matter" the word is doing phrase duty, not describing anything as funny. This is exactly the confusion Korean learners already make between the -ing form of a verb of reaction (laughing/boring/interesting) and its cause-vs-experiencer sense.
items.correction: Change korean to "웃는, 웃음의 (laughing matter 웃어넘길 일)". If you prefer to keep the card focused on the phrase, "(laughing matter 웃어넘길 일, 가벼운 일)" alone is safer than any gloss containing 웃기는. Note that the English `word` field is not being changed, so no Azure Ava clip is affected by this fix. The same one-line change must be made in pr140-1.json, which carries the identical entry.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-140-s001 english (also blocks[instruction]); cards 'laughing' and 'matter' quote the same phrase
items.original: Recognizing the healing power of humor, many hospitals are starting to take laughing matter seriously.
items.problem: 'laughing matter' is a countable noun phrase ('a laughing matter', 'no laughing matter', 'laughing matters'). A bare singular 'take laughing matter seriously' is unidiomatic, and native readers stumble on it. The intended pun on 'no laughing matter' works with the plural.
items.correction: ...many hospitals are starting to take laughing matters seriously. (or '...to take laughter seriously'). The card glosses '(laughing matter 웃을 일)' stay valid. Changing the English removes the sentence's voice clip, so regenerate it in the same change with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 2023 — card word "consumer-driven"; source entry readingVocabulary[] {"word":"consumer-driven"} in pr145.json AND the paired variant pr145-1.json (both carry the identical gloss)
items.original: consumer-driven	adj.	소비가 이끄는	Our society is a [consumer-driven] culture.
items.problem: The gloss renders the compound as if the first element were "consumption" (소비), not "consumer" (소비자). consumer-driven means 소비자가 주도하는 / 소비자 주도의; 소비가 이끄는 is the gloss for consumption-driven or consumption-led. The card's whole teaching value is that it is a transparent compound the learner can take apart, and taking it apart is exactly what this gloss breaks. It is worse here than it would be elsewhere because the passage turns on the consumer/consume pair two sentences later — reading-145-s002 is "What drives the consumer to consume?" — so the learner meets consumer as a person in the passage while the card has just told them the same morpheme means 소비. (The lesson's own Korean translation of s001 repeats the same 소비가 이끄는; only the card is in my scope, but the translation has the same slip.)
items.correction: Change korean to "소비자가 주도하는, 소비자 중심의". English text is untouched, so no audio clip is affected. Apply the same change in pr145-1.json.

items.original: "korean": "더 쉬운 (easy 의 비교급)"
items.problem: There is a stray space between the Latin headword and the Korean particle 의. Korean particles attach directly to the preceding word with no space, including after a Latin-script word. The repository's own convention confirms this is an error rather than a house style: of the 28 comparative glosses across content/lessons/reading/, 24 are written correctly without the space (e.g. pr154 "더 질긴 (strong의 비교급)", TSV line 2147, in this same review batch), and only two lesson pairs carry the stray space — pr151/pr151-1 ("easy 의") and pr170/pr170-1 ("clean 의").
items.correction: "더 쉬운 (easy의 비교급)". Apply to pr151.json and pr151-1.json. The same one-character fix applies to pr170.json and pr170-1.json ("clean 의 비교급" → "clean의 비교급"), which are outside my line range but share the defect. Korean-only edit, so no audio impact.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-153-s002 korean (also pr153-1 KO block)
items.original: 즐겁거나 슬플 수도, 흥분시키거나 안도시킬 수도 있는, 이런 아름다운 소리는 계획하고 함께 작업한 결과이다.
items.problem: 'relaxing' means soothing or calming (편안하게 해 주는), not 'relieving someone from worry' (안도시키다). The contrast word 'But' at the start of the sentence is also missing from the Korean.
items.correction: 그러나 즐겁거나 슬플 수도, 신나거나 편안할 수도 있는 이 아름다운 소리는 계획하고 함께 작업한 결과이다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-154-s005 and reading-154-s008 korean (also pr154-1 KO block)
items.original: 가지는 쪄지고, 삶아지고, 그리고 나서 여러 번 씻겨지면서 불순물들이 제거되게 된다. / 이것은 사람들이 매일매일 직면하는 어려움들과 고난들을 이겨내면서 좀 더 단련되어지고 현명해지는 것과 유사하다.
items.problem: '씻겨지면서' and '단련되어지고' are double passives (씻기다+어지다, 단련되다+어지다), which are non-standard in Korean, and '제거되게 된다' is redundant. The meaning is correct.
items.correction: '…여러 번 씻기면서 불순물이 제거된다.' / '…좀 더 단련되고 현명해지는 것과 비슷하다.'

items.original: 우리는 외국어를 배우거나 물리학 증명을 하는 것과 같은 형식적인 기술을 교과서를 읽고 추상적인 원리를 이해함으로써가 아니라, 해당 분야의 문제를 실제로 해결함으로써 배운다. / card formal: "형식적인, 체계적인"
items.problem: 'formal skills' here means skills taught through formal instruction, like school subjects (a foreign language, physics). In everyday Korean '형식적인' mostly means perfunctory or just for show (겉치레의), so '형식적인 기술' can read as 'superficial skills'. The card gives 형식적인 as its first gloss.
items.correction: Sentence: '…같은 체계적인(정규 교육으로 배우는) 기술을…'. Card: '(교육이) 정규의, 체계적인'.

items.original: But even the prescient coauthor of the Federalist Papers might be amazed at the abundant fulfillment of his vision by Americans of the present day.
items.problem: The source (TIME, 1978) says 'Americans of the late 1970s'. The edited text changes this to 'the present day'. As a result, a 1978 editorial judgment is presented as a statement about today, and the next sentence reads as current fact: 'The nation has entered a period of factionalism'. The Korean '현재의 미국인' repeats the error.
items.correction: If the passage is kept after legal review, restore the time frame, e.g. 'by Americans of the late 1970s' / '1970년대 후반의 미국인들', or add a source line (TIME, 1978). Regenerate the clip if the English changes.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-157-s004 korean (also pr157-1 KO block)
items.original: 그 나라는 수많은 부분들의 끊임없는 요구로 사회의 더 큰 바람들을 들을수 없는 당파주의의 시기로 접어들었다.
items.problem: There is a spacing error: '들을수' should be '들을 수'. Also, 'can scarcely be heard' means 'can hardly be heard' (거의 들리지 않는), and the Korean flattens it to a plain 'cannot hear'.
items.correction: 그 나라는 수많은 집단들의 끈질긴 아우성 때문에 사회 전체의 더 큰 바람은 거의 들리지 않는 당파주의의 시기에 접어들었다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-158-s005 korean (also pr158-1 KO block)
items.original: 그러나, 돌은 행동의 다른 과정들을 구분할 수 없기에 이런 종류의 선택에 직면하지 않는다.
items.problem: 'courses of action' is a set phrase meaning 'possible ways of acting / options'. It is not 'processes of an action'. The literal 행동의 다른 과정들 teaches a wrong meaning for a common collocation, and it breaks the link to 'options' in s003.
items.correction: 그러나 돌은 서로 다른 행동 방식(행동 방침)을 구별할 수 없기 때문에 이런 종류의 선택에 직면하지 않는다.

items.original: 대조적으로, 당신의 친구는 부정적인 반응을 가졌을지도 모르며, 격렬한 폭풍우 동안에 거친 바다를 항해했던 게 생각나 똑같은 것(그림)이 그의 마음에 두려움을 가져온다고 말했을지도 모른다.
items.problem: 'the same things' (plural) refers to 'the dark colors and enormous waves' from s002, but the gloss '(그림)' names the painting instead. The speech level also changes within the passage: s001 '있나요?' and s002 '있겠죠.' are polite, while s003 '모른다.' is plain.
items.correction: 반면에 당신의 친구는 부정적인 반응을 보이며, 격렬한 폭풍우 속에서 거친 바다를 항해했던 기억이 떠올라 똑같은 것들(어두운 색과 거대한 파도)이 마음에 두려움을 불러일으켰다고 말했을지도 모릅니다. Use the same polite ending in s001-s003.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-160-s003 korean (also pr160-1 KO block)
items.original: 토끼는 어린나무의 겨울눈을 먹고 사는데, 더 깊이 얼어붙은 눈을 밟고 올라서면 더 많은 눈에 닿을 수 있다.
items.problem: English: 'the deeper icy snow helps the animal to reach more buds'. The Korean has two problems. (1) 'deeper' describes how deep the snow is, but '더 깊이 얼어붙은 눈' means 'snow frozen more deeply'. (2) In a passage about snow (눈), '더 많은 눈에 닿을 수 있다' uses 눈 in the sense of 'bud' in the same clause as 눈 'snow'. A learner naturally reads it as 'can reach more snow', which hides the key point of the passage: why deep snow helps the rabbit.
items.correction: 토끼는 어린나무의 겨울눈을 먹고 사는데, 눈이 더 깊이 쌓여 얼어 있으면 그 위에 올라서서 더 많은 겨울눈(새싹)에 닿을 수 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences[2], id "reading-160-s003" (korean field). Backs cards at TSV lines 2233 'young' and 2234 'deeper'.
items.original: EN: "Since it feeds on the winter buds of young trees, the deeper icy snow helps the animal to reach more buds."  KO: "토끼는 어린나무의 겨울눈을 먹고 사는데, 더 깊이 얼어붙은 눈을 밟고 올라서면 더 많은 눈에 닿을 수 있다."
items.problem: The Korean uses the bare noun 눈 twice in the same clause with two different referents. The first ("더 깊이 얼어붙은 눈") is snow; the second ("더 많은 눈에 닿을 수 있다") is supposed to be buds, rendering the English "reach more buds". Because the snow sense was just established four words earlier, and because the whole lesson is about deep snow (the word 눈=snow appears 5 times in this passage per the card's freq field), the second 눈 reads as snow on first pass — i.e. "can touch more snow", which is meaningless. The lesson itself already fixes the equivalence 'winter buds' = 겨울눈 earlier in the very same sentence, so the abbreviation to bare 눈 is an internal inconsistency, not a translation choice.
items.correction: Change the tail of the Korean to "... 더 많은 겨울눈에 닿을 수 있다." (or "... 더 많은 새싹에 닿을 수 있다."). Apply the identical edit to the same sentence id in pr160-1.json, which carries the byte-identical string. This edits Korean only, so the English sentence hash is unchanged and no Azure Ava clip is lost.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr161.json readingSentences #1 (reading-161-s001), the only entry; same in pr161-1.json
items.original: All we really need to know about how to live and what to do, we learned in kindergarten, including "share everything," "play fair," and "say you're sorry when you hurt somebody." Sadly, however, we don't apply these rules to our family life, work or government when we become adults.
items.problem: Two English sentences, and a Korean text of three sentences, are stored as one sentence entry. As a result the lesson shows '1개 핵심 문장'. The Step 1 and Step 4 '1:1 직독직해' pairs the whole passage with the whole translation, so there is nothing to match sentence by sentence. The whole passage becomes one sentence clip, and there is only 1 cloze item. The Step 3 pronunciation test uses S[0], so it asks the learner to read the whole 51-word passage in one breath, which makes speech recognition cut-offs and low scores likely.
items.correction: Split into two entries. EN1 = 'All we really need to know about how to live and what to do, we learned in kindergarten, including "share everything," "play fair," and "say you're sorry when you hurt somebody."' / KO1 = '우리가 어떻게 살아야 할지 … 미안하다고 말하라.” 등이 있다.' EN2 = 'Sadly, however, we don't apply these rules to our family life, work or government when we become adults.' / KO2 = '그러나 슬프게도, 우리가 어른이 되었을 때 우리는 이 규칙들을 가족 생활과 일, 정부에 적용하지 않는다.' Do the same in pr161-1.json and regenerate clips (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr164.json readingSentences #1-#2 (reading-164-s001/s002) + card 'administration'; same in pr164-1.json
items.original: Consumer advocates call for additional testing of crops and mandatory labeling of genetically engineered products. Administration officials say that it is unnecessary, and the food industry has argued that it would unfairly stigmatize bio-tech food.
items.problem: An old U.S. news snippet (the card glosses 'administration' as '(미국) 행정부') is presented in the present tense ('call for', 'say that it is unnecessary'; KO '요구하고 있다'), as if the U.S. government currently opposes mandatory labeling. The U.S. has in fact required bioengineered-food disclosure since the 2016 federal law, with mandatory compliance from January 1, 2022 (National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard).
items.correction: Add a Korean note to the translation, e.g. '※ 2016년 미국 연방법 제정 이전의 논쟁입니다. 미국은 2022년 1월 1일부터 생명공학(유전자 변형) 식품 표시를 의무화했습니다.' Alternatively, change the English to the past tense ('called for … said that it was unnecessary') and regenerate the clips.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 generated from readingSentences #1 (reading-164-s001)
items.original: Consumer advocates call for additional testing of crops and mandatory labeling of genetically engineered products.
items.problem: The blank is 'mandatory' ('…additional testing of crops and _______ labeling of…'). The distractors are 'advocates', 'officials' and one random word from {consumer, additional, labeling, engineered, products, industry, unfairly, stigmatize, bio-tech}. When 'additional' is drawn (about 1 in 9 visits), 'additional labeling of genetically engineered products' is also grammatical and makes sense, but it is marked wrong.
items.correction: Exclude adjectives already in the same sentence from the distractors (or exclude 'additional' for this item), or blank a word with no competing fillers.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr165.json readingSentences #4 english (reading-165-s004); same in pr165-1.json
items.original: Since the questions on the objective test are presented in true―false or multiple choice form, the student may be encouraged to guess answers for which he has no accurate knowledge.
items.problem: 'true―false' uses U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR, a legacy character that displays like a long dash, where a hyphen is needed. The compound adjective should be 'true-false' (or 'true/false'), and 'multiple choice' used before a noun is normally hyphenated. The same token 'true―false' is also in the cloze distractor pool: item 1 picks 3 of {university, true―false, encouraged, analytical}, so it appears as an option about 75% of the time.
items.correction: '…are presented in true-false or multiple-choice form, …' then regenerate the clip (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr166.json readingSentences #6 korean (reading-166-s006); same in pr166-1.json readingSentences and the instruction block
items.original: 물체들의 본질적인 형태가 원근법으로, 다시 말해 인간의 눈에 보이는 대로 그리기 위해 수학이 사용되었다.
items.problem: The Korean particle is wrong. '형태' is the object of '그리기' (to portray the form), so it needs '를', not the subject marker '가'. As written, the sentence does not parse.
items.correction: 물체들의 본질적인 형태를 원근법으로, 다시 말해 인간의 눈에 보이는 대로 그리기 위해 수학이 사용되었다. (This is a Korean-only change, so no English clip is affected. Also update the pr166-1.json instruction block, which must equal the joined KO.)

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2 generated from readingSentences #2... actually #3 (reading-166-s003), via generateClozeItems (src/lib/readingUtils.ts:691-761)
items.original: Prior to the Renaissance, objects in paintings were flat and symbolic rather than real in appearance.
items.problem: The cloze blanks 'paintings' ('objects in _______ were flat…'). The distractors are the two words of equal length (different, essential) plus one random pick from 11 words one letter longer or shorter, and that pool includes 'painting'. 'objects in painting were flat and symbolic' is also correct English (painting as the art form), yet only 'paintings' is accepted. This happens on about 1 in 11 visits. It is the same generator weakness recorded in maps/reading.md §12-3 (inflection distractors).
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, drop distractors that share a stem with the target (e.g. w.startsWith(target.toLowerCase().replace(/s$/, '')) or vice versa), or keep a per-lesson exclusion list for this item.

items.original: Children must be taught their native tongue and the necessary training takes a long time. | Language is not something that is inherited; it is an art that can be passed on from one generation to the next only by intensive education.
items.problem: The passage states as fact that children must be taught their native language, that language passes between generations 'only by intensive education', and (in #2) that 'there is nothing automatic about language'. That is an old view. Modern research on first-language learning finds that children pick up their native language from exposure and interaction, without explicit teaching. Only a small share of vocabulary growth comes from direct instruction, and the capacity to learn language is biologically based. The claim that a particular language is not inherited is true, but 'only by intensive education' is wrong: languages pass fully between generations in communities with no schooling at all. There is no note or framing, so learners take the claim as settled.
items.correction: Option A, keep the English and add a Korean note on the Step 4/-1 translation: '※ 옛 관점의 글입니다. 현대 언어학에서는 아이들이 모국어를 따로 배우지 않아도 주변 말에 노출되며 스스로 습득한다고 봅니다. 특정 언어는 물려받지 않지만, 언어를 배우는 능력은 타고납니다.' Option B, rewrite #3/#4, e.g. 'Children learn their native tongue from the people around them, and the process takes years.' / 'Language is not something that is inherited; it is passed on from one generation to the next through constant exposure and use.' Update the KO rows and pr167-1.json to match, and regenerate the clips with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 generated from readingSentences #1 (reading-167-s001)
items.original: Language is so much a part of our daily activities that some of us may come to look upon it as a more or less automatic and natural act like breathing or winking.
items.problem: The blank is 'automatic' ('a more or less _______ and natural act like breathing or winking'). The distractors are 3 of {breathing, necessary, something, inherited, intensive, education}, and in about 80% of visits at least one of 'necessary' or 'inherited' is shown. Both give a grammatical sentence that makes sense ('a more or less necessary/inherited and natural act like breathing'). Only the next sentence ('nothing automatic about language') points to the key.
items.correction: Blank a different word in this sentence, or exclude 'necessary' and 'inherited' from this item's distractors.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr168.json readingSentences #2 english (reading-168-s002); same in pr168-1.json
items.original: …had a significant impact on the prevalence of objects that emphasized design over styling― and the other way round.
items.problem: A legacy U+2015 horizontal bar is used as a dash, stuck to the word before it with a space only after it ('styling― and'). This is a PDF/encoding leftover, not standard punctuation.
items.correction: '…that emphasized design over styling—and the other way round.' (em dash, no spaces) or '… styling – and the other way round.' Then regenerate the clip.

items.original: The old Sumerian cuneiform could not be used to write normal prose but was a mere telegraphic shorthand, whose vocabulary was restricted to names, numerals and units of measure.
items.problem: The sentence cuts off the source list. Jared Diamond's original reads 'names, numerals, units of measure, words for objects counted, and a few adjectives'. Once shortened, the claim is factually wrong: the earliest cuneiform tablets were mostly administrative records with signs for the goods counted (grain, sheep, beer, textiles, workers), about 1,100 ideographic signs besides the numerals. The KO repeats the error ('이름과 숫자와 측정 단위만 담을 수 있는').
items.correction: EN: '…whose vocabulary was restricted to names, numerals, units of measure, words for the objects counted, and a few adjectives.' KO: '그것은 이름, 숫자, 측정 단위, 세는 물건을 가리키는 말과 몇몇 형용사만 담을 수 있는, 전보문 같은 속기에 불과했다.' Update pr169-1.json too and regenerate the clip. The copyright question stays with R-75.

items.original: #4 People who follow this custom sometimes ask, “Why should we eat with utensils that other people have used? | #5 Our own hands may be cleaner.” They also point out that they know whether their hands are clean and that nobody else uses them.
items.problem: The sentence boundary falls inside a quotation. #4 ends with an open quote, and #5 starts mid-quote and then carries on into a separate sentence. The Step 1 and Step 4 hover/HUD, the 1:1 pairs and the per-sentence audio all show fragments with unbalanced quotation marks (the KO rows have the same split).
items.correction: #4 = 'People who follow this custom sometimes ask, “Why should we eat with utensils that other people have used? Our own hands may be cleaner.”' / KO '이 관습을 따르는 사람들은 때때로 이렇게 묻는다. “왜 다른 사람들이 썼던 식사 도구로 먹어야 하나요? 우리 손이 더 깨끗할 수도 있어요.”'. #5 = 'They also point out that they know whether their hands are clean and that nobody else uses them.' / KO '그들은 또한 자기 손이 깨끗한지는 스스로 알고, 다른 사람은 그 손을 쓰지 않는다는 점을 지적한다.' Update pr170-1.json and regenerate both clips.

items.original: 발의자, 작성자 (author of the amendment 개정안 발의자)
items.problem: In Korean, 발의(자) means formally introducing a bill, which is a legislator's act. Alice Paul drafted the ERA but was not a member of Congress. It was introduced on December 13, 1923 by Rep. Daniel Anthony (House) and Sen. Charles Curtis (Senate). The card's first gloss and its example ('개정안 발의자') therefore suggest a wrong fact. It also disagrees with the sentence translation, which correctly says '작성한'.
items.correction: 작성자, 입안자 (author of the amendment 수정안 작성자)

items.original: {"word":"author","lemma":"author","partOfSpeech":"n.","korean":"발의자, 작성자 (author of the amendment 개정안 발의자)"} — context: "Like many other reformers, Alice Paul, [author] of the Equal Rights Amendment introduced in Congress in 1923, received little honor in her lifetime but has gained considerable fame posthumously."
items.problem: "Author" has no sense meaning 발의자 (the legislator who formally introduces a bill); it means 작성자/저자/입안자. The gloss puts the wrong sense FIRST and then repeats it in the collocation line ("author of the amendment 개정안 발의자"), so the wrong reading is reinforced twice. It is also factually false about this sentence: Alice Paul drafted the Equal Rights Amendment, but it was introduced in Congress in December 1923 by Rep. Daniel R. Anthony Jr. in the House and Sen. Charles Curtis in the Senate — the sentence itself keeps the two roles apart with the separate participle "introduced in Congress in 1923". Three internal contradictions confirm it: (1) the same lesson glosses readingVocabulary[5] "introduced" as "(법안을) 발의하다, 제출하다", so two different words in a one-sentence passage are both taught as 발의; (2) the lesson's own sentence translation, readingSentences[0].korean, renders it "…수정안(Equal Rights Amendment)을 작성한 앨리스 폴" — 작성한, not 발의한; (3) the whole lesson is this single sentence, so this card carries an outsized share of the lesson.
items.correction: Set korean to "작성자, 입안자 (author of the amendment 수정안을 작성한 사람)" — drop 발의자 entirely and leave 발의하다 to the "introduced" card.

items.original: {"word":"congress","lemma":"congress","partOfSpeech":"n.","korean":"(미국) 의회"} — context: "…the Equal Rights Amendment introduced in [Congress] in 1923…"
items.problem: The passage has the capitalized proper noun "Congress", but the card's headword is lowercase "congress", which is a different word-sense — a formal meeting or convention of delegates (the Congress of Vienna, a medical congress). The gloss "(미국) 의회" is correct only for the capitalized form, so headword and gloss do not match each other. The dataset preserves capitals elsewhere when it matters: pr170 readingVocabulary[0] keeps "word":"Western" while lowercasing only the lemma.
items.correction: Set "word":"Congress" (leave lemma and korean unchanged), matching the pr170 "Western" pattern.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 (generated at runtime from reading-173-s001 by generateClozeItems in src/lib/readingUtils.ts)
items.original: Different groups develop ideas in different ways.
items.problem: The generator masks 'develop'. It draws the 3 wrong options at random from the 7 passage words of the same length: produce, members, prosper, whereas, leaders, achieve, results. So 'produce' is offered about 43% of the time (3 in 7). 'Different groups produce ideas in different ways.' is grammatical and sensible, and the next sentence of the passage itself says 'individuals are encouraged to produce imaginative and original ideas'. A learner who picks 'produce' is marked ❌ even though the answer is valid.
items.correction: Keep 'produce' out of this item's options. One way is a per-lesson exclusion list or curated distractors. Another is to change the generator so it never offers a passage word that fits the same slot. A different target word also works, for example mask 'groups' instead.

items.original: 그들은 다른 쾌락을 추구하며, 다른 방식으로 돈을 소비한다.
items.problem: 'seeking different pleasures' here refers to vacations, carpets and a second car. 쾌락 carries a hedonistic or sensual connotation in Korean that the English does not have. The lesson's own card for 'pleasures' correctly gives '즐거움'.
items.correction: 사람들은 저마다 다른 즐거움을 추구하며 서로 다른 방식으로 돈을 쓴다.

items.original: 그들은 아침 식사로 섬유질이 풍부한 빵과 곡류와 같은 음식을 선택하며, 사업상의 약속을 준비하기 위해 점심으로 샐러드를 선택한다.
items.problem: The English is 'They choose foods rich in fiber, such as bread and cereal for breakfast, and salads for lunch to prepare them for business appointments.' The Korean has three problems. (1) 'cereal for breakfast' is breakfast cereal (시리얼), not 곡류 (grains in general). (2) In the passage's list of situations, both the high-fiber breakfast and the lunch salad are the 'business appointment' example, but the Korean ties the purpose to the salad only. (3) 'prepare them for business appointments' means getting themselves ready for the appointments (대비하다), not preparing the appointment itself (약속을 준비하다).
items.correction: 그들은 업무상 약속에 대비하기 위해 아침으로는 빵과 시리얼 같은 섬유질이 풍부한 음식을, 점심으로는 샐러드를 고른다.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2 (generated at runtime from reading-175-s002)
items.original: They have certain ideas about which food will increase their athletic ability, help them lose weight, or put them in the mood for romance.
items.problem: The target word is 'athletic' (8 letters). The wrong options come at random from the 7 eight-letter passage words: patterns, increase, strength, physical, activity, business, romantic. 'physical' is offered about 43% of the time. 'increase their physical ability' is fully grammatical and matches the passage, which later says 'strength for physical activity'. A learner who picks it is graded wrong.
items.correction: Keep 'physical' out of this item's options, or mask a different word in this sentence (for example 'romance' or 'weight').

items.original: 어떤 사람은 들은 다음 말해봄으로써 외국어를 배울 수 있다.
items.problem: 'just by hearing it' ('only by listening') is the point this sentence contrasts with the next one ('Other people have to read it and write it'). The Korean drops 'just' (그저 ~만으로), and it also drops the object 'it', so the contrast is lost. The lesson's card for 'just' teaches '단지, 그저'.
items.correction: 어떤 사람들은 외국어를 그저 듣고 나서 말해 보는 것만으로도 배울 수 있다.

items.original: But ideas about how to punish children differ from culture to culture and family to family.
items.problem: The target is 'culture', and only its first occurrence is masked. The learner sees 'differ from _______ to culture and family to family.', so the answer is printed right after the blank and the item tests nothing. This is the same generator pattern the reading map already records for pr100.
items.correction: When the target occurs twice in the sentence, mask both occurrences or pick another word (for example 'punish' or 'family'). This should be fixed in generateClozeItems for every lesson, not by editing pr177 alone.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-179-s002 .korean (same text in pr179-1.json readingSentences and pr179-1 instruction block)
items.original: 그들은, 사회를 위해 그들이 행하는 것에 가치를 인정해주는 사람들이 거의 없다는 것을 전혀 꺼리지 않고, 가난한 자와 절망적인 사람들을 위해 무보수의 여러 시간 일하는데 헌신하였다.
items.problem: This translation of 'They devoted themselves to hours of unpaid work for the poor and helpless, never minding that few appreciated what they were doing for society.' has three errors. (1) 'helpless' means powerless or with no one to rely on, not 절망적인 (hopeless/desperate). (2) 'never minding' means not caring about something. The verb 꺼리다 means to be reluctant or to avoid, so '~것을 전혀 꺼리지 않고' does not say that. The lesson's own vocabulary card for 'minding' correctly gives '개의치 않다'. (3) '무보수의 여러 시간 일하는데' is ungrammatical Korean.
items.correction: 그들은 사회를 위해 자신들이 하는 일을 알아주는 사람이 거의 없다는 것에 개의치 않고, 가난하고 의지할 데 없는 사람들을 위해 여러 시간씩 무보수로 일하는 데 헌신했다. (Change it in pr179.json and in pr179-1.json, both readingSentences and the instruction block. Only Korean changes, so no audio clip is affected.)

items.original: 예를 들어, 많은 고용주들이 그런 훈련 경험을 가진 가능성 있는 직원을 찾고 있다.
items.problem: 'would-be workers' means people who want to become workers (job seekers or prospective hires). '가능성 있는 직원' reads in Korean as 'promising employees', which is a different meaning. The next sentence ('those seeking a job -- the young and the unskilled') confirms the job-seeker meaning.
items.correction: 예를 들어, 오늘날 많은 고용주들이 훈련 경험이 있는 구직자(취업 희망자)를 찾고 있다.

items.original: 그들은 때때로 일종의 문화적 편견을 지닌 태도에 의해 버림받은 사람처럼 다루어진다.
items.problem: The English says 'They are often treated like outcasts'. 'often' means frequently (자주/흔히). 때때로 means 'sometimes' and weakens the author's claim.
items.correction: 그들은 일종의 문화적 편견 때문에 흔히 버림받은 사람처럼 취급된다.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] reading-181-s005 korean (same text in pr181-1.json blocks[1] instruction)
items.original: Photographs can be changed by computer; photographs are sometimes false. -> 사진은 컴퓨터로 쉽게 변형될 수 있으며, 사진도 때로는 거짓일 수 있다.
items.problem: The Korean adds '쉽게' (easily), which is not in the English. A learner matching words sentence by sentence will look for an 'easily' that is not there.
items.correction: 사진은 컴퓨터로 변형될 수 있으며, 사진도 때로는 거짓이다. (Update pr181-1 blocks[1] instruction text too so it still equals the joined translations.)

items.original: Until recently, people in many parts of the country could have orange juice during only a few months. / Now orange juice is put up in cans, so that it is available regardless of the season.
items.problem: The passage presents canned orange juice as a recent change ('Until recently ... Now'). Canned and frozen-concentrate orange juice became commercially common in the US in the 1940s (the USDA concentrate process dates from 1945, and the first commercial frozen concentrate from 1946). Year-round orange juice was established by the 1950s-60s, so a 2026 learner is told a mid-20th-century change is current. 'The country' is also never named: the original context is the US, but the Korean '전국의 많은 지역 사람들은' reads as if it were Korea.
items.correction: Add framing, e.g. 'In the early 1900s, people in many parts of the United States could have orange juice during only a few months of the year. Later, orange juice was put up in cans, so that it became available regardless of the season.' Update the Korean to match ('1900년대 초에는 미국의 많은 지역 사람들이 1년 중 몇 달 동안만...'). Alternatively, add a note that the text describes the 1940s. Regenerate the Azure clips if the English changes.

items.locator: readingSentences[5] id reading-185-s006 (also inside blocks[1] instruction text of pr185.json)
items.original: In jazz, on the contrary, the performers often improvise their own melodies.
items.problem: 'On the contrary' is used to deny or reverse a statement just made (e.g. 'He wasn't offended; on the contrary, he enjoyed it'). It is not used to contrast two different things. Here the passage compares classical music (composers in control) with jazz (performers improvise), which calls for 'by contrast' or 'in contrast'. Korean learners very often confuse these two markers, and the Korean '반대로' hides the difference, so the model sentence reinforces the error.
items.correction: In jazz, by contrast, the performers often improvise their own melodies. (Korean '반대로 재즈에서는...' can become '이와 달리 재즈에서는...'.) Changing the English removes this sentence's Azure clip, so re-run node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: Observers, on the other hand, are informed and appreciative. They have spent the time and energy to make art meaningful to themselves. / They don't simply exist side by side with art. They are aware of its existence in even the smallest part of their daily life.
items.problem: Each of these rows holds two separate sentences, so the passage has 7 sentences but only 5 rows. The rest of the course segments one sentence per row. As a result, sentence numbering, per-sentence TTS, hover translation and speaking practice treat two sentences as one unit here. The EN and KO rows are still aligned with each other; this is a segmentation inconsistency, not a meaning error.
items.correction: Split s004 into 'Observers, on the other hand, are informed and appreciative.' / '반면 감상자는 아는 것이 많고 감상할 줄 안다.' and 'They have spent the time and energy to make art meaningful to themselves.' / '그들은 예술이 자신에게 의미 있게 되도록 시간과 힘을 들였다.' Split s005 the same way. Apply the same change to pr186-1.json and regenerate the Azure clips for the new sentence texts.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 (generated from reading-193-s001, target 'cream')
items.original: If you ask most children what their favorite treat is, they will answer “Ice cream!” There is nothing like a delicious ice-cream cone on a hot summer day.
items.problem: The masked sentence the learner sees is 'they will answer “Ice _______!” There is nothing like a delicious ice-cream cone...'. The answer 'cream' is still visible in 'ice-cream' in the same text, so the item tests nothing. This is the same pattern the map records for pr100.
items.correction: Choose another target for s001 (e.g. 'favorite' or 'delicious'), or make the generator reject a target that still appears elsewhere in the masked sentence, including inside hyphenated words.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze items 2 and 3 (generated from reading-193-s002 and reading-193-s003; target 'ice-cream' in both)
items.original: Every year Americans eat more than four billion ice-cream cones.
items.problem: generateClozeItems (src/lib/readingUtils.ts:723-747) picks the same target 'ice-cream' for items 2 and 3. Its equal-length distractor group is exactly {delicious, americans, according, suggested}, so 3 of these 4 are shown every time, and 'delicious' appears on about 75% of page loads. 'Every year Americans eat more than four billion delicious cones.' is grammatical and makes sense, and so does '...the delicious cone became famous by accident?'. The passage itself says 'a delicious ice-cream cone', so a learner who picks 'delicious' is marked ❌ although the answer fits the blank. Two of the three items also test the same word.
items.correction: Change the target for s002/s003 (e.g. 'billion' / 'famous'), or make the generator skip a target already used and leave out distractors that sit next to the target anywhere in the passage (here 'delicious' in 'delicious ice-cream cone').

items.locator: reading-198-s002 korean (also pr198-1 instruction block and src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: 결국, 어른은 오랫동안 계속 걸어왔다.
items.problem: Here 'After all' gives the reason: adults already know how to walk, which is why skiing is humbling. It means 따지고 보면 / 어쨌든, not 결국 ('in the end'). With 결국 the Korean reads as a conclusion and breaks the logic. The line-by-line view also teaches learners that 'after all' equals 결국 in exactly the sense where it does not.
items.correction: 따지고 보면 어른은 오랫동안 걸어 왔다. (keep the -1 page and the central copy in sync)

items.locator: reading-198-s002 korean and reading-198-s004 korean (also pr198-1 instruction block and src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: 어딘가로 가기 위해 한 발을 다른 발 앞에 어떻게 두는 가를 알고 있다. / 일어서는데 어려움을 겪고
items.problem: Korean spacing errors. '-는가' is an ending and attaches to the verb, so it should be 두는가를. In '~하는 데 어려움을 겪다', 데 is a dependent noun and takes a space, so it should be 일어서는 데.
items.correction: …어떻게 두는가를 알고 있다. / 일어서는 데 어려움을 겪고

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2 (generated from reading-198-s002, target 'knows')
items.original: After all, an adult has been walking for a long time; he knows where his feet are; he knows how to put one foot in front of the other in order to get somewhere.
items.problem: Only the first 'knows' is masked, so the learner sees 'he _______ where his feet are; he knows how to put one foot...' with the answer printed a few words later. The equal-length distractor group also includes 'feels', which fits the blank ('he feels where his feet are').
items.correction: Use a different target (e.g. 'walking' or 'somewhere'), or skip targets that occur more than once in the sentence.

items.locator: reading-199-s004 korean (also pr199-1 instruction block and src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: 결국 누구의 직감도 늘 옳지는 않은데, 언제 직감을 따르고 언제 무시해야 하는지 어떻게 알 수 있을까?
items.problem: 'After all, no one's instincts are always correct' gives the reason why using instincts takes effort. It means 따지고 보면 / 어쨌든, not 결국 ('in the end'). This is the same mistranslation as pr198 #2.
items.correction: 따지고 보면 누구의 직감도 늘 옳지는 않은데, 언제 직감을 따르고 언제 무시해야 하는지 어떻게 알 수 있을까?

items.locator: reading-200-s004 korean (also pr200-1 instruction block and src/lib/readingSentences.json)
items.original: 내가 정말로 주장하는 것은 성공은 행복의 한 가지 요소에 불과할 수 있으며, 그것을 얻기 위해 다른 모든 요소를 희생했다면 너무나 큰 대가를 치르고 산 것이라는 점이다.
items.problem: 'success can only be one ingredient in happiness' is a firm claim: success cannot be more than one ingredient. '불과할 수 있으며' turns it into a possibility ('may be merely one ingredient') and weakens the author's main thesis.
items.correction: …성공은 행복의 한 가지 요소일 수밖에 없으며 (or: 한 가지 요소에 불과하며), 그것을 얻기 위해 다른 모든 요소를 희생했다면…

items.locator: readingSentences reading-201-s001 and reading-201-s002 KO (same in pr201-1.json readingSentences and instruction block)
items.original: 우리가 “옳다”, “공평하다”, “좋다”, “나쁘다”고 생각하는 것에 맞추어 다른 사람들이 살기를 바라면서 그들에게 우리의 가치를 강요하려고 할 때 부조화가 우리의 관계에 들어온다. / 만약 그들이 우리의 가치를 받아들이지 않는다면, 우리는 짜증을 내게 되고 화가 나게 된다.
items.problem: 'values' here means moral standards (가치관), and the lesson's own card says 'values | 가치관'. The sentence translation uses '우리의 가치', which in Korean more naturally reads as 'our worth', so the translation and the card disagree. s001 also drops 'and so on' (등).
items.correction: s001: '우리가 “옳다”, “공평하다”, “좋다”, “나쁘다” 등으로 여기는 것에 맞춰 다른 사람들이 살기를 바라면서 그들에게 우리의 가치관을 강요하려 할 때 우리의 관계에 불화가 생긴다.' s002: '그들이 우리의 가치관을 받아들이지 않으면, 우리는 짜증이 나고 화가 난다.'

items.locator: readingSentences reading-201-s003 and reading-201-s004 KO (same in pr201-1.json)
items.original: s003: 그러나 우리는 어느 누구도 단지 우리가 그들이 행동해야한다고 생각하는 방식의 기대를 충족시키기 위해서 행동을 바꿀 의무는 없다는 것을 깨달아야 한다. / s004: 사람들은 우리를 방해하거나 화나게 할 수도 있지만 모든 사람이 그들의 행동에 반대하지는 않는다는 사실은 아마 문제가 우리에게 있을 수도 있다는 것을 가리킨다.
items.problem: s003 has a spacing error: '행동해야한다고' should be '행동해야 한다고'. In s004, 'disturb' in this context means 'upset or bother' (the card itself gives '불쾌하게 하다' first), but the sentence translation uses '방해하다'. 'probably' is also weakened to '아마 … 있을 수도 있다' ('might possibly'), which softens the author's claim.
items.correction: s003: '…우리가 생각하는 방식대로 그들이 행동하기를 바라는 기대를 충족시키려고 누구도 변해야 할 의무는 없다는 것을…' (at minimum '행동해야 한다고'). s004: '사람들이 우리를 불쾌하게 하거나 화나게 할 수는 있지만, 모든 사람이 그들의 행동에 반대하는 것은 아니라는 사실은 아마도 문제가 우리에게 있다는 것을 보여 준다.'

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr202.json lines 65-66 and 70-71 (readingSentences[3] and readingSentences[4]); same text inside the instruction block at line 28. Reaches the vocabulary cards at reading-vocab-context.tsv lines 2824 ('discontinued') and 2829 ('lack'), whose context sentences these are.
items.original: A year later the newspaper was discontinued for a while due to a fire. It had to close in 1888 because of lack of money.
items.problem: The passage treats two different newspapers as one. Hanseong Sunbo (한성순보), founded 31 Oct 1883, did NOT stop 'for a while' — it stopped permanently when its printing office (박문국) burned during the Gapsin Coup of Dec 1884, and it never resumed. The paper that closed in July 1888 for lack of funds was its successor Hanseong Jubo (한성주보), a weekly founded 25 Jan 1886 — a different paper with a different name, a different publication cycle, and mostly Korean script rather than Classical Chinese. So both 'for a while' (implying it came back) and 'It had to close in 1888' (attributing 한성주보's closure to 한성순보) are false as written. The vocabulary glosses themselves are correct — 'discontinued v. 중단하다 (be discontinued 중단되다)' and 'lack n. 부족 (lack of money 자금 부족)' — but both cards carry these false sentences into flashcard review as their context.
items.correction: Rewrite the two sentences so the two papers are distinguished, keeping the card words 'discontinued' and 'lack' in place so the cards stay valid. Suggested: "A year later the newspaper was discontinued when its printing office burned down during a failed coup. Its successor, Hanseong Jubo, carried on until 1888, when it had to close because of lack of money." Then update the matching readingSentences korean. NOTE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: per the repo rules, changing English text deletes that sentence's voice clip (clip key is a text hash), so re-run `node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs` in the same task; and the mp3 at /audio/reading/pr202.mp3 still speaks the old wording, so either re-record it or leave the English alone and instead correct only the Korean — a decision the owner should make, not a silent edit.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-202-s003 and reading-202-s004 KO (same in pr202-1.json readingSentences and instruction block)
items.original: s003: 한 달에 세 번씩 그 신문은 국내와 외부 세계에 대한 뉴스를 독자들에게 가져다 주었다. / s004: 일년 후에, 그 신문은 화재 때문에 잠시 동안 중단되었다.
items.problem: These are Korean spelling and spacing errors. '가져다주다' is a single registered verb, so it should be written '가져다주었다'. A unit noun is spaced from its number, so '일년' should be '일 년' (or '1년').
items.correction: s003: '…독자들에게 가져다주었다.' s004: '일 년 후, 그 신문은 화재로 잠시 발간이 중단되었다.'

items.locator: readingSentences reading-202-s004 and reading-202-s005 (EN + KO); same text in pr202-1.json readingSentences and the instruction block
items.original: A year later the newspaper was discontinued for a while due to a fire. / It had to close in 1888 because of lack of money. / KO: 그 신문은 1888년에 자금 부족 때문에 폐간해야 했다.
items.problem: The passage treats Hanseong Sunbo as one paper that paused after a fire and then closed in 1888. In fact Hanseong Sunbo stopped in December 1884, when its facilities (박문국) burned during the Gapsin Coup, and it never came back under that name. In January 1886 a successor was launched as a different, weekly paper, Hanseong Jubo. It was that weekly which stopped on 7 July 1888 because the government could no longer fund it. Korean learners are taught this split (한성순보 1883–84 / 한성주보 1886–88) in Korean history, so the passage and its translation teach a date that contradicts what they learn and are tested on.
items.correction: Option A, no audio change: add a note to the Korean of s005 in pr202.json and pr202-1.json (both readingSentences and the instruction block), e.g. '그 신문은 (1886년 주간지 『한성주보』로 이름을 바꿔 다시 나왔다가) 1888년에 자금 부족으로 문을 닫아야 했다.' Option B: rewrite s005 EN as 'It returned in 1886 as a weekly, Hanseong Jubo, but had to close in 1888 because of lack of money.' and regenerate the Ava clip in the same change (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs), because the clip key is a hash of the text.

items.original: 더 중요한 것은 논의를 바꾸어 "독일어를 쓰면 독일인이다"라고 말할 수 없다는 점이다.
items.problem: 'switch the argument' here means reversing the proposition, i.e. taking the converse of 'if English → speaks English'. The lesson's own card glosses 'switch' as '뒤바꾸다'. '논의를 바꾸어' reads as 'change the topic or discussion', which hides the logical point the passage makes.
items.correction: 더 중요한 것은 그 논리를 뒤집어 "독일어를 쓰면 독일인이다"라고 말할 수는 없다는 점이다.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 2887; content/lessons/reading/pr207.json readingVocabulary[1]; same entry in content/lessons/reading/pr207-1.json
items.original: "word": "congress", "lemma": "congress", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "(미국) 의회", "freq": 3
items.problem: The headword is printed lowercase, but the gloss given is the proper-noun sense "(미국) 의회", and all three occurrences in the passage are capitalized ("The job of Congress is to pass laws.", "both houses of Congress", "each house of Congress"). Lowercase "congress" is a different word meaning a formal meeting or assembly (회의, 대회); the legislature sense is "often capitalized" per Wiktionary. The card is rendered to the learner as the bare headword (src/components/ReadingLearningView.tsx line 800-802 shows kw.word), so the learner studies the wrong form of the word the passage actually uses.
items.correction: Set "word" (and "lemma") to "Congress". The data model already supports capitals — 4 headwords elsewhere in the corpus keep them (pr069/pr069-1 "Buddhist", pr170/pr170-1 "Western") — so no pipeline change is needed, and the Korean gloss needs no edit. Apply the same change in pr207-1.json. This edit touches only the vocabulary entry, not passage English, so no voice clip is affected.

items.locator: reading-vocab-context.tsv line 2889; content/lessons/reading/pr207.json readingVocabulary[3] (line 102-105); same entry duplicated in content/lessons/reading/pr207-1.json (line 102-105)
items.original: "word": "overpowered", "lemma": "overpower", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "압도하다, 뒤집다 (be overpowered 뒤집히다)"  — context sentence: "If the president rejects a bill, it can still become a law if the president's rejection is overpowered by at least a two-thirds majority of each house of Congress."
items.problem: The card teaches 뒤집다 / 뒤집히다 (to overturn, to be overturned) as a meaning of "overpower". No major dictionary records any such sense: overpower means only to subdue by superior force, to overwhelm in intensity, or to render imperceptible. The gloss exists only because the passage itself uses "overpowered" where the standard English term for this exact civics fact is "overridden" — the U.S. Senate glossary entry for the procedure is literally "Override of a Veto". So the second gloss is a meaning invented to patch a non-standard word in the passage, and it is the gloss the learner is most likely to memorize because it is the one that fits the sentence.
items.correction: Change the passage sentence to the standard wording — "...if the president's rejection is overridden by at least a two-thirds majority of each house of Congress." — and change the card to "overridden | v. | (거부권을) 무효화하다, 뒤집다 (be overridden 무효화되다)" with lemma "override". If the English sentence is edited, the sentence's voice clip key changes, so the clip must be regenerated in the same task with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs, and the identical entry in pr207-1.json must be changed too. If the passage text must be left as it is, the card should at minimum drop 뒤집다 and read "압도하다 (여기서는 '무효화되다'의 뜻으로 쓰임; 표준 표현은 override)".

items.locator: readingSentences reading-207-s003 EN, and readingVocabulary card 'overpowered' (same in pr207-1.json)
items.original: If the president rejects a bill, it can still become a law if the president's rejection is overpowered by at least a two-thirds majority of each house of Congress. / card: "word": "overpowered", "lemma": "overpower", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "압도하다, 뒤집다 (be overpowered 뒤집히다)"
items.problem: The standard term for Congress cancelling a presidential veto is 'override' (a veto). 'Overpower' means to subdue by superior force or to overwhelm. No dictionary gives it a sense of reversing or cancelling a decision. The card goes further and invents that sense ('뒤집다', 'be overpowered 뒤집히다') to fit the unusual wording. Learners will memorise 'overpower = 뒤집다' and say 'overpower a veto', which is not idiomatic. 'Rejection' in place of 'veto' also hides the key civics term.
items.correction: Preferred: change s003 EN to 'If the president vetoes a bill, it can still become a law if the veto is overridden by at least a two-thirds majority in each house of Congress.' Regenerate the Ava clip in the same change, and replace the cards with 'vetoes | veto | v. | (법안에) 거부권을 행사하다' and 'overridden | override | v. | (결정·거부권을) 무효화하다'. Minimal (no audio change): keep the text and change the card to '(힘으로) 제압하다, 압도하다 — 여기서는 대통령의 거부를 꺾는다는 비유. 정식 표현은 override a veto(거부권을 무효화하다)'.

items.original: "word": "congress", "lemma": "congress", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "(미국) 의회"
items.problem: The card shows the word as-is (ReadingLearningView.tsx:801), so learners see lowercase 'congress' glossed '(미국) 의회'. With the meaning 'US legislature' the word is a proper noun and is always written 'Congress'. Lowercase 'congress' is the common noun (a formal assembly or conference). The passage itself writes 'Congress' three times. The same lowercase card also exists in pr171, which is outside this scope.
items.correction: Set word (and lemma) to 'Congress'. Optionally gloss it '(미국) 의회 (고유명사, 대문자 C) / congress: (일반) 회의, 대회'.

items.original: Books can take us out of ourselves. / KO: 책은 우리를 우리 자신 밖으로 데려다줄 수 있다.
items.problem: 'take someone out of themselves' is an idiom meaning to make someone forget their own worries and become less absorbed in themselves. The Korean is a word-for-word rendering that does not convey this meaning. The idiom is the topic sentence of the passage.
items.correction: 책은 우리가 자기 자신에게만 갇혀 있지 않도록(자신의 걱정을 잊도록) 해 줄 수 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences #1 korean (reading-212-s001); same in pr212-1.json and src/lib
items.original: 일반적으로 부모님들은 그들이 다른 아이들에게서 느끼지 못하는 특별한 사랑을 자신의 아이들에게 느낀다.
items.problem: 'love ... that they do not feel for other children' is rendered with '에게서' ('from'). '다른 아이들에게서 느끼지 못하는 사랑' can be read as 'love they do not sense coming from other children', which is not the meaning. The honorific '부모님들은' is also odd in a general statement; #3 uses '부모'.
items.correction: 일반적으로 부모는 다른 아이들에게는 느끼지 않는 특별한 사랑을 자기 자식에게 느낀다.

items.locator: passage instruction block and readingSentences #7-#8 (the Sue story ends at #7, the Robert story starts at #8)
items.original: Sometimes Sue woke up feeling sick. However, she delivered the newspapers not to disappoint her customers. Robert's friends made fun of him because he could not ride a bicycle.
items.problem: Two unrelated stories from a test sheet (Sue's newspaper route, then Robert learning to ride a bike) run together as one paragraph, with no break, label or transition. The earlier audit (R-66) decided to keep both because they share a theme (perseverance), but nothing on the page (EN block, Step 1 sentence list, or -1 KO page) tells the learner that a second story begins. It reads as if Robert suddenly enters Sue's story.
items.correction: Keep both stories as R-66 decided, but mark the switch: for example, start the second story with '(B)' / add a paragraph break in the passage block and the -1 KO text, or add a bridging sentence such as 'Robert showed the same kind of persistence.' (An English change needs audio regeneration.)

items.locator: readingSentences #2, #5, #6, #14 korean (reading-213-s002/s005/s006/s014); same in pr213-1.json and src/lib
items.original: #2 "그녀는 그녀의 고객들을 위해 매일 아침 5시 30분에 신문을 배달하기 위해 일어났다." / #5 "그녀의 고객들은 그들이 아침 일찍이 신문을 받을 것을 확신했었기 때문에 모두 만족했다." / #6 "때로는 Sue는 아프다고 느끼면서 일어났다." / #14 "같은 일은 자꾸자꾸 일어났으며 그리고 그 일들은 그를 다치게 했다."
items.problem: These are word-for-word renderings that read unnaturally or shift the meaning. #2 uses '위해' twice and turns 'to her customers' into 'for her customers'. #5 drops 'always' ('were always sure') and uses the unnecessary '했었기'. #6 renders 'woke up feeling sick' as '아프다고 느끼면서 일어났다'. #14 doubles the connective ('~으며 그리고').
items.correction: #2 그녀는 고객들에게 신문을 배달하려고 매일 아침 5시 30분에 일어났다. / #5 고객들은 늘 아침 일찍 신문을 받을 수 있다고 확신했기 때문에 모두 만족했다. / #6 가끔 Sue는 몸이 아픈 채로 잠에서 깼다. / #14 같은 일이 계속 되풀이되었고, 그 때문에 그는 다쳤다.

items.locator: readingSentences #7 english (reading-213-s007) and the passage instruction block
items.original: However, she delivered the newspapers not to disappoint her customers.
items.problem: Negative purpose with a bare 'not to' is non-standard. Standard English uses 'so as not to' or 'in order not to'. Without them the sentence can also be misread as 'she did not deliver the newspapers in order to disappoint'.
items.correction: However, she delivered the newspapers so as not to disappoint her customers. (Regenerate this sentence's audio in the same change; the KO '실망시키지 않기 위해서' stays as it is.)

items.locator: readingSentences #8 korean (reading-213-s008); same in pr213-1.json and src/lib
items.original: Robert의 친구들은 그가 자전거를 탈줄 몰랐기 때문에 그를 놀렸다.
items.problem: This is a Korean spacing error. '줄' is a bound noun, so it must be written apart from the verb: '탈 줄'.
items.correction: Robert의 친구들은 그가 자전거를 탈 줄 몰라서 그를 놀렸다.

items.locator: readingSentences #10 korean (reading-213-s010); same in pr213-1.json and src/lib
items.original: 어느 오후에 그는 그의 큰형에게 가르쳐 달라고 부탁했다.
items.problem: 'big brother' means an older brother (형). '큰형' specifically means the eldest of several older brothers, which the text does not say. The lesson's own card translates it correctly: 'brother n. 형제 (big brother 형)'.
items.correction: 어느 날 오후 그는 형에게 가르쳐 달라고 부탁했다.

items.locator: readingSentences #2 korean (reading-214-s002); same text in pr214-1.json and src/lib
items.original: Smith 씨가 믿는 바와는 반대로 음악과 공연 예술에서의 컴퓨터 기술의 역할은 상당히 주목할 만하다.
items.problem: 'has been considerable' (present perfect: the role has been large) is rendered as present-tense '상당히 주목할 만하다' ('is quite noteworthy'). This changes both the tense and the meaning (large in extent becomes noteworthy). It also conflicts with the lesson's own card 'considerable adj. 상당한'.
items.correction: Smith 씨의 생각과 달리, 음악과 공연 예술에서 컴퓨터가 해 온 역할은 상당히 컸다.

items.locator: readingSentences #4 english (reading-214-s004) and the passage instruction block
items.original: Composers, performers, and audience can all have digital control of their music.
items.problem: 'audience' is a singular countable noun and appears here without an article, in a list of plural nouns ('Composers, performers'). Standard English needs 'audiences' or 'the audience'.
items.correction: Composers, performers, and audiences can all have digital control of their music. (Regenerate the sentence audio in the same change, since the clip key is the text hash; the KO '작곡가, 연주자, 청중 모두 ...' needs no change.)

items.locator: readingSentences #5 korean (reading-214-s005); same text in the pr214-1.json instruction block and src/lib/readingSentences.json pr214
