items.original: 만약 현대의 최고의 록 가수가 그 혹은 그녀의 다음 음악을 인터넷상에 올리면, 그 음악은 2천만 객석을 갖춘 극장에서 연주되는 것처럼 연주될 수 있을 뿐만 아니라, 각각의 청자가 또한 그 음악을 각자의 취향에 맞게 변화를 줄 수 있다.
items.problem: The English is a second (hypothetical) conditional: 'If today's top rock singer released ..., it would not only be like playing in a theater with 20 million seats, but each listener could also transform ...'. The Korean turns it into an ordinary real conditional ('올리면 ... 수 있다'), so the 가정법 is lost. It also garbles the main clause: 'it would be like playing in a theater' says releasing the song online is like performing for a 20-million-seat audience, but the Korean reads '그 음악은 ... 연주되는 것처럼 연주될 수 있을' ('the music can be played as if it is played'). '그 혹은 그녀의' is a word-for-word rendering of 'his or her'.
items.correction: 오늘날 최고의 록 가수가 다음 곡을 인터넷에 공개한다면, 그것은 2천만 석짜리 극장에서 공연하는 것과 같을 뿐 아니라, 듣는 사람 각자가 자기 취향에 따라 그 음악을 바꿀 수도 있을 것이다. (Apply the same text to all three copies: pr214.json readingSentences, pr214-1.json instruction block + readingSentences, and src/lib/readingSentences.json.)

items.locator: readingSentences #1 korean (reading-217-s001); same in pr217-1.json and src/lib
items.original: 몇몇 작가들은 독자를 감동시키기 위하여 긴 단어를 많이 사용하여 지적인 것처럼 들리도록 노력해야 한다고 생각한다.
items.problem: 'to impress their readers' here means making readers admire the writer's learning, not moving them emotionally ('감동시키다'). The earlier audit (RV-24) fixed the card for this reason, and the card now reads 'impress v. 깊은 인상을 주다'. The sentence translation still uses '감동시키기', so the card and the sentence disagree. The scare quotes around "intellectual", which carry the irony, are also dropped.
items.correction: 어떤 글쓴이들은 독자에게 깊은 인상을 주려면 긴 단어를 많이 쓰고 '유식하게' 들리도록 애써야 한다고 생각한다.

items.locator: readingSentences #1, #3, #4, #5 korean (reading-219-s001/s003/s004/s005); same in pr219-1.json and src/lib
items.original: #3 "초기 사춘기 때에, 그들은 무엇이든 그들의 부모와 논쟁한다." / #4 "나이가 들어감에 따라 논쟁의 양은 감소하지만, 질은 증가한다." / #5 "논쟁은 사춘기 소년소녀들이 그들의 가정 생활에서 할 필요가 있는 것이다." / #1 "엄격한 집안에서는 말대꾸하며 따지는 것을 흔히 무례하다고 여긴다."
items.problem: '질은 증가한다' is not idiomatic Korean: quality rises (높아진다), it does not increase in amount. The lesson's own card translates 'increases' as '높아지다'. '초기 사춘기 때에' and '사춘기 소년소녀들' are awkward renderings of 'early adolescence' and 'adolescents', and the cards give '청소년기 초기' and '청소년'. '가정 생활' should be written as one word, '가정생활'. The passage's key term 'argument/arguing' is rendered '말대꾸하며 따지는 것' in #1 but '논쟁' in #2-#5.
items.correction: #3 청소년기 초기에는 무엇이든 부모와 말다툼을 벌인다. / #4 나이가 들수록 말다툼의 양은 줄지만 질은 높아진다. / #5 말다툼은 청소년이 가정생활에서 꼭 해야 하는 일이다. (Use one consistent term for argument/arguing across #1-#5.)

items.locator: readingSentences #2 english (reading-219-s002) and the passage instruction block; card 'normal' (readingVocabulary #11)
items.original: Arguing, however, is a way of life with normal developing youths.
items.problem: The intended meaning is 'youths who are developing normally', which needs the adverb: 'normally developing' (the standard developmental-psychology phrase, like 'typically developing'). The Korean already reads it as an adverb ('정상적으로 자라는'). The card 'normal adj. 정상적인' supports the ungrammatical reading.
items.correction: Arguing, however, is a way of life with normally developing youths. (Regenerate this sentence's audio in the same change. Replace the card with 'normally adv. 정상적으로' in all three card copies.)

items.original: "word": "latin", "lemma": "latin"
items.problem: 'Latin' is a proper adjective and is always capitalized in English. The card shows 'latin'. This is one instance of the case-mismatch pattern that maps/reading.md §2 records as cosmetic (80 lessons), but here the lowercase form is an actual spelling error, not just a case difference from the passage.
items.correction: "word": "Latin", "lemma": "Latin". The word-clip key may change, so check whether the Ava word clip needs regenerating.

items.original: The word canary comes from the _______ word canis, meaning dog.
items.problem: The answer 'Latin' keeps its capital letter, while the distractors are lowercase pool words (for example canary, named, birds, comes, canis). The capital letter gives the answer away. This is the same generator issue as the pr228 and pr230 items.
items.correction: Show the target and distractors in the same case, or leave proper adjectives out of the targets (src/lib/readingUtils.ts:728-746).

items.original: "word": "latin", "lemma": "latin", "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "라틴어의"
items.problem: 고유형용사 Latin 을 소문자 headword 'latin' 으로 저장했다. ReadingLearningView.tsx:801 이 word 필드를 그대로 출력하므로 학습자에게 'latin' 으로 보인다. 정작 같은 파일의 지문 본문은 "the Latin word canis" 로 대문자로 쓰고 있어 화면 안에서 철자가 어긋난다. 저장소 전체 reading 어휘 카드 중 대문자 headword 는 4건(Buddhist, Western)뿐이므로 파이프라인 제약이 아니라 이 카드의 오류다.
items.correction: "word": "Latin", "lemma": "Latin" 으로 수정. (지문 문장 텍스트가 아니라 어휘 카드 필드이므로 문장 음성 클립에는 영향이 없다.)

items.original: readingVocabulary[1]: "word": "islands", "korean": "섬"  /  readingVocabulary[12]: "word": "isle", "korean": "섬"
items.problem: 같은 과 14개 카드 중 두 카드의 뜻풀이가 글자 그대로 동일한 "섬" 이다. 카드 UI 는 문맥 문장 없이 품사+단어+뜻만 보여주므로(ReadingLearningView.tsx:795-842), 학습자는 islands 와 isle 을 구별할 단서를 전혀 받지 못한다. isle 은 문어체·시적 어휘로 일상 영어에서 island 과 교체 사용되지 않는다.
items.correction: isle 의 korean 을 "섬 (island의 문어체·시적 표현; Isle of Dogs 개의 섬)" 로 수정해 두 카드를 구별시킨다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-222-s006 .korean (also in pr222-1.json and in the pr222-1 instruction block)
items.original: 그러나 그것들의 원시성은 우리가 정보에 대한 지속적이고 즉각적으로 접근할 수 있는 세계, 즉 근본적으로 다른 세계에 살고 있다는 우리의 느낌만을 확인할 뿐일 것이다.
items.problem: The Korean is ungrammatical. '정보에 대한 지속적이고' (an adnominal phrase) is joined to '즉각적으로 접근할 수 있는' (an adverbial phrase), which mixes two constructions. '느낌만을 확인할 뿐' also doubles the limiting marker (만 and 뿐).
items.correction: 그러나 그것들의 원시성은 우리가 정보에 끊임없이, 즉각적으로 접근할 수 있는 근본적으로 다른 세계에 살고 있다는 우리의 생각을 굳혀 줄 뿐일 것이다. Apply the same change in pr222-1.json.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-223-s005 .korean (also in pr223-1.json and in the pr223-1 instruction block)
items.original: 나의 부인과 아이들이 조화를 이루고 산다면 난 행복하다.
items.problem: '부인(夫人)' is the honorific for someone else's wife. Using it for the narrator's own wife ('my wife') is a well-known Korean usage error. The natural word is 아내.
items.correction: 내 아내와 아이들이 화목하게 지낸다면 나는 행복하다. Apply the same change in pr223-1.json.

items.original: "word": "intelligence", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "지성"  — context: "some people value their religion, or their [intelligence], or their health"
items.problem: 사전들이 일제히 1순위로 싣는 뜻 '지능' 이 빠지고 2순위인 '지성' 만 제시됐다. 이 문장에서 '자신의 지능을 소중히 여긴다' 가 가장 자연스러운 독해인데, 카드만 외운 학습자는 intelligence 를 '지능' 으로 옮기지 못한다.
items.correction: "korean": "지능, 지성" 으로 수정.

items.original: 봄 (at first sight 첫눈에)
items.problem: '봄' is a correct dictionary gloss (the noun form of 보다), but on its own on a card most Korean learners will read it as 'spring (the season)'. The card shows only this gloss before the parenthesis.
items.correction: 보기, 봄(보는 것) (at first sight 첫눈에)

items.locator: Step 3 cloze items 1 and 2 (generated from reading-225-s001 and reading-225-s002)
items.original: Some people insist on “love at first _______,” but I suggest that they calm down and take a second look. / There is no such thing as love at first _______.
items.problem: Two of the lesson's three cloze items have the same answer ('sight') in the same fixed phrase ('love at first ___'). After the first item, the second is trivial.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, skip a sentence (or choose another word in it) when its target equals a target already used in this lesson.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-227-s001 .korean (also s004 .korean; the same text is in pr227-1.json)
items.original: 사람들은 자신들을 따뜻하게 유지시키기 위해 담요를 이용하는데 익숙해져 있다.
items.problem: Korean spacing error. '데' here is a dependent noun (for doing something), so it must be written '이용하는 데'. In s004, '한 쪽으로부터 다른 한 쪽으로' should be spelled '한쪽' as one word.
items.correction: 사람들은 몸을 따뜻하게 하려고 담요를 이용하는 데 익숙해져 있다. / s004: …열이 담요의 한쪽에서 다른 쪽으로 통과해 가는 것을 막는 것이다. Apply the same changes in pr227-1.json.

items.original: surrounding | lemma surround | adj. | 주위의, 둘러싼
items.problem: In the passage ('the colder air surrounding it'), 'surrounding' takes an object ('it'), so it is a present participle of the verb 'surround'. It is not the attributive adjective 'surrounding' (as in 'the surrounding air'). The card's POS (adj.) and lemma (surround) disagree with each other, and the POS does not match the use in this sentence.
items.correction: partOfSpeech 'v.', korean '둘러싸다 (the air surrounding it 그것을 둘러싼 공기)'. Or keep 'adj.' and set lemma 'surrounding' with the example 'the surrounding air 주위의 공기'.

items.original: "word": "warm", "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "따뜻한", "freq": 3 — the third of those three occurrences is "Expecting that a blanket will always make something warm, they think that it must warm ice, too." (reading-227-s003)
items.problem: The card carries freq 3, i.e. it stands for all three occurrences of "warm" in the passage, but two are the adjective ("make themselves warm", "make something warm") and the third, "it must warm ice, too", is a transitive verb (따뜻하게 하다). Only the adjective is tagged and glossed, so the one occurrence that is grammatically hard for a learner - a bare verb after the modal "must" - is the one the card does not cover.
items.correction: "partOfSpeech": "adj./v.", "korean": "따뜻한; 따뜻하게 하다 (must warm ice 얼음을 따뜻하게 만들다)"

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 1 (generated from reading-228-s001 by generateClozeItems, src/lib/readingUtils.ts:723-746)
items.original: "People often think that being an usher is an easy job, but it isn't," says Peter _______, an usher at the Palladium theater.
items.problem: The graded blank is the surname 'Sullivan'. It tests no English vocabulary and cannot be worked out from context. The target keeps its capital letter, but the distractors come from the lowercased word pool (for example palladium, theater, difficult). So 'Sullivan' is the only capitalized option, which gives the answer away. One of this lesson's three cloze items is therefore wasted.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, skip tokens that are capitalized mid-sentence (proper nouns) or contain digits when choosing validTargetWords, and show every option in the same case. For this sentence the generator would then choose a word such as 'usher' or 'easy'.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-229-s004 .korean (same text in pr229-1.json readingSentences and in the pr229-1 instruction block)
items.original: 그들의 어조는 독서할 시간이 있는 사람은 어쨌든 한가한 사람이라는 것을 암시한다.
items.problem: The English is 'Their tone implies that anyone with time to read books is somehow an idler.' The translation has two errors. First, 'somehow' (어딘가, 어쩐지) is rendered as '어쨌든' (anyway), which changes the meaning. The card for 'somehow' in this same lesson correctly says '어쩐지, 왠지'. Second, 'idler' (게으름뱅이, according to this lesson's own card) is softened to '한가한 사람' (a person with free time). That is almost a restatement of 'anyone with time to read books', so the passage's key point is lost: the businessmen are sneering that readers are lazy. The card and the sentence contradict each other.
items.correction: 그들의 어조에는 책 읽을 시간이 있는 사람은 어딘가 게으른 사람(빈둥거리는 사람)이라는 뜻이 담겨 있다. Apply the same change in pr229-1.json (readingSentences and the instruction block).

items.locator: readingSentences reading-230-s005..s009 .korean (and s001 '항해자'); the same text is in pr230-1.json and the pr230-1 instruction block
items.original: sea shanties는 항해자들에게 귀중한 친구였으며 항해자들이 하나의 팀으로 일하도록 도움이 됐다.
items.problem: s003 translates the term as '뱃노래(sea shanty)', but s005–s009 leave it as untranslated English ('sea shanties는', '몇몇 shanties는', '또 다른 shanties는'). This produces mixed-script Korean that also carries an English plural. 'Sailors' is rendered as '항해자' throughout, while the lesson's 'sailors' card says '선원'.
items.correction: From s005 on, use '뱃노래' (for example s005: '뱃노래는 선원들에게 소중한 친구였으며, 선원들이 한 팀으로 일하도록 도와주었다.'; s006: '어떤 뱃노래는 긴 항해의 지루함을 달래 주었다.'). Use '선원' consistently. Apply the same changes in pr230-1.json.

items.original: Sailors in the _______ had a hard life.
items.problem: The graded blank is the number '1800s'. The distractors are all lowercase words of the same length (for example songs, ships, trips, lives), so the only option that contains digits is obviously the answer. No vocabulary is tested.
items.correction: Exclude tokens that contain digits, and capitalized proper nouns, from the cloze target candidates (src/lib/readingUtils.ts:728). For this sentence the next candidate would be 'Sailors' or 'hard'. Keep the options' case uniform.

items.original: "word": "aboard", "partOfSpeech": "adv.", "korean": "(배에) 타고" — card sentence: "They found rare comfort in the simple songs that they sang aboard their ships."
items.problem: In the sentence the card is built from, "aboard" governs the object "their ships", so it is a preposition, not an adverb. The adverb tag is right only for the passage's other occurrence, "the sea shanties made their stay aboard less difficult" (reading-230-s009), which the single card also has to cover (freq 2). As written, the tag matches the second occurrence and contradicts the first.
items.correction: "partOfSpeech": "prep./adv.", "korean": "(배에) 타고, 배 위에서 (aboard their ships 배를 타고)"

items.original: [ Passoff Reading 231-1 ]
items.problem: All 511 other READING files use '[ K-IG 교육 Reading NNN(-1) ]'. This one keeps the old 'Passoff' brand. ReadingLearningView does not render the heading block, but it ships in the page's RSC payload.
items.correction: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 231-1 ]

items.locator: readingSentences[0] and [1] (reading-231-s001, s002), Korean; same in pr231-1.json blocks[1]
items.original: 당신은 현대 음악 작곡가를 당신의 첫 번째 영웅으로 선택할 수 있는가? / 혹은 동시대 걸작을 만들어 낸 화가를 선택할 수 있는가?
items.problem: 'Would X be your first choice for a hero?' asks about preference or likelihood (would). '선택할 수 있는가' asks about ability (can). This changes the modality, and #3's answer 'no' then reads as 'you cannot'.
items.correction: 영웅을 꼽으라면 현대 음악 작곡가를 가장 먼저 떠올리겠는가? / 아니면 현대 걸작을 그린 화가를 떠올리겠는가?

items.locator: readingVocabulary.reason: pr231[0] music, pr232[5] average, pr232[9] crowded, pr233[11] live, pr236[8] potential, pr237[2] speed (and the same cards in the -1 files)
items.original: 지문 핵심 주제문 구성 어휘 · 중학 필수 독해 기본 어휘 · 지문의 성격을 수식하는 핵심 형용사 (평가 점수: 109점)
items.problem: The auto-generated 'reason' label calls nouns and verbs '핵심 형용사' (music n., average n., live v., potential n.) and calls an adjective and a noun '핵심 동사' (crowded adj., speed n.). This contradicts partOfSpeech. The field is not rendered (maps/reading.md §1.2) but ships in the payload.
items.correction: Regenerate the 'reason' strings from partOfSpeech, or drop the field from the lesson payload.

items.original: "word": "pumping", "lemma": "pump", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "(펌프로) 뿜어 넣다"  — sentence: "We are pumping huge quantities of CO2 into the atmosphere, and a large share of it comes from cars."
items.problem: The parenthetical "(펌프로)" states a means that is not in the sentence and is factually wrong for it: cars emit CO2 through exhaust, not through a pump. This is the figurative "pour/emit in large amounts" sense - Wiktionary illustrates exactly this sense with a near-identical sentence about greenhouse gases and the atmosphere, which does not involve a mechanical pump. The lesson's own Korean renders it "내뿜고 있으며", with no pump.
items.correction: "korean": "(대량으로) 뿜어내다, 쏟아붓다" — remove "(펌프로)", or replace it with the collocation hint "(pump A into B) A를 B에 쏟아붓다".

items.locator: readingSentences[4] (reading-234-s005), Korean; same in pr234-1.json blocks[1]
items.original: 이런 요인들이 국가들 간의 정치적 경제적 차이들을 야기시킨다.
items.problem: The English 'These factors have caused …' is present perfect (a result up to now), but the Korean uses the timeless present. '야기시키다' is a redundant causative; the standard form is '야기하다'.
items.correction: 이러한 요인들이 국가들 사이에 정치적·경제적 차이를 낳아 왔다(야기해 왔다).

items.original: Thus, the most important issue facing these countries is understanding the difference among cultures.
items.problem: Singular 'the difference among cultures' is unnatural, and it clashes with the passage's own plural 'differences' (#4-#6). 'Among' with several items takes the plural 'differences'. The Korean already says '문화간의 차이들'.
items.correction: 'Thus, the most important issue facing these countries is understanding the differences among cultures.' Regenerate the sentence clip.

items.original: "word": "involving", "lemma": "involve", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "관련시키다, 끌어들이다"  — sentence: "Global politics, as a result, has become more complex, involving countries from many civilizations."
items.problem: Both glosses give the agentive/causative sense of involve (sense 3 in Wiktionary: "to cause or engage (someone or something) to become connected, implicated, or participate"). The sentence uses the inclusive sense (sense 1: "to have (something) as a component or a related part; to comprise, to include") - global politics does not drag countries in, it now comprises them. The sense actually used is missing from the card, and 끌어들이다 (drag in / rope in) additionally adds an agent and an intention that the English does not have. The lesson's own Korean translation of the same sentence disagrees with the card: "국제 정치는 보다 복잡해져서, 많은 문명권들을 포함하고 있다."
items.correction: "korean": "포함하다, 수반하다" (e.g. "involving countries from many civilizations 여러 문명권의 나라들을 포함하면서"). If a second sense is wanted, keep 관련시키다 but put 포함하다 first; drop 끌어들이다.

items.locator: readingSentences[1] (reading-235-s002), English; same row in pr235-1.json; blocks[1] instruction
items.original: This means that the center of interest― the subject―is just a spot, too small to have any impact.
items.problem: The dashes are U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR, spaced unevenly: a space after the first, none around the second. On screen this reads 'interest― the subject―is'. For the speaking check, normalizeText (src/lib/speechRecognition.ts:68-91) strips only . , ? ! ; : " ' ( ), so 'subject―is' stays one token that a recogniser can never return. The matcher only looks 2 words ahead, so after that token every later word also fails. I ran the real evaluatePronunciation (transpiled from the repo) on a word-perfect transcript: 62 points, '💪 거의 맞았어요 (Almost!)', matched 7/18, red: subject―is | just | a | spot, | too | small | to | have | any | impact.
items.correction: Write the dashes as a spaced em dash or commas, e.g. 'This means that the center of interest — the subject — is just a spot, too small to have any impact.', in pr235.json and pr235-1.json (readingSentences + blocks[1]). The English text changes, so regenerate the clip in the same change (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs). Alternatively, also make normalizeText treat ―/—/– as spaces.

items.locator: readingSentences[4] (reading-235-s005), Korean; same in pr235-1.json blocks[1]
items.original: 다른 사진작가들의 작품을 볼 때, 그들이 어떻게 구도를 채우는지 주목하라.
items.problem: 'fill the frame' is the photography term for filling the picture area (화면/프레임). '구도' means composition, and '구도를 채우다' is not idiomatic. It also conflicts with the lesson's card 'frame | (사진의) 화면, 프레임'.
items.correction: 다른 사진작가들의 작품을 볼 때, 그들이 화면(프레임)을 어떻게 채우는지 주의 깊게 보라.

items.original: Rarer cases involve people selling paintings that were actually painted by famous painters. Therefore, before you have a garage sale, call an antique dealer to help you separate the valuable from the worthless junk.
items.problem: Seven sentence rows in scope hold two English sentences (and two Korean ones), while every other row holds one. pr236 is entirely 3 double rows for 6 sentences. The per-sentence clip, the speaking test and the '[n]' numbering therefore work on double-length units, inconsistent with the rest of the course (the 2026-09-17 audit set 'one sentence per row', R-72). The other merged rows: pr231 'If you are like most people, the answer to both questions is “no.” More likely, …', pr237 'In short, the game had little action. According to studies …', pr237 'Not everyone was in favor of the bigger ball, however. Some players, …', pr238 '… other purposes. Presently coal and oil …'.
items.correction: Split each into two rows with matching Korean halves (the Korean already splits cleanly at the period). Renumber the ids and regenerate the clips for the new sentence texts.

items.locator: readingSentences[0] (reading-236-s001), Korean; same text in pr236-1.json readingSentences[0] and blocks[1] instruction
items.original: 창고를 청소할 때, 수집할 만한 물건으로서 그것의 가능성을 결정할 때까지는 어떤 “쓰레기”도 버리지 말라. 사실, 가치 없는 낡은 쓰레기 조각이 귀중한 것일 수도 충분히 있다.
items.problem: (1) 'until you determine its potential as a collectible' means 'until you find out / assess its value as a collectible'. '가능성을 결정할 때까지' uses the wrong sense of determine (to decide), and this lesson's own card teaches determine = '알아내다, 판단하다' (readingVocabulary[10]). (2) 'what often appears to be a piece of worthless old junk' loses 'appears to be' / 'often'. The Korean then says outright that worthless junk may be valuable, which contradicts itself and loses the point of the passage (it only LOOKS worthless).
items.correction: 창고를 청소할 때, 수집품으로서의 가치를 확인하기 전까지는 어떤 “잡동사니”도 버리지 마라. 사실, 쓸모없는 낡은 잡동사니처럼 보이는 것이 꽤 값진 물건일 가능성도 충분히 있다.

items.original: Energy beyond that provided by human or animal muscles is needed for operating our factories, for heating and cooking our homes, for powering most forms of transportation, and for hundreds of other purposes. Presently coal and oil supply the majority of our energy needs.
items.problem: 'for heating and cooking our homes' makes 'our homes' the object of 'cooking' too, so it literally says we cook our homes. The Korean ('가정에 난방을 하고 요리를 하며') already fixes this silently, so English and Korean do not match structurally. The row also merges two sentences.
items.correction: '…for heating our homes and cooking our food, …' (or 'for heating and lighting our homes, for cooking, …'). Split 'Presently coal and oil supply the majority of our energy needs.' into its own row, with the Korean '현재는 석탄과 석유가…'. Regenerate the clips.

items.original: Around the world, people are wrestling with the question of humane death - especially in the face of painful terminal illnesses.
items.problem: A spaced hyphen stands in for a dash. It becomes a separate '-' token in the speaking check, which shows it as a red 'missed word' on a perfect reading (repo evaluatePronunciation: 96 points, red: '-'). Other passages use ―.
items.correction: '…the question of humane death — especially in the face of painful terminal illnesses.' (spaced em dash, normalised in the speaking check), or a comma.

items.locator: readingSentences[0] (reading-240-s001), English; readingVocabulary[5] 'evidenced'; same in pr240-1.json
items.original: It is now evidenced that what seems to be a single memory is actually a complex construction.
items.problem: 'It is (now) evidenced that …' is not idiomatic English. The verb 'evidence' is used as 'as evidenced by …' or '… is evidenced by X', not as an impersonal reporting passive with a that-clause. The card 'evidenced | evidence | v. | 입증하다 (be evidenced 입증되다)' teaches this pattern for learners to reuse. The source this passage adapts (Mohs, HowStuffWorks) uses a plain 'now known' construction.
items.correction: 'It is now known that what seems to be a single memory is actually a complex construction.' (or 'There is now evidence that…'). Replace card #6 with a word from the new sentence and regenerate the sentence and word clips.

items.original: Most foreign workers are being taught by Korean coworkers or volunteers who have no or little teaching experience.
items.problem: The fixed English expression is 'little or no' (e.g. 'little or no experience'). 'no or little' is unidiomatic, and learners who shadow or dictate this sentence will learn the wrong order. The R-73 fix corrected 'coworkers of volunteers' in this sentence but left this phrase.
items.correction: …volunteers who have little or no teaching experience. This changes English text, so regenerate the Azure clip for the sentence.

items.original: 하지만 당신의 가장 친한 친구는 당신이 같은 날 그의 생일 파티에 와 주기를 원한다. / 그래서, 어떤 순서로 무엇을 할 것인지 결정할 능력은 여러 개의 사회적 역할을 수행하기 위한 중요한 기술이다. / 일반적으로, 당신은 자신에게 기대되는 것이 무엇인지 알기 때문에 당신의 각각의 역할을 수행하는 데 어려움을 거의 갖지 않는다.
items.problem: s011: 'his or her birthday party' is deliberately gender-neutral, but '그의' reads as male. s013: 'an essential skill' is weakened to '중요한 기술'; essential means 필수적인. s005: '어려움을 거의 갖지 않는다' is literal translationese rather than natural Korean.
items.correction: s011: …같은 날 자기 생일 파티에 와 주기를 원한다. / s013: …수행하는 데 꼭 필요한 기술이다. / s005: …각 역할을 수행하는 데 거의 어려움을 겪지 않는다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-245-s009 korean (also in the pr245-1 block)
items.original: 당신이 상충하는 여러 역할들을 요구받을 때, 당신은 아주 불편하게 느끼고 때때로 좌절감을 느낄 수 있다.
items.problem: The English is 'When many roles make conflicting demands on you'. In the English the roles are the subject and the demands conflict. The Korean says 'when you are asked for several conflicting roles', which drops 'make demands on', the phrase the lesson's own card teaches (demands: make demands on ~에게 요구하다).
items.correction: 여러 역할이 당신에게 서로 상충하는 요구를 할 때, 당신은 꽤 불편하고 때로는 좌절감을 느낄 수 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-246-s002 and s006 (framing of the whole passage)
items.original: This seemingly reasonable explanation has held up for over a century, but it is probably wrong, says Robert Simmons, a behavioral ecologist.
items.problem: The passage uses the present tense ('says') for a 1996 hypothesis (Simmons & Scheepers, 'Winning by a Neck', American Naturalist 1996). It ends on Simmons's conviction and gives no hint that the idea is contested. Mitchell et al. (2009, Journal of Zoology) found no male-female difference in neck proportions and concluded that sexual selection is not the origin of the long neck. National Geographic describes the question as still open. A learner may leave believing Darwin's feeding explanation has been disproved.
items.correction: Change s002 to 'says' → 'said Robert Simmons in 1996', or add a final sentence such as 'Other scientists disagree, and the question is still open.' with its Korean translation. Any English change requires regenerating the Azure clip. The alternative, which needs no audio change, is a Korean note on the -1 page.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-248-s003, s004, s006 korean (s005 aspect)
items.original: 야생 식물들의 자연 서식지에 대한 무관심과 그 파괴때문에, 몇몇의 야생 식물들의 미래는 불확실한 상태이다. / 이런 상황이 되자 이러한 사람들은 한국에서 자라고 있는 야생 식물들을 보존하는데 애쓰기 시작했다. / 그들의 노력으로 현재는 많은 한국인들이 야생 식물들의 가치를 충분히 이해한다.
items.problem: There are two spacing errors under Korean spelling rule 42, which requires a space before a dependent noun: '파괴때문에' should be '파괴 때문에', and '보존하는데' should be '보존하는 데'. s004 'have striven' (애써 왔다) is rendered '애쓰기 시작했다' ('began to'), while s005 'launched efforts' is rendered '애쓰고 있다', so the aspect is swapped between the two sentences. s006 'more Koreans now understand' becomes '많은 한국인들' and loses the comparative 'more than before', which matters because the passage began with 'A small number of people'. 'precious' is also left untranslated.
items.correction: s003: …무관심과 그 파괴 때문에, 일부 야생 식물은 불확실한 미래에 직면해 있다. / s004: 이런 상황에서 이 사람들은 한국에서 자라는 야생 식물을 보존하는 데 애써 왔다. / s005: …식물 종의 가치를 알리고, 다음 세대를 위해 야생 식물을 보존하려는 노력을 시작했다. / s006: 이러한 노력 덕분에 이제 더 많은 한국인이 소중한 야생 식물의 가치를 온전히 이해한다.

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item #1, generated from readingSentences reading-248-s001 (missingWord 'value')
items.original: A small number of people have recognized the value of wild plants in Korea.
items.problem: The target 'value' has 5 letters. 'korea' and 'plant' are always offered, and the third distractor is 1 of 11 six- or four-letter words. One of those is 'beauty', from s002 'fascinated by the beauty of these plants'. When it is drawn (about 9% of loads), 'recognized the beauty of wild plants in Korea' is equally correct, but it is graded wrong.
items.correction: Same mechanism as cloze item #2: exclude 'beauty' for this target through a per-lesson exclusion, or choose another target word.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-249-s002 english, and the Step 3 cloze item #2 generated from it (missingWord '175cm')
items.original: One is 165cm tall and the other is 175cm tall.
items.problem: Standard English (SI) style puts a space between number and unit: '165 cm'. Because '175cm' is written as one token of 5 or more characters, the cloze generator picks it as the '핵심 키워드'. The blank then tests recall of a number rather than a vocabulary word ('One is 165cm tall and the other is _______ tall.'), and '165cm' can appear as a distractor.
items.correction: Write '165 cm' and '175 cm'. The generator then finds no target word in this sentence and moves on to the next candidate sentence. This changes English text, so regenerate the sentence's Azure clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.original: 그래서, 당신은 당신이 알고 있는 특정한 남녀로부터 대체적인 남녀에 관한 결론을 내린다. / 이런 식으로 당신의 일상적 판단과 추측은 당신의 경험에 달려있다.
items.problem: s007: 'men and women as a whole' is rendered '대체적인 남녀' ('approximate/general men and women'), which is not natural Korean and blurs the particular-to-general point of the passage. s008 drops 'many of', turning 'many of your judgments' into all of your judgments, which overgeneralizes the claim.
items.correction: s007: 그래서 당신은 알고 지낸 특정한 남녀들로부터 남녀 전체에 관한 결론을 끌어낸다. / s008: 이런 식으로 당신의 일상적인 판단과 추측 가운데 상당수는 경험에 달려 있다.

items.locator: content/lessons/reading/pr250.json readingSentences[1].korean, line 56 (adjacent to the "performance" card at TSV line 3492)
items.original: "이러한 경우에, 외부 컨설턴트를 고용하여 회사의 능력을 분석하고, 회사가 보다 더 효율적으로 되도록 변화를 권고하도록 하는 것은 유익할 수 있다."  — for "In this case, it can be useful to get an outside consultant to analyze the company's performance and recommend changes to make it more efficient."
items.problem: "the company's performance" is the company's results/how it is doing (실적, 성과), not 능력 (ability, capability) — a consultant here is analysing outcomes, not innate capability. This also directly contradicts the lesson's own vocabulary card for the same word: readingVocabulary[4] (line 127) glosses "performance" as "실적, 성과". Found while verifying the "performance" card (TSV line 3492) against the passage; the card itself is correct, so this is the sentence translation, one step outside my card unit, reported because the two learner-facing texts on the same lesson page disagree.
items.correction: "이러한 경우에, 외부 컨설턴트를 고용하여 회사의 실적(성과)을 분석하고, 회사가 보다 더 효율적으로 되도록 변화를 권고하도록 하는 것은 유익할 수 있다."

items.locator: readingSentences reading-250-s002 korean (also the pr250-1 instruction block)
items.original: 이러한 경우에, 외부 컨설턴트를 고용하여 회사의 능력을 분석하고, 회사가 보다 더 효율적으로 되도록 변화를 권고하도록 하는 것은 유익할 수 있다.
items.problem: 'the company’s performance' means results or output (실적, 성과), not ability (능력). The same lesson's vocabulary card says 'performance — 실적, 성과', so the translation bar and the card disagree. '효율적으로 되도록' is also ungrammatical Korean; it should be '효율적이 되도록'.
items.correction: 이런 경우에는 외부 컨설턴트에게 회사의 실적을 분석하고 회사를 더 효율적으로 만들 변화를 권고하게 하는 것이 유익할 수 있다.

items.original: 이런 컨설턴트는 회사가 직면하고 있는 기회와 위협 뿐만아니라 회사의 강점과 약점도 보다 더 객관적으로 분석할 수 있다.
items.problem: Spacing error: '뿐' after a noun is a particle and attaches to it, and '아니라' is a separate word. The correct form is '위협뿐만 아니라'.
items.correction: 이 컨설턴트는 회사가 직면한 기회와 위협뿐만 아니라 회사의 강점과 약점도 더 객관적으로 분석할 수 있다.

items.locator: TSV lines 3490 and 3496; content/lessons/reading/pr250.json readingVocabulary[2] "goals" (korean at line 103) and readingVocabulary[8] "objectives" (korean at line 177)
items.original: { "word": "goals", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "목표" } ... { "word": "objectives", "partOfSpeech": "n.", "korean": "목표" }  — context sentence: "Suppose a company realizes that it is not achieving its goals or objectives effectively."
items.problem: Two different cards in the same 14-card grid carry the identical Korean gloss 목표, and they come from the same sentence, where the two words are deliberately contrasted ("its goals or objectives"). The lesson's own Korean translation of that sentence distinguishes them — readingSentences[0].korean (line 51) reads "목표나 목적을 효과적으로 달성하지 못하고" — so the card set contradicts the translation shown on the same lesson page. ReadingLearningView.tsx renders the 14 cards as a grid where the learner taps "뜻 확인하기" to reveal the meaning (src/components/ReadingLearningView.tsx lines 783-842), so the learner self-tests on two cards that reveal the same word and cannot tell which English word belongs to which.
items.correction: Change the "objectives" card's korean to "목적, 세부 목표" (or simply "목적"), matching the lesson's own sentence translation "목표나 목적" and the sibling card in pr247 (TSV line 3456), where "objective" is already glossed 목적. Leave "goals" as 목표.

items.locator: TSV line 3516; content/lessons/reading/pr252.json readingVocabulary[0], partOfSpeech at line 78, korean at line 79
items.original: { "word": "perceived", "lemma": "perceive", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "인식하다 (perceived age 스스로 느끼는 나이)" }  — context sentence: "A recent study suggests that perceived age may be a more reliable predictor of marketing success on the gray market than actual age."
items.problem: In this sentence "perceived" is an attributive adjective modifying "age" — the subject of the that-clause is the noun phrase "perceived age" and its verb is "may be". Tagging it v. 인식하다 describes a use that does not occur anywhere in the passage (the other occurrence, "focus on perceived age in marketing campaigns", is attributive too). The same dataset tags the parallel attributive participles as adj.: "intended" in "its intended results" (pr250, TSV line 3494), "developing" in "the developing minds" (pr254, TSV line 3548) and "troubling" in "equally troubling ethical problems" (pr256, TSV line 3581), so pr252 is the odd one out. The POS label is not incidental — it is rendered as a prominent green badge next to the headword (src/components/ReadingLearningView.tsx lines 797-802).
items.correction: Set "partOfSpeech": "adj." and "korean": "인식된, 스스로 느끼는 (perceived age 스스로 느끼는 나이)", keeping the existing lemma "perceive".

items.original: "word": "perceived", "lemma": "perceive", "partOfSpeech": "v.", "korean": "인식하다 (perceived age 스스로 느끼는 나이)"
items.problem: In both occurrences ('perceived age') the word is a past participle used as an adjective before a noun, not a finite verb. The card labels it 'v.' with the verb gloss '인식하다'. The same course labels the parallel case 'developing' (pr254, 'developing minds') as adj., so the POS treatment is inconsistent.
items.correction: "partOfSpeech": "adj.", "korean": "(스스로) 인식된, 체감하는 (perceived age 체감 나이)". Alternatively keep 'v.' but add 'p.p. 형용사적 용법'.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-253-s002 (korean); same text inside the pr253-1.json instruction block
items.original: 만약 농부가 젖소의 먹이를 갑자기 바꾸면, 먼저 젖소의 체중이 감소할 것이다.
items.problem: The English says 'the cow may first lose weight', which is a possibility. The Korean '감소할 것이다' states it as a near-certain prediction. The next sentence renders the same modal correctly ('may give less milk' -> '줄어들 수 있다'), so the side-by-side view (Step 4 원문 대조) gives two different Korean equivalents for 'may' within two lines. The passage also switches between '소' (s001, s003) and '젖소' (s002, s004) for the same 'cow'.
items.correction: 만약 농부가 소의 먹이를 갑자기 바꾸면, 소는 우선 체중이 줄 수 있다. (Update the pr253-1 instruction block too, because it is the joined Korean sentences. Optionally use one word, '소' or '젖소', throughout.)

items.locator: Step 3 cloze item 2, generated from readingSentences id reading-254-s002 (generator: src/lib/readingUtils.ts generateClozeItems, lines 713-746)
items.original: And we realize that our youngsters are ignorant of Latin, put Mussolini in the same category as Dostoevsky and cannot recite the Periodic Table by heart.
items.problem: The generator's target is always the middle word of 12 valid words, which is 'Dostoevsky'. So on every visit the learner is asked to fill in a proper name, not a vocabulary word. Distractors come from a lower-cased pool (readingUtils.ts:719), while the answer keeps its capital letter. The options are therefore 'Dostoevsky', 'youngsters', 'developing' and one of education/standards/mathematics/mussolini/frustrate. The answer is the only capitalized option, and when 'mussolini' is drawn it appears incorrectly in lower case.
items.correction: Keep proper nouns out of the target, for example by skipping words that are capitalized mid-sentence in validTargetWords (readingUtils.ts:728). Then this item would target a real word such as 'category' or 'ignorant'. Also keep the pool's original case for proper nouns, or leave them out of the pool.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-254-s001 (korean); same text inside the pr254-1.json instruction block
items.original: 우리 교육이 수학과 언어같은 기본 과목에 있어 높은 수준을 충족시키지 못하고 있다는 건 의심할 여지가 없다.
items.problem: 'basic skills' is rendered as '기본 과목' (basic subjects), which changes skills into school subjects. Also, '언어같은' should be spaced '언어 같은' under standard Korean spacing.
items.correction: 우리 교육이 수학과 언어 같은 기초 능력에서 높은 수준에 미치지 못한다는 것은 의심할 여지가 없다.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-254-s004 (korean); context sentence of vocab card 'frustrate'
items.original: 진정 그들의 자기표현의 기회를 좌절시키길 원하는가?
items.problem: 'frustrate their opportunities' means to block or thwart the opportunities. In Korean, '좌절시키다' takes a person or a plan as its object, so '기회를 좌절시키다' is an unnatural collocation. The card already gives the better sense '가로막다'. The double '의' also reads as translationese.
items.correction: 우리는 정말로 아이들이 자신을 표현할 기회를 가로막고 싶은가?

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-256-s004 (korean); context sentence of vocab cards 'medical' and 'offered'
items.original: 새로운 의료기술이 중병에 걸린 사람에게 희망과 심지어 생명조차 제공해 준다.
items.problem: 'New medical treatments have offered...' is translated with '의료기술' (medical technology) and the simple present '제공해 준다'. The 'medical' card, whose context is this sentence, glosses 'medical treatments' as '치료법'.
items.correction: 새로운 치료법은 중병을 앓는 사람들에게 희망을, 심지어 생명 그 자체를 주었다.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-256-s006 (korean); context sentence of vocab cards 'ethical', 'troubling', 'created'
items.original: 그러나 기술의 엄청난 가능성이 똑같이 골치 아픈 도덕적 문제를 야기하고 있다.
items.problem: 'ethical' is translated as '도덕적', but the next sentence (s007) and the 'ethical' card, whose context is this sentence, both use '윤리적'. 'have created' is also given in the present progressive ('야기하고 있다').
items.correction: 그러나 기술의 엄청난 가능성은 그만큼 골치 아픈 윤리적 문제들을 낳았다.

items.locator: readingSentences id reading-256-s008 (korean); same text inside the pr256-1.json instruction block; also the context sentence of vocab card 'decide'
items.original: 그렇다면, 어디에 한계선을 그어야 하는가?
items.problem: The English is 'If so, how do we decide where to draw the line?' The Korean leaves out 'how do we decide' and turns the question into 'where should we draw the line?'. The passage is asking about the process of deciding, a point it continues in 'And who should decide?'. This is also the context sentence for the vocab card 'decide' (freq 2), so the learner sees 'decide' highlighted in a sentence whose translation has no counterpart for it.
items.correction: 그렇다면, 어디에 선을 그을지 어떻게 정하는가? (Update the pr256-1 instruction block too.)

items.locator: readingVocabulary card #11 'according' (same pattern in pr021, pr077, pr085, pr117, pr124 — outside this scope)
items.original: according | according | adv. | (according to) ~에 따르면
items.problem: The meaning shown is the prepositional phrase 'according to' (~에 따르면), and dictionaries classify 'according to' as a preposition. Labelling the card 'adv.' is wrong for the way it is used in the sentence ('according to American law').
items.correction: partOfSpeech: 'prep.' (and word 'according to' if the card format allows it). Apply the same fix to the other five 'according' cards course-wide.

items.original: Dr. Hilton Kline has done studies indicating that, in some cases, warts and pimples get worse with anxiety.
items.problem: I found no record of a researcher named 'Dr. Hilton Kline'. The closest real match is Milton V. Kline, a psychologist who published on hypnosis for skin conditions, including warts in children. The name may be garbled or invented. The findings are presented as real research: pimples before exams, and 'He's also shown that warts can be cured through hypnosis'. The hypnosis-for-warts evidence is mixed. Published studies report partial success rates of about 27-55%, which is not an established cure.
items.correction: Expert or editorial check. Either confirm the source, or de-personalize the claims ('Studies have indicated that...'; 'Some studies suggest that warts can be helped by hypnosis...'). Update the Korean ('Hilton Kline 박사는' → '연구들에 따르면') and regenerate the audio for any changed English sentence.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-095-s005 korean (and pr095-1.json instruction); vocab card #12 'effective'
items.original: EN: That would, according to him, depend on how effective governments were in dealing with their economic problems. / KO: 그에 의하면, 그것은 정부가 그들의 경제적 문제들을 얼마나 효율적으로 다루느냐에 달려 있다고 한다.
items.problem: 'effective' means 효과적인, but the translation uses '효율적으로', which means 'efficient(ly)'. The vocabulary card for the same word says 'effective | 효과적인', so the sentence translation contradicts the card. Effective vs efficient is a classic confusable pair for Korean learners.
items.correction: KO s005: '그에 의하면, 그것은 각국 정부가 경제 문제에 얼마나 효과적으로 대처하느냐에 달려 있다고 한다.' Update the same text in pr095-1.json's instruction block.

items.original: Upon closer analysis, “emerging” countries are not only vastly different from one another, they are also composed of numerous unique individuals and communities.
items.problem: Two independent clauses are joined only by a comma after 'not only ...' with no 'but'. This is a comma splice, and the correlative 'not only ... but also' is left incomplete in a formal expository text that learners copy as a model.
items.correction: 'Upon closer analysis, “emerging” countries are not only vastly different from one another but also composed of numerous unique individuals and communities.' The Korean needs no change. Regenerate the audio for the sentence.

items.original: Mother’s singing can help. / Some children, especially boys, like to have their own music players and may play these for very long periods of time.
items.problem: The childcare advice assumes the mother is the caregiver and makes an unsupported gender generalization ('especially boys'). It is mild, but it reads as dated in a commercial product for adults.
items.correction: Editorial decision for the owner. For example: 'A parent’s singing can help.' / 'Some children like to have their own music players...' (KO: '부모의 노래가... / 어떤 아이들은...'). Regenerate the audio for the changed sentences.

items.original: rhymes | rhyme | n. | 동요 (nursery rhymes)
items.problem: 'rhyme' on its own means 운(韻) or a short rhyming verse. It means 동요 only in the phrase 'nursery rhyme'. With the gloss printed as the word's meaning, a learner will memorize rhyme = 동요.
items.correction: korean: '(nursery rhyme) 동요, 전래 동시' or '운, 운문 (nursery rhymes 동요)'.

items.original: Item 1: Water, which is _______ for life, costs nothing. / Item 2: On the other hand, diamonds, which are _______ for nothing, cost a lot." (both answers 'essential')
items.problem: Two of the three cloze items have the same answer, 'essential', and nearly the same options (certainly + 2 of diamonds/writer's). Once item 1 is answered, its feedback gives away item 2.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, skip a target already used by an earlier item in the same lesson (take the next valid word).

items.original: #1 EN: An eighteenth-century scholar said, "Water, which is essential for life, costs nothing. / #2 EN: On the other hand, diamonds, which are essential for nothing, cost a lot." (KO #1 ends with an open 「"」, KO #2 closes it)
items.problem: The sentence split runs through the middle of a quotation, so row #1 has an unclosed quotation mark and row #2 has a stray closing mark, in both English and Korean. Row #1 is also the passage's pronunciation-test sentence (S[0]), which shows the unbalanced quote.
items.correction: Either merge s001 and s002 into one sentence row (EN and KO), or rewrite as reported speech (see the previous finding) so that each row is self-contained.

items.original: An eighteenth-century scholar said, "Water, which is essential for life, costs nothing. / On the other hand, diamonds, which are essential for nothing, cost a lot." / ...a writer's comment, "When the well's dry, we know the worth of it."
items.problem: Both passages inside quotation marks are not the original wording. Adam Smith (Wealth of Nations, 1776) wrote 'Nothing is more useful than water: but it will purchase scarcely anything...', so the passage gives a paraphrase in direct-quote form. Franklin's proverb (Poor Richard's Almanack, 1746) is 'When the well's dry, we know the worth of water'; the passage changes 'water' to 'it'. The facts themselves (18th century, over 200 years ago) are correct.
items.correction: Remove the quotation marks and use reported speech ('An eighteenth-century scholar observed that water, which is essential for life, costs nothing, while diamonds...'), or quote the originals exactly. For s005 use '...we know the worth of water.' Regenerate the audio for the changed sentences.

items.original: In an experiment on their behavior, baby monkeys were separated from their _______ at birth and provided with artificial mothers.
items.problem: The answer 'mothers' is still visible later in the same sentence ('artificial mothers'), so the blank can be answered without reading. This is already noted as an observation in docs/qa-2026-09-18/maps/reading.md:277, but not as a fix.
items.correction: In generateClozeItems, skip a target that occurs more than once in the sentence (or mask every occurrence).

items.original: Some of their artificial mothers were made of cold, hard wire while others were made of warm, soft towel cloth.
items.problem: In Harlow's 1958 experiment the wire surrogate was also heated. Harlow wrote that the wire mother 'is warmed by radiant heat' and 'differs in no essential way from that of the cloth mother surrogate other than in the quality of the contact comfort'. Contrasting 'cold' with 'warm' suggests warmth was the variable, when the experiment isolated touch (contact comfort), which is the point of the passage's last sentence.
items.correction: '...were made of bare, hard wire while others were covered with soft towel cloth.' KO: '일부는 딱딱한 철사로만 되어 있었고 다른 일부는 부드러운 수건 천으로 싸여 있었다.' Regenerate the audio for the changed sentence.

items.original: The capacity to store and distribute information has increased through the use of computers and other devices. Thus, personal information has been collected and distributed without control, causing harm to the right to privacy.
items.problem: Two sentences are merged into one row, so this 3-row passage has one 36-word unit. The learner map flagged it for content review (pr143#3).
items.correction: Split after 'devices.' into two rows, with the Korean split to match: '정보의 축적과 배포 능력은 컴퓨터와 다른 장비의 사용을 통해 커졌다.' / '그 결과, 사적 정보는 통제되지 않고 수집 및 배포되어, 사생활에 대한 권리가 침해되고 있다.' Renumber and regenerate the clips.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-143-s003 korean (second half); also the pr143-1 instruction block
items.original: 그 결과, 사적 정보는 통제되지 않고 수집 및 배포되어, 개인의 사생활에 해를 끼치고 있다.
items.problem: The English says 'causing harm to the right to privacy', but the Korean drops 'right' (권리) and says only '개인의 사생활'. 'right' is a card in this passage (권리, freq 2) and is the key term of the passage. Its second occurrence has no counterpart in the translation.
items.correction: 그 결과, 개인 정보가 통제 없이 수집되고 배포되어, 사생활에 대한 권리가 침해되고 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-146-s002 korean and reading-146-s006 korean; also the pr146-1 instruction block
items.original: 구 모델이 고장나자마자 새 모델을 산다면 그들은 돈을 더 많이 벌 것이다. / 새 것을 살 수 있는데 왜 헌 것을 수리해야 하는가?
items.problem: The Korean spacing is non-standard. '새것' and '헌것' are single words and are written closed. '고장 나다' is two words and is written open. This passage's own 'fails' card already spells it '고장 나다', so the sentence and the card disagree.
items.correction: 구 모델이 고장 나자마자 새 모델을 산다면 그들은 돈을 더 많이 벌 것이다. / 새것을 살 수 있는데 왜 헌것을 수리해야 하는가?

items.original: This has been mainly caused by the drift of large numbers of people from the rural areas. These people have become dissatisfied with the traditional life of farming, and have come to the cities hoping for better work and pay.
items.problem: Two full sentences sit in one sentence row, and its Korean also holds two sentences. Every other row in this passage is one sentence. The sentence steps (listening, shadowing, hover translation) therefore treat a 38-word, two-sentence block as one unit. The learner map (maps/reading.md §2) flagged this row as 'possible merged sentences — content review'.
items.correction: Split into two rows. s002a: 'This has been mainly caused by the drift of large numbers of people from the rural areas.' / '이는 주로 많은 사람이 농촌 지역을 떠나온 데서 비롯되었다.' s002b: 'These people have become dissatisfied with the traditional life of farming, and have come to the cities hoping for better work and pay.' / '이런 사람들은 전통적인 농업 생활에 만족하지 못해서, 더 나은 직업과 보수를 바라며 대도시로 몰려들었다.' Renumber the ids and regenerate the clips.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-147-s002 korean; also the pr147-1 instruction block
items.original: 이는 주로 주로 많은 사람이 농촌 지역을 떠나온 데서 비롯되었다.
items.problem: The adverb '주로' is doubled, which is a typo. It shows in the sentence translation and on the -1 script page.
items.correction: 이는 주로 많은 사람이 농촌 지역을 떠나온 데서 비롯되었다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-147-s003 korean; also the pr147-1 instruction block
items.original: 그러나, 불행히도 주택 문제, 위생 악화, 실업 등의 도시 지역의 악조건이 빈곤, 질병, 범죄의 증가를 가져왔다.
items.problem: The English is a general present-tense statement ('poor conditions ... bring about an increase'), but the Korean puts it in the past ('가져왔다'). 'lack of housing' is also rendered only loosely as '주택 문제'.
items.correction: 그러나 불행히도 주택 부족, 위생 악화, 실업 같은 도시 지역의 열악한 여건은 빈곤, 질병, 범죄의 증가를 초래한다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-147-s005 korean; also the pr147-1 instruction block
items.original: 이는 사람들이 농촌으로 가서 일하도록 유인책 제공함으로써 달성될 수 있다.
items.problem: The object particle is missing: '유인책 제공함으로써' is ungrammatical Korean.
items.correction: 이는 사람들이 농촌으로 가서 일하도록 유인책을 제공함으로써 달성될 수 있다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-147-s007 korean; also the pr147-1 instruction block
items.original: 농촌 지역의 선행적 발전 없이는 도시 자체는 발전할 수 없기에, 농촌 지역의 개선은 두 배는 더 중요하다.
items.problem: 'doubly important' here means important on two counts: for rural people and, as the because-clause explains, for the cities. The literal '두 배는 더 중요하다' reads as a quantity ('twice as much more') and is unnatural. The translation also says '농촌 지역의 개선' where the English says 'The improvement of rural life'.
items.correction: 도시 자체도 농촌 지역이 먼저 발전하지 않고는 발전할 수 없기 때문에, 농촌 생활의 개선은 더욱더(이중으로) 중요하다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-148-s001 (english + korean); also the pr148 instruction block and the pr148-1 instruction block
items.original: In the United States, about 10 million computers are thrown away every year! / 미국에서는 매년 약 1,000만 대의 컴퓨터가 버려지고 있다!
items.problem: The sentence gives a fixed figure in the present tense, as if it were current, but the number is decades old and far too low. The National Safety Council, as cited in CRS report RL31505, projected 500 million PCs becoming obsolete in the US between 1997 and 2007, about 50 million a year. Scientific American (2007) reported that US users 'scrap about 133,000 PCs daily', about 48 million a year. Every source from the 2000s onward gives tens of millions, not 10 million.
items.correction: Either date the claim or remove the exact number. For example: 'In the United States, tens of millions of computers are thrown away every year!' / '미국에서는 매년 수천만 대의 컴퓨터가 버려진다!' Update the pr148 and pr148-1 instruction blocks to match. Because the English text changes, regenerate the sentence clip in the same change with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-148-s002 korean; also the pr148-1 instruction block
items.original: 원치 않는 대부분의 컴퓨터가 쓰레기장으로 보내지기 때문에 심각한 문제를 야기해 왔다.
items.problem: The English says only 'they have caused a problem', but the Korean adds '심각한' (serious). The Korean also leaves out the subject 'they' (the computers), so the sentence reads without a clear subject.
items.correction: 쓸모없어진 컴퓨터 대부분이 쓰레기 매립장으로 보내지기 때문에, 그것들은 문제를 일으켜 왔다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-149-s002 korean; also the pr149-1 instruction block
items.original: 빈부 격차와 같은 많은 갈등이 깊이 뿌리박힌 신념 아래에서 벌어진다.
items.problem: 'struggles such as rich versus poor' means conflicts between the rich and the poor. '빈부 격차' means 'the wealth gap', which is a condition, not a struggle, so the list '빈부 격차와 같은 많은 갈등' does not hold together logically.
items.correction: 부자 대 빈자의 대립과 같은 많은 투쟁이 깊이 자리 잡은 신념을 앞세워 벌어진다.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-149-s005 english; also the pr149 instruction block
items.original: One of the major problems we face both as individuals and as a society is simplistic thinking―or the failure to think at all.
items.problem: The dash is U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR, a Korean-keyboard artifact, not an English em dash (U+2014). It has no spaces around it, so whitespace tokenizers treat 'thinking―or' as one word. readingUtils.ts:716-719 builds the cloze distractor pool with split(/\s+/) and keeps inner punctuation, so this token can enter the pool. The same character appears in 11 other reading files, as a note for the owner.
items.correction: One of the major problems we face both as individuals and as a society is simplistic thinking—or the failure to think at all. (U+2014 em dash). If the audio key hashes the text, regenerate the clip.

items.locator: readingSentences reading-149-s005 korean; also the pr149-1 instruction block
items.original: 우리가 개인으로서, 그리고 사회로서 직면한 주요 문제 중 하나는 단순한 사고방식, 혹은 생각하기를 아예 포기하는 것이다.
items.problem: 'simplistic' is pejorative ('overly simple'), and this passage's own card gives '지나치게 단순한'. The sentence translation has the neutral '단순한', which loses the criticism. 'the failure to think at all' means 'not thinking at all', not '포기하는 것' (giving up).
items.correction: 우리가 개인으로서, 그리고 사회로서 직면한 주요 문제 중 하나는 지나치게 단순한 사고, 혹은 아예 생각하지 않는 것이다.

items.original: "I am Korean." / "He is Japanese." / "You are American." / "She is Filipino." / "It is yours."
items.problem: Several common, correct variants grade incorrect (0): "I am a Korean.", "You are an American.", "She is Filipina." / "She is a Filipina." (Filipina is the dictionary word for a Filipino woman), and "That is yours." for 그것은 당신의 것이다. "He is a Japanese." is also 0, but is best left unaccepted.
items.correction: Add the alternatives "I am a Korean.", "You are an American.", "She is Filipina.", "She is a Filipina." and "That is yours."

items.original: KO "7시이다." / EN "It is seven o'clock."
items.problem: The prompt writes the time as the digit 7. The grader does not treat digits and number words as equal, so "It's 7 o'clock." and "It is 7 o'clock." are graded incorrect (0 points). Both are standard written English. This is a free lesson that new users see first.
items.correction: Add the alternative "It is 7 o'clock." The grader already expands "It's", so this also covers "It's 7 o'clock."

items.locator: gh1-006 #24 (gh1-006.json, gh1-006-2.json; EN gh1-007.json, gh1-007-2.json); gh1-012 #35 (gh1-012.json, gh1-012-2.json; EN gh1-013.json, gh1-013-2.json)
items.original: KO "그는 무엇이냐? (신분이나 직업을 묻는 말)" / EN "What is he?"; KO "그는 무엇이었니? (뭐하는 사람이었니?)" / EN "What was he?"
items.problem: The note teaches "What is he?" as the way to ask about someone's job or status. In everyday English, the usual job question is "What does he do?" or "What's his job?". A bare "What is he?" is unusual for this and can sound like a question about what kind of being he is, or his ethnicity. The natural forms are graded incorrect: "What does he do?" and "What did he do?" both score 0.
items.correction: Add the alternatives "What does he do?" and "What is his job?" (#24), and "What did he do?", "What did he do for a living?" and "What was his job?" (#35). Better still, make those the model answers and keep "What is he?" / "What was he?" as alternatives. Reword the note, for example: (직업을 물을 때는 보통 What does he do?).

items.original: "1. I was poor."
items.problem: An extraction remnant (the item number) is still inside the answer text. The view strips it, but the clip generator keys the raw text (maps/grammar1.md §6.1), so a regeneration would key the wrong string. Production playback of the stripped clip was verified as 206 on 2026-09-16 (NEW-04).
items.correction: "I was poor." (the key of the stripped text is unchanged, so no new clip is needed).

items.original: KO "그것들은 그들의 펜들이었다." / EN "Those were their pens." (no alternatives)
items.problem: The present-tense twin, gh1-007 #9, accepts "They are their pens.", but here "They were their pens." gets only partial credit (70). The two lessons are inconsistent.
items.correction: Add the alternative "They were their pens."

items.original: "그녀는 결혼 했었니? (기혼이었니?)"
items.problem: 결혼하다 is one word, so there should be no space before 했었니. gh1-006 #15 correctly writes 결혼했나.
items.correction: "그녀는 결혼했었니? (기혼이었니?)"

items.original: KO "결혼 전 그녀의 성은 무엇이었니?" / EN "What was her maiden name?" (no alternatives)
items.problem: "maiden name" is vocabulary this beginner be-verb lesson never teaches. A correct paraphrase such as "What was her last name before she got married?" grades incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add the alternatives "What was her last name before she got married?" and "What was her family name before marriage?", or add a hint (maiden name) to the KO prompt.

items.original: #24 KO "그녀는 어디 있었니?" / EN "Where was she?"; #34 KO "그녀는 어디 있었니?" / EN "Where was she?"
items.problem: The exercise asks the same item twice. In the parallel present-tense lesson (gh1-006), #24 is a different sentence ("What is he?").
items.correction: Replace #24 with the past-tense counterpart of gh1-006 #24, for example KO "그는 무엇을 하는 사람이었니?" / EN "What did he do?" (or "What was he?"). Generate the new clip.

items.locator: #39 (KO in gh1-008.json and gh1-008-2.json; EN in gh1-009.json and gh1-009-2.json)
items.original: KO "그때는 7시였다." / EN "It was seven o'clock."
items.problem: The Korean prompt says 그때는 (then), but the model answer has no "then". A faithful answer, "It was seven o'clock then.", has 5 words, which is more than 4 × 1.15, so the grader marks it incorrect. The prompt also writes the time as the digit 7, and the grader does not treat "7" as equal to "seven", so "It was 7 o'clock." is also incorrect.
items.correction: Make the model "It was seven o'clock then." and add these alternatives: "It was seven o'clock.", "It was 7 o'clock then.", "It was 7 o'clock." Or remove 그때는 from the prompt and add only the digit alternative. Regenerate the Ava clip for any changed English text.

items.original: "Didn't I have a dream?" … "Didn't they like it?" (#38 and #39 carry alternatives "Was there not a boy?" / "Were there not boys?")
items.problem: The uncontracted negative question is accepted for #38 and #39 but not for #40–#46. "Did I not have a dream?" and "Did you not like it?" get only partial credit (70).
items.correction: Add the uncontracted alternatives to #40–#46: "Did I not have a dream?", "Did you not have a dream?", "Did he not have a dream?", "Did they not have dreams?", "Did you not like it?", "Did he not like it?", "Did they not like it?".

items.original: #2 KO "이 사람은 나의 친구이다." / EN "This is my friend."; #32 KO "왜 너는 나를 보니?" / EN "Why do you look at me?"
items.problem: "This person is my friend." is a literal, correct translation of 이 사람은, but scores 0. For #32, the everyday reading of 왜 나를 보니? is the ongoing action, "Why are you looking at me?", which also scores 0. The simple-present model reads as a habitual action.
items.correction: Add the alternatives "This person is my friend." and "Why are you looking at me?"

items.original: "Whom does he know?" / "Whom do they know?" / "Whom do you love?"
items.problem: Object "who" is the normal everyday form, and "whom" is formal. "Who does he know?", "Who do they know?" and "Who do you love?" get only partial credit (70).
items.correction: Add the alternatives "Who does he know?", "Who do they know?" and "Who do you love?".

items.original: KO "너는 어떤 것을 원하나?" / EN "Which do you want?" alternatives ["What do you want?"]
items.problem: 어떤 것 means "which one". The most natural English, "Which one do you want?", has 5 words, which is more than the 4 × 1.15 length cap, so the grader marks it incorrect.
items.correction: Add the alternative "Which one do you want?" (it could also be the model answer).

items.original: #15 "너는 점심을 먹지 않았지 (안 먹었지?)"; #40 "그는 그의 아들 각각에게 돈을 주었다"
items.problem: #15 is a question, but its main clause has no question mark (only the parenthesis does). #40 has no final period, unlike every other prompt.
items.correction: #15 "너는 점심을 먹지 않았지? (안 먹었지?)"; #40 "그는 그의 아들 각각에게 돈을 주었다."

items.original: "He wants much money, doesn't he?" alternatives ["He wants a lot of money, doesn't he?"]
items.problem: The fix for G1-11 added the natural form as an alternative, but the unnatural affirmative "much money" is still what is shown and spoken as the 모범 답안, in all 4 steps.
items.correction: Swap them: make the model "He wants a lot of money, doesn't he?" and keep "much money" as the alternative. The model clip must be regenerated.

items.original: #17 "She needs a little money, doesn't she?"; #19 "I want apples." alternatives ["I want an apple."]; #31 "I am home."; #42 "They loved each other."
items.problem: Common correct variants lose points. "She needs some money, doesn't she?" → partial. "I want some apples." → 0. "I am at home." → 0, although the prompt's first meaning is 집에 있다. "They loved one another." → 0.
items.correction: Add the alternatives "She needs some money, doesn't she?", "I want some apples.", "I am at home." and "They loved one another."

items.original: #20 KO "그도 그래." / EN "So does he."; #22 KO "그녀도 그래." / EN "So is she."; #26 KO "나도 그래." / EN "Neither do I."
items.problem: The same lesson accepts both reply patterns elsewhere: #32 accepts "I am, too." and "So am I.", and #36 accepts "I don't either." and "Neither do I.". Here only the So/Neither form is accepted. "He does, too.", "She is, too." and "I don't either." all grade incorrect (0), although they are equally correct. Also, the three identical prompts "…도 그래." depend on the item before them, and nothing in the prompt says so.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #20 "He does, too."; #22 "She is, too."; #26 "I don't either." Optionally add a hint such as (앞 문장에 대한 대답) to these prompts.

items.original: KO "아무도 그것을 좋아하지 않아." / EN "Nobody likes it."
items.problem: "No one likes it." is equally standard, but it has 4 words against 3, which goes over the length cap, so it grades incorrect (0). The 2026-09-17 fix (G1-41) already accepts "No one" in gh1-096.
items.correction: Add the alternative "No one likes it."

items.original: KO "누구는 좋아하나?" / EN "Who does?"
items.problem: Nothing in the prompt signals that an elliptical reply is expected. "Who likes it?" and "Who does like it?" are correct translations, but both grade incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add the alternatives "Who likes it?" and "Who does like it?", or add a hint such as (앞 문장에 이어서, 짧게).

items.original: KO "모든 학생이 각각 자기 방이 있다. (each)" / EN "Each student has his own room."
items.problem: The only accepted answer uses generic "his" for a student of unspecified gender. Current style guides recommend singular "their" instead. "Each student has their own room." is only partial (70), and "Each student has his or her own room." is incorrect (0).
items.correction: Make the model "Each student has their own room." and add the alternatives "Each student has his or her own room." and "Each student has his own room."

items.original: KO "모두(각각) 서로를 미워했다.(each)" / EN "Each hated the other."
items.problem: "Each hated the other" means exactly two people ("the other" = the one other person). The prompt says 모두, which suggests a group of more than two. The natural translation, "They hated each other.", grades incorrect (0).
items.correction: Either change the KO to "둘은 각각 서로를 미워했다. (each)", or change the EN to "Each hated the others." In both cases add the alternative "They hated each other."

items.locator: Answer data layout: gh1-015.json has two sentences blocks (#1–#23, then #24–#43); gh1-015-2.json has a block holding only #23, then #24–#43
items.original: gh1-015.json block 3 ends {"n":"23","text":"She is beautiful, isn't she?"…}; block 4 starts {"n":"24","text":"Who doesn't like it?"}. gh1-015-2.json block 1 = only {"n":"23","text":"She is beautiful, isn't she?","alternatives":["She looks beautiful, doesn't she?"]}
items.problem: The whole-lesson top player reads only the FIRST sentences block (src/app/[course]/[lesson]/page.tsx:482-484). So on gh1-014 it plays 23 of the 43 answers, and on gh1-014-2 it plays 1 of 21. The step views flatten the blocks, so the item lists look complete.

items.original: #1 "He enjoys every minute of the trip." items.original: It is a book.
items.problem: For singular 그것 only "it" is accepted. For plural 그것들 the same lessons use "Those" as the main answer (gh1-023 n=8 "Those are books.", gh1-025 n=32 "Are those books?"). A learner who carries 그것들=those over to 그것=that writes "That is a book." / "Is that a book?" / "Isn't that a book?" / "That was not a book.", and each of these grades only PARTIAL (70). "That" is a standard dictionary sense of 그것. Other answers on the same items: "It is a cat." (gh1-021 n=12), "It is not a book.", "Is it a book?", "Isn't it a book?", "It was a book.", "It was not a book.", "Was it a book?", "Wasn't it a book?".
items.correction: Add the "that" form as an alternative on each listed item. Examples: "That is a cat.", "That is a book.", "That is not a book.", "Is that a book?", "Isn't that a book?" / "Is that not a book?", and the past-tense equivalents ("That was a book.", "Was that a book?", "Wasn't that a book?" / "Was that not a book?", "That was not a book.").

Target auxiliary never blanked: gh1-021 n=23,24; gh1-025 n=45,47,48; gh1-029 n=45,47,48; gh1-031 n=11,13,15,17,18. Cause: src/components/GrammarLearningView.tsx:30-40 and 75-115 (buildCloze)
items.original: Isn't he a boy?
items.problem: buildCloze splits on the apostrophe, and GRAMMAR_KEYWORDS contains no contractions. In negative questions and don't/doesn't sentences, the blank is therefore either half a word or not the target structure. (1) The blank is "Isn", "Aren", "Wasn", "Weren", "don" or "doesn", shown as ___ ' t. Typing the natural whole word "Isn't", "Aren't", "don't" or "doesn't" is marked ✗ (gradeAnswer("Isn't","Isn") = incorrect); only the fragment "isn" is accepted. (2) In "Aren't I your friend?", "Isn't this a pen?", "Aren't those books?" and "She doesn't love your brother.", the contracted auxiliary these lessons teach stays visible and the blank falls on your / this / these / those / my / his / her instead.
items.correction: Treat a contraction as one cloze token (e.g. split on /(\s+|[.,?!;:"()]+)/ without the apostrophe) and add isn't, aren't, wasn't, weren't, don't, doesn't, didn't to GRAMMAR_KEYWORDS. Alternatively, grade a typed full contraction against the whole token. This is code-level: the same pattern affects every contraction item in the course, beyond this scope.

items.original: 그들은 책들이 아니었다.
items.problem: 그들 means 'they' for people, so the prompt says "they (people) were not books". Every parallel item in this drill uses 그것들 for books: gh1-022 n=24 "그것들은 책들이 아니다.", gh1-026 n=8 "그것들은 책들이었다.", n=23 "이것들은 펜들이 아니었다.". The answer's alternative "Those were not books." also shows the source meant 그것들. The prompt is a typo that blurs the 그들 (people) / 그것들 (things) distinction the drill relies on.
items.correction: 그것들은 책들이 아니었다.

items.original: 그는 그녀의 누이를 사랑한다.  /  그는 그녀의 누이를 사랑하지 않는다.
items.problem: 누이 is the word a male uses for his own sister (표준국어대사전 / 한국어기초사전: '남자가 여자 형제를 이르는 말'). "그녀의 누이" (her 누이) is therefore a misuse in Korean. The English "He loves her sister." is fine.
items.correction: 그는 그녀의 여동생을 사랑한다. / 그는 그녀의 여동생을 사랑하지 않는다. (or 언니; English answer unchanged, optionally add "her younger sister" as an alternative)

items.original: gh1-032 #26 "그가 그녀의 누이를 사랑하나?"; gh1-032 #35 "그가 그녀의 누이를 사랑하지 않나?"; gh1-040 #44 "그는 그녀의 누이를 사랑하지?"; gh1-042 #31 "그가 그녀의 누이를 사랑하지 않나?"
items.problem: 누이 means a man's sister (남자의 여자 형제), so 그녀의 누이 ('her sister' said with a male-sibling word) is a contradiction in Korean. The English answers ('her sister') are fine; only the Korean prompt is unnatural. Items such as '나의 누이' and '너의 누이' are acceptable and are not included here.
items.correction: Change 그녀의 누이 to 그녀의 언니 or 그녀의 여동생 (for example "그가 그녀의 언니를 사랑하나?"). Leave the English answers unchanged, so no clip is affected.

Read literally, "그들은 그들의 것들이다" says that some people belong to them. The answer 'Those are theirs.' (the main answer in gh1-043) does not translate 그들, so learners get a wrong picture of 그들 versus 그것들. That contrast is the point of these pronoun drills. The same prompt also has its main answer and alternative swapped between gh1-033 and gh1-043. For #49, the natural 'Aren't those yours?' grades only partial.

items.original: "n": "24", "text": "그녀는 무엇이냐?"  →  "What is she?"
items.problem: Without context, '그녀는 무엇이냐?' does not read as a question about someone's job, and 'What is she?' about a person is ambiguous in modern English. It can sound like asking what kind of being, or what ethnicity, she is. The course's own earlier items explain the intent: gh1-006 n24 '그는 무엇이냐? (신분이나 직업을 묻는 말)' and gh1-012 n35 '(뭐하는 사람이었니?)'. This review item drops that note. The standard job question, 'What does she do?', scores INCORRECT.
items.correction: Change the prompt to "그녀는 무엇이냐? (직업을 묻는 말)". Add alternatives "What does she do?" and "What does she do for a living?". Changing the Korean prompt does not affect English audio clips.

items.original: "n": "24", "text": "그녀는 무엇이었니?"  →  "What was she?"
items.problem: This is the same issue as gh1-050 n24, in the past tense. The job-meaning hint that gh1-012 n35 gives ('(뭐하는 사람이었니?)') is missing. 'What was she?' is ambiguous about a person, and 'What did she do (for a living)?' is not accepted (measured: incorrect).
items.correction: Change the prompt to "그녀는 무엇이었니? (직업을 묻는 말)". Add alternatives "What did she do for a living?" and "What was her job?".

items.locator: gh1-053 n18 (prompt gh1-052 n18 '그들은 아팠니?(병이 있었니?)'); also gh1-053-1
items.original: "n": "18", "text": "Were they sick?" (no alternatives)
items.problem: 'Were they ill?' is the standard British English answer, and the prompt's own note '(병이 있었니?)' points to ill health. The real grader scores it INCORRECT (3 words, so no partial credit).
items.correction: Add the alternative "Were they ill?" in gh1-053 and gh1-053-1.

items.locator: gh1-055 n7 (prompt gh1-054 n7 '그는 하나의 자전거를 갖고 있다.'); also gh1-055-1
items.original: "n": "7", "text": "He has a bicycle."
items.problem: 'He has a bike.' is a very common, correct translation of 자전거, but the grader scores it INCORRECT.
items.correction: Add the alternative "He has a bike." in gh1-055 and gh1-055-1.

items.locator: gh1-055 n24, n28, n29, n30, n32, n33, n35 (prompts contain 그것을); also gh1-055-1 / gh1-055-2
items.original: "He knows it." / "Does he want it?" / "Do you want it?" / "I wanted it." / "He knew it." / "They wanted it." / "Did I want it?"
items.problem: 그것 translates as both 'it' and 'that'. This course accepts 'that' for 그것 in neighbouring review lessons: gh1-051 n12 'That is mine.', n28, n32; gh1-053 n11, n32; gh1-057 n8, n9 and n12 'Why did he study that?'. Here 'that' is not accepted. Measured: 'He knows that.', 'I wanted that.', 'He knew that.' and 'They wanted that.' are INCORRECT. 'Does he want that?', 'Do you want that?' and 'Did I want that?' are only partial.
items.correction: Add a 'that' alternative to each: "He knows that.", "Does he want that?", "Do you want that?", "I wanted that.", "He knew that.", "They wanted that.", "Did I want that?". Make the same change in gh1-055-1/-2. Course-wide, 114 그것 items accept only 'it', so the owner may prefer one it/that policy for the whole course.

items.original: "Wasn't there water?" / "Weren't there girls?" / "Didn't I have money?" / "Didn't you have a vision?" / "Didn't he have lunch?" / "Didn't they have dinner?" / "Didn't you love her?" / "Didn't he know her?" / "Didn't they know me?"
items.problem: gh1-045 n42-n45 and n70-n79, and gh1-057 n14, accept the uncontracted forms ('Is this not mine?', 'Why were you not studying English?') as exact. gh1-055 has no alternatives, so 'Did he not know her?', 'Did I not have money?' and 'Was there not water?' score only partial.
items.correction: Add the uncontracted alternative to each item, e.g. "Was there not water?", "Were there not girls?", "Did I not have money?", "Did you not have a vision?", "Did you not love her?", "Did he not know her?", "Did they not know me?". For n42/n43, see the 'eat' finding.

items.original: "n": "10", "text": "그 차는 나의 것이다"
items.problem: The final period is missing. Every other declarative prompt in the lesson ends with '.'.
items.correction: "그 차는 나의 것이다."

items.locator: gh1-056 n24 vs n35 (KO); gh1-057 n24 / n35 (EN); split pages gh1-056-2 / gh1-057-2
items.original: n24 "그들은 누구였나?" → "Who were they?"; n35 "그들은 누구였니?" → "Who were they?"
items.problem: n35 repeats n24 in the same lesson. Only the Korean ending differs (나 vs 니), and the English answer is identical.
items.correction: Replace n35 with a new wh-question, e.g. "그들은 어디에 살았니?" → "Where did they live?". Update gh1-056-2 and gh1-057-2, then generate the Ava clip.

items.original: "This lady did it." / "Why are you studying it?" / "Who likes it?" / "Who wants it?"
items.problem: In this same lesson, n12 '왜 그는 그것을 공부했나?' accepts "Why did he study that?", but the other 그것을 items do not accept 'that'. Measured: 'Who likes that?' and 'Who wants that?' are INCORRECT; 'This lady did that.' and 'Why are you studying that?' are only partial.
items.correction: Add alternatives: n11 "This lady did that."; n13 "Why are you studying that?"; n33 "Who likes that?"; n34 "Who wants that?".

items.locator: gh1-057 n26 (prompt gh1-056 n26 '그녀는 누구를 아나?'); also gh1-057-2
items.original: "n": "26", "text": "Whom does she know?" (no alternatives)
items.problem: 'Whom' as an object in a question is formal and old-fashioned. Everyday English uses 'Who does she know?', which is only partial here. The model answer presents the formal form as the only correct one, with no hint that 'who' is normal.
items.correction: Add the alternative "Who does she know?". Better still, make "Who does she know?" the main answer and keep "Whom does she know?" as the alternative. Changing the main text needs a new Ava clip (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs). The same pattern appears in gh1-013 n27/n28, gh1-015 n9 and gh1-059 n8, outside this scope.

items.locator: gh1-057 n32 (prompt gh1-056 n32 '왜 그는 그녀를 보니?'); also gh1-057-2
items.original: "n": "32", "text": "Why does he look at her?"
items.problem: 보다 can also mean 'watch'. 'Why does he watch her?' is a valid translation, but the grader scores it INCORRECT.
items.correction: Add the alternative "Why does he watch her?".

items.original: KO "그는 누구를 사랑하나?" EN "Whom does he love?"
items.problem: In everyday English, 'Who does he love?' is the normal form and 'whom' is formal. The grader gives 'Who does he love?' only partial credit (70), not full credit. The same gap exists outside this scope at gh1-012 #27/#28, gh1-014 #9 and gh1-056 #26.
items.correction: Add the alternative 'Who does he love?'. Optionally note that 'whom' is formal.

items.original: KO #19 "그는 사과를 원한다." EN "He wants apples." | KO #20 "나도 그래(나도 원해)" EN "So do I." | KO #21 "나의 어머니도 그래." EN "So does my mother."
items.problem: Korean does not mark plural, so 'He wants an apple.' and 'He wants some apples.' are valid for #19, but both grade 0. #20 and #21 give no cue that the 'So do I' structure is required, and the natural translations 'Me too.', 'I do too.' and 'My mother does too.' all grade 0.
items.correction: #19: add 'He wants an apple.' and 'He wants some apples.'. #20: either add 'Me too.' and 'I do too.' as alternatives or put a cue in the prompt (e.g. '(So ~ 구문)'). #21: add 'My mother does too.', or use the same cue.

items.original: gh1-059 #29 "Each student has his own idea." (alt "Every student has his own idea.") | #30 "Does each student have his own plan?" (alt "Does every student have his own plan?") | gh1-067 #57 "Does each student have his own room?"
items.problem: '자기 자신의' does not specify gender. Current standard usage (APA, Merriam-Webster, Purdue OWL) favours singular 'their', or 'his or her', over generic 'his'. The grader gives 'their own' only partial credit (70) and gives 0 to 'his or her own idea'. This is also inconsistent within the course: gh1-067 #76/#77 accept the 'didn't they?' tag after every/each boy.
items.correction: Add the alternatives 'Each student has their own idea.', 'Every student has their own idea.', 'Does each student have their own plan?', 'Does every student have their own plan?' and 'Does each student have their own room?'. Optionally also add the 'his or her' variants.

items.original: #1 "How did he go there?" | #18 "How do all the boys go there?" | #22 "How does she go there?"
items.problem: When asking about the means of travel (어떻게 그곳에 가나/갔나), the usual idiom is 'get there': 'How did he get there?', 'How does she get there?'. The grader gives these 0 (go/get are not treated as similar).
items.correction: Add the alternatives 'How did he get there?', 'How do all the boys get there?' and 'How does she get there?'.

items.original: KO #2 "그는 얼마나 빨리 그곳에 가나?" EN "How fast does he go there?" | KO #3 "그 소녀는 얼마나 빨리 여기에 오나?" EN "How fast does the girl come here?" | KO #9 "그는 가능한 한 빨리 여기에 왔다." EN "He came here as soon as possible."
items.problem: 빨리 covers both speed and earliness. 'How quickly does he go there?', 'How quickly/How soon does the girl come here?', 'He came here as quickly as possible.', 'He came here as fast as possible.' and 'He came here as soon as he could.' all grade 0. #3's model 'How fast does the girl come here?' (asking about her speed while coming) is also an odd question compared with 'How quickly does the girl get here?'.
items.correction: #2: add 'How quickly does he go there?'. #3: add 'How quickly does the girl come here?' and 'How soon does the girl come here?'. #9: add 'He came here as quickly as possible.', 'He came here as fast as possible.' and 'He came here as soon as he could.'.

items.original: #26 "Who loves you more than I?" (alt "Who loves you more than I do?") | #7 alts "He has more money than I do.", "He has more money than me."
items.problem: #7 accepts the everyday 'than me', but #26 does not, so 'Who loves you more than me?' gets only partial credit (70). This is inconsistent within one page.
items.correction: Add the alternative 'Who loves you more than me?', or note why 'than me' is avoided here (it could mean 'more than [they love] me').
