items.original: gh1-061 #31 alt "All of them don't like it." | gh1-069 #79 alt "Every boy didn't receive a prize, did he?" | #81 alt "All the boys didn't receive a prize, did they?" | #82 alt "All of them don't come." | #83 alt "All of them didn't come."
items.problem: These lessons contrast partial negation (모두가 ~하지는 않는다) with total negation (#84-87 아무도). The listed alternatives use 'All/Every + negative verb', which native speakers find ambiguous and often read as total negation ('none of them came'). They are shown to learners as '다른 정답' / '(또는: …)' and graded exact, which teaches that these forms reliably mean partial negation.
items.correction: Remove these alternatives and keep only the unambiguous 'Not all…/Not every…' forms. If the traditional reading is kept for leniency, add a note that 'All … not' is ambiguous and that 'Not all …' is the clear form.

items.original: #3 "Is your son healthy?" | #6 "Is my son healthy?" | #12 "Is your mother healthy?"
items.problem: When asking whether someone is in good health (건강한가/건강하시니), 'Is your mother well?' is the idiomatic form. It grades 0.
items.correction: Add the alternatives 'Is your son well?', 'Is my son well?' and 'Is your mother well?'.

items.original: gh1-062 #26 KO "당신의 아들과 딸은 꿈이 있습니까?" EN "Do your son and daughter have a dream?" (alts only vary sons/daughters) | gh1-064 #28 KO "당신의 아들은 꿈을 갖고 있지 않습니까? (단수로)" alt "Doesn't your son have dreams?"
items.problem: #26 has no '(단수로)' cue, unlike #25 and #33-38, and for two people 'Do your son and daughter have dreams?' is the more natural form. That answer grades 0. The rule is applied inconsistently: #27 accepts 'dreams', and #28 accepts 'dreams' even though its prompt explicitly says (단수로).
items.correction: Add the alternative 'Do your son and daughter have dreams?' to #26, or add '(단수로)' to its prompt. Make #28 consistent with its (단수로) cue: remove the 'dreams' alternative or remove the cue.

items.original: KO "왜 그 영국 여인이 그곳에 앉아있었습니까?" EN "Why was the British woman sitting there?"
items.problem: 영국 is commonly rendered 'English' by Korean learners, and 'Englishwoman' / 'English woman' is a standard dictionary rendering of 영국 여인. The grader gives 'Why was the English woman sitting there?' and 'Why was the Englishwoman sitting there?' 0.
items.correction: Add the alternatives 'Why was the English woman sitting there?' and 'Why was the Englishwoman sitting there?'.

items.original: KO #71 "그 모든(all) 소년이 한 상을 받는다." EN "All the boys receive a prize." | KO #74 "그 모든(all) 소년이 한 상을 받았다." EN "All the boys received a prize."
items.problem: 'All of the boys receive(d) a prize.' is equally correct, but it grades 0 because the short sentence plus one extra word goes over the length cap. In longer items (#78, gh1-069 #81) the same variant only gets partial credit.
items.correction: Add the alternatives 'All of the boys receive a prize.' (#71) and 'All of the boys received a prize.' (#74). Consider 'All of the boys…' alternatives for #78 and gh1-069 #81 as well.

items.original: e.g. #70 "모든(Every) 소년이 한 상(a prize)을 받는다." | #79 "모든(every) 소년이 한 상을 받지는 않았죠?"
items.problem: '한 상을 받는다' is translationese that mirrors English 'a prize'. Natural Korean is '상을 (하나) 받는다'. The (a prize) hint already tells the learner to use the article.
items.correction: Use '상을 하나 받는다' / '상을 받는다' and keep the (a prize) hint on #70.

items.locator: gh1-067 paragraph block after #63; gh1-069 paragraph blocks after #79, #80, #81 (sentences split into 2 and 4 blocks)
items.original: gh1-067 paragraph "63, She is happy, isn't she?" | gh1-069 paragraphs "Not every boy received a prize, did he?", "received a prize, did he?", "Not all the boys received a prize, did they?"
items.problem: These are leftover extraction fragments (one is truncated: 'received a prize, did he?'). The view does not render them. However, they split the answer sheets into several 'sentences' blocks, and the top 'whole lesson' player reads only the first block. Per maps/grammar1.md §12.2, the player on gh1-066 covers 10 of 25 sentences and on gh1-068 only 1 of 27. This has not been reproduced on production.
items.correction: Delete the four paragraph blocks and merge the sentences blocks of gh1-067 (n54-78) and gh1-069 (n79-105) into one block each. The English text does not change, so no clip regeneration is needed.

items.original: #88 "Were there 60 girls in the classroom?" | #89 "There were 60 girls in the classroom, weren't there?" | #90 "There weren't 60 girls in the classroom, were there?" | #105 "You study English more than ten hours every day, don't you?"
items.problem: The grader does not treat digits and words as equal. 'sixty' gets 0 on #88-#90 and '10 hours' gets 0 on #105. The prompts ('60명', '열 시간') do not tell the learner which form is expected, and this one page uses digits for one number and words for the other.
items.correction: Add the alternatives with 'sixty' to #88-#90 and 'You study English more than 10 hours every day, don't you?' to #105. Alternatively, make the grader treat numerals and number words as equal.

items.original: #8 KO "그 차는 그의 것이었다." -> "The car was his."; #22 KO "그 땅은 너의 것이었니?" -> "Was that land yours?"
items.problem: The same Korean '그 N' is modelled as 'the' in #8 and 'that' in #22, and neither item accepts the other. "That car was his." and "Was the land yours?" both get only partial (70). gh1-079 #10 shows the course's own fix of listing both.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #8 "That car was his."; #22 "Was the land yours?".

items.original: KO "그것들은 너의 것이었니?" -> EN "Were those yours?" (no alternatives)
items.problem: In the same lesson, #4 (그것들 -> Those/They) accepts 'They', and so does gh1-073 #2. #23 does not. "Were they yours?" is correct and is graded incorrect (0, LCS 2/3 < 0.7).
items.correction: Add alternative "Were they yours?".

items.original: #16 "그들은 어디에 있었니?" / "Where were they?"; #26 "그들은 어디에 있었니?" / "Where were they?"
items.problem: The same prompt and answer appear twice in one 28-item lesson. The same sentence also appeared one lesson earlier (gh1-074 #26).
items.correction: Replace #26 with a new item practising the same pattern, e.g. '너의 형제들은 어디에 있었니?' -> "Where were your brothers?" (then generate its clip).

items.original: KO "그는 어디에 가니?" -> EN "Where does he go?"
items.problem: The everyday meaning of '어디에 가니?' is 'Where is he going (now)?', while habitual 'Where does he go?' is the less likely reading. Real grader: "Where is he going?" = incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add alternative "Where is he going?", or disambiguate the prompt (e.g. '그는 (보통) 어디에 가니?').

items.original: #2 "Were there solutions?"; #4 "Are there videotapes?"; #6 "Do they have money?"; #22 "Weren't there boys?"
items.problem: 'any' in questions is the standard, most natural form and is what textbooks teach. Real grader: "Were there any solutions?", "Are there any videotapes?", "Do they have any money?" and "Weren't there any boys?" are all incorrect (0). The one extra word exceeds the 1.15 length cap on these short sentences.
items.correction: Add the 'any' version of each as an alternative. Consider making the 'any' form the displayed model, since the bare plural is less natural. If the displayed model text changes, regenerate its Ava clip.

items.original: KO "왜 그것은 재미있니?" -> EN "Why is it interesting?"
items.problem: '재미있다' is equally 'fun'. "Why is it fun?" is graded incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add alternative "Why is it fun?".

items.original: "너는 이 주말에 일하고 있지 않니?"
items.problem: '이 주말에' is unnatural Korean. The standard phrase for 'this weekend' is '이번 주말에'.
items.correction: "너는 이번 주말에 일하지 않니?" (or keep '일하고 있지 않니' to cue the progressive: "너는 이번 주말에 일하고 있지 않니?").

items.original: "너의 어머니는 얼마나 많은 누이가 있니?"
items.problem: '누이' is the word a MALE uses for his female sibling. A mother cannot have a 누이; her sisters are 언니/여동생/자매. The Korean prompt is semantically wrong. The same generic misuse also appears outside this scope, e.g. gh1-030 #8 "그는 그녀의 누이를 사랑한다."
items.correction: Change the prompt to '너의 어머니는 자매가 몇 명 있으시니?' (or '...여자 형제가 몇 명 있으시니?'). The English model "How many sisters does your mother have?" stays unchanged.

items.original: #4 KO "왜 너의 누이는 나를 보니?" -> "Why does your sister look at me?"; #39 KO "누가 이것에 대하여 이야기하니?" -> "Who talks about this?"
items.problem: Out of context these Korean questions usually mean something happening now. Real grader: "Why is your sister looking at me?" = partial. "Who is talking about this?" = incorrect (0). The course's -고 있다 cue for the progressive explains why the simple present is the model, but the progressive is equally correct.
items.correction: Add alternatives "Why is your sister looking at me?" (#4) and "Who is talking about this?" (#39).

items.original: #18 "Why don't you feel the same?"; #20 "You don't remember the night, do you?"; #29 "When do you think about that night?"; #24 "My dog ate all the bones, didn't it?"
items.problem: Equally correct variants get only partial credit (70). #18 "...feel the same way?". #20 uses 'the night' and #29 uses 'that night' for the same Korean '그 밤', and neither accepts the other; 'that night' is the more natural form in #20. #24: owners normally tag a pet dog as he/she, so "didn't he?" / "didn't she?" is common. Item #34 in this lesson already lists he/she/they tag alternatives.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #18 "Why don't you feel the same way?"; #20 "You don't remember that night, do you?"; #29 "When do you think about the night?"; #24 "My dog ate all the bones, didn't he?" and "...didn't she?".

items.original: KO "너는 농담하고 있니?(kid)" -> EN "Are you kidding?"
items.problem: "Are you kidding me?" is the most idiomatic form of this expression and is graded incorrect (0), because one extra word breaks the length cap on a 3-word model.
items.correction: Add alternative "Are you kidding me?".

items.original: KO "그는 누군가를 만나지?" -> EN "He meets someone, doesn't he?"
items.problem: The model is grammatical but unnatural. A simple-present habit with an unspecified 'someone' is not something English speakers say, and the Korean most naturally means 'he is seeing (dating) someone'. Real grader: "He's seeing someone, isn't he?" = incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add alternative "He is seeing someone, isn't he?". Better: change the prompt to a clear habitual sentence, e.g. '그는 매주 누군가를 만나지?' -> "He meets someone every week, doesn't he?" (regenerate the clip if the English changes).

items.original: KO #35 "너는 그녀의 부모님을 만났니?" -> "Did you meet her parents?"; KO #30 "너는 누군가를 만났지?" -> "You met someone, didn't you?"
items.problem: The present perfect is a very common and natural translation, and this lesson already accepts it on #19. Real grader: "Have you met her parents?" = incorrect (0). "You've met someone, haven't you?" = incorrect (0).
items.correction: Add alternatives: #35 "Have you met her parents?"; #30 "You have met someone, haven't you?".

items.original: "(police, people, children 은 항상 복수)"
items.problem: The rule is over-stated. 'people' is not always plural: 'a people' (a nation or ethnic group) is singular, with the plural 'peoples'. 'children' is simply the plural form of 'child', so listing it with police/people as a word that is 'always plural' is confusing. The point the item needs is that these nouns take plural verbs and 'they' tags.
items.correction: "(police, people(사람들), children 은 복수 취급 → 동사·대명사는 복수: they)"

items.original: KO #6 "경찰이 15사람을 체포했죠? (police, people, children 은 항상 복수)" -> "The police arrested 15 people, didn't they?"; KO #7 "경찰은 어디에서 15사람을 체포했나?" -> "Where did the police arrest 15 people?"
items.problem: The grader does not treat digits and words as equal. "The police arrested fifteen people, didn't they?" and "Where did the police arrest fifteen people?" are graded incorrect (0), although spelling out numbers under 100 is the normal written style. The Korean '15사람' is also unnatural. Natural Korean is '15명' or '열다섯 사람'.
items.correction: Add alternatives with 'fifteen' to #6 and #7. Change the prompts to '경찰이 15명을 체포했죠?' / '경찰은 어디에서 15명을 체포했나?'.

items.original: KO "당신의 여자 친구는 속삭이지만, 당신의 부인은 소리 지른다. (whisper, shout)" -> EN "Your girlfriend whispers but your wife shouts."
items.problem: The sentence assumes the learner ('you') has both a wife and a girlfriend, which is an infidelity joke. It also casts the wife as the one who shouts, a nagging-wife stereotype. In a paid course for a general adult audience this is the same kind of content as the jokes already held for the owner's decision.
items.correction: Replace with a neutral pair that keeps whisper/shout, e.g. KO '그 아이는 속삭이지만, 그의 형은 소리 지른다.' -> EN "The child whispers, but his brother shouts." If the English text changes, regenerate the Ava clip in the same change (node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs).

items.original: #3 "Does he get up early?"; #14 "What time did you get up?"; #4 "Does your sister go to bed early?"; #13 "What time did you go to bed last night?" (KO #3 "그는 일찍 일어나니?", #14 "당신은 몇 시에 일어났나?", #4 "당신의 누나는 일찍 자니?", #13 "...잠자리에 들었나?")
items.problem: '일어나다' is equally 'wake up', and '자다' is equally 'go to sleep'. Real grader: "Does he wake up early?", "What time did you wake up?", "Does your sister go to sleep early?" and "What time did you go to sleep last night?" are all incorrect (0), because one differing content word fails the match.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #3 "Does he wake up early?"; #14 "What time did you wake up?"; #4 "Does your sister go to sleep early?"; #13 "What time did you go to sleep last night?".

items.original: #15 KO "당신은 몇 시에 출근했나?" -> "What time did you get to work?"; #16 KO "왜 너는 늦게 집에 왔나?" -> "Why did you get home late?"
items.problem: #16's Korean '집에 왔나' is literally 'come home', and "Why did you come home late?" is correct, but the grader marks it incorrect. For #15, '출근하다' is most commonly rendered 'go to work'. "What time did you go to work?" is also graded incorrect. Only the 'get to/get home' versions are accepted.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #16 "Why did you come home late?"; #15 "What time did you go to work?" (optionally also "What time did you leave for work?").

items.original: #20 "Do you have breakfast?"; #21 "What did you have for breakfast?"; #22 "What time do you have lunch?"; #23 "Where does he have lunch?" (KO: "당신은 아침 식사하나?", "...무엇을 먹었나?", "...점심을 먹나?", "...점심을 먹나?")
items.problem: The Korean prompts literally say 먹다 (eat). "eat breakfast/lunch" is fully correct and very common, yet it has no alternative. Real grader: "Do you eat breakfast?", "What did you eat for breakfast?", "What time do you eat lunch?" and "Where does he eat lunch?" are all graded incorrect (0). The course already accepts this elsewhere: gh1-014 #15 lists "You didn't eat lunch, did you?" as an alternative.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #20 "Do you eat breakfast?"; #21 "What did you eat for breakfast?"; #22 "What time do you eat lunch?"; #23 "Where does he eat lunch?" (in gh1-081.json and the matching gh1-081-1/-2 files).

items.original: KO "그는 언제 미국으로 돌아가나?" -> "When does he return to the U.S.?" alternatives ["When does he go back to the U.S.?"]
items.problem: Real grader: "When does he return to the United States?", "When does he go back to America?" and "When is he going back to the U.S.?" are all incorrect (0). The course accepts these names elsewhere: gh1-016 #32 lists "the US", "the U.S.A." and "the United States" as alternatives for 미국. The progressive-future form is also the most natural English for a planned return.
items.correction: Add alternatives "When does he return to the United States?", "When does he go back to the United States?", "When does he go back to America?", "When is he going back to the U.S.?".

items.original: #30 "Who shouts?"; #31 "Who cries?"; #37 "Who looked for me?"; #32 "Do your children cry often?"
items.problem: Common correct variants score 0 or 70. "Who yells?" = incorrect. "Who is shouting?" / "Who is crying?" = incorrect; these are the most natural readings of the out-of-context '누가 고함지르나/우나?'. "Who was looking for me?" = incorrect, and it is the most natural English for '찾아다녔나'. "Do your children often cry?" (standard frequency-adverb position) = partial only.
items.correction: Add alternatives: #30 "Who yells?", "Who is shouting?"; #31 "Who is crying?"; #37 "Who was looking for me?"; #32 "Do your children often cry?".

items.original: KO "당신은 화났나?" -> EN "Are you mad?" alternatives ["Were you mad?"]
items.problem: The standard translation of '화났니?' is "Are you angry?", and it is graded incorrect (0). The model 'mad' in the sense of angry is informal and mainly US. In British English 'mad' usually means crazy, so the model alone is also a questionable teaching form.
items.correction: Add alternatives "Are you angry?" and "Were you angry?". Consider noting that 'mad' = angry is informal US usage.

items.original: "그 스키 리조트는(resort)그것의 스스로의 눈을 만든다.(its own)"
items.problem: '그것의 스스로의 눈' is not grammatical Korean. It is a word-for-word gloss of 'its own snow', and the hint (its own) already supplies the English. There is also no space after '(resort)'.
items.correction: "그 스키 리조트는(resort) 자체적으로 눈을 만든다.(its own)" or "그 스키 리조트는(resort) 자기 눈을 직접 만든다.(its own)"

items.original: "그 폭풍(storm)은 3피트의(three feet of)눈을 쏟아 붓는다.(dump)"
items.problem: '쏟아붓다' is a single compound verb in the standard dictionary and must be written without a space. There is also no space between '(three feet of)' and '눈을'.
items.correction: "그 폭풍(storm)은 3피트의(three feet of) 눈을 쏟아붓는다.(dump)"

items.original: #10 "나의 어머니는 실험 결과를 기다린다.(wait for, test results)"; #17 "그들은 실험 결과를 기다리고 있나?"; #18 "그는 실험 결과를 기다리고 있지 않니?"; #19 "그들은 실험 결과를 기다리지 않았니?"
items.problem: The English 'test results' in this everyday context (a mother waiting) means medical or other test results, which in Korean is '검사 결과'. '실험 결과' means experimental (laboratory research) results. The Korean and English do not match in sense.
items.correction: Change '실험 결과' to '검사 결과' in #10, #17, #18 and #19 (English unchanged).

items.original: KO #15 "그들은 섬에서 약간의 시간을 보내지 않았지?" -> "They didn't spend any time on an island, did they?"; KO #16 "그들은 섬에서 약간의 시간을 보내고 있지 않았다." -> "They were not spending any time on an island."
items.problem: The prompt says '약간의' and the earlier hint taught 'some time', but the model silently switches to 'any'. The some -> any change in negatives is correct and worth learning, but no note explains it. A learner who follows the prompt gets partial (70) without knowing why. The English also changes the meaning to 'no time at all', while the Korean literally says 'not a little time'.
items.correction: Add a hint to both prompts, e.g. '(부정문에서는 some → any)', and/or reword the Korean to '섬에서 전혀 시간을 보내지 않았지?' so that it matches 'any'.

items.original: There is no evidence.
items.problem: The equally correct "There isn't any evidence." is scored 0 (grader: incorrect), even though item 17 of the same lesson accepts the 'any' pattern as an alternative ("Isn't there any evidence?").
items.correction: Add "There isn't any evidence." / "There is not any evidence." to item 3's alternatives.

items.original: The navy found his body.
items.problem: The prompt is "해군이 그의 시체를 발견했다.(body)" - 발견하다 is 'discover' first and 'find' second, and the hint only fixes the noun. "The navy discovered his body." => incorrect (0점) with the repo's grader.
items.correction: Add "The navy discovered his body." to alternatives.

items.original: Didn't soldiers leave the city?
items.problem: For "군인들이 그 도시를 떠나지 않았나?" the bare plural with no determiner is unnatural in a negative question; English uses 'the soldiers' (the soldiers already in the lesson's story) or 'any soldiers'. Both natural answers are scored 0 by the repo's grader: "Didn't the soldiers leave the city?" => incorrect, "Didn't any soldiers leave the city?" => incorrect (the extra word exceeds the grader's 1.15 length cap on a 5-word model).
items.correction: Use "Didn't the soldiers leave the city?" as the model answer and add "Didn't any soldiers leave the city?" and the current "Didn't soldiers leave the city?" as alternatives.

items.original: {"n": "15", "text": "The microphone is still on.", "alternatives": ["The mike is still on."]}
items.problem: The only short form accepted is the dated spelling 'mike'. The modern and far more common spelling 'mic' is scored 0: "The mic is still on." => incorrect with the repo's grader (the grader's fuzzy match cannot bridge mic/mike/microphone).
items.correction: Add "The mic is still on." to the alternatives (keeping 'mike').

items.original: Was the congressman unhappy?
items.problem: 국회의원 is rendered only as the US-specific, male-marked 'congressman'. For a Korean 국회의원 the usual English is 'lawmaker' or 'member of the National Assembly', and the neutral/female forms are equally correct. Grader: "Was the lawmaker unhappy?" => incorrect (0점), "Was the assemblyman unhappy?" => incorrect; only "Was the congresswoman unhappy?" limps in as partial (70점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Was the lawmaker unhappy?", "Was the congresswoman unhappy?" (and optionally "Was the legislator unhappy?").

items.original: Was this handgun yours?
items.problem: 권총 is standardly 'pistol' as well as 'handgun', and the item gives no vocabulary hint. "Was this pistol yours?" => incorrect (0점) with the repo's grader.
items.correction: Add "Was this pistol yours?" to alternatives (and optionally "Was this gun yours?").

items.original: Were Democrats and Republicans cooperative?
items.problem: With party names English normally takes the article ('Were the Democrats and Republicans cooperative?'), but the grader's length cap rejects any added word on this 5-word model: "Were the Democrats and Republicans cooperative?" => incorrect and "Were the Democrats and the Republicans cooperative?" => incorrect (both 0점).
items.correction: Add "Were the Democrats and Republicans cooperative?" and "Were the Democrats and the Republicans cooperative?" to alternatives.

items.original: 그 재정구역은 큰 재건 작업에 직면하지 않았니?
items.problem: 'Financial district' is 금융가 / 금융 지구 in Korean; 재정 means public (government) finance, and 재정구역 is not a Korean word at all - a learner cannot get from it to 'financial district'. The English answer also accepts only 'major' for 큰: "Didn't the financial district face a big rebuilding job?" => incorrect (0점) with the repo's grader.
items.correction: Change the prompt to "그 금융가는 큰 재건 작업에 직면하지 않았니?" (or 금융 지구), and add "Didn't the financial district face a big rebuilding job?" to alternatives.

items.original: Do they take airplanes frequently?
items.problem: For the habitual sense of 그들은 자주 비행기를 타나?, native usage is 'Do they fly often?' or 'Do they take planes often?'; 'take airplanes' is unidiomatic (a plane is taken for one specific trip). The natural answers are all scored 0 by the repo's grader: "Do they fly often?" => incorrect, "Do they take planes often?" => incorrect, "Do they often fly?" => incorrect.
items.correction: Use "Do they fly often?" as the model answer, with "Do they take planes often?", "Do they often take planes?" and the current "Do they take airplanes frequently/often?" as alternatives.

items.locator: gh1-090 item 39 vs gh1-092 item 39 (same n, same English answer in gh1-091 and gh1-093)
items.original: gh1-090 #39 "왜 그것은 국경 밖에서 일어나니?"  /  gh1-092 #39 "왜 그것은 국경선 밖에서 발생하나?"  - both answered by "Why does it take place outside the border?" with the same alternative "Why does it happen outside the border?"
items.problem: The last item of lesson 39강 (gh1-090) is repeated as the first item of 40강 (gh1-092) with only the Korean wording changed, carrying the same number 39 and the same answer. This is the only such repeat in the 127 items of this scope; the second Korean version says 발생하나 ('occur'), yet 'occur' is not accepted ("Why does it occur outside the border?" => incorrect).
items.correction: Drop the repeat from one of the two lessons (or renumber it), and add "Why does it occur outside the border?" to the alternatives of whichever item keeps the 발생하다 wording.

items.original: 그 상원의원은 한 선택 안을 갖고 있지 않니?   /   모든 신부가 그 모금 회에 참석했지?
items.problem: Korean spacing errors in two prompts: 선택 안 should be 선택안 (one noun) and 모금 회 should be 모금회. As written, '한 선택 안을' reads as 'one choice inside' and '모금 회' as two separate words.
items.correction: Fix to "그 상원의원은 한 선택안을 갖고 있지 않니?" and "모든 신부가 그 모금회에 참석했지?".

items.original: Why were the people taking the president's speech kindly?
items.problem: 'take kindly' is an idiom meaning 'accept willingly', and dictionaries mark it as chiefly/usually negative ('did not take kindly to'); it also normally requires 'to' before the object. "taking the president's speech kindly" is not natural English, and the Korean prompt "...연설을 친절하게 받아들이고 있었나?" is a literal mis-rendering of the idiom - 친절하게 means 'in a kind manner', not '호의적으로'.
items.correction: Rewrite both sides, e.g. Korean "왜 그 사람들은 대통령의 연설을 호의적으로 받아들이고 있었나?" with "Why were the people taking the president's speech well?" or "Why were the people receiving the president's speech favorably?", and keep the old sentence out of the answer key.

items.locator: gh1-093 item 57; gh1-095 item 76; gh1-097 items 77 and 95
items.original: Does each student have his own project?
items.problem: Four graded items assume a male referent for a gender-neutral Korean noun (각 학생 -> 'his own project'; 각 시장 -> 'didn't he'; 그 외과 의사 -> 'didn't he'; 모든 신부 -> 'didn't he') and list no neutral alternative. The neutral English is penalised: "Does each student have his or her own project?" => incorrect (0점) and "Does each student have their own project?" => partial (70점); "Each mayor received a warning, didn't they?" and "The surgeon paid for the medicine, didn't they?" => partial. The course elsewhere knows better: gh1-066 items 76/77 do carry "... didn't they?" as alternatives.
items.correction: Add the neutral alternatives: "Does each student have their own project?" and "... his or her own project?"; "Each mayor received a warning, didn't they?"; "The surgeon paid for the medicine, didn't she/they?"; "Every priest attended the fundraiser, didn't they?".

items.original: She was different from most girls, wasn't she?
items.problem: The prompt is "그녀는 대부분의 여자와 달랐지?". 여자 is 'woman'; 'girls' back-translates to 여자아이/소녀. The same lesson translates 여자 as 'woman' in item 58 ("He wakes up next to a beautiful woman"), so the course is inconsistent, and the faithful answer is rejected: "She was different from most women, wasn't she?" => incorrect (0점).
items.correction: Make "She was different from most women, wasn't she?" the model answer (or at least an alternative), keeping "most girls" / "most of the girls" as alternatives.

items.original: Every agency increases security.
items.problem: 보안을 강화한다 is 'strengthen/tighten security'; 'increase security' is a loose paraphrase. The direct translations are scored 0: "Every agency strengthens security." => incorrect, "Every agency tightens security." => incorrect. The item also demands three forms ('3가지로') and the alternatives cover only the every/each/all variation, not the verb.
items.correction: Add "Every agency strengthens security." and "Every agency tightens security." (plus the each/all variants of those) to alternatives, or change the model answer to 'tightens security'.

items.original: Nobody likes the terms, do they?   /   Nobody hated her, did they?
items.problem: Neither item lists the 'no one' spelling, while gh1-097 items 84-87 (the very next lesson, same 아무도 pattern) all do. Because 'no one' is two words, the grader's length cap rejects it outright: "No one likes the terms, do they?" => incorrect, "No one hated her, did they?" => incorrect. Item 68 also translates 조건 only as 'terms'; "Nobody likes the conditions, do they?" => incorrect although 조건 = condition is the primary dictionary equivalent.
items.correction: Add "No one likes the terms, do they?" / "No one likes the conditions, do they?" to item 68 and "No one hated her, did they?" to item 69.

items.locator: items 75 and 76 (gh1-095 items[].alternatives vs the following paragraph blocks)
items.original: {"n": "75", "text": "Each boy did his homework.", "alternatives": ["Every boy did his homework."]}  ... {"type": "paragraph", "text": "All the boys did their homework."}
items.problem: gh1-095 keeps several correct answers in `paragraph` blocks, which the view never renders and the grader never sees: "All the boys did their homework." (for item 75) and "All the priests attended the fundraiser, didn't they?" (for item 76). Both are correct translations of 모든 소년이 그의 숙제를 했다 / 모든 신부가 그 모금 회에 참석했지?, and both score 0 with the repo's grader (=> incorrect). The parallel lesson gh1-066 does carry "Every boy received a prize, didn't they?" and "Each boy received a prize, didn't they?" as alternatives on items 76/77, so the course is inconsistent with itself here.
items.correction: Move the paragraph text into `alternatives`: item 75 += "All the boys did their homework."; item 76 += "All the priests attended the fundraiser, didn't they?" and "Every priest attended the fundraiser, didn't they?".

items.original: All of them face a cleaning job.
items.problem: 'a cleaning job' normally means paid employment as a cleaner; the task-after-a-mess sense of 청소하는 일 is 'a cleanup job'. The natural answer is only partially credited ("All of them face a cleanup job." => partial, 70점).
items.correction: Change the model answer to "All of them face a cleanup job." and keep "All of them face a cleaning job." plus "They all face a cleanup job." as alternatives.

items.original: Were there many researchers in the lab?
items.problem: The prompt is "그 실험실에는 많은 연구원들이 있었나?". 실험실 is 'laboratory'; the answer accepts only the clipped 'lab', and the full word is rejected: "Were there many researchers in the laboratory?" => incorrect (0점) (the grader's prefix rule needs 4 shared letters, and lab/laboratory share only 3).
items.correction: Add "Were there many researchers in the laboratory?" to alternatives.

items.original: Did many ministers go there?
items.problem: 목사 is translated only as 'minister'. 'Pastor' is the more common equivalent and scores 0: "Did many pastors go there?" => incorrect. It is also confusing that the same English word 'ministers' is the answer for 장관 in gh1-088 item 14 ("Where are the ministers today?") - two different Korean words share one English answer two lessons apart with no note.
items.correction: Add "Did many pastors go there?" (and optionally "Did many clergymen go there?") to alternatives, and consider a one-line note that minister = 장관/목사 depending on context.

items.original: There were 60 officers in the police station, weren't there?   /   There weren't 60 officials in the office, were there?
items.problem: Both model answers use the digit '60'. The grader treats digits and spelled-out numbers as different words ('7' != 'seven'), so the spelled form - the normal choice in a written English sentence, and the only thing a learner can say aloud in the mic step - is rejected: "There were sixty officers in the police station, weren't there?" => incorrect, "There weren't sixty officials in the office, were there?" => incorrect. The rest of the course spells numbers out (gh1-085 #2 "There are thirty thousand troops.").
items.correction: Make 'sixty' the model answer on both items and keep the '60' spelling as an alternative (or vice versa), so both are accepted.

items.original: He doesn't go on a date today, does he?
items.problem: This alternative is unnatural English. The simple present cannot be used for a single arrangement on a specific day ("today"); it is reserved for habits and timetables. The Korean prompt "그는 오늘 데이트하러 가지 않지?" is a today-arrangement, which the main answer renders correctly with the present progressive.
items.correction: Delete this alternative, or replace it with "He is not going on a date today, is he?" / "He isn't going out on a date today, is he?".

items.locator: item n=107 (KO in gh1-098.json, EN in gh1-099.json)
items.original: Why didn't North and South Korea reach a compromise?
items.problem: The prompt is "왜 남북한은 타협에 이르지 않았나?". The literal rendering of 남북한 is "South and North Korea" (the Korean order), and "the two Koreas" is the standard news wording. Both return "incorrect" (0점) from the grader, because swapping the two proper nouns breaks the word alignment.
items.correction: Add alternatives: "Why didn't South and North Korea reach a compromise?" and "Why didn't the two Koreas reach a compromise?".

items.locator: items n=104 and n=112 (Korean prompts, gh1-098.json)
items.original: 그녀는 매일 여러 번(많은 회수) 그를 보지?
items.problem: Korean spelling/spacing errors in the prompts: n=104 "회수" should be "횟수" (回數; 회수 means 回收, 'retrieval'), and n=112 "필리핀사람이" should be spaced "필리핀 사람이".
items.correction: n=104 → "그녀는 매일 여러 번(많은 횟수) 그를 보지?"; n=112 → "그 여자는 필리핀 사람이 아니었지?".

items.locator: items n=111 and n=112 (KO in gh1-098.json, EN in gh1-099.json)
items.original: She was American, wasn't she?
items.problem: The prompts are "그 여자는 미국인이었지?" (n=111) and "그 여자는 필리핀사람이 아니었지?" (n=112). "그 여자" literally means "that woman", and elsewhere in this course a demonstrative + noun prompt is translated literally (e.g. n=96 "그 운동선수들" → "The athletes"). "The woman was American, wasn't she?" and "The woman was not Filipino, was she?" both return "incorrect" (0점) — the extra word pushes the answer past the 1.15 length cap.
items.correction: Add "The woman was American, wasn't she?" (n=111) and "The woman was not Filipino, was she?" / "The woman was not Filipina, was she?" (n=112); or change the prompts to "그녀는 …" so that "She" is the only reading.

items.locator: blocks[4] (paragraph block between the two sentences blocks), gh1-100.json
items.original: 않았니)?
items.problem: A leftover extraction fragment from item n=127 sits in the file as its own paragraph block. It is not rendered by GrammarLearningView today, but it is corrupt data that any future renderer or export would show.
items.correction: Delete the paragraph block; the text is already part of item n=127's prompt.

items.original: The captain gets on the plane, doesn't he?
items.problem: "그 기장" carries no gender in Korean, but the only accepted answer assumes a male captain. "The captain gets on the plane, doesn't she?" scores only partial (70점) instead of exact.
items.correction: Add alternatives "The captain gets on the plane, doesn't she?" and "The captain gets on the plane, don't they?".

items.original: Didn't he turn the mike off?
items.problem: "mike" is the older spelling; "mic" is now the dominant spelling of the abbreviation and is a full dictionary entry. The grader does not treat them as the same word, so "Didn't he turn the mic off?" and "Didn't he turn off the mic?" both return "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Didn't he turn the mic off?" and "Didn't he turn off the mic?" ("Didn't he turn off the mike?" already scores partial).

items.locator: item n=122 (KO in gh1-100.json, EN in gh1-101.json)
items.original: 그녀는 따분하지 않지?
items.problem: With a person as subject, "따분하다" is normally read as the person FEELING bored, not as the person BEING boring. The model answer is "She's not boring, is she?", and the natural reading "She's not bored, is she?" returns "incorrect" (0점). bored/boring is the classic Korean-learner confusion, so an ambiguous prompt on exactly that pair is the worst place to leave it.
items.correction: Disambiguate the prompt, e.g. "그녀는 지루한 사람이 아니지?" (for "boring"), or keep the prompt and add "She's not bored, is she?" as an alternative if both readings are intended.

items.original: Which did you choose?
items.problem: The prompt is "너는 어느 것을 선택했니?(which)". "Which one did you choose?" is the more idiomatic English for 어느 것 and returns "incorrect" (0점): the model has only 4 words, so one extra word exceeds the 1.15 length cap.
items.correction: Add alternatives "Which one did you choose?" and "Which one did you pick?".

items.original: 좋나(됐나?) 혹은, 그것이 거래(합의, 협정)인가?
items.problem: The prompt is not a sentence to translate but raw glossary notes: two competing readings joined by "혹은," plus three parenthetical synonyms. It is impossible to tell what one English sentence is wanted (the answer is the idiom "Is that a deal?").
items.correction: Rewrite as a single prompt, e.g. "그럼 합의한 거지? (거래 성립인가?)", keeping "Is that a deal?" / "Is it a deal?" as the answers.

items.locator: file metadata: gh1-102.json label/heading/audio, gh1-103.json instruction
items.original: "label": "[ Page 103]"
items.problem: gh1-102 carries the label and heading of page 103 ("[ Page 103]" in both `label` and blocks[0].text) and its audio[] lists only gh1-103.mp3 with the label "영작 연습 문제 (Question Audio)" — the question audio for page 102 is missing. The pair file gh1-103.json also says "영작문제 2" where every other answer sheet says "영작문제 2 답안".
items.correction: Set gh1-102 label/heading to "[ Page 102]", restore the gh1-102.mp3 question-audio entry (or drop the audio array as other pages do), and set gh1-103's instruction to "영작문제 2 답안".

items.locator: item n=138 (KO in gh1-102.json, EN in gh1-103.json)
items.original: You will take me out some other time, won't you?
items.problem: "다음 기회에" translates most directly as "next time"; "You will take me out next time, won't you?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternative "You will take me out next time, won't you?".

items.original: Why can't you wait till tomorrow?
items.problem: Only the informal "till" is accepted. The standard form "Why can't you wait until tomorrow?" returns "incorrect" (0점) because the grader does not equate till/until.
items.correction: Add alternative "Why can't you wait until tomorrow?" (and optionally "Why can't you wait until tomorrow morning?" is not needed — just until).

items.locator: item n=144 (KO in gh1-102.json, EN in gh1-103.json)
items.original: Will the United States undoubtedly face future terrorist threats?
items.problem: A yes/no question containing a certainty adverb is self-contradictory: you cannot ask whether something will 'undoubtedly' happen. The source sentence is clearly a statement ("The United States will undoubtedly face future terrorist threats.") that was mechanically flipped into a question, and the Korean prompt inherits the oddity.
items.correction: Make it a statement on both sides: "미국은 의심의 여지없이 미래의 테러 위협에 직면할 것이다." → "The United States will undoubtedly face future terrorist threats." (regenerate the clip for the changed English).

items.locator: item n=145 (KO in gh1-102.json, EN + alternatives in gh1-103.json)
items.original: When did our forces defeat the enemy?
items.problem: The prompt is "우리의 군대는 언제 적을 무찔렀나?". 군대 is normally "army" or "troops"; "When did our army defeat the enemy?" returns "incorrect" (0점). Separately, the existing alternative "When did our forces defeat enemies?" is unnatural English (a bare plural with a one-off past event).
items.correction: Add "When did our army defeat the enemy?" and "When did our troops defeat the enemy?"; delete the alternative "When did our forces defeat enemies?".

items.locator: item n=146 (KO in gh1-102.json, EN in gh1-103.json)
items.original: Haven't they emerged yet?
items.problem: The prompt "그들은 아직 나타나지 않았나?" maps first to "appear" or "show up"; "emerge" is a narrow, news-register choice. "Haven't they appeared yet?" and "Haven't they shown up yet?" both return "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Haven't they appeared yet?" and "Haven't they shown up yet?".

items.original: What was that like then?
items.problem: For "그것은 그때 어땠니?" the idiomatic English is "What was it like back then?", which returns "incorrect" (0점) — "back" is an extra word the 5-word model cannot absorb.
items.correction: Add alternative "What was it like back then?" (and "What was that like back then?").

items.locator: item n=5 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: Where did they seize the two vehicles?
items.problem: "압수하다" is most often taught as "confiscate"; "Where did they confiscate the two vehicles?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternative "Where did they confiscate the two vehicles?".

items.locator: item n=6 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: 그 경찰은 협력하고 있나?
items.problem: "그 경찰" with the demonstrative reads most naturally as one specific officer, but the only accepted answer treats it as the force ("Are the police cooperating?"). "Is the police officer cooperating?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Change the prompt to "경찰은 협력하고 있나?" (as item n=7 already does), or add "Is the police officer cooperating?" as an alternative.

items.locator: item n=7 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: The police were not questioning the man.
items.problem: "심문하다" translates directly as "interrogate"; "The police were not interrogating the man." returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternative "The police were not interrogating the man.".

items.locator: item n=13 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: The CIA confirmed the report, didn't it?
items.problem: The Korean prompt is "“씨아이에이”가 그 보도가 사실이라고 확인했죠?" — 'confirmed THAT THE REPORT WAS TRUE'. The model answer drops the whole that-clause, so the faithful translation "The CIA confirmed that the report was true, didn't it?" returns "incorrect" (0점, over the length cap).
items.correction: Either shorten the prompt to "“씨아이에이”가 그 보도를 확인했죠?" or add the alternative "The CIA confirmed that the report was true, didn't it?".

items.locator: item n=23 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: Why is the anniversary usually a somber occasion?
items.problem: "엄숙한" is "solemn"; "somber" is "침울한/우울한". The prompt therefore points at a different word than the only accepted answer, and "Why is the anniversary usually a solemn occasion?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Change the Korean to "왜 그 기념일은 보통 침울한 행사인가?", or add "Why is the anniversary usually a solemn occasion?" as an alternative.

items.locator: item n=24 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: Who made the taped confession?
items.problem: "녹화된" = recorded/videotaped. "Who made the recorded confession?" and "Who made the videotaped confession?" both return "incorrect" (0점); only the dated "taped" is accepted.
items.correction: Add alternatives "Who made the recorded confession?" and "Who made the videotaped confession?".

items.locator: item n=30 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: Did they always have to type their assignments?
items.problem: The prompt says "숙제", whose standard English is "homework"; "Did they always have to type their homework?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternative "Did they always have to type their homework?".

items.original: Fortunately he was fast and accurate. wasn't he?
items.problem: The model answer is broken: a full stop before the tag question and a lower-case "wasn't". A tag question must be attached with a comma. This is the only punctuation of its kind in the six lessons reviewed, and this lesson's entire topic is tag questions.
items.correction: "Fortunately, he was fast and accurate, wasn't he?" — and regenerate the Azure clip for the new text (the clip key is a hash of the English).

items.locator: item n=35 (KO in gh1-106.json, EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: They will have dinner together some other time.
items.problem: The prompt "그들은 다음에 함께 저녁 식사할 것이다" means 'next time'; "They will have dinner together next time." returns "incorrect" (0점). The Korean prompt is also the only one in the lesson with no sentence-final period.
items.correction: Add alternative "They will have dinner together next time." and add the missing period to the Korean prompt.

items.locator: items n=18 and n=21 (EN in gh1-107.json)
items.original: The Interior Department acquired the home, didn't it?
items.problem: Both items assert as fact something that never happened. Public Law 107-137 (signed 2002-02-06) only AUTHORISED the Secretary of the Interior to purchase Reagan's Dixon, Illinois boyhood home, and explicitly said the national historic site designation would not take effect until the Department acquired the property. The Department never acquired it: the house was gifted to Young America's Foundation in December 2020 and has never been designated a national historic site. Item n=21 ("Why did Reagan's childhood home become a federal historic site?") presupposes the same non-event.
items.correction: Neutralise both items, e.g. n=18 "내무부가 그 집을 취득할 권한을 받았죠?" → "The Interior Department was authorized to acquire the home, wasn't it?"; n=21 → "Why was Reagan's childhood home to become a federal historic site?" (regenerate clips for any changed English).

items.original: When will they finish their freshman year?
items.problem: "일학년" is also "first year"; "When will they finish their first year?" returns "incorrect" (0점) even though it is a correct translation (the following item n=37 already teaches the freshman/sophomore vocabulary).
items.correction: Add alternative "When will they finish their first year?".

items.locator: item n=39 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: This is a reasonably large area, isn't it?
items.problem: "꽤" is normally "quite / pretty / fairly"; "reasonably" is an unusual choice. "This is a pretty large area, isn't it?" and "This is quite a large area, isn't it?" both return "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "This is a pretty large area, isn't it?", "This is a fairly large area, isn't it?" and "This is quite a large area, isn't it?".

items.original: Someday, he wants to be a language teacher.
items.problem: Fronting "Someday" attaches it to "wants" rather than to "be", which is not how the sentence is meant; natural English puts it at the end: "He wants to be a language teacher someday." That natural version scores only partial (70점).
items.correction: Make "He wants to be a language teacher someday." the model answer (regenerate its clip) and keep the current sentence as an alternative.

items.locator: item n=41 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: When did they have their final examinations?
items.problem: "시험을 보다" is "take an exam" — the standard collocation — but "When did they take their final exams?" returns "incorrect" (0점); only "have … examinations" is accepted.
items.correction: Add alternatives "When did they take their final exams?" and "When did they take their final examinations?".

items.locator: item n=42 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: Sometimes he cut classes, didn't he?
items.problem: "수업을 빼먹다" is most commonly "skip class"; "Sometimes he skipped classes, didn't he?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Sometimes he skipped classes, didn't he?" and "Sometimes he skipped class, didn't he?".

items.locator: item n=47 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: When did he open a small grocery store in his hometown?
items.problem: "잡화점" is a general/variety store (miscellaneous goods); "grocery store" is 식료품점. "When did he open a small general store in his hometown?" returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives with "general store" and "variety store", or change the prompt to "작은 식료품점".

items.locator: item n=48 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: Within two years, he added another.
items.problem: "또 다른 하나를" is literally "another one", but "Within two years, he added another one." returns "incorrect" (0점) — the 6-word model cannot absorb one extra word under the 1.15 cap.
items.correction: Add alternative "Within two years, he added another one.".

items.locator: item n=51 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: Why does Phil rarely go to the shopping district?
items.problem: Two accepted-answer gaps in one item: "좀처럼 ~않다" is the textbook equivalent of "seldom" ("Why does Phil seldom go to the shopping district?" → incorrect, 0점), and "상가" is normally "the mall / the shopping center" ("Why does Phil rarely go to the mall?" → incorrect, 0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Why does Phil seldom go to the shopping district?", "Why does Phil rarely go to the mall?", "Why does Phil seldom go to the mall?", "Why does Phil rarely go to the shopping center?".

items.locator: item n=55 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: When did customs agents seize the financial records?
items.problem: "세관원" is standardly "customs officers/officials" and "압수하다" is standardly "confiscate"; "When did customs officers seize the financial records?" returns "incorrect" (0점), as does any version with "confiscate".
items.correction: Add alternatives "When did customs officers seize the financial records?", "When did customs officials seize the financial records?", "When did customs agents confiscate the financial records?".

items.locator: item n=60 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: 그것은 결정적으로 그래.
items.problem: "decidedly" in "It is decidedly so." means 확실히/틀림없이 (definitely), not 결정적으로 (decisively/crucially). The Korean prompt therefore teaches the wrong sense of the word, and it is also not a Korean sentence anyone would say.
items.correction: "그것은 확실히 그래." or "틀림없이 그래.", and add alternatives "It is definitely so." / "It definitely is." if the loose sense is to be accepted.

items.locator: item n=62 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN + alternative in gh1-109.json)
items.original: It's nicer than my place.
items.problem: The prompt is "그것은 나의 집보다 더 좋아." — "더 좋아" is "better". "It is better than my house." returns "incorrect" (0점); only "nicer" is accepted.
items.correction: Add alternatives "It's better than my place." and "It's better than my house.".

items.locator: item n=67 (KO in gh1-108.json, EN in gh1-109.json)
items.original: Did the athletes deliver a peak performance?
items.problem: "deliver a peak performance" is a narrow sports-psychology collocation that cannot be derived from "그 선수들이 최고의 성적을 냈나(경기를 했나)?", and no alternatives are provided: "Did the athletes give their best performance?" and "Did the athletes perform at their best?" both return "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "Did the athletes give their best performance?", "Did the athletes perform at their best?", "Did the athletes put in their best performance?".

items.original: 그 화산이 수천마일 떨어진 곳에서 재난을 만들어냈지?
items.problem: Spacing error: the unit noun must be separated — "수천 마일".
items.correction: "그 화산이 수천 마일 떨어진 곳에서 재난을 만들어냈지?"

items.locator: item n=78 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: It is high noon in Los Angeles, isn't it?
items.problem: The prompt "지금 로스엔젤리스에서는 정오이지?" contains 지금 (now) and plain 정오 (noon), but the model answer has no "now" and uses the emphatic idiom "high noon". "It is noon in Los Angeles now, isn't it?" returns "incorrect" (0점) and "It is noon in Los Angeles, isn't it?" only partial (70점).
items.correction: Add alternatives "It is noon in Los Angeles now, isn't it?" and "It is noon in Los Angeles, isn't it?".

items.locator: item n=80 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: They are probably up.
items.problem: "그들은 아마 안 자고 있을 거야." is most directly "They are probably awake.", which returns "incorrect" (0점) — the 4-word model gives no room and "up" is an idiom a learner cannot be expected to pick.
items.correction: Add alternatives "They are probably awake." and "They are probably still up.".

items.locator: item n=86 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: The Defense Department wouldn't comment any further than that.
items.problem: The Korean is present tense ("언급하려 하지 않는다") while the English is past ("wouldn't" = declined at the time). The consistent present-tense answer "The Defense Department won't comment any further than that." scores only partial (70점).
items.correction: Either change the Korean to "…언급하려 하지 않았다." or add the alternative "The Defense Department won't comment any further than that.".

items.locator: item n=87 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: That could reduce the fear of suspects.
items.problem: "the fear of suspects" is ambiguous in English and reads most naturally as 'fear OF suspects' (people being afraid of suspects), the opposite of the Korean "용의자들의 두려움" (the fear FELT BY suspects). The unambiguous answer "That could reduce suspects' fear." returns "incorrect" (0점).
items.correction: Change the model to "That could reduce suspects' fear." (regenerate the clip) or add it as an alternative alongside "That could reduce the suspects' fear.".

items.locator: item n=90 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: How did the government boost its sales?
items.problem: "판매를 올리다" is normally "increase/raise sales"; "How did the government increase its sales?" returns "incorrect" (0점). The sentence is also confusing on its own: in the surrounding chewing-tobacco story it is a company, not a government, that has sales — "그 정부의 판매" is left unexplained.
items.correction: Add alternatives "How did the government increase its sales?" and "How did the government raise its sales?"; check against the source story whether the subject should be 그 회사 / the company.

items.locator: item n=95 (EN in gh1-111.json); compare gh1-100 n=126
items.original: I totally won the bet.
items.problem: "완전히" is standardly "completely", but "I completely won the bet." returns "incorrect" (0점). The same course already accepts both totally and completely for 완전히 in gh1-100 n=126, so the treatment is inconsistent.
items.correction: Add alternative "I completely won the bet.".

items.locator: item n=98 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: Who offered a better deal?
items.problem: The prompt here is "누가 더 나은 제안을 했나?" (made a better OFFER). "Who made a better offer?" returns "incorrect" (0점) because only 3 of 5 model words align.
items.correction: Add alternative "Who made a better offer?" (preferably make it the model answer for this item, which also removes the duplication with gh1-106 n=29).

items.locator: item n=99 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: All 1900 Olympia outlets will be serving it within 60 days, won't they?
items.problem: "1900" without a thousands separator reads as a year at first glance. English convention writes "1,900" for the count. (Grading is unaffected — the comma is stripped.) The Korean prompt's "그것을 서브(제공)하고 있게 되겠지?" is also awkward machine-style Korean.
items.correction: "All 1,900 Olympia outlets will be serving it within 60 days, won't they?"; rewrite the Korean as "모든 1,900개 올림피아 매장이 60일 안에 그것을 제공하게 되겠지?" (regenerate the clip if the English changes).

items.original: 그것은 일시적인 억제명령을 받아내려고 애쓰지 않았니?
items.problem: "억제명령" is not the Korean legal term for a temporary restraining order; the usual renderings are "임시 금지명령" or "가처분(명령)". The English answer ("a temporary restraining order") is correct, so only the Korean is off.
items.correction: "그것은 임시 금지명령(가처분)을 받아내려고 애쓰지 않았니?"

items.locator: item n=106 (KO in gh1-110.json, EN in gh1-111.json)
items.original: You can't attend the party because you have a previous engagement, can you?
items.problem: "선약" is just as commonly "a prior engagement"; that answer returns "incorrect" (0점) because prior/previous are not treated as the same word.
items.correction: Add alternatives with "a prior engagement" and "a previous appointment".

items.locator: items n=77 and n=78 (Korean prompts, gh1-110.json)
items.original: 사실상 그들 중 많은 사람들은 로스엔젤리스 출신이지?
items.problem: "로스엔젤리스" is not the standard Korean transliteration; the 외래어 표기법 form is "로스앤젤레스". The same lesson set is also inconsistent about Atlanta: gh1-106 n=28 writes "아틀란타" while gh1-110 n=100 writes the standard "애틀랜타".
items.correction: Use "로스앤젤레스" in n=77 and n=78, and change "아틀란타" to "애틀랜타" in gh1-106 n=28.

items.locator: gh1-110-1 last item / gh1-110-2 first item (and gh1-111-1 / gh1-111-2), n=90
items.original: 그 정부가 어떻게 판매를 올렸나?
items.problem: Item n=90 is the last item of page 110-1 AND the first item of page 110-2 (same on the answer side, 111-1 / 111-2), so the two half-lesson pages hold 20 + 19 = 39 entries for a 38-item lesson. Every other split lesson in GRAMMAR I partitions its main lesson exactly.
items.correction: Remove n=90 from gh1-110-2.json and gh1-111-2.json (keeping it on the -1 pages), so the split pages cover 71-90 and 91-108.

items.locator: items n="113" (model answer side; also in gh1-113-1.json)
items.original: Oh, it's on the tip of my tongue.
items.problem: The model answer opens with an interjection "Oh," that has no counterpart anywhere in the Korean prompt ("그것은 나의 혀의 끝 위에 있다. (입에서 빙빙 도는데 생각이 안 난다. 말이 안 나온다)"), and no alternative without it is listed. Traced through src/lib/grammarGrading.ts: the perfect answer "It's on the tip of my tongue." matches 8 of the model's 9 normalized words, so it returns "partial", not "exact".
items.correction: Add the alternative "It's on the tip of my tongue." (safest - it leaves every English sentence that already has an Azure clip untouched), or drop "Oh, " from the model answer and regenerate the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs.

items.locator: items n="129" (Korean prompt side; also in gh1-112-2.json)
items.original: 너는 나에게 들리지 않을래?
items.problem: Korean spelling error: 들리다 means "to be heard", while the verb meant here is 들르다 ("to stop by"), whose correct form is 들르지. The model answer is "Won't you drop in on me?", so as written the prompt reads to a learner as something about hearing and cannot be translated into the expected sentence.
items.correction: "너는 나에게 들르지 않을래?" - more natural still: "우리 집에 들르지 않을래?" (Korean-only change, so no audio clip is affected.)

items.locator: items n="9" (Korean prompt side; also in gh1-116-1.json)
items.original: 그 백신은 군대 인사들에게 대부분 접종되었지?
items.problem: 인사(人士) in Korean means a person of standing or a public figure, so "군대 인사들" reads as "military VIPs", not "military personnel" (the English model answer is "The vaccine was administered mostly to military personnel, wasn't it?"). The English word personnel corresponds to 장병 / 병력 / 인력, not 인사.
items.correction: "그 백신은 대부분 군 장병들에게 접종되었지?" (Korean-only change, so no clip is affected.)

items.locator: items n="14" (model answer side; also in gh1-117-1.json)
items.original: The operation would last 24 to 72 hours.
items.problem: The Korean prompt "그 작전은 24시간 내지 72시간 지속될 것이다." uses -ㄹ 것이다, which renders most directly as "will last"; only "would" is accepted, so "The operation will last 24 to 72 hours." is capped at partial credit. Item 8 on the very same page does supply this kind of modal alternative ("It could be improved, couldn't it?" / "It can be improved, can't it?"), so the omission is an inconsistency rather than a policy.
items.correction: Add the alternative "The operation will last 24 to 72 hours.".

items.locator: items n="18" (model answer side; also in gh1-117-1.json)
items.original: Where were five international peace keepers killed?
items.problem: "peacekeeper" is a single closed compound in current dictionaries; "peace keepers" is not standard. (Grading is unaffected - gradeSpacingOnly treats a spacing-only difference as exact - so the damage is limited to what the learner reads and copies.)
items.correction: "Where were five international peacekeepers killed?" - regenerate the sentence clip afterwards, since the English text changes.

items.locator: items n="22" (model answer side; also in gh1-117-2.json)
items.original: More than forty more were wounded, weren't they?
items.problem: The Korean prompt writes the number as a numeral ("40명 이상이 더 부상당했지?") but the only accepted answer spells it "forty". Traced through grammarGrading.ts: "40" against "forty" is not a function word and fails looksLikeSameWord (edit distance > 1, shared stem < 4), so "More than 40 more were wounded, weren't they?" grades "incorrect" - 0 points, not partial.
items.correction: Add the alternative "More than 40 more were wounded, weren't they?" (alternatives are text-only data; the spoken clip belongs to the model answer, so nothing needs regenerating).

items.locator: items n="29" (model answer side; also in gh1-117-2.json)
items.original: When did the remains of seven servicemen return home?
items.problem: Same defect as item 22: the Korean prompt uses the numeral ("언제 7명 군인들의 유해가 귀국했나?") while the only accepted answer spells "seven". "When did the remains of 7 servicemen return home?" grades "incorrect" (0 points), because "7" and "seven" fail looksLikeSameWord.
items.correction: Add the alternative "When did the remains of 7 servicemen return home?" (an alternative with "soldiers" would also be reasonable, as item 31 on the same page already accepts servicemen/soldiers).

items.lesson: GRAMMAR I gh1-116 / gh1-117 and gh1-120 / gh1-121
items.locator: gh1-117.json items n="11"; gh1-121.json items n="35" (model answer side)
items.original: Don't officials have evidence?  /  He addressed cadets.
items.problem: On very short model answers, adding the definite article - which the Korean prompts 관리들은 / 사관생도들에게 invite, since they refer to a specific group - pushes the answer past MAX_ANSWER_LEN_RATIO and turns a correct sentence into 0 points rather than partial credit. "Don't the officials have evidence?" is 6 normalized words against a 5-word model (cap 5.75) and "He addressed the cadets." is 4 against a 3-word model (cap 3.45); both grade "incorrect". On longer sentences the same extra "the" only costs partial credit, so the penalty is arbitrary.
items.correction: Add the article variants as alternatives: "Don't the officials have evidence?" (gh1-117 n=11) and "He addressed the cadets." (gh1-121 n=35). If this class of problem is to be fixed at the root instead, exempt pure function-word insertions from the length cap in src/lib/grammarGrading.ts - but that is a grader change and needs its own verification run.

items.lesson: GRAMMAR I gh1-116 / gh1-117 and gh1-122 / gh1-123
items.locator: gh1-116.json and gh1-116-2.json: `paragraph` block after items n=28; gh1-123-2.json: `paragraph` block after items n=58
items.original: 28 그 위협은 그들의 보복하는 방식이 아닌가?
items.problem: A leftover extraction fragment: a second, differently worded copy of item 28 (the item itself reads "그 위협은 그들의 보복 방식이 아닌가?") is stored as a `paragraph` block inside gh1-116.json and gh1-116-2.json. gh1-123-2.json carries the same kind of artifact, "58 It'll be a little harder.", which its own main file gh1-123.json does not have. I verified the pairing is not affected: only `sentences` blocks are flattened into items, so gh1-116 still lines up 37-to-37 with gh1-117 and gh1-122-2 19-to-19 with gh1-123-2.
items.correction: Delete the three `paragraph` blocks. Content-data-only change, no text that has a voice clip is touched.

items.locator: items n="49" (model answer side; also in gh1-119-1.json)
items.original: Can they produce a short term deficit?
items.problem: "short term" is a compound modifier in front of "deficit" and takes a hyphen: "short-term deficit". As a side effect the correctly hyphenated answer is only graded "partial" (the hyphen is not stripped by the grader's normalizer, so "short-term" and "short term" tokenize differently).
items.correction: "Can they produce a short-term deficit?" - this changes the English text, so regenerate the sentence clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change. Alternatively keep the model and add the hyphenated form as an alternative.

items.locator: items n="54" (model answer side; also in gh1-119-1.json)
items.original: What time did they wake up on their fiftieth anniversary?
items.problem: The Korean prompt uses a numeral ordinal ("그들은 그들의 50번째 기념일에 몇 시에 잠이 깼나?") but only the spelled-out "fiftieth" is accepted. "50th" against "fiftieth" fails looksLikeSameWord (edit distance far above 2; first 4 characters "50th" vs "fift" differ), so "What time did they wake up on their 50th anniversary?" grades "incorrect".
items.correction: Add the alternative "What time did they wake up on their 50th anniversary?".

items.locator: items n="58" (model answer side; also in gh1-119-2.json)
items.original: Weren't three of the victims Danes?
items.problem: "덴마크인" is correctly rendered either as the noun "Danes" or the adjective "Danish", but only "Danes" is accepted. Traced through grammarGrading.ts: "danish" vs "danes" is 2 edits on a 6-letter word (threshold is 1 below length 8) and the 5-character stems differ ("danis" vs "danes"), so "Weren't three of the victims Danish?" grades "incorrect" (0). This is inconsistent with gh1-117 item 19, where the authors deliberately listed both "Weren't the other two Germans?" and "Weren't the other two German?".
items.correction: Add the alternative "Weren't three of the victims Danish?".

items.locator: items n="71" (model answer side, gh1-119-2.json) and the Korean prompt n="71" in gh1-118.json
items.original: It will cover your sex change operation, won't it?
items.problem: "sex change" is explicitly listed as outdated terminology by the AP Stylebook and the NLGJA stylebook, which tell writers to use gender-affirming / gender-confirmation surgery instead. The sentence is drilled and graded, so the course is actively teaching the dated phrasing to learners who will use it in real conversation.
items.correction: "It will cover your gender-affirming surgery, won't it?" with the Korean prompt updated to "그것은 너의 성확정 수술을 커버하겠지?". This changes the English text, so regenerate the clip with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs. If the owner would rather keep the recorded wording, this is one to decide deliberately rather than by default.

items.locator: items n="9" (model answer side; also in gh1-121-1.json)
items.original: Where is new evidence?
items.problem: Unnatural English as a model answer. The Korean prompt "새 증거가 어디에 있나?" asks about specific evidence in a specific case, which in English requires the determiner: "Where is the new evidence?". A bare mass noun here reads like a broken headline. It is also a graded trap: the model is 4 words, so the natural answer (5 words) exceeds MAX_ANSWER_LEN_RATIO (4 x 1.15 = 4.6) and grades "incorrect" - 0 points.
items.correction: Make "Where is the new evidence?" the model answer and keep "Where is new evidence?" as an alternative. Changing the model answer text orphans its Azure Ava clip (the clip key is a hash of the text), so regenerate with node scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.locator: items n="13" and n="14" (Korean prompt side; also in gh1-120-1.json)
items.original: 우리는 알라스카에 많은 충성스런 시청자를 갖고 있다.
items.problem: "알라스카" is a non-standard transliteration; the Korean spelling fixed by 국립국어원 is 알래스카. The same misspelling appears in item 14 ("알라스카도 시간대가 있나?").
items.correction: "우리는 알래스카에 많은 충성스런 시청자를 갖고 있다." and "알래스카도 시간대가 있나?" (Korean-only change.)

items.locator: items n="20" (Korean prompt side; also in gh1-120-2.json)
items.original: 왜 무바락이 그 회담을 취소했나?
items.problem: The same person is transliterated two different ways one item apart: item 19 has "무바라크 이집트 대통령" and item 20 has "무바락". 무바라크 is the standard Korean transliteration of Mubarak.
items.correction: "왜 무바라크가 그 회담을 취소했나?" (Korean-only change; note the particle also changes from 이 to 가.)

items.locator: items n="17" (model answer side; also in gh1-121-1.json)
items.original: Secretary of State Colin Powell is returning home from his Middle East trip.
items.problem: These six lessons are built from 2002 news broadcasts and several items state 2002 facts in the present tense with nothing on the page dating them: this one (Powell was Secretary of State 2001-2005 and died in 2021), gh1-121 n=19/20 ("Egyptian President Mubarak" - out of office since 2011, died 2020), gh1-119 n=52 ("President Bush"), and the Afghanistan/anthrax-vaccine items throughout gh1-116/117 and gh1-122/123. Note that `instruction` and `paragraph` blocks are not rendered by GrammarLearningView, so a note added there would be invisible.
items.correction: Surface a short dated-source line in a field the view actually renders (lesson subtitle / header area for gh1-116 to gh1-123), e.g. "2002년 뉴스 방송 기반 문장입니다". This adds a note only - no English sentence changes, so no audio regeneration is needed.

items.locator: items n="44" (model answer side; also in gh1-123-1.json)
items.original: That information came from war prisoners.
items.problem: "전쟁 포로" is the standard term prisoner of war; "war prisoners" is the marginal variant, and it is the only accepted answer. Traced through grammarGrading.ts: "That information came from prisoners of war." is 7 normalized words against a 6-word model, which exceeds MAX_ANSWER_LEN_RATIO (6 x 1.15 = 6.9), so it grades "incorrect" - 0 points.
items.correction: Add the alternative "That information came from prisoners of war." (and, if the wording is ever changed on the model side, regenerate the clip).

items.locator: items n="65" (model answer side; also in gh1-123-2.json)
items.original: Isiah was arrested April 15.
items.problem: The model uses the American news-wire habit of dropping "on" before a date, but the Korean prompt has the particle 에 ("Isiah는 4월 15일에 체포되었다."), which maps to "on April 15". The model is 5 words, so the natural answer "Isiah was arrested on April 15." (6 words) exceeds MAX_ANSWER_LEN_RATIO (5 x 1.15 = 5.75) and grades "incorrect" - 0 points.
items.correction: Add the alternative "Isiah was arrested on April 15.".

items.locator: gh2-007-1 items[] n="3" (and the same fault at n="9")
items.original: 더 열심히 공부하지 않는 한 (당신은) 결코 그 시험에 통과(합격)하지못할 것입니다.
items.problem: Missing space in '하지못할' (should be '하지 못할'). The same fault is at item 9 of this file: '나는 메시지를 하나(한 메시지를)남겨 두었습니다.' has no space after the closing parenthesis before '남겨'.
items.correction: item 3 → '…그 시험에 통과(합격)하지 못할 것입니다.'; item 9 → '…메시지를 하나(한 메시지를) 남겨 두었습니다.'

items.locator: gh2-008-1 items[] n="10" (Korean prompt for gh2-008 item 10 "It will be ready in a week.")
items.original: 그것은 일주일 내에 준비가 될 것이다.
items.problem: 'in + 기간' with a future verb means AFTER that period has passed (일주일 후에), not within it. '일주일 내에' is 'within a week', which in English is 'within a week' / 'in less than a week' — a different statement. This is the one item in the lesson that teaches the time use of 'in', the lesson's own grammar point, so the gloss teaches the wrong meaning of the target preposition, and it happens to be the exact confusion Korean learners already have. It also breaks grading: I ran the learner answer 'It will be ready within a week.' through the repo's own grader (src/lib/grammarGrading.ts, gradeAgainstReferences) and it scores "incorrect", because 'within' is not in FUNCTION_WORDS and is not a near-miss spelling of 'in'.
items.correction: 그것은 일주일 후에 준비가 될 것이다.  (If the '내에' reading is wanted as a separate drill, it needs its own item with the English 'It will be ready within a week.')

items.original: I used to major in architecture but I dropped it for I was not good at it.
items.problem: 'for' as a coordinating conjunction needs a comma in front of it, otherwise it is first parsed as a preposition and the reader garden-paths on 'I dropped it for …'. The sentence also has no comma before 'but' joining two independent clauses. The item's own alternative punctuates correctly ('I once majored in architecture, but I dropped it because I wasn't good at it.'), so the model answer is the odd one out. Note: this lesson's grammar point is the conjunction 'for', which is exactly where the missing comma hurts most.
items.correction: I used to major in architecture, but I dropped it, for I was not good at it.  (Editing this English text invalidates the sentence's Azure voice clip — regenerate with scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.)

items.original: 나는 건축을 전공한 적이 있었지만, 그것을 잘하지 않았기 때문에 그만 두었다.
items.problem: 'I was not good at it' is an inability, so Korean needs the 능력 부정 '잘하지 못했기 때문에'. '잘하지 않았기 때문에' is the 의지 부정 — 'because I chose not to do it well' — which is both unnatural here and a different claim. ('그만 두었다' is also normally written '그만두었다' as a single word.)
items.correction: 나는 건축을 전공한 적이 있었지만, 그것을 잘하지 못했기 때문에 그만두었다.

items.locator: gh2-010-1 items[] n="6" (Korean prompt for gh2-010 item 6 "They had a disagreement over the best way to do it.")
items.original: 그들은 그것을 하는 가장 좋은 방법에 대한 차이(의견의)가 있었다.
items.problem: The parenthetical is in the wrong place: the intended phrase is '의견의 차이' but it is written '차이(의견의)', which reads as broken Korean. As written the head noun is bare '차이' = 'difference', so the learner is steered to 'They had a difference over the best way to do it.' The repo's grader scores 'They had a difference of opinion over the best way to do it.' as "incorrect" (difference/disagreement is a content-word swap).
items.correction: 그들은 그것을 하는 가장 좋은 방법을 두고 의견 충돌이 있었다.  (If '의견 차이' is preferred as the gloss, also add "They had a difference of opinion over the best way to do it." to the item's alternatives.)

items.original: 모든 그 선물들은 당신을 위해서입니다.
items.problem: This is the only 존댓말 line among the 16 prompts of gh2-010-1 (the other 15 end in 반말 '~다'), and the determiner order '모든 그 선물들은' is a word-for-word tracing of 'All the presents' that no Korean writes; the natural order is '그 선물들은 모두' or '그 선물 전부는'. The same one-off register break occurs at gh2-009-1 item 3.
items.correction: 그 선물들은 모두 당신을 위한 것이다.

items.original: 일월로써는(치고는) 날씨가 꽤 따뜻하다.
items.problem: '로써' is the instrumental particle (수단); the qualifying sense wanted here is '로서는' or, more naturally, the parenthetical that is already there, '치고는'. Item 12 of the same lesson gets it right ('초심자로서는'), so this is a slip rather than a convention.
items.correction: 일월치고는(일월로서는) 날씨가 꽤 따뜻하다.

items.locator: gh2-010-1 items[] n="15" (Korean prompt for gh2-010 item 15 "You are either for me or against me.")
items.original: 너는 내 편이든지 적이다.
items.problem: Two problems. (1) The Korean is not parallel — 'either A or B' is rendered as '~이든지 ~이다', so the 'either … or' frame is invisible. (2) 'against me' is replaced by the noun '적' (enemy), which removes the preposition the lesson is built around ('for' vs 'against'). A learner rendering this prompt writes something like 'You are either on my side or my enemy.', which the repo's grader scores "incorrect" (only 4 of 8 model words align).
items.correction: 너는 내 편이든지 아니면 나에게 반대하는 편이든지 둘 중 하나다.

items.original: {"n":"1","text":"Whom do you live with?"}
items.problem: 'Whom …with?' is the least-used of the three possible forms: modern standard English for this Korean prompt ('너는 누구와 함께 사나?') is 'Who do you live with?', with 'With whom do you live?' as the formal register. Both score only "partial" against the current reference list (measured with src/lib/grammarGrading.ts), and neither is listed as an alternative. Elsewhere this course does supply such variants (travelled/traveled in item 9 of this same lesson, theatre/theater, on/in the subway), so the omission here is inconsistent rather than deliberate.
items.correction: Add alternatives: ["Who do you live with?", "With whom do you live?"]. (Adding alternatives does not change any existing sentence text, so no voice clip is affected.)

items.locator: gh2-011 items[] n="6" (with its Korean at gh2-011-1 n="6")
items.original: With the Asian economy in recession, the IMF is demanding structural reforms.
items.problem: This describes the 1997-98 Asian financial crisis, but both the English and the Korean ('아이엠에프는 구조 개혁을 요구하고 있다') are in the present progressive, so a 2026 learner meets it as a statement about the present. There is no such Asia-wide recession or IMF structural-reform programme now; the Korea, Thailand and Indonesia programmes belong to 1997-98. The grammar point (the 'with + noun + phrase' absolute construction) does not depend on the topic.
items.correction: Put it in the past — 'With the Asian economy in recession, the IMF demanded structural reforms.' — or replace the content entirely, e.g. 'With the meeting running late, we ordered dinner.' Either edit changes the English text, so regenerate the voice clip with scripts/generate-azure-ava.mjs in the same change.

items.original: 그는 한 책을 갖고 왔다.
items.problem: '한 책' is not grammatical Korean — a counter is obligatory ('책 한 권'). This is a systematic convention in the course (it exists to cue the English article 'a'), and most instances are harmless, but a few produce Korean that cannot be said: gh2-011-1 item 2 '한 책을', gh2-007-1 item 9 '메시지를 하나(한 메시지를)', gh2-010-1 item 10 '하나의 충고를'. The article can still be cued with a well-formed counter.
items.correction: 그는 책 한 권을 가지고 왔다.  (gh2-007-1 #9 → '메시지를 하나 남겨 두었습니다.'; gh2-010-1 #10 → '충고 한마디를 들으려고'.)

items.original: 그 연극은 셰익스피어에 의하여 씌어졌다(셰익스피어가 썼다).
items.problem: '씌어졌다' stacks two passives ('쓰이-' + '-어지-'), which standard Korean rejects; the correct passive of '쓰다' here is '쓰였다'. Since this item is the course's showcase of the English passive ('was written by'), the Korean rendering of a passive should itself be well formed.
items.correction: 그 연극은 셰익스피어에 의해 쓰였다(셰익스피어가 썼다).

items.original: {"n":"20","text":"He will solve the problem.","alternatives":["He would solve the problem."]}
items.problem: The Korean prompt is the plain future '그는 그 문제를 해결할 것이다.' Standing alone, 'He would solve the problem.' does not render that: 'would' is either a past-in-the-future inside reported speech, a conditional consequence, or a past habit — none of which the prompt supplies. Accepting it for full marks tells the learner that 'will' and 'would' are interchangeable in a lesson (items 10-21) whose whole purpose is to separate the modals. The same conflation appears in item 12 of this lesson from the other direction.
items.correction: Delete the alternative. If a 'would' drill is wanted, give it its own item with a Korean prompt that supplies the past frame, e.g. '그는 그 문제를 해결할 것이라고 말했다.' → "He said he would solve the problem."

items.locator: gh2-013-1 items[] n="1" (Korean prompt for gh2-013 item 1 "I ask you out of curiosity.")
items.original: 나는 호기심으로부터 너에게 묻는다.
items.problem: '호기심으로부터' is not Korean anyone writes; it is a word-for-word tracing of 'out of'. The natural form is '호기심에서' or '호기심으로'. Worse, '~으로부터' maps to the English 'from', so the prompt actively pushes the learner to 'I ask you from curiosity.' — which the repo's grader scores "incorrect" (only 4 of 6 model words align, below the 0.7 floor). The lesson's point is the idiom 'out of + 원인', so the prompt undermines the item.
items.correction: 나는 호기심에서 너에게 묻는다.

items.locator: gh2-013-1 items[] n="12" (Korean prompt for gh2-013 item 12 "He would not answer.")
items.original: 그는 대답하지 않으려 한다(했다, 할 것이다).
items.problem: 'would not' here is past refusal, so the only correct gloss is '대답하지 않으려 했다'. The prompt leads with the present '한다' and explicitly offers the future '할 것이다', both of which translate to 'He will not answer.' — a different sentence from the model answer. A learner who takes the offered '할 것이다' reading writes 'He will not answer.' and the repo's grader scores it "partial", not full, because will/would are both function words. In a lesson whose entire subject is modal nuance, the prompt erases the nuance it is testing.
items.correction: 그는 (끝내) 대답하지 않으려 했다.

items.original: 그는 그 시험에 대하여 준비할 때 도서관에 가곤 했다.
items.problem: '준비하다' takes the object particle '을/를'; '~에 대하여 준비하다' is a tracing of 'prepare for' and is ungrammatical Korean. (The same '에 대하여' tracing appears at gh2-012-1 item 14, '소매치기에 대하여 경고 받는다', where '소매치기를 조심하라는 경고를 받는다' is natural.)
items.correction: 그는 그 시험을 준비할 때 도서관에 가곤 했다.

items.locator: gh2-014-1 items[] n="8" (and '세 폭탄이' again at n="10")
items.original: 세 폭탄이 폭발하여 하나가 25 사람을 부상시켰다.
